signals.title: feat(ptu): fetch azure_billing flat cost via Cost Management API (LIT-4077 POC)
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Part of the LIT-1697 Azure PTU cost attribution stack; stacked on #33439 (stage 5) ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4077 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review Opened as a draft POC to align on the customer-facing story before a real review pass. Full merge review follows after v1 (stages 1-5) ships and the customer walkthrough lands ## Delays in PR merge? Not applicable; POC, not requesting review yet ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live end-to-end against a real Azure subscription. Both flags enabled at runtime, a reservation with `cost_source=azure_billing` created via API, the backfill CLI acquires a real Entra ID token, calls Cost Management, and writes the response Backfill log: ``` 2026-07-20 16:29:53 INFO azure.identity._internal.get_token_mixin: ClientSecretCredential.get_token_info succeeded 2026-07-20 16:29:55 INFO LiteLLM Proxy: PTU rollup: azure_billing reservation=fd26ded5-... day=2026-07-20 resource=/subscriptions/<redacted>/.../deployments/gpt-4-ptu returned $0.0000 [2026-07-20] reservations=2 rows_written=1 ``` The $0.00 is a real Azure response for a resource id with no billing history in the dev sub; a customer's own PTU deployment returns its accrued cost on the same code path. Currency is USD, verified against the sub via the Cost Management response Validator rejection when `azure_resource_id` is missing: ``` $ curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4097/ptu_reservation/new \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"team_id":"...","model":"...","cost_source":"azure_billing","effective_from":"2026-07-01T00:00:00Z"}' HTTP 400 {"detail":{"error":"azure_resource_id is required when cost_source='azure_billing'"}} ``` Restart persistence (both flags survive `_sync_ui_settings_to_general_settings`): ``` INFO proxy_server: PTU reservation rollup job scheduled at 00:15 UTC daily (no-ops until enable_ptu_cost_attribution is set) INFO proxy_server: Synced UI settings to general_settings on startup: ['enable_ptu_cost_attribution', 'enable_azure_ptu_billing_pull'] ``` ## Type New Feature ## Changes A thin async client at `litellm/integrations/azure_cost_management/` calls one Cost Management endpoint the rollup needs. Entra ID auth is inherited from `get_azure_ad_token_from_entra_id` so no new dependency lands. The client is deliberately narrow (one public method) and follows the `litellm/integrations/` pattern (see `datadog/`, `langfuse/`, etc.) A new UI settings flag `enable_azure_ptu_billing_pull` composes below `enable_ptu_cost_attribution` and reuses the stage 5 machinery (UISettings model, `ALLOWED_UI_SETTINGS_FIELDS`, `_RUNTIME_GENERAL_SETTINGS_FLAGS`). Persistence and startup sync are inherited without touching those code paths `_compute_daily_flat_cost` in the rollup branches on `cost_source`: manual keeps the existing (`ptu_count * cost_per_ptu`) / days-in-month formula, `azure_billing` calls the injected fetcher, unknown values return 0 with a warning. The function is now async since it awaits the client, and existing sync tests were converted accordingly The scheduler wraps the rollup in a small callable that builds a fetcher just-in-time via `_build_azure_cost_fetcher_if_enabled` so runtime flag flips take effect without a proxy restart. The helper reads `general_settings.enable_azure_ptu_billing_pull`, the configured `subscription_id`, and env vars for creds; on any missing input it returns None and the rollup no-ops for `azure_billing` rows The CRUD gate is relaxed: the earlier blanket reject on `cost_source=azure_billing` becomes a check that `azure_resource_id` is present. The pydantic domain validator from stage 1 already enforces the rest (`ptu_count`/`cost_per_ptu` must be null, `azure_resource_id` required) The backfill CLI grows a matching helper (`_build_backfill_azure_fetcher`) so operators running `scripts/ptu_reservation_backfill.py` exercise the same code path as the scheduler when `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` and Entra ID env creds are set Deferred to follow-up tickets: retry/backoff on 429/503, sliding-window reconciliation for Azure's 24-72h reporting lag, UI toggle for `cost_source` on the reservation create form, non-USD currency handling, Prometheus counter for fetch failures ## Behavior changes `cost_source=azure_billing` on `POST /ptu_reservation/new` is now accepted (previously rejected with "not supported in this release") when `azure_resource_id` is present For reservations with `cost_source=azure_billing` that reach the daily rollup: with `enable_azure_ptu_billing_pull` on and Entra ID env creds resolvable, `flat_cost` is fetched from Azure; with the flag off or creds missing, the reservation is skipped with a warning and no sentinel row is written No change to manual reservations or to the read path (`/team/daily/activity`, Usage page) ## QA runbook Prereqs: dev proxy on 4097 with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`; env vars `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` from a service principal with `Cost Management Reader` on the target subscription; `config.yaml` has `general_settings.azure_ptu_billing.subscription_id: os.environ/AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` 1. `curl -X PATCH http://localhost:4097/update/ui_settings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"enable_ptu_cost_attribution": true, "enable_azure_ptu_billing_pull": true}'` 2. `curl -X POST http://localhost:4097/ptu_reservation/new` with a body that sets `cost_source=azure_billing` and a real Azure `azure_resource_id` 3. `.venv/bin/python scripts/ptu_reservation_backfill.py --date $(date -u +%F)`; watch for the log line `PTU rollup: azure_billing reservation=... returned $...` 4. `curl 'http://localhost:4097/team/daily/activity?team_ids=<team>&start_date=<today>&end_date=<today>'`; `flat_cost` is populated when the Azure resource has billing history 5. Restart the proxy; startup log shows `Synced UI settings to general_settings on startup: ['enable_ptu_cost_attribution', 'enable_azure_ptu_billing_pull']` 6. Toggle either flag off via `/update/ui_settings` and re-run backfill; azure_billing reservation is skipped with a warning, manual reservations continue to accrue ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(bedrock): preserve tools in Converse streams
signals.text: ## What this fixes When a Bedrock Converse request combines `response_format` with normal user tools, a real tool call can be exposed to a streaming client as ordinary JSON text instead of an OpenAI-compatible `tool_call`. Agent SDKs then treat the JSON as a final assistant message and do not run the tool. For example, a model response intended as: ```text tool_call: get_metrics_by_prefix({"prefix":"trace.grpc.server"}) ``` could be emitted as: ```text assistant message: {"prefix":"trace.grpc.server"} ``` ## Why it happens LiteLLM uses the internal `json_tool_call` tool to emulate `response_format` for Bedrock models that cannot use native structured output. There are two independent streaming paths where that internal tool can be confused with a real user tool: 1. **Bedrock's real stream**: content blocks can be interleaved. A single mutable "current tool name" is overwritten by a `json_tool_call` block, so a later delta belonging to a real tool is filtered as JSON output. 2. **Fake stream**: LiteLLM first receives one complete Converse response and wraps it as a stream. With `json_mode=True`, the wrapper converted the first tool call to text without checking its name. ## What changed - Track tool names by Bedrock `contentBlockIndex`, isolating interleaved blocks in the real stream decoder. - In fake streams, identify the internal `json_tool_call` by name. - Convert only that internal tool to message text; keep real tools as `tool_use` so OpenAI-compatible streaming clients can execute them. ## Behaviour preserved - A response containing only LiteLLM's internal `json_tool_call` still produces the structured JSON text expected by `response_format`. - Requests without `json_mode` keep their existing behavior. ## Tests - Interleaved real-tool and `json_tool_call` Bedrock stream blocks preserve the real tool's arguments. - Fake stream with a real tool preserves `tool_use`. - Fake stream with only `json_tool_call` still emits JSON text. ```bash python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/bedrock/chat/test_converse_transformation.py::test_streaming_interleaved_json_tool_call_does_not_hide_real_tool_delta -q python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/bedrock/chat/test_invoke_handler.py -k 'fake_stream_json_mode' -q ``` All three targeted tests pass.

signals.title: fix(fireworks_ai): support router slugs via routers/ prefix
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `fireworks_ai/<slug>` always expands to `accounts/fireworks/models/<slug>`, so Fireworks routers 404 on short slugs - Only workaround is the full id `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/routers/<id>`, which most users do not know - Chat and text-completion transforms had drifted: chat had a `-fast` router branch, text completion did not How it solves it: - Add shared `resolve_fireworks_resource_name` helper mapping `routers/<id>` and `models/<id>` onto `accounts/fireworks/...` - Keeps the `-fast` router heuristic and defaults bare slugs to `models/`, so existing configs keep working - Both chat and text-completion transforms call it, so the two paths cannot drift again ## User Flow Before: a developer whose traffic goes through a Fireworks router gets 404s unless they know the full resource path 1. The proxy admin configures a deployment with `model: fireworks_ai/routers/glm-latest` and starts the proxy 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "fw-glm-latest"` 3. They get back HTTP 404 with "Model not found, inaccessible, and/or not deployed", because the request went out addressed to a model path instead of the router 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/completions against the same deployment fails the same way 5. The only fix is rewriting the config to the full `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/routers/glm-latest` id After: the same short config reaches the router and returns completions 1. The proxy admin configures a deployment with `model: fireworks_ai/routers/glm-latest` and starts the proxy 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "fw-glm-latest"` 3. They get HTTP 200 with a completion from whichever model the Fireworks router selected 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/completions against the same deployment also returns 200 5. Existing configs using bare slugs like `fireworks_ai/glm-4p6` still resolve to `accounts/fireworks/models/glm-4p6` and keep working unchanged ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5294 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Before this change, the auto-expanded target for a router slug is a model path, which 404s: ``` $ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $FIREWORKS_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"accounts/fireworks/models/firerouter","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":1}' {"error":{"message":"Model not found, inaccessible, and/or not deployed","param":"model","code":"NOT_FOUND","type":"error"}} HTTP 404 ``` With this change, `fireworks_ai/routers/<id>` resolves to the router path. Config used: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: fw-firerouter litellm_params: model: fireworks_ai/routers/firerouter api_key: os.environ/FIREWORKS_API_KEY - model_name: fw-glm-latest litellm_params: model: fireworks_ai/routers/glm-latest api_key: os.environ/FIREWORKS_API_KEY ``` Started with `litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000`, then: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"fw-firerouter","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in one word"}],"max_tokens":8}' {"id":"chatcmpl-5a6b452b5be84d979cc43ebe318f2ab9","model":"fw-firerouter","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"length","index":0,"message":{"content":"1. Identify the core request:","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":17,"total_tokens":25}} HTTP 200 $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"fw-glm-latest","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":5}' {"id":"chatcmpl-0139d1112d714e46887a4183266ccc85","model":"fw-glm-latest","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"length","index":0,"message":{"content":"Let me consider how to","role":"assistant"}}]} HTTP 200 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Rerank and embeddings are intentionally untouched; they use different endpoint naming rules - Bare slugs still default to `models/`, so routers must be addressed as `routers/<id>` ## Changes `resolve_fireworks_resource_name` centralizes the model-to-resource mapping that was previously inlined in the chat transform and partially in the text-completion transform. Both transforms now call it. Rerank and embeddings are intentionally untouched because they use different endpoint naming rules (embeddings explicitly rejects the `accounts/fireworks` prefix) Rebased onto current `litellm_internal_staging` after the LIT010 / LIT011 lint pass landed, so the chat transform now binds the resolved name to a `Final` local instead of rebinding the `model` parameter, and the text-completion transform keeps its `Final` on `data`. Dropping those two parameter rebinds lowers the LIT011 ceiling in `type-discipline-budget.json` by 3, per `make lint-budget-update` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(anthropic_messages): make tool_result images visible to OpenAI-compatible providers
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Images returned by tools vanish on `/v1/messages` for OpenAI-compatible models: the chat adapter buries them as text inside `role:"tool"` messages and the Responses adapter (the default openai/azure path) drops them entirely - The model answers from the filename or hallucinates a description instead of seeing the image How it solves it: - The adapter emits tool_result images as structured `image_url` parts - A shared helper moves tool images into a `role:"user"` message right after the tool messages, the shape OpenAI documents for image-producing tools - The Responses adapter forwards them as `input_image` parts ## Relevant issues Fixes #24968 (closed as stale, never fixed). That report describes the single-image flattening on the bedrock converse route; change 1 below is the direct fix for it, and the reporter's sentinel-text-block workaround becomes unnecessary ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real providers, no mocks. Plain Claude Code (claude CLI 2.1.215) with only its built-in Read tool, pointed at the proxy and asked to read a local png containing an unguessable token; the model can only report the token if it truly received the pixels ```yaml model_list: - model_name: vision-model litellm_params: model: mistral/mistral-medium-2508 # chat-completions adapter path api_key: os.environ/MISTRAL_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config config.yaml --port 4000 --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee proxy.log # from the directory containing screenshot.png: HOME=/tmp/cchome \ ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-1234 \ ANTHROPIC_MODEL=vision-model ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL=vision-model \ claude --allowedTools "Read" \ -p "Read $(pwd)/screenshot.png once. If the result isn't a viewable image, reply exactly NO_IMAGE and stop -- no retry, no OCR, no more thinking. If you can see it, reply only with the exact text in the image." ``` Note on the commit hashes below: the branch has since been rebased onto current `litellm_internal_staging` and squashed to a single commit, `bc8d2b6539`. The proof was captured at `729064d4a2`, which no longer exists in the PR. The rebase carried the fix forward unchanged apart from typing-syntax modernization that staging now requires (`Union[A, B]` written as `A | B`, `: Final` on the new module constants, and the two hook lines rewritten to bind a new local instead of rebinding the `messages` parameter now that LIT011 is enforced, plus a one-line `reportUnnecessaryComparison` suppression in `factory.py` where the widened tool-message type makes a defensive Anthropic-native image branch look dead to the type checker), so the behavior the capture shows is the behavior at the current head BEFORE (commit 1b2a7ce518): the model answers NO_IMAGE. proxy.log confirms the image reached litellm but zero image_url parts went out to Mistral; the data URI sits as text inside the `role:"tool"` message AFTER (commit 729064d4a2): the model replies with the exact token in the image ("WOMBAT-5391"). proxy.log shows the tool message carrying only the placeholder and the image going out in the next user message: ``` role': 'tool', 'tool_call_id': 'fG3gku10x', 'content': '[Tool returned an image - see the following user message]' {'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': {'url': 'data:image/png;b... ``` Responses path (model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini, the default openai route), same setup driven by the Agent SDK (claude-agent-sdk 0.2.125). BEFORE, the image is dropped and `function_call_output.output` is an empty string. AFTER: ``` ASSISTANT: The image shows the text **"ZEBRA-4712"** in large blue letters on a white background. ``` ``` function_call_output', 'call_id': 'call_NoVf5Ueh4zhHrEvCoBFYEq2R', 'output': '[Tool returned an image - see the following user message]' input_image', 'image_url': 'data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEU... ``` An MCP tool returning an image (the other real-client shape) trips and fixes the same way on both paths Both proofs re-run at 2e248c769c (post-review cleanup commit): built-in Read on the mistral path and MCP on the gpt-5.4-mini Responses path both read the exact token, with the placeholder in the tool output and the image going out in the following user message Re-run once more at 79b0ef2c66, after merging litellm_internal_staging and the type-discipline refactor: built-in Read through the mistral chat path and the gpt-5.4-mini Responses path both read the exact token from a fresh image, and the outbound bodies carry the placeholder in the tool output plus the hoisted image in the following user message on both paths ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Tools that return images on `/v1/messages` (Claude Code's built-in Read, MCP tools, computer-use screenshots) produce an Anthropic `tool_result` block with an `image` item. The chat-completions adapter (mistral, xai, qwen, openrouter, groq and every other OpenAI-compatible provider) serialized that image as a data-URI string inside the `role:"tool"` message, where the OpenAI spec only allows text, so providers read it as text. The Responses API adapter (the default for openai and azure) only extracted text parts, so the image was dropped outright. This PR fixes both paths: 1. `adapters/transformation.py`: a single-image `tool_result` becomes a structured `image_url` part instead of a bare string. This matters beyond consistency: a bare URL string is indistinguishable from a tool legitimately returning a URL as text, so no downstream code could ever fix that case. Single-item text results keep the string format 2. `common_utils.py`: new `hoist_images_from_tool_messages` replaces image content in tool messages with a text placeholder and inserts the images as a `role:"user"` message after the run of consecutive tool messages, preserving the tool_calls/tool adjacency that strict providers validate. It runs at the top of `OpenAIGPTConfig._transform_messages`, which every OpenAI-compatible provider config reaches, and in `AzureOpenAIConfig.transform_request`, which builds its request outside that pipeline 3. `responses_adapters/transformation.py`: tool_result images become `input_image` parts in the user message that already follows the `function_call_output` items; the output keeps its text plus the placeholder 4. `types/llms/openai.py`: `ChatCompletionToolMessage.content` now admits image parts, which the adapter has produced for multi-item results since computer-use support landed Native providers are unaffected: they never hit these adapters and the hoist runs only in the OpenAI-compatible layer. The Gemini and Bedrock chat-completions converters already handle structured `image_url` parts, so change 1 routes their single-image case through the supported branch; for bedrock non-Claude models that fixes the latent bug in #24968 where the data URI was forwarded as toolResult text. One pre-existing gap stays out of scope: sambanova, azure_ai and github_copilot override `_transform_messages` without reaching the base implementation Tests cover the helper in isolation (base64 and URL sources, multi-item results, parallel tool calls, bare-string and None-content pass-through, no input mutation), the full anthropic-to-openai pipeline at the transform_request level, mistral's override chain, sync and async transforms, and the responses adapter. Existing tests that pinned the bare-string shape were updated ## QA runbook Run the two proofs above: start the proxy with the mistral config and run the claude CLI command from a directory containing a png with readable text (expect the model to quote the text), then switch the model to `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and repeat (Responses path). In both runs grep proxy.log for `image_url` / `input_image` to confirm the image goes out in a user message and the tool output carries the placeholder ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(router): register arbitrary custom pricing thresholds
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem: * Router dropped undeclared `*_above_<N>_tokens` pricing fields. * Threshold discovery depended on input-cost fields, so standalone output and cache thresholds were accepted but silently ignored. Solution: * Preserve declared and regex-matched custom pricing fields during initial and dynamic Router registration. * Select the highest applicable threshold independently for input, output, cache creation, cache creation above 1 hour, and cache read pricing. * Preserve base-rate and service-tier fallback behavior. ## Relevant issues Fixes #34378 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist * [x] I have added meaningful tests * [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks — all 25 GitHub Actions workflows pass on the current head * [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem * [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Verified PR head: ```text b64d0a6eee85da7947ab4901f7ba9b0821fd4edd ``` Standalone output threshold: ```text registered_output_tier=1.8e-05 actual_completion_cost=0.018000000000000002 expected_completion_cost=0.018000000000000002 ``` Standalone cache-read threshold: ```text registered_cache_tier=4e-06 actual_cache_read_rate=4e-06 expected_cache_read_rate=4e-06 ``` An inactive input threshold no longer suppresses an independently active output threshold. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes * Preserve arbitrary `*_above_<N>_tokens` fields accepted by `LiteLLM_Params`. * Apply the registration helper during initial and dynamic deployment registration. * Keep deployment pricing isolated from shared backend entries. * Select thresholds independently for all supported cost categories. * Parse nested keys such as `cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_1hr_above_32k_tokens`. * Add output-only, cache-only, and independent-threshold regression coverage. ## Tests ```text Cost calculation: 105 passed Router isolation: 20 passed, 2 deselected Custom pricing: 16 passed Ruff format/lint: passed GitHub Actions workflows: 25 passed ``` All GitHub Actions workflows, including OSV Scan, pass on the current head. ### Final Attestation * [x] Tests cover standalone output/cache configurations and independent thresholds * [x] The fix exercises real Router registration and cost-calculation paths * [x] No dependency or lockfile changes are included

signals.title: fix(caching): cache anthropic /v1/messages responses, including streaming
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/v1/messages` requests never hit the response cache - Anthropic-only params (`system`, `top_k`) skipped the cache key - Streamed `/v1/messages` responses had no cache path How it solves it: - Add `anthropic_messages`/`aanthropic_messages` to cached call types - Feed the Anthropic Messages request shape into cache keys - Tee streams out, replay stored SSE bytes on a hit ## User Flow Before: a team routing Claude traffic through `/v1/messages` on a cache-enabled proxy never gets cache hits, so every repeated request is billed again 1. The proxy admin enables response caching (`cache: true`) and restarts the proxy 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":64,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: LIT-4796 cache probe"}]}` and gets an answer with id `msg_011Ce3Ls1e...` after ~12.6s 3. They repeat the identical request and a different id `msg_011Ce3LsMB...` comes back after ~4.3s, so the provider answered and billed both calls 4. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=caching the Cache Hits vs API Requests chart shows `/v1/messages` traffic at zero hits while the same prompts on `/v1/chat/completions` show real hits 5. The admin works around it by adding `anthropic_messages` to `cache_params.supported_call_types`; repeats now hit the cache, but a request whose only difference is `"system":"Always answer with the single word BETA"` is answered with the ALPHA response cached for a different system prompt, a wrong answer served across requests 6. Still under the workaround, sending the request with `"stream": true` twice returns two different `msg_` ids at full latency, so streams are always billed After: the same `/v1/messages` traffic is served from cache with no config override, streams replay byte for byte, and differing system prompts stay separate 1. The proxy admin enables response caching (`cache: true`) and restarts the proxy 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same body and gets an answer with id `msg_011Ce3ZKCC...` after ~2.5s 3. They repeat the identical request and the same `msg_011Ce3ZKCC...` id returns in ~0.007s, served from cache with no provider charge 4. A request differing only in `"system":"Always answer with the single word BETA"` gets its own fresh BETA answer, and repeating the ALPHA request replays the ALPHA entry 5. Sending the request with `"stream": true` twice gets the second stream back in ~0.013s, byte-identical to the first with the same `msg_` id 6. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=caching now shows `/v1/messages` cache hits and cached completion tokens climbing ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4796 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two live proxies hitting the real Anthropic API (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`), config is just `cache: true` with `cache_params.type: local`, no `supported_call_types` override: a before proxy at merge base `422d925334` (`litellm_internal_staging`) and an after proxy at `9a1e63c9f0` (this PR's tip) A side by side before/after recording of the same runs is in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1784934769340439?thread_ts=1784934769.340439&cid=C0BE49SAUE6), captured at an earlier tip of this branch Before, at `422d925334`; the same request twice returns two different `msg_` ids at full latency, so both calls were billed ``` $ for i in 1 2; do curl -s -o /tmp/ns_$i.json -w "non-streaming #$i latency=%{time_total}s " http://localhost:35726/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":64,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: LIT-4796 cache probe"}]}' python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/ns_$i.json'));print('id='+d['id'],'text='+d['content'][0]['text'])"; done non-streaming #1 latency=12.574026s id=msg_011Ce3Ls1eD4JeLETNiD75Jh text=LIT-4796 cache probe non-streaming #2 latency=4.302459s id=msg_011Ce3LsMBxMcxQzbzJVp8dX text=LIT-4796 cache probe ``` Before, at `422d925334`, with the call type forced into `cache_params.supported_call_types` as a workaround; caching turns on but two different system prompts share one entry, and the BETA request is answered with the ALPHA response at cache-hit latency ``` $ for s in ALPHA BETA; do curl -s -w ' latency=%{time_total}s
' http://localhost:35726/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -d "{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":16,"system":"Always answer with the single word $s","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}"; done system=ALPHA id=msg_011Ce3M1gKs2KuYUhheiNVHH text=ALPHA latency=6.075752s system=BETA id=msg_011Ce3M1gKs2KuYUhheiNVHH text=ALPHA latency=0.182374s ``` Before, at `422d925334`; streaming is never cached under either config, two runs of the same request return two different streams at full latency ``` stream 1: latency=5.217521s first id: msg_011Ce3LuUZGaFeSxZV33an9a stream 2: latency=2.089916s first id: msg_011Ce3LudSZGKzQM5h2XzzFk $ diff p1_stream1.sse p1_stream2.sse # STREAMS DIFFER ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; non-streaming repeats now serve from cache ``` non-streaming #1 latency=2.485229s id=msg_011Ce3ZKCCLQ9YyEvBN7UxCQ text=LIT-4796 cache probe non-streaming #2 latency=0.100351s id=msg_011Ce3ZKCCLQ9YyEvBN7UxCQ text=LIT-4796 cache probe non-streaming #3 latency=0.006568s id=msg_011Ce3ZKCCLQ9YyEvBN7UxCQ text=LIT-4796 cache probe ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; system prompts no longer collide, and repeating the first one replays its own entry ``` $ for s in ALPHA BETA ALPHA; do curl -s -w ' latency=%{time_total}s
' http://localhost:29752/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -d "{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":64,"system":"Always answer with the single word $s","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}"; done system=ALPHA id=msg_011Ce3ZKqSwN6ZLqcXKNdTW5 text=ALPHA latency=1.305376s system=BETA id=msg_011Ce3ZKwGvvzEzerYCbPdSa text=BETA latency=1.331643s system=ALPHA id=msg_011Ce3ZKqSwN6ZLqcXKNdTW5 text=ALPHA latency=0.004050s ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; an Anthropic-native param gets its own cache entry (`stop_sequences` shown live because the Anthropic API now rejects `top_k` as deprecated on claude-sonnet-5; `top_k` and `stop_sequences` key separation are both unit-tested) ``` stop_sequences #1 latency=1.145369s id=msg_011Ce3ZLeuDVXa9AaMhxEof2 text=LIT-4796 cache probe stop_sequences #2 latency=0.007018s id=msg_011Ce3ZLeuDVXa9AaMhxEof2 plain repeat: latency=0.007410s id=msg_011Ce3ZKCCLQ9YyEvBN7UxCQ (its own entry stayed intact) ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; streaming replays the stored SSE byte for byte ``` $ for i in 1 2; do curl -s -N -o /tmp/st_$i.sse -w "streaming #$i latency=%{time_total}s
" http://localhost:29752/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":32,"stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: LIT-4796 stream probe"}]}'; done streaming #1 latency=2.535861s 1325 bytes id=msg_011Ce3ZMLXSghN3PAbRW6KeQ streaming #2 latency=0.012872s 1325 bytes id=msg_011Ce3ZMLXSghN3PAbRW6KeQ $ diff /tmp/st_1.sse /tmp/st_2.sse && echo "streams byte-identical" streams byte-identical ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; controls on the shared surfaces stay healthy: `/v1/chat/completions` repeats hit (same `chatcmpl-c0a1efa0...` id, 0.008s), `/v1/responses` repeats serve the cached payload (identical inner output id and `created_at`, 0.005s; the outer `resp_` envelope id is re-minted, which is pre-existing Responses behavior), and a non-streaming request after the streaming pair gets a fresh normal JSON message rather than the cached SSE bytes ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `anthropic_messages` and `aanthropic_messages` join `CachingSupportedCallTypes` and the default supported call types, which are now a single `DEFAULT_CACHING_SUPPORTED_CALL_TYPES` tuple instead of the same literal list repeated in `Cache.__init__`, `enable_cache` and `update_cache` Enabling the call type on its own would have been unsafe. The cache key is built from `ModelParamHelper._get_all_llm_api_params()`, which is the union of the chat completions, embeddings, transcription, rerank and Responses API param sets; none of those contain `system`, `top_k` or `stop_sequences`, so a `/v1/messages` request keyed on the remaining fields collides with any other request that differs only in those, as the second "before" run above shows. The Anthropic Messages request shape now contributes to that union. `system` is added to the logging exclusion set so it stays out of standard logging model parameters like `messages` and `prompt` do, and `litellm_metadata` joins `metadata` in the excluded kwargs since it is per-request bookkeeping rather than part of the request identity Streaming needed a separate path. A streamed response is handed back to the caller before `LLMCachingHandler.async_set_cache` runs; chat completion streams are teed inside `CustomStreamWrapper` and Responses API streams inside their own iterator, and Anthropic Messages had no equivalent, so `wrap_streaming_result_for_cache` wraps the outgoing iterator in `AnthropicMessagesStreamCacheWriter`. It forwards every chunk unchanged and buffers the raw bytes, then decodes, splits into SSE events, and writes them under the same cache key only once the joined stream ends in `message_stop` without an `error` event, so an abandoned or failed stream is never stored, and `aiter_bytes()` frames that split a multibyte character or an SSE line across chunk boundaries neither crash the stream nor defeat the terminal-event check. On a hit, `CachedAnthropicMessagesStreamIterator` replays those bytes and runs the usual end-of-stream logging with `cache_hit` set, and the passthrough logging handler reports zero cost for it instead of billing the replay Tests cover the miss-then-hit for both modes, the system prompt separation, `top_k` and `stop_sequences` separation, streamed and non-streamed entries not sharing a key, the two cases where a stream must not be cached, and chunk-split regressions (a multibyte character, the `message_stop` line, and an `error` event each split across frames); the cache key assertions live alongside the existing key tests in `tests/test_litellm/caching/test_caching.py` ## Caveats (if any) - `cache: true` proxies start caching `/v1/messages` by default now - Streamed and non-streamed requests cache under separate entries - Provider-specific params outside the Anthropic request shape still need `enable_caching_on_provider_specific_optional_params` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c1d7d5eab6d44b6f9a56086768f3b8e8 Requested by: @shivamrawat1

This follows the same pattern as other JSON providers (e.g. Pinstripes). ## Test plan - [x] Added `tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/test_openinfer_provider.py` - [ ] `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/test_openinfer_provider.py` - [ ] Manual: `litellm.completion(model="openinfer/<model>", api_key=...)` when a key is available Closes #34357 Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signals.title: feat(providers): add SCX.ai as a JSON-configured OpenAI-compatible provider
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - SCX.ai is not a supported provider, so callers have to route through `openai/` with a custom `api_base` - SCX.ai takes `max_tokens` rather than `max_completion_tokens`, and caps `temperature` How it solves it: - Registers `scx-ai` in `litellm/llms/openai_like/providers.json` with the parameter mapping and the ceiling as a constraint, so no Python module is needed - Adds GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.8 Max to the cost map, and registers the provider in the endpoint matrix and the dashboard ## Relevant issues Docs live in the other repo, so the provider page goes up separately in [BerriAI/litellm-docs#808](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/808). That one is a prerequisite here: `documentation` and `code-quality` both run `tests/documentation_tests/test_env_keys.py`, which checks out `BerriAI/litellm-docs` and fails while `SCX_API_KEY` is read under `./litellm` but mentioned nowhere in the docs. Both jobs go green once it merges ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All captured at `1e24f93d3` against the real SCX.ai API, with the proxy started as `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config scx_config.yaml --port 4000` on a config with both models pointed at `os.environ/SCX_API_KEY` Chat completions, with the cost header showing the new rates being applied ```bash $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS -D /tmp/h_$m.txt http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Reply with exactly: hello from SCX\"}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", content: .choices[0].message.content}" grep -i "^x-litellm-response-cost:" /tmp/h_$m.txt done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","content":"hello from SCX"} x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0002285815 {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","content":"hello from SCX"} x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0004901237 ``` Tool calling and `json_schema` structured output on both ```bash $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is the weather in Sydney? Use the tool.\"}],\"tools\":[{\"type\":\"function\",\"function\":{\"name\":\"get_weather\",\"description\":\"Get the weather for a city\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"city\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"city\"]}}}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", tool: .choices[0].message.tool_calls[0].function}" done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","tool":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Sydney\"}","name":"get_weather"}} {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","tool":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Sydney\"}","name":"get_weather"}} $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"City is Sydney\"}],\"response_format\":{\"type\":\"json_schema\",\"json_schema\":{\"name\":\"c\",\"schema\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"city\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"city\"],\"additionalProperties\":false}}},\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", content: .choices[0].message.content}" done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","content":"{\n \"city\": \"Sydney\"\n}"} {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","content":"{\"city\":\"Sydney\"}"} ``` Image input on Qwen3.8 Max, which is the one of the two that declares `supports_vision`, sending a 64x64 solid red PNG as a data URI ```bash $ IMG=$(base64 -i red64.png) $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"scx-qwen3.8-max\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"What colour fills this image? One word.\"},{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":{\"url\":\"data:image/png;base64,$IMG\"}}]}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c '{content: .choices[0].message.content, image_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens_details.image_tokens}' {"content":"Red","image_tokens":66} ``` The Add Model form reads `/public/providers/fields`, which now returns the provider ```bash $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/public/providers/fields | jq -c '.[] | select(.litellm_provider=="scx-ai") | {provider, provider_display_name, default_model_placeholder}' {"provider":"SCX_AI","provider_display_name":"SCX.ai","default_model_placeholder":"scx-ai/GLM-5.2"} ``` With that proxy running and `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`, Models and Endpoints then Add Model lists SCX.ai in the Provider dropdown with its logo ## Type New Feature ## Changes `providers.json` carries the base URL, `SCX_API_KEY`, the `SCX_API_BASE` override, the `max_completion_tokens` to `max_tokens` mapping and a `temperature_max` of 1.99. SCX accepts `temperature` in `[0.0, 2.0)` and returns a 400 on 2.0 exactly, and the clamp is an inclusive `min()`, so 2.0 would let through a value the endpoint rejects. The slug is registered in `LlmProviders`, the OpenAI-compatible provider and endpoint lists, the api base autodetection branch, and the endpoint support matrix Two chat models go into the cost map. GLM-5.2 has a 1M context window and is text only; Qwen3.8 Max has a 1M window and takes image input. Both cap output at 131072, which is what the endpoint's own validator enforces rather than what the catalogue advertises, and both do implicit prompt caching, so each carries a cache read rate The dashboard needs both the display metadata in `provider_info_helpers.tsx` and an entry in `provider_create_fields.json`, since the Add Model form renders from the latter Tests cover registration, config values, model resolution, api base override and autodetection, the temperature clamp, the parameter mapping, router config, cost map and backup sync, the create-fields entry and the dashboard helpers I work at SCX.ai ## QA runbook Export `SCX_API_KEY`, start the proxy on the config above and run the curl commands in the proof section ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): start on consoles that cannot encode the startup banner
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The proxy will not start on a console that cannot encode the startup banner - That is the default on Windows, where the code page is usually cp1252 - `show_banner` is the first thing `run_server` does, so it dies before binding a port - `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` works around it, but nothing tells you that How it solves it: - Fall back to a plain `LiteLLM` when the stream cannot encode the box-drawing banner ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Windows 11, PowerShell, `PYTHONIOENCODING` unset so stdout comes up as cp1252, which is what a default Windows console gives you. **Before, at `24123269cc`** (base of this branch): ``` PS> python litellm\proxy\proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4000 File "litellm\proxy\common_utils\banner.py", line 15, in show_banner click.echo(f"\n{LITELLM_BANNER}\n") File "click\utils.py", line 345, in echo file.write(out) File "encodings\cp1252.py", line 19, in encode return codecs.charmap_encode(input,self.errors,encoding_table)[0] UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 5-7: character maps to <undefined> ERROR: Application startup failed. Exiting. EXITCODE=3 ``` Nothing is listening on 4000; the server never got far enough to bind. **After, at `ae9aad8160`** (this branch), same shell, same command, `PYTHONIOENCODING` still unset: ``` PS> python litellm\proxy\proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4000 LiteLLM LiteLLM: Proxy initialized with Config, Set models: qwen-local ``` It serves: ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness "I'm alive!" $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"qwen-local","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say OK"}],"temperature":0,"seed":7}' {"id":"chatcmpl-7829679d-...","created":1785149271,"model":"qwen-local","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"OK","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":35,"total_tokens":37}} ``` That is a live proxy in front of a local ollama serving `qwen2.5:3b`, no mocks. On a UTF-8 console the full banner still prints, unchanged. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `show_banner` already guards against `click` being absent. It now also catches `UnicodeEncodeError` and prints a plain `LiteLLM` instead. `click.echo` encodes the whole string before writing, so the failure happens before any bytes reach the stream and the fallback cannot produce a half-drawn banner. `tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_banner.py` is new, since `banner.py` had no mapped test file. It redirects stdout to a `TextIOWrapper` opened with `cp1252`, which is the same condition a Windows console produces, and asserts `show_banner` still writes something recognisable; a second case asserts the full banner still goes out on a UTF-8 stream. With `banner.py` reverted to base and the tests kept, the first one fails on the real cause rather than on a missing symbol: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_banner.py -q E UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 4-6: character maps to <undefined> FAILED tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_banner.py::TestShowBanner::test_show_banner_survives_a_stdout_that_cannot_encode_it 1 failed, 1 passed ``` `LITELLM_BANNER` itself is unchanged, so the HTML use in `common_utils/html_forms/cli_sso_success.py` is unaffected. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): serve aggregate MCP endpoint on bare /mcp instead of 307-redirecting
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Connecting an MCP client to the gateway with the aggregate URL spelled without a trailing slash (`https://<gateway>/mcp`) fails: the proxy 307-redirects `POST /mcp` to `/mcp/`, and behind a TLS-terminating ingress the redirect Location is scheme-downgraded to `http://` (uvicorn only trusts `X-Forwarded-Proto` from `forwarded-allow-ips`, default loopback), so clients strip the Authorization header on the cross-origin follow; the observable symptom in Claude Code is "Got new credentials, but reconnecting failed: ECONNRESET" right after a successful OAuth flow - The redirect fires before auth, so the bare spelling also never returns the RFC 9728 `WWW-Authenticate` challenge OAuth clients need to start the flow How it solves it: - Registers an explicit route for the bare `/mcp` spelling beside the existing `/toolset/{name}/mcp` and `/{name}/mcp` routes, forwarding to `handle_streamable_http_mcp` with the same scope rewrite those routes already use, so `POST /mcp` is served with semantics identical to `/mcp/` and no redirect remains on the path ## Relevant issues - `POST /mcp` (no trailing slash) was 307-redirected instead of served; the scheme-downgraded Location breaks MCP reconnect behind TLS-terminating ingresses - The fix serves the bare spelling directly; `/mcp/`, `/mcp/{server}`, `/{server}/mcp` and `/toolset/{name}/mcp` are unchanged - Regression tests drive the real app router, so a lost route registration (not just a broken handler body) fails the tests ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4802 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Rig: config-only proxy (no DB) on `:4802` launched from this branch, one MCP server `demo_mcp` in `mcp_servers` pointing at a local FastMCP stub upstream on `:8933`, master key auth. Same commands before and after the fix Before (unfixed code): the bare spelling is redirected, with or without auth, and the Location scheme comes from forwarded-proto trust (from a non-trusted peer it stays `http://`, which is the downgrade customers hit behind a TLS-terminating ingress) ``` $ curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp -H 'x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-****' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d "$INIT_BODY" HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect location: http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp/ $ curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp -d "$INIT_BODY" # no auth: redirect fires before auth HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect location: http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp/ $ curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp -H 'X-Forwarded-Proto: https' -d '{}' HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect location: https://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp/ # scheme follows trusted X-Forwarded-Proto; untrusted peers get http:// $ curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp/ -H 'x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-****' ... -d "$INIT_BODY" HTTP/1.1 200 OK mcp-session-id: df232db72eb24863b4549074f8cc4730 ``` After (this branch): bare `/mcp` served identically to `/mcp/`, auth consulted, canonical spelling unchanged, exact-match boundary holds ``` $ curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp -H 'x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-****' ... -d "$INIT_BODY" HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: text/event-stream mcp-session-id: ecc602c1e9a84b9ab46f4526e3778b33 $ curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp -d "$INIT_BODY" # no auth: proper OAuth challenge now HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="http://127.0.0.1:4802/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp" $ curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp/ -H 'x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-****' ... -d "$INIT_BODY" HTTP/1.1 200 OK mcp-session-id: 533bb79b227a48f893ec9288e1dd0b77 $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcp -H 'x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-****' ... \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' | grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' | head -3 "name":"demo_mcp-echo" $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4802/mcpx -H 'x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-****' -d '{}' 404 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - New `aggregate_mcp_route` in `proxy_server.py` registered on `BASE_MCP_ROUTE` (`/mcp`) with the same method set as the sibling MCP routes, forwarding via the existing `_stream_mcp_asgi_response(handle_streamable_http_mcp, ...)` idiom with `path=/mcp` and `_original_path` preserved for OAuth challenge URL selection - Guarded with `is_mcp_available()` so the bare spelling 404s exactly like `/mcp/` does when the `mcp` package is absent - Three regression tests in the mapped `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_dynamic_mcp_route.py`, driven through the real app router with `TestClient(follow_redirects=False)`: bare-path served for GET/POST/DELETE with the exact forwarded scope, `/mcpx` never reaches the handler, unavailable-MCP 404 parity - Regenerated `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/lib/http/schema.d.ts` for the new route's OpenAPI path entry (no hand edits) - Assigned the bare `/mcp` route (exact path) and the lazily-mounted `/mcp` sub-app (mount path) to the backend component in `backend/routes/allowlist.py`; the existing `/mcp/` prefix cannot match the bare spelling, and without the exact entry the componentized backend's startup trim would drop the new route The fix is deliberately not at the mount or via `redirect_slashes=False`: a Starlette mount structurally cannot match its bare prefix, and disabling slash redirects app-wide would change unrelated surfaces (an existing test pins the `/ui` static mount's 307). The exact-match route and the `/mcp` mount have disjoint match sets, so registration order cannot matter. Uvicorn's `forwarded-allow-ips` trust (the reason redirect Locations downgrade at all) is deployment configuration and is deliberately not changed here; deployments behind a TLS-terminating ingress can additionally set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` so any remaining redirects on other paths keep their scheme ## QA runbook 1. Start a proxy from this branch with any config that has at least one entry under `mcp_servers` and a `master_key` 2. `curl -si -X POST http://localhost:4000/mcp -H 'x-litellm-api-key: Bearer <master key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl","version":"0"}}}'; expect `200` with an `mcp-session-id` header (on main you get `307` with a `location:` header) 3. Repeat against `/mcp/`; expect the same `200` (unchanged) 4. `curl -si -X POST http://localhost:4000/mcp` with no auth header; expect `401` with a `www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` challenge, not a redirect 5. In Claude Code, add the gateway MCP server with the URL spelled WITHOUT the trailing slash (`https://<gateway>/mcp`), authenticate, and confirm tools list and calls work; before this fix the reconnect after OAuth fails with ECONNRESET behind a TLS-terminating ingress ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches the MCP HTTP entry path and OAuth challenge routing for a widely used URL spelling; scope is narrow and covered by integration-style tests, but mis-routing could affect MCP auth and client connectivity. > > **Overview** > **Fixes MCP clients using `https://<gateway>/mcp` (no trailing slash)** by serving the aggregate endpoint directly instead of returning a **307** to `/mcp/`, which behind TLS-terminating ingresses can downgrade the redirect scheme and break reconnects (e.g. OAuth flows dropping `Authorization` on follow). > > Adds **`aggregate_mcp_route`** on `BASE_MCP_ROUTE` (`/mcp`) in `proxy_server.py`, forwarding through the existing **`_stream_mcp_asgi_response` / `handle_streamable_http_mcp`** path with **`_original_path`** preserved (same pattern as toolset/dynamic MCP routes). Returns **404** when MCP is unavailable via **`is_mcp_available()`**. > > Updates **`backend/routes/allowlist.py`** so the bare `/mcp` route and `/mcp` mount stay on the backend component when routes are trimmed. Adds router-level regression tests in **`test_dynamic_mcp_route.py`** and regenerates dashboard OpenAPI types for the new path. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 3d4b50cd01b677cebd8ffc4b56ec44b253d9df5f. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(anthropic cost): apply regional geo uplift to cached tokens
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Anthropic regional uplift skipped cache read and write cost - Cache-heavy regional spend under-reported by roughly 10% How it solves it: - Geo multiplier now scales the full cost - `fast` multiplier stays cache-exclusive as before - Spend log cost breakdown line items carry the same multiplier, so they keep summing to the total ## User Flow Before: a developer running long-context Anthropic traffic out of a US region sees the gateway report almost exactly the non-regional price, so their spend never matches the Anthropic invoice 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `claude-opus-4-8` with `"inference_geo": "us"` and a large system prompt marked for 1h prompt caching 2. The reply comes back reporting 14784 cache-creation tokens and 9 plain input tokens 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is logged at $0.14788950, no higher than the $0.14791000 the same call without a region logs 4. The US price list is 10% above global, so they expected about $0.16270, and what they got means the uplift only reached the 9 non-cache tokens 5. They end the month reconciling by hand, adding a flat 10% on top of the gateway's Anthropic spend After: the same request is logged at the regional price, so no manual correction is needed 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and the same cached system prompt 2. The reply again reports 14784 cache-creation tokens and 9 plain input tokens 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows $0.16270100, 10% above the $0.14791000 global price 4. Traffic with no region, or on global inference, still logs $0.14791000 5. Opening that request's cost breakdown (also on GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=<response id>) shows the cache-creation line item at the uplifted rate, and the line items sum to the logged total ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4866 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy against the real Anthropic API, real spend, `claude-sonnet-5` (carries `us: 1.1` in the price map; Anthropic accepts `inference_geo` for it and echoes it back in usage). The fix rides the shared Anthropic cost path, so both legs proved all three unified endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, and /v1/responses. Every request sent a unique ~18k-token system prompt marked `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}` so nearly every prompt token is a fresh cache-creation token, the shape that made the uplift vanish, with only 9 non-cache input tokens and 0 output tokens. Cost read off the `x-litellm-response-cost` response header, the surface a caller sees Before leg at `f03df1bb42` (the merge base on `litellm_internal_staging`), after leg at `e94a97fcfc` (this PR's head). Six requests per leg: each endpoint once with `"inference_geo": "us"` in the body and once without ```bash H=(-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234') curl -sD - localhost:$PORT/v1/chat/completions "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_tokens":16,"inference_geo":"us", "messages":[{"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<18k-token unique prompt>","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}]}, {"role":"user","content":"Say OK."}]}' curl -sD - localhost:$PORT/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_tokens":16,"inference_geo":"us", "system":[{"type":"text","text":"<18k-token unique prompt>","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}], "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say OK."}]}' curl -sD - localhost:$PORT/v1/responses "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_output_tokens":16,"inference_geo":"us", "input":[{"role":"system","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"<18k-token unique prompt>","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}]}, {"role":"user","content":"Say OK."}]}' # plus the same three with inference_geo removed, each with a fresh unique prompt ``` Before, at `f03df1bb42`, asking for `us` costs the same as not asking (the 10% uplift reaches only the 9 non-cache tokens; every header value decomposes exactly as cache_tokens x $2.50/M + 9 x $2.20/M with geo vs 9 x $2.00/M without): ``` /v1/chat/completions geo=us 0.0462423 cache_create=18489 | global 0.046328 cache_create=18524 ratio 0.998 /v1/messages geo=us 0.0464923 cache_create=18589 | global 0.046488 cache_create=18588 ratio 1.000 /v1/responses geo=us 0.0464823 cache_write=18585 | global 0.046493 cache_write=18590 ratio 1.000 ``` After, at `e94a97fcfc`, the geo cost is exactly 1.10x the closed-form global price of its own token counts, cache included, and no-geo traffic is unchanged: ``` /v1/chat/completions geo=us 0.0508673 cache_create=18490 | global 0.0462305 cache_create=18485 normalized ratio 1.1000 /v1/messages geo=us 0.05113405 cache_create=18587 | global 0.0464855 cache_create=18587 raw ratio 1.1000 /v1/responses geo=us 0.05112855 cache_write=18585 | global 0.046498 cache_write=18592 normalized ratio 1.1000 ``` Every header value decomposes exactly as cache_tokens x $2.75/M + 9 x $2.20/M with geo vs cache_tokens x $2.50/M + 9 x $2.00/M without; the /v1/messages pair even landed on identical cache token counts, making the raw ratio exactly 1.1000 The review-round commit (`e94a97fcfc`) also mirrors the uplift into the per-token-type cost breakdown that spend logs carry, so line items keep summing to the total. Same live setup, breakdown read from GET /spend/logs?request_id=<response id> under `metadata.cost_breakdown`, chat geo=us shown, /v1/messages and /v1/responses matched: ``` before (d330b64943) total 0.05086455 cache_creation_cost 0.04622250 (= 18489 x $2.50/M, base rate) residual input 0.00464205 landing on the 9 non-cache tokens after (e94a97fcfc) total 0.05086730 cache_creation_cost 0.05084750 (= 18490 x $2.75/M, uplifted) residual input 0.00001980 (= 9 x $2.20/M); line items sum to the header cost exactly ``` Observations from the run: - Usage echoes `inference_geo: "global"` when the param is omitted; this PR leaves that alone - `cache_control` rides /v1/responses system input fine; this PR leaves that alone - The model refused the random-word prompts (0 output tokens); totals are purely input cost ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Merged current `litellm_internal_staging` into the branch - Streaming still logs no region, fixed by #34857 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/13d7b3dbf5a641f0a24aa0b48893d315

signals.title: fix(anthropic): populate inference_geo from the request so regional pricing applies
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streamed Anthropic usage loses the region it was served from - Regional traffic then gets billed at global rates How it solves it: - Streaming reassembly carries `inference_geo` through - Requested region is the fallback when the response omits it ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming Anthropic traffic out of a US region sees the gateway log no region at all, so regional pricing never applies to any streamed request 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true` 2. The response streams back fine, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at the global price with no region recorded 3. They repeat it on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages with `"stream": true`, and both log the same way 4. Dropping `"stream": true` on any of the three routes does record `us`, so their spend is only correct for non-streaming traffic After: the same streamed requests record the region, so streamed and non-streamed traffic price the same way 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true` 2. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the request served from `us` 3. The same holds on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages with `"stream": true` 4. A request that asks for no region, or that Anthropic serves globally, still records `global` and prices as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4867 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Screen recording of the before and after run, in one video, is in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1786414063855749?thread_ts=1786408619.329699&cid=C0BE49SAUE6). It captured the before at `1d3b64c66f` (current `litellm_internal_staging`) and the after at `82a64de9a2`, and reproduced the runs below Live proxy against the real Anthropic API, real spend, `claude-opus-4-8`, one request per route with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true`. Region and cost were read off the standard logging payload ```bash H=(-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01') curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions "${H[@]}" -d @chat_geo_stream.json curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d @msg_geo_stream.json curl -sS localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d @pt_geo_stream.json ``` Before, at `1d3b64c66f`, every streamed route drops the region: ``` route=acompletion geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 route=anthropic_messages geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 route=pass_through_endpoint geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 ``` After, at `82a64de9a2`, all three keep it: ``` route=acompletion geo=us cost=0.14788949999999998 route=anthropic_messages geo=us cost=0.14788949999999998 route=pass_through_endpoint geo=us cost=0.14799949999999998 ``` The cost barely moves because the uplift itself is #34850, and the point here is that without the region reaching cost calculation that PR can never fire on streamed traffic. signals.title: fix(anthropic): aggregate 5m/1h cache-write split across iterations path
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Anthropic reports cache writes per iteration when a request loops over tool calls - That nested 5m/1h split is dropped, so 1h cache writes get billed at the 5m rate How it solves it: - The per-iteration `cache_creation` breakdowns are summed into one 5m/1h split - Cache writes an iteration reports without a breakdown are billed at the default 5m rate - Top-level `cache_creation` stays the source when there are no iterations ## User Flow Before: a developer whose Anthropic traffic loops over tool calls is undercharged for 1h cache writes, so their gateway spend does not match the Anthropic console 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with a `cache_control` block of `{"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}` and tools that make the request run several iterations 2. Anthropic returns usage where each iteration carries its own `cache_creation` breakdown showing the writes were 1h 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the cache-write tokens billed at the 5m rate, roughly 40% under the 1h price After: the same request bills the 1h rate, matching what a single-iteration request with the same cache writes already cost 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages request 2. Anthropic returns the same per-iteration usage breakdown 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the cache writes at the 1h rate 4. An iteration that reports cache-write tokens without a 5m/1h breakdown still bills those writes at the 5m rate, and requests with no iterations at all are billed exactly as before The same holds on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses, which bill this traffic identically ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4868 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Screen recording of the original before and after run on the shape this PR fixes, in one video, is in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1786414063855749?thread_ts=1786408619.329699&cid=C0BE49SAUE6). It captured the before at `1d3b64c66f` and the after at the PR's first commit; the full re-run below supersedes it as written proof Latest full QA run: before at `f03df1bb42` (merge base, current `litellm_internal_staging` without the fix), after at `0ab23f5ce9` (this PR's head). Each leg booted a live proxy plus Postgres-backed spend logs from its own worktree and hit all three unified endpoints; every cost below was confirmed both in the `x-litellm-response-cost` response header and in the persisted row returned by `GET /spend/logs`. Two halves, because the two usage shapes cannot both come from the same place First, the shape this PR fixes. Nothing we could send made the real API return an `iterations` usage breakdown, so this half was driven from a stand-in Anthropic upstream emitting it: 1000 cache-write tokens, all 1h, split 500+500 across two iterations, plus 10 input and 5 output tokens ```bash H=(-H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json') curl -sS -i localhost:$PORT/v1/chat/completions "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"opus48-iter","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' curl -sS -i localhost:$PORT/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"opus48-iter","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' curl -sS -i localhost:$PORT/v1/responses "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"opus48-iter","input":"hello"}' ``` Before, at `f03df1bb42` (proxy on port 24583), the split is lost and every route bills the 5m rate: ``` /v1/chat/completions cost=0.006425 spend_log=0.006425 /v1/messages cost=0.006425 spend_log=0.006425 /v1/responses cost=0.006425 spend_log=0.006425 ``` 0.006425 = 1000 x $6.25/M (5m write rate) + 10 x $5/M + 5 x $25/M After, at `0ab23f5ce9` (proxy on port 25733), every route bills the 1h rate, and the response usage carries the aggregated split `{ephemeral_5m_input_tokens: 0, ephemeral_1h_input_tokens: 1000}`: ``` /v1/chat/completions cost=0.010175 spend_log=0.010175 /v1/messages cost=0.010175 spend_log=0.010175 /v1/responses cost=0.010175 spend_log=0.010175 ``` 0.010175 = 1000 x $10/M (1h write rate) + 10 x $5/M + 5 x $25/M Second, the shape that was already correct, live against the real Anthropic API with real spend, `claude-opus-4-8`, a fresh unique ~8k-token system text cached with `"ttl": "1h"` on every call (same curl form, bodies in the worktree's payload files): Before, at `f03df1bb42`, all three routes bill the 1h rate to the digit: ``` /v1/chat/completions cost=0.08714 (8708 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) /v1/messages cost=0.08626 (8620 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) /v1/responses cost=0.08592 (8586 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) ``` After, at `0ab23f5ce9`, unchanged, still the 1h rate to the digit: ``` /v1/chat/completions cost=0.08037 (8031 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) /v1/messages cost=0.07972 (7966 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) /v1/responses cost=0.07959 (7953 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) ``` So the iterations path now agrees with what the same writes already cost through the top-level shape, on every unified endpoint, in the header and the spend log alike Observations from the run, all pre-existing and untouched by this PR: - Spend-log request_id lookup wants response id, not call id - Unflushed spend rows are lost when the proxy dies - Real calls sometimes return refusals with zero output tokens ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Current `litellm_internal_staging` is merged into the branch - The `iterations` half of the proof is not real-provider traffic, see above for why - Resolving the split moved into one helper so the value is computed once instead of being reassigned across branches ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/13d7b3dbf5a641f0a24aa0b48893d315
