signals.title: feat(proxy): serve Anthropic-native /v1/models for Claude Code gateway discovery
signals.text: *Re-lands #30273 (reverted during staging)*. No functional changes to the original; rebased onto current main and refactored so the diff is purely additive. ## The problem Claude Code 2.1.126+ added gateway model discovery: when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a gateway, it queries {base_url}/v1/models at startup and populates the /model picker with the discovered models. That discovery only parses the Anthropic-native Models API shape, so against litellm - which returns OpenAI's {id, object, created, owned_by} list - Claude Code finds nothing and the picker stays empty, even though /v1/messages already works. ## The fix This serves the Anthropic-native shape from the same /v1/models route via content negotiation on the anthropic-version header. Claude Code already sends that header for /v1/messages, so when it is present the endpoint returns the Anthropic Models envelope (type / display_name / created_at per entry, plus top-level has_more / first_id / last_id); otherwise the response is byte-for-byte the existing OpenAI shape, so aider and other OpenAI-compatible clients are unaffected. Entries also carry the model's token limits when litellm knows them: max_input_tokens as-is, and the output budget as max_tokens, the name the Messages API uses for it. Both come from create_model_info_response, the same helper the OpenAI listing goes through, so cost-map values and router-configured overrides resolve identically in either shape A separate endpoint was not used because Claude Code discovers at the gateway root's /v1/models, and a global config flag would break the OpenAI clients that share the route. ## Design notes - Full list returned, client filters. Claude Code applies its own claude/anthropic id-prefix filter client-side, so no server-side filtering is imposed - a model aliased to claude-* pointing at any backend still shows up, which is the point for gateway users. - display_name falls back to the model id, the stable label a gateway can offer for arbitrary upstream models. - created_at is the ISO 8601 (Z-suffixed) form of the same timestamp the OpenAI shape already returns. - Hidden/unhealthy models are filtered before formatting in both the scope=expand and normal branches, exactly as for the OpenAI shape. - Both branches now build the OpenAI listing first and reshape it for Anthropic callers, so team name translation, hidden-model filtering and token limits can never drift between the two shapes. A model with no known limits simply omits the keys. - The formatter lives in litellm/llms/anthropic/common_utils.py per the repo rule against provider-specific code outside llms/; the request parameter is optional so existing direct (non-HTTP) callers of model_list are unaffected. ## Tests - tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/test_anthropic_common_utils.py: full envelope shape (per-entry type/display_name/created_at with a Z-suffixed ISO timestamp, top-level has_more/first_id/last_id, no object) and the empty-list case (first_id/last_id null). - tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/test_anthropic_common_utils.py also pins the token limits: max_input_tokens passes through, max_output_tokens is renamed to max_tokens, and a model with only one known limit or none omits the rest. - tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_routes_models.py: drives GET /v1/models (and /models) with the anthropic-version header and asserts the negotiated Anthropic shape, including the limits for a model that has them and their absence for one that does not; the existing happy-path test pins that the default response stays OpenAI. All three affected test files pass locally (215 tests). No server-side state or config changes.

signals.title: fix(proxy): return 401 not 500 on auth failure in master-key-only mode
signals.text: ## Problem On a proxy started **without** a `DATABASE_URL` (a master-key-only deployment — a documented, supported configuration), **every** auth failure returns an unrelated HTTP **500** instead of a **401**. This includes a plain unauthenticated request: ```yaml model_list: [] general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_KEY ``` ``` $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:4000/health 500 # expected 401 ``` ## Root cause `PrismaDBExceptionHandler.is_database_connection_error` and its siblings — `is_prisma_data_error`, `is_database_transport_error`, `is_prisma_engine_internal_error` — did an unconditional `import prisma` inside the method body. `prisma` is an **optional** dependency: it is only installed when the proxy is generated against a configured `DATABASE_URL` (pulled in by `prisma generate`). A master-key-only deployment never installs it. `is_database_connection_error` runs from `_user_api_key_auth_builder`'s exception handler on **every** auth failure, not just DB-related ones. So on a master-key-only proxy, any request with a missing or wrong API key crashes the classifier itself with: ``` ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'prisma' ``` which surfaces as a 500 instead of the correct 401. ## Fix Guard the `prisma` import **once at module load** and short-circuit each classifier to `False` when prisma is unavailable: ```python try: import prisma # optional dependency, only installed when the proxy is generated against a DATABASE_URL PRISMA_AVAILABLE = True except ImportError: PRISMA_AVAILABLE = False ``` ```python if not PRISMA_AVAILABLE: return False ``` Rationale for `False`: with no `DATABASE_URL` there is no DB layer to be unavailable, so none of these can be a DB error — the request must fall through to the normal 401 auth path. Behavior is **unchanged** when prisma is installed (the in-method `import prisma` is simply hoisted to module scope). The diff is surgical — one guarded import plus a one-line short-circuit in each of the four classifiers. ## Test Added a focused, parametrized regression test in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_exception_handler.py` asserting all four classifiers return `False` (and do **not** raise `ModuleNotFoundError`) when prisma is unavailable, simulated by monkeypatching `PRISMA_AVAILABLE` to `False`. ``` tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_exception_handler.py .... (47 passed) ``` The existing `test_exception_handler.py` suite continues to pass unchanged. Fixes #35457

signals.title: feat(ui): manage admin-owned logging destinations
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Destinations can only be managed by hand through the credentials API How it solves it: - Adds destinations to Logging & Alerts, with their backend and scope - Lets an admin create one and edit which teams or orgs it reaches - Keeps the existing proxy-wide OTEL callbacks as separate dropdown entries ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4764 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Last of five stacked PRs splitting #30873; stacked on `litellm_otel_v2_dest_4_disclosure`. Frontend only. The Add Callback dropdown offers both shapes side by side: picking "Arize" still creates a proxy-wide callback through `/config/update` exactly as before, and "Arize (scoped destination)" creates a scoped destination through `/credentials`. Keeping both means the existing flow is untouched and the new one is a deliberate choice rather than a silent change of meaning. Editing a destination's scope resends its whole stored `credential_info` with only `access` swapped, because `PATCH /credentials` replaces `credential_info` wholesale. Stack: 1. `litellm_otel_v2_dest_1_credential_model` - credential model, access validation, destination mapping 2. `litellm_otel_v2_dest_2_resolver` - resolve a request's destinations from its identity 3. `litellm_otel_v2_dest_3_export` - export the trace to them 4. `litellm_otel_v2_dest_4_disclosure` - surface them on team/org info 5. **this PR** - admin UI --- ## Update Four defects found by driving these screens in a browser against a live proxy, with a dashboard built from this branch. The Scope column read `credential_info.access` on its own, so a destination the resolver excludes still rendered a scope badge: one with no backend name and one whose adapter rejects its values both showed "Global access" while `/team/info` listed neither. The verdict now comes from the backend's `resolves_to_destination` (added in #35513), computed by `destination_for_credential` so it cannot drift from the resolver or the disclosure. A destination keeps the name its admin gave it. Passing it through the callback registry renamed one called `datadog` to "Datadog", leaving it indistinguishable in the name column from the real Datadog callback row. The delete dialog was written for a callback: it said "Delete Callback", listed "Callback Name", and printed "Mode: success" for a destination that has no mode and that the table renders as "—". It now names the destination and its backend, and says the stored collector credentials go with it. A read-only admin has no action available on a destination, since destinations get no Test, so the trigger opened a menu with zero items and read as broken rather than restricted. It is no longer rendered; config-callback rows keep theirs because Test stays available to that role. Every regression test was mutation-checked by reverting its own fix in isolation A later pass over the dashboard found two more. A stored `credential_info.access` whose `teams` or `orgs` is not a list threw during render, and the error boundary blanked the whole Logging and Alerts page, taking every other destination with it including the delete action needed to remove the offending row; the read model already fails closed on that shape, so the table now coerces it the same way. Separately, a destination name carrying a URL delimiter addressed a different path on delete and update, and since the endpoint answers 200 for a name that does not exist, the dashboard reported success while the destination kept receiving traces ## Live verification Re-run on this head against a live proxy on real Postgres, driving the dashboard bundled from this branch in a browser. **125 of 126 checks pass.** The one failure is pre-existing and outside this stack: the config-callback delete dialog prints `Mode: success` while the row badge reads "Success & Failure". That line is byte-identical to staging and this diff only moves it into the config branch, so it is left alone. The admin view renders config callbacks and scoped destinations in one table. Mode is blank for a destination and Scope is blank for a config callback, the scope badges resolve team and organization ids to their aliases, more than four grants collapse to "+2 more", and a destination that cannot be built from its stored values reads "Not active" rather than showing the scope it was granted. The two rows named `datadog` stay distinguishable, the destination keeping the name its admin gave it. ![Admin destinations table](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr35513-35517/pr30873/ui-admin-destinations-table.png) A read-only admin keeps full read parity and loses every write affordance. Same rows, same scope verdicts, no Add Callback button, and no actions trigger on any destination row, while the config-callback row keeps its menu because Test stays available to that role. ![Read-only admin parity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr35513-35517/pr30873/ui-viewer-readonly-parity.png) The delete dialog names the destination and its backend and states that the stored collector credentials go with it, instead of the callback wording that printed a mode a destination does not have. ![Delete destination dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr35513-35517/pr30873/ui-delete-destination-dialog.png) The scope editor loads the destination's current grants and writes back only the access map. ![Edit scope dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr35513-35517/pr30873/ui-edit-scope-dialog.png)

signals.title: feat(ui): add Microsoft Entra ID directory search to the invite-user flow
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Inviting a user today requires typing their email address by hand - Admins on Microsoft-SSO tenants already have the directory data; there was no way to search it from the invite flow How it solves it: - Adds `GET /user/directory_search`, backed by a pluggable `DirectorySearchProvider` protocol (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/directory_search/`) so a future identity provider (Okta, Google Workspace, generic SAML/SCIM) can be added as one new file plus a registry entry, with no changes to the endpoint or `ui_sso.py` - Ships one provider today: Microsoft Entra ID via an app-only Graph query gated behind `MICROSOFT_DIRECTORY_SEARCH_ENABLED` - Reuses the existing SSO app registration's credentials (`MICROSOFT_TENANT`/`CLIENT_ID`/`CLIENT_SECRET`) by default, or a dedicated `MICROSOFT_DIRECTORY_*` registration if configured separately - The invite-user modal's email field becomes a combined search-or-type `AutoComplete` when the feature is enabled, backed by a new `AdDirectoryUserSearch` component ## Relevant issues Fixes #35745 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Tested end to end against a live proxy (`litellm-local-fork:ad-user-search`, commit a45c7f92e1) with a real Microsoft Entra ID tenant, no mocks. Unauthenticated request is rejected: ``` $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:5173/user/directory_search?query=st" HTTP 401 ``` Query shorter than the minimum length short-circuits without contacting Graph: ``` $ curl -s "http://localhost:5173/user/directory_search?query=s" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" [] ``` `/sso/get/ui_settings` reflects the feature as configured: ``` $ curl -s "http://localhost:5173/sso/get/ui_settings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" | jq .MICROSOFT_DIRECTORY_SEARCH_ENABLED true ``` Live search against the real tenant for "stephe" (emails redacted, structure and count as returned): ``` $ curl -s "http://localhost:5173/user/directory_search?query=stephe" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" | jq . [ {"display_name": "Stephen Law", "email": "***@***"}, {"display_name": "Stephen Law", "email": "***@***"}, {"display_name": "Stephen Raj", "email": "***@***"}, {"display_name": "Stephen M", "email": "***@***"}, {"display_name": "Stephen Raj S", "email": "***@***"}, {"display_name": "Stephen M", "email": "***@***"}, {"display_name": "Stephen Law", "email": "***@***"} ] (7 results) ``` A screenshot of the same search running live in the Admin UI's Invite User modal will be attached as a comment on this PR. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/directory_search/base.py`: new `DirectorySearchProvider` protocol and `get_configured_directory_search_provider()` registry lookup, so callers don't know which identity provider backs a search - `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/directory_search/microsoft.py`: the Graph token acquisition (with caching scoped to the current tenant/client credentials, single-flight locking, and 401 retry-once), the directory search request, and the `MICROSOFT_DIRECTORY_SEARCH_ENABLED`/credential resolution helpers, now implementing `DirectorySearchProvider` - `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/internal_user_endpoints.py`: new `GET /user/directory_search` endpoint, restricted to `PROXY_ADMIN`/`PROXY_ADMIN_VIEW_ONLY`, calling through the provider registry - `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/ui_sso.py`: `/sso/get/ui_settings` now reports `MICROSOFT_DIRECTORY_SEARCH_ENABLED` based on whether any provider is configured, guarded so a secret manager failure can't break the endpoint for every user - `litellm/types/proxy/management_endpoints/internal_user_endpoints.py`: adds the provider-agnostic `DirectoryUser` response model (renamed from `MicrosoftDirectoryUser`) - `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/common_components/AdDirectoryUserSearch.tsx`: new debounced search `AutoComplete`, registered directly as the invite form's `user_email` field when the feature is enabled, falling back to a plain input otherwise - `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/CreateUserButton.tsx`, `networking.tsx`: wiring for the above - Corresponding test files for all of the above

signals.title: fix(datadog_llm_obs): map tool_calls to DD Message schema and cache tokens to span metrics
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Datadog Tools panel stays empty for every tool call - Cache hit ratio and cache write tokens never populate How it solves it: - Map tool calls into DD's ToolCall shape on the output message - Forward prompt-cache counts into top-level span metrics ## Relevant issues Fixes #35786 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Details Datadog's LLM Observability intake reads tool calls from `meta.output.messages[].tool_calls` using its own ToolCall shape (`name`, `arguments`, `tool_id`, `type`), and reads prompt-cache counts from top-level span `metrics`; see https://docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/setup/api/. The callback was passing the raw OpenAI-style message straight through, where the call sits under a nested `function` dict, and it was leaving cache counts nested in `metadata.usage_object`. In both cases the data reached Datadog but in a place Datadog does not read, so the Tools panel and the cache hit ratio rendered empty `_get_response_messages` now maps the assistant message into the DD shape; `arguments` that fail to parse as JSON are kept as the raw string rather than dropping the call. `create_llm_obs_payload` forwards `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_write_input_tokens` and `non_cached_input_tokens` into span metrics, and `LLMMetrics` gains those three fields The existing output tool-call test asserted the old nested-`function` shape, so it now pins the documented DD schema instead; new tests cover cache metric forwarding, an absent `usage_object`, malformed arguments, and a plain response with no tool calls Scoped out deliberately: `meta.tool_definitions` and input-side `tool_results` from the same issue. Happy to follow those up separately ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I don't have a Datadog account or paid provider credentials, so I can't post an intake screenshot from a live proxy. What I can show is the exact payload the callback now hands to `safe_dumps`, driven through `create_llm_obs_payload` with the reporter's Bedrock-style usage object (176 cache write, 16695 cache read, 16872 prompt): ``` $ python proof_of_fix.py meta.output.messages: [ { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [ { "name": "task", "arguments": { "description": "Find DD callback code" }, "tool_id": "toolu_bdrk_01F8", "type": "function" } ] } ] metrics: { "input_tokens": 16872.0, "output_tokens": 704.0, "total_tokens": 17576.0, "time_to_first_token": 0.5, "cache_read_input_tokens": 16695.0, "cache_write_input_tokens": 176.0, "non_cached_input_tokens": 177.0 } ``` Before this change the same input produced `tool_calls` still wrapped in the OpenAI `function` dict, and `metrics` carried only input/output/total tokens with the cache counts stranded in `meta.metadata.usage_object`. If a maintainer with a DD account wants the live trace before merging, I'm glad to supply the config

signals.title: feat(fireworks_ai): translate NIM/vLLM extra params to Fireworks-native args
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - NIM/vLLM clients send extras Fireworks names differently or historically rejected - The legacy `/v1/completions` path 500'd on `reasoning_effort` and `response_format` How it solves it: - Translates truncate, reasoning, and guided-decoding extras to Fireworks-native params - Strips extras with no Fireworks equivalent, with a debug log - On conflicts the Fireworks-native value silently wins, matching the Fireworks gateway - Applies the same translation on the text completion path, fixing its 500 - Drops `reasoning_effort: "auto"`; omitting it already means the model default ## User Flow Before: chat requests carry the NIM/vLLM knobs, but the legacy completions endpoint dies with a 500 inside the gateway 1. Point an existing NIM/vLLM OpenAI-compatible client at the gateway and send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with a Fireworks model, `truncate_prompt_tokens: 4096`, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`, and a `guided_json` schema 2. The 200 reply honors the knobs: thinking is off and the content is valid JSON matching the schema (the Fireworks API accepts the NIM/vLLM names natively as of 2026-08-13; when this PR was opened they were ignored or rejected) 3. Send the NIM/vLLM knobs to the legacy `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/completions` with a `prompt` plus `reasoning_effort: "low"` and `best_of: 2`, and the call dies with `500 AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'reasoning_effort'` before ever reaching Fireworks After: the same client works on both endpoints 1. Point an existing NIM/vLLM OpenAI-compatible client at the gateway and send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with a Fireworks model, `truncate_prompt_tokens: 4096`, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`, and a `guided_json` schema 2. The 200 reply honors the knobs: thinking is off and the content is valid JSON matching the schema (now guaranteed by the gateway's own translation to the Fireworks-native names, not by the provider tolerating the NIM/vLLM ones) 3. The same legacy `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/completions` request returns 200 with the completion text ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5322 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? signals.title: fix: no-log should not disable spend tracking
signals.text: ## The problem `Logging.should_run_callback` already intends to keep the proxy's cost-tracking callback running on a `no-log` request. The comment says so explicitly: ```python if litellm_params.get("no-log", False) is True: # proxy cost tracking cal backs should run if not ( isinstance(callback, CustomLogger) and "_PROXY_" in callback.__class__.__name__ ): return False ``` But the cost-tracking callback's class is **`_ProxyDBLogger`** (`litellm/proxy/hooks/proxy_track_cost_callback.py`), and the test is a case-sensitive substring match: ```python >>> "_PROXY_" in "_ProxyDBLogger" False ``` `_PROXY_` (upper-case, trailing underscore) never appears in `_ProxyDBLogger`. The exemption is dead code, so `_ProxyDBLogger` is skipped along with every other callback and **`no-log` silently disables spend tracking**. Other proxy hooks (`_PROXY_MaxParallelRequestsHandler`, `_PROXY_MaxBudgetLimiter`, …) do match the pattern, which is presumably why this went unnoticed — the one callback the comment is actually about is the one that doesn't match. Present on `litellm_internal_staging`, `main`, `v1.96.0-rc.1` and as far back as `v1.88.2`. ## Why it matters `no-log` is a reasonable thing for an application to send when it already reports its own traces and doesn't want the proxy to duplicate them. Nothing signals that it also turns off billing. We hit this in production: three services set `no-log` purely to avoid duplicate Langfuse traces, and their keys reported **$0** and were absent from `/team/daily/activity` for months, while every other key reported correctly. One of them was ~$170/month. Nobody had opted out of cost tracking — the flag just did more than its name implies. For a proxy used as a metering and budget-enforcement chokepoint, a request-level flag that lets any caller zero their own spend is worth closing. Budgets are affected too: with spend never incrementing, `max_budget` on those keys can never trip. ## The fix Replace the class-name heuristic with an explicit opt-in on `CustomLogger`: ```python class CustomLogger: # Set True on callbacks that must still run for `no-log` requests -- # metering, billing and budget enforcement, as opposed to observability. runs_on_no_log: bool = False ``` `_ProxyDBLogger` sets `runs_on_no_log = True`, and `should_run_callback` honours it: ```python if not ( isinstance(callback, CustomLogger) and ( callback.runs_on_no_log # Retained for callbacks predating `runs_on_no_log`. or "_PROXY_" in callback.__class__.__name__ ) ): ``` This keeps `no-log` meaning *"do not send this request to logging integrations"*, while accounting keeps working. ## Backwards compatibility - The `"_PROXY_"` check is **kept**, so any existing callback relying on the naming convention behaves exactly as before. - `runs_on_no_log` defaults to `False`, so every existing third-party callback is unaffected. - `litellm.global_disable_no_log_param` is untouched. - The only behaviour change is the one the existing comment already asks for: the cost callback now runs on `no-log` requests. ## Tests New: `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_no_log_spend_tracking.py` - `_ProxyDBLogger` **runs** on `no-log` (the regression) - an observability-style callback is still **skipped** on `no-log` - any callback can opt in via `runs_on_no_log` (not just the proxy's) - everything runs when `no-log` is absent or `False` - legacy `_PROXY_*`-named callbacks remain exempt without setting the flag - `global_disable_no_log_param` still overrides everything ## Alternative considered Simply correcting the string match (e.g. `startswith("_Proxy")`) is a one-liner, but keeps behaviour coupled to class naming, which is what allowed the bug to hide. An explicit attribute makes the intent checkable and lets other infrastructure callbacks (metering, budget enforcement) opt in deliberately. Happy to reduce this to the one-line string fix instead if you'd prefer the smaller change.

signals.title: feat(proxy): global SSE keepalive ping interval for OpenAI-shaped streaming routes
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - OpenAI-shaped streams send zero bytes until the first model token - Ingresses and load balancers kill those silent connections at their idle timeout - Keepalive pings today require per-deployment `keepalive_seconds` opt-in How it solves it: - Adds global `litellm_settings.sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds` - Used when neither the request nor the deployment sets an interval - A deployment's explicit `keepalive_seconds: 0` disable still wins - Also arms keepalive on router-less proxies ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming a long document to their self-hosted model through the company ingress gets a 504 before the first token ever arrives 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "qwen-local"`, `"stream": true`, and a ~16k-token document prompt 2. The self-hosted backend starts crunching the prompt; the first token is about 2.5 minutes away and the connection carries zero bytes in the meantime 3. At exactly 60 seconds the ingress gives up on the silent connection and returns `504 Gateway Time-out`; no SSE data ever arrives 4. Every retry dies the same way, so requests past the ingress idle timeout can never complete After: the same request emits `: ping` comments within seconds, holds the connection open through the whole prompt crunch, and completes 1. The proxy admin sets `litellm_settings.sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds: 3` and restarts the gateway 2. The developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same document prompt 3. Within ~3 seconds a `200` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream` arrives, followed by a `: ping` comment every 3 seconds 4. About 2.5 minutes in the real `data:` chunks arrive, then `data: [DONE]`; SSE-conformant clients ignore the comment lines, so nothing else about the stream changes ## Relevant issues Fixes #31865 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5300 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs ran the identical config below against real backends: gpt-5.6 (OpenAI, real API), claude-sonnet-5 (Anthropic, real API), and qwen-local, a self-hosted llama-server (Qwen2.5-0.5B Q8_0, CPU) whose ~16k-token prompt takes ~2.5 minutes of prefill before the first token. Each proxy sat behind a real nginx ingress mirror with two listeners: `proxy_read_timeout 10s` (aggressive) and `proxy_read_timeout 60s` (the nginx default). Before leg is the merge base 422d925334, after leg is this PR's head e53f044d20 ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6 litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.6 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: claude-sonnet-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: qwen-local litellm_params: model: openai/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct api_base: http://127.0.0.1:47611/v1 api_key: none timeout: 600 litellm_settings: anthropic_sse_ping_interval_seconds: 3 sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds: 3 general_settings: master_key: sk-qa-36154 ``` ### /v1/chat/completions, self-hosted slow backend through the 60s ingress ```bash curl -sS -N -i --max-time 300 http://127.0.0.1:<ingress-60s>/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-36154" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "qwen-local", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<74k-char document>"}], "stream": true, "max_tokens": 40}' ``` Before (422d925334): the proxy sends nothing while the backend prefills, so the ingress 504s at its read timeout with zero bytes delivered ```text [t+ 60.06s] HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out [t+ 60.06s] ping_comments=0 data_chunks=0 ``` After (e53f044d20): headers plus the first ping arrive in ~3s, 55 pings bridge the 164s prefill, and the stream completes ```text [t+ 3.16s] HTTP/1.1 200 OK [t+ 3.16s] Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8 [t+ 3.16s] : ping [t+ 6.16s] : ping [t+ 9.16s] : ping [t+ 167.28s] data: {"id":"chatcmpl-BOY3tXGcuL7uE6knLd2ItTlAj9KKL8HY","created":1786518422,"model":"qwen-local","object":"chat.completion.chunk",... [t+ 167.63s] data: [DONE] [t+ 167.64s] curl exit=0 ping_comments=55 data_chunks=20 ``` ### /v1/responses, gpt-5.6 with reasoning effort high through the 10s ingress openai SDK, real OpenAI API: `client.responses.create(model="gpt-5.6", input=<hard math prompt>, stream=True, reasoning={"effort": "high"})` Before (422d925334): the first reasoning gap exceeds the ingress timeout and the stream dies mid-flight ```text [t+ 0.64s] first event: response.created [t+ 10.99s] STREAM FAILED: RemoteProtocolError: peer closed connection without sending complete message body (incomplete chunked read) ``` After (e53f044d20): pings cover every reasoning gap and the stream runs to completion ```text [t+ 0.49s] first event: response.created [t+ 205.39s] STREAM COMPLETED: 396 events, answer tail: ...'\\]\n\nintegers \\(n\\) with \\(0\\le n\\le 20000\\) make \\(n^2+n+41\\) prime.' ``` ### /v1/messages, claude-sonnet-5 through the 10s ingress (regression check, route untouched) anthropic SDK, real Anthropic API: `client.messages.stream(model="claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens=600, ...)`. This route keeps its pre-existing Anthropic ping events and completes on both legs ```text before: [t+ 4.86s] STREAM COMPLETED: 6 text deltas after: [t+ 4.05s] STREAM COMPLETED: 6 text deltas ``` ### Known limit, identical on both legs: hosted-provider chat completions with a slow first token OpenAI holds the entire HTTP response, headers included, until the first post-reasoning token, so no gateway-level layer can emit anything before that. gpt-5.6 chat completions through the 10s ingress 504s identically before and after; proof it is provider-side, bypassing LiteLLM entirely: ```text curl -N https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (gpt-5.6, reasoning_effort=high, stream=true) [openai-direct][t+ 45.02s] curl: (28) Operation timed out after 45005 milliseconds with 0 bytes received ``` Once headers do arrive, mid-stream gaps on chat completions are covered the same way as shown for /v1/responses above ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Hosted providers hold headers until first token; that wait stays uncoverable - Deployment `keepalive_seconds`, including explicit `0`, still beats the global - `/v1/messages` untouched; Anthropic ping events already cover it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(bedrock): resolve aliases in batch file records
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock batch records naming a proxy model alias reach AWS untransformed - The batch then reports Completed while every record failed validation How it solves it: - Resolve `model_alias_map` aliases before picking each record's provider transform - Fall back to the batch's own deployment model when a record's model matches no Bedrock provider ## User Flow Before: the batch reports Completed, but the output holds only `anthropic_version: Field required` errors and no model replies 1. The proxy admin lists `bedrock-batch` -> `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` in `model_list`, plus the batch S3 bucket and job role 2. A developer uploads their JSONL with POST http://litellm-domain/v1/files (multipart: `purpose=batch`, `model=bedrock-batch`), each line's body carrying `"model": "bedrock-batch"`, and gets back a long encoded file id 3. They create the batch with POST http://litellm-domain/v1/batches sending `{"input_file_id": "<that id>", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "completion_window": "24h", "model": "bedrock-batch"}` and get a batch id with status `validating` 4. They poll GET http://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until `"status": "completed"` (~10-15 minutes) 5. They download results via GET http://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and every line is an error naming `anthropic_version: Field required`; not one record contains a model reply After: the same upload now returns a model reply for every record 1. The proxy admin lists `bedrock-batch` -> `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` in `model_list`, plus the batch S3 bucket and job role 2. A developer uploads their JSONL with POST http://litellm-domain/v1/files (multipart: `purpose=batch`, `model=bedrock-batch`), each line's body carrying `"model": "bedrock-batch"`, and gets back a long encoded file id 3. They create the batch with POST http://litellm-domain/v1/batches sending `{"input_file_id": "<that id>", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "completion_window": "24h", "model": "bedrock-batch"}` and get a batch id with status `validating` 4. They poll GET http://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until `"status": "completed"` (~10-15 minutes) 5. GET http://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content now returns one `modelOutput` with assistant content per record and no validation errors ## Relevant issues Fixes #36156 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5304 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two live proxies, one per leg, each booted with the same config (`bedrock-batch` -> `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, an SSE-KMS-enforced S3 bucket, and a Bedrock batch job role) and fed the same 110-record JSONL whose every line's body says `"model": "bedrock-batch"`. Real Bedrock model-invocation jobs in us-west-2, no mocks. Before leg at merge base f03df1bb42, after leg at this PR's head e8c1fe8b11 **Before (f03df1bb42, proxy on port 60641): batch says Completed, every record failed** Upload and batch create: ```bash curl http://localhost:60641/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -F purpose=batch -F model=bedrock-batch -F "file=@batch_alias.jsonl" # -> {"id":"file-bGl0ZWxsbTpzMzovL2xpdGVsbG0ta21zLXFhLTM1MTQ4...","object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"uploaded",...} curl http://localhost:60641/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"input_file_id": "<that id>", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "completion_window": "24h", "model": "bedrock-batch"}' # -> {"id":"batch_bGl0ZWxsbTphcm46YXdzOmJlZHJvY2s6dXMtd2VzdC0yOjQzOTE1ODA3NDY1Mjptb2RlbC1pbnZvY2F0aW9uLWpvYi9rZTg2MDAza2gwajU...","status":"validating",...} ``` Final batch object after polling (validating -> in_progress -> completed): ```bash curl "http://localhost:60641/v1/batches/{batch_id}?model=bedrock-batch" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" # -> {"status":"completed","completed_at":1786753624,"error_file_id":null,"errors":null, # "metadata":{"job_arn":"arn:aws:bedrock:us-west-2:439158074652:model-invocation-job/ke86003kh0j5","failure_message":""}, # "output_file_id":"file-bGl0ZWxsbTpzMzovL2xpdGVsbG0ta21zLXFhLTM1MTQ4L2xpdGVsbG0tYmF0Y2gtb3V0cHV0cy8...",...} ``` Output content through the proxy (HTTP 200, 110 lines), first records verbatim: ```bash curl "http://localhost:60641/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content?model=bedrock-batch" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" ``` ```json {"modelInput":{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the number 7 and nothing else."}],"max_tokens":16},"error":{"errorCode":400,"errorMessage":"anthropic_version: Field required","expired":false,"retryable":false},"recordId":"req-17"} {"modelInput":{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the number 0 and nothing else."}],"max_tokens":16},"error":{"errorCode":400,"errorMessage":"anthropic_version: Field required","expired":false,"retryable":false},"recordId":"req-30"} ``` Counts over all 110 records: 110 `anthropic_version: Field required` errors, 0 other errors, 0 model replies. The rejected `modelInput` lines still carry the raw OpenAI-shaped body, untransformed **After (e8c1fe8b11, proxy on port 57789): same flow, every record answered** Same upload and batch create against port 57789 (file `litellm-bedrock-files-bedrock-batch-0ef2cc3f-...`, job `arn:aws:bedrock:us-west-2:439158074652:model-invocation-job/bco4nk5uh1hn`), polled to `"status":"completed"` with `"error_file_id":null` and empty `failure_message`. Output content through the proxy (HTTP 200), first record verbatim: ```bash curl "http://localhost:57789/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content?model=bedrock-batch" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" ``` ```json {"modelInput":{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reply with the number 6 and nothing else."}]}],"max_tokens":16,"anthropic_version":"bedrock-2023-05-31"},"modelOutput":{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5-20251001","id":"msg_bdrk_01WCAn5P5adweBWVA9KwQiLV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"6"}],"stop_reason":"end_turn","usage":{"input_tokens":18,"output_tokens":5}},"recordId":"req-46"} ``` Counts over all 110 records: 110 assistant `modelOutput` replies, 0 errors of any kind, recordIds exactly req-1..req-110. Each `modelInput` shows the proxy rewrote the alias body into Bedrock-native form with `anthropic_version: "bedrock-2023-05-31"` injected, which is precisely the fix under test Surprises hit during QA: - Batch reports completed with request_counts all zero - error_file_id stays null; errors live inside output file - Bedrock reorders output records (req-46 first) - Batches finished in ~10-12 min, not 30-50 - Short-lived SSO creds expire mid-batch; static key needed ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Records naming some other router alias still need `model_alias_map` - Alias names containing a provider word (e.g. "team-meta-proxy") are still inferred as that provider, exactly as on the base branch; `model_alias_map` covers those too ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(streaming): keep upstream usage when the usage chunk also carries choices
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Upstream `usage` is dropped when the usage chunk also has `choices` - `cached_tokens` lost, so streaming cost is billed at the full input rate How it solves it: - Normalize provider SDK usage objects to litellm's `Usage` on ingest ## Relevant issues Fixes #36168 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on `localhost:4000`, config below, streaming `/v1/chat/completions` through it. The upstream is a stand-in OpenAI-compatible server replaying the exact final SSE chunk from the issue (`choices: [{"index": 0, "delta": {}}]` plus `usage` with `cached_tokens`), because this box cannot reach an external provider that emits that shape ```yaml model_list: - model_name: kimi litellm_params: model: openai/moonshotai/kimi-k3 api_base: http://127.0.0.1:8931/v1 api_key: sk-x model_info: input_cost_per_token: 0.0000006 output_cost_per_token: 0.0000025 cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.00000015 general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash curl -s -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"kimi","stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ciao"}]}' | tail -3 ``` Before, at b66d4e6965 (upstream's 38679 prompt tokens replaced by a tokenizer estimate of 9, `prompt_tokens_details` gone) ``` data: {"id":"49c0","created":1786090761,"model":"kimi","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":1,"prompt_tokens":9,"total_tokens":10,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":32,"text_tokens":0}}} data: [DONE] ``` After, at 7853a0c607 ``` data: {"id":"49c0","created":1786090907,"model":"kimi","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":32,"prompt_tokens":38679,"total_tokens":38711,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":32,"text_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":38400}}} data: [DONE] ``` The SpendLogs row for the fixed run bills the cache read rather than the full input rate ```bash curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:4000/spend/logs' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' ``` ``` {'spend': 0.0060074, 'prompt_tokens': 38679, 'completion_tokens': 32} ``` which is `(38679 - 38400) * 6e-7 + 38400 * 1.5e-7 + 32 * 2.5e-6`, so the 38400 cached tokens are priced at the cache-read rate instead of the full input rate ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `chunk_creator` normalized the upstream usage into litellm's `Usage` when parsing the chunk, then a few lines later overwrote it with the raw `chunk.usage`, which for OpenAI-compatible providers is openai's `CompletionUsage`. That overwrite was invisible while the usage arrived on a `choices: []` chunk, since that shape returns early and never reaches it The raw object then reaches `calculate_total_usage` and `_usage_chunk_calculation_helper`, which read it with `"prompt_tokens" in usage`. Only litellm's `Usage` defines `__contains__`; on a plain pydantic model that membership test falls through to `BaseModel.__iter__` and compares the key against `(name, value)` tuples, so every field reads as absent and the usage silently counts as zero. Token counts then fall back to the local tokenizer and `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` disappears, which is the 4x over-billing in the issue The fix normalizes at both ingest points: `_normalize_usage` before the assignment in `chunk_creator`, and `_extract_usage_chunk` in the chunk builder, which declared `-> Usage | None` while happily returning whatever the chunk carried ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(streaming): preserve upstream usage with non-empty choices
signals.text: ## Problem OpenAI-compatible providers can put the final streaming `usage` object on a chunk that still contains a content-free `choices` entry. LiteLLM currently loses the provider's prompt-token counts and `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` in that shape, so downstream aggregation falls back to local tokenization and can overbill cached input. ## Root Cause The OpenAI-compatible streaming path first normalizes provider usage into LiteLLM's `Usage` model. A later generic assignment overwrites that normalized value with the raw OpenAI SDK usage object. The raw object is not handled by the streaming usage accumulator's nested detail parser, so cached-token details and provider counts are discarded. ## Solution Keep the already-normalized LiteLLM usage value when it exists, and only copy the raw chunk usage when no normalized value was produced. ## Changes - Guard the generic usage assignment in `CustomStreamWrapper.chunk_creator()` so it cannot clobber normalized usage. - Add a regression test to the existing core streaming-handler test path covering a non-empty `choices` array with provider-reported cached tokens. ## Testing - Focused regression logic — passed in the local standalone wrapper/SSE reproduction. - Local HTTP/SSE reproduction — both `choices=[]` and `choices=[{"delta":{}}]` preserve `prompt_tokens=39779` and `cached_tokens=39424`. - `py -3 -m ruff check litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py` — passed. - `py -3 -m ruff format --check litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py` — passed. - `py -3 -m py_compile litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py` — passed. - `git diff --check` — passed. - Core test file collection is not locally verifiable because this sparse Windows environment has a pre-existing Pydantic forward-reference failure while importing the existing test module; the new test includes the same model-rebuild setup used to exercise the path. - `basedpyright` — not run; the executable is not installed in this environment. - Full suite — not run; repository-wide generated/workspace dependencies are unavailable in this environment. ## Compatibility/Risk Low risk. This changes only the precedence of usage objects in the OpenAI-compatible streaming path. Providers that do not supply a normalized usage value retain the existing fallback assignment. ## Notes for Reviewer The regression is isolated to ingress parsing of provider chunks with non-empty choices. It is distinct from PR #28736, which changes LiteLLM's egress shape to emit usage-only chunks with empty choices, and from PR #32130, which prevents a later usage chunk from clobbering an earlier prompt-token detail object. The test now lives under `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils`, which is covered by the repository's Core Utilities CI job. ## Linked Issue Closes #36168

signals.title: fix(rerank): populate token usage in spend logs and /ui/usage
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - /ui/usage always shows 0 tokens for rerank calls, for every provider, not just hosted_vllm - hosted_vllm rerank servers returning Cohere-style `meta` usage get silently zeroed to 0 How it solves it: - Added a `meta.billed_units`/`meta.tokens` fallback to both usage-extraction functions in litellm_logging.py - Made HostedVLLMRerankConfig read usage from either `meta` (Cohere-style) or `usage` (OpenAI-style) ## Relevant issues Fixes #36185 ([Bug]: /ui/usage shows 0 tokens for rerank calls (hosted_vllm and other providers) ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Commit tested: 518d9aca9a (branch fix/rerank-usage-tracking, based on v1.95.0) 1. Rerank request: curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/rerank \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{ "model": "local/BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", "query": "Что такое vLLM?", "documents": ["vLLM это быстрый движок инференса", "Сегодня идет дождь"] }' Response: {"id":"rerank-77dab01cce4844158840b6d6778fb3d8","results":[{"index":0,"relevance_score":0.9978354573249817,"document":{"text":"vLLM это быстрый движок инференса"}},{"index":1,"relevance_score":0.000016201263861148618,"document":{"text":"Сегодня идет дождь"}}],"meta":{"billed_units":{"total_tokens":38},"tokens":{"input_tokens":38}}} 2. Spend log lookup for that request: curl "http://127.0.0.1:4000/spend/logs?request_id=rerank-77dab01cce4844158840b6d6778fb3d8" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" Relevant fields from the response (trimmed for brevity): { "request_id": "rerank-77dab01cce4844158840b6d6778fb3d8", "call_type": "arerank", "model": "hosted_vllm/BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", "total_tokens": 38, "prompt_tokens": 38, "completion_tokens": 0, "spend": 0.0 } Before this fix, total_tokens/prompt_tokens in the spend log were always 0 for rerank calls regardless of the raw response's meta.billed_units.total_tokens. After the fix, they correctly match the model's reported usage (38). ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/llms/hosted_vllm/rerank/transformation.py`: read usage from `meta` or `usage` - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py`: `get_usage_from_response_obj` and `get_usage_as_dict` now fall back to `meta.billed_units`/`meta.tokens` when there's no top-level `usage` - Added regression tests in `tests/logging_callback_tests/test_standard_logging_payload.py` and `tests/test_litellm/llms/hosted_vllm/test_hosted_vllm_rerank_transformation.py`

signals.title: feat(ui): persist usage page filters across reload, fix Safari date-picker close
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - /ui/usage resets time range, view, and tab to defaults on every reload - relative date presets ("Today", "7d") were frozen at page-load time, not the actual current day - Apply button in the date picker never closes the dropdown in Safari How it solves it: - Persist the selected date-range preset (or custom range), usage view, and activity tab index to localStorage - Recompute relative presets fresh on load and on tab focus/visibility change - Close the date-picker dropdown before scheduling the requestIdleCallback-based background adjustment, with a setTimeout fallback for Safari ## Relevant issues Fixes #36190 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Will attach: before/after reload showing the same date range + Model Activity tab selection retained; Safari screenshot showing Apply closes the dropdown. ## Type New Feature Bug Fix ## Changes - `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/shared/date_range_presets.ts`: extracted relative-time-preset logic (new file, shared between the picker and the page) - `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/shared/advanced_date_picker.tsx`: uses the shared presets module; fixed the Safari close-on-Apply bug - `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/app/(dashboard)/usage/_components/components/UsagePageView.tsx`: persists date range/view/tab to localStorage, controlled TabGroup - Added/updated tests in `advanced_date_picker.test.tsx` (incl. a regression test that removes requestIdleCallback to emulate Safari) and `UsagePageView.test.tsx` (localStorage isolation fix)

signals.title: feat(search): add Nimble as a search provider
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nimble's Search API is not reachable through LiteLLM - No cost tracking or dashboard entry for Nimble searches How it solves it: - Adds `NimbleSearchConfig`, the 18th native search provider - Registers it in the enum, config map, pricing map, and dashboard Disclosure: I work at Nimble. The pricing entry is our public pay-as-you-go list rate and the logo is our own mark ## User Flow Before: a developer whose gateway already serves Perplexity and Tavily searches cannot route to Nimble at all 1. They add a `search_tools` block with `search_provider: nimble` and restart the proxy 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/search/nimble-search with `{"query": "latest AI developments", "max_results": 3}` 3. The request fails before leaving the gateway with `Search is not supported for provider: nimble` 4. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=search-tools and Nimble is absent from the provider dropdown, so there is no way to configure it from the UI either After: the same block works, and Nimble behaves like every other search provider 1. They add the same `search_tools` block with `search_provider: nimble` and restart the proxy 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/search/nimble-search request 3. They get back `{"object": "search", "results": [...]}` with three ranked results, each carrying a title, a URL, and a snippet 4. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request logged at non-zero spend 5. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=search-tools, see "Nimble" in the provider dropdown with its logo, and can round-trip a query with the Test Connection button ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) `code-quality` and `documentation` are the only red checks. Both fail on the same line, `Environment variables read under ./litellm but mentioned nowhere in the docs: ['NIMBLE_API_BASE']`, and both go green once BerriAI/litellm-docs#838 merges, since those jobs check out that repo. Every other check passes. Greptile is at 5/5 with no open findings ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All runs captured at `bef49e6388` against the live Nimble API with a real key, billed at Nimble's normal rate. No mocks **1. Proxy end to end, exercising the unified params and two Nimble-native ones** ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/search/nimble-search \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query":"nimble web scraping api","max_results":3,"search_depth":"fast","country":"gb","search_domain_filter":["nimbleway.com","-reddit.com"]}' | jq ``` ```json { "object": "search", "results": [ { "title": "Nimble Web API | Complete, Structured Web Data From Any Page", "url": "https://www.nimbleway.com/nimble-api/web", "snippet": "Nimble APIs receives the request and handles everything else from coll..." }, { "title": "Guide to Industry-Specific Web Scraping with Nimble's API", "url": "https://www.nimbleway.com/blog/use-nimble-api-scraping-by-industry", "snippet": "Presale & Event Announcements: Scrape social media, artist websites, a..." }, { "title": "AI-Powered Web Scraping Browser for Data Automation", "url": "https://www.nimbleway.com/nimble-api/browser", "snippet": "Nimble Browserless Drivers handle JavaScript-heavy sites, scale automa..." } ] } ``` **2. What actually went on the wire, from the proxy's own debug log** `country` is upper-cased to the ISO form Nimble documents, `search_domain_filter` is split on the `-` prefix, and `search_depth` passes through untouched ``` POST Request Sent from LiteLLM: curl -X POST \ https://sdk.nimbleway.com/v2/search \ -H 'Authorization: Be****a0' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Client-Source: litellm' \ -d '{'include_domains': ('nimbleway.com',), 'exclude_domains': ('reddit.com',), 'search_depth': 'fast', 'query': 'nimble web scraping api', 'max_results': 3, 'country': 'GB'}' ``` **3. Cost tracking** ``` response_cost: 0.005 ``` **4. SDK path** ```bash python -c " import litellm r = litellm.search(query='latest AI developments', search_provider='nimble', max_results=3) print('tracked cost:', r._hidden_params['response_cost']) " ``` ``` tracked cost: 0.005 ``` **5. Missing-key path names the variable to set** ```bash env -u NIMBLE_API_KEY python -c "import litellm; litellm.search(query='x', search_provider='nimble')" ``` ``` litellm.APIConnectionError: NIMBLE_API_KEY is not set. Set `NIMBLE_API_KEY` environment variable. ``` **6. Errors are attributed to the provider** A deliberately invalid combination, showing that Nimble's own `{"detail": ...}` message is unwrapped rather than dumped as raw JSON ``` Nimble Search: search_depth='fast' is only supported with focus='general'. See https://docs.nimbleway.com/api-reference/search/search for details. ``` **7. Dashboard discovery** ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/search_tools/ui/available_providers -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq -c '.providers[] | select(.provider_name=="nimble")' ``` ```json {"provider_name":"nimble","ui_friendly_name":"Nimble"} ``` UI screenshot of the provider dropdown and a passing Test Connection to follow ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes `NimbleSearchConfig` calls `POST https://sdk.nimbleway.com/v2/search` with a bearer key resolved through `resolve_server_api_key`, so the host-aware guard against leaking a server key to a caller-supplied `api_base` applies here like everywhere else. `NIMBLE_API_BASE` overrides the host, and `/search` is appended only when the base does not already end in it, after stripping any trailing slash Nimble already uses the Perplexity unified spec's parameter names, so the request transform is close to a pass-through. `max_results` goes over unclamped, so Nimble's own 1-100 validation produces a clearer error than silently rewriting the caller's request. `country` is upper-cased to the ISO form Nimble documents. `max_tokens_per_page` is dropped, having no equivalent. Everything else is forwarded untouched, which keeps `focus`, `search_depth`, `time_range`, `start_date`/`end_date`, `locale`, `output_format`, `content_type` and `max_subagents` reachable without LiteLLM having to track Nimble's surface `search_domain_filter` splits into `include_domains` and `exclude_domains` on the unified spec's `-` prefix. No other provider decodes that prefix today; they map the list straight onto their include field. A list with no `-` entries behaves identically to those providers, so this is additive. An explicitly supplied `include_domains` or `exclude_domains` wins over anything derived from the unified param, rather than being silently overwritten On the response side, `snippet` prefers `content` and falls back to `description`, matching the Firecrawl config. `date` carries only the absolute `publish_date`; news results often carry a relative `publish_date_raw` instead, which is not a date, so the whole `additional_data` object rides through as an extra on `SearchResult` and nothing is lost. Results keep the order Nimble ranked them in. The body is parsed into Pydantic models straight from the response bytes, so a non-JSON body and a JSON body of the wrong shape both raise one attributed error instead of being reported as a successful zero-result search, and a single degraded result degrades to empty strings rather than failing the whole call One shared file changes beyond registration: `BaseSearchConfig.get_supported_perplexity_optional_params` now returns a module-level `frozenset[str]` instead of building a fresh mutable `set` on every call. All thirteen callers use it for membership tests inside a per-parameter loop, and none mutate it Two duplications are left alone on purpose, since fixing either means touching eight providers' behavior inside a PR that adds one. Nimble is the ninth copy of the `api_base or env or default` plus append-`/search` pattern, and it is the only copy that strips a trailing slash first. And the base states no rule about whether a native param or a unified param wins, so each provider invents one. Both look like good follow-ups ## QA runbook ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(helm): add startupProbe and hpa.behavior to the componentized chart
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Componentized chart cannot set a `startupProbe` on any component - Slow cold starts get liveness-killed before they finish booting - Componentized chart cannot set HPA `spec.behavior` - No control over scale-up/scale-down policies or stabilization windows How it solves it: - Adds a `startupProbe` knob to gateway/backend/ui deployments - Adds an `hpa.behavior` passthrough to gateway/backend/ui HPAs - Both empty by default, so existing renders are unchanged - Same `{{- with ... }}` / `toYaml` pattern already used for other knobs ## User Flow Before: an operator deploying the componentized chart onto a cluster where the proxy has a slow cold start cannot express either knob through values. 1. They set `gateway.startupProbe` in their values and run `helm upgrade` 2. `kubectl get deploy litellm-gateway -o yaml` shows **no** `startupProbe` — the value is silently dropped, so a slow first boot is liveness-killed and the pod crash-loops on scale-up 3. They set `gateway.hpa.behavior` to slow scale-down and run `helm upgrade` 4. `kubectl get hpa litellm-gateway -o yaml` shows **no** `spec.behavior`; scaling uses the Kubernetes defaults and the value is ignored After: the same values render onto the manifests. 1. They set `gateway.startupProbe` in their values and run `helm upgrade` 2. `kubectl get deploy litellm-gateway -o yaml` now shows the `startupProbe` verbatim; liveness/readiness only begin once startup succeeds, so a slow boot no longer crash-loops 3. They set `gateway.hpa.behavior` and run `helm upgrade` 4. `kubectl get hpa litellm-gateway -o yaml` now shows `spec.behavior` verbatim, so their scale-up/scale-down policies take effect ## Relevant issues <!-- none filed; parity gap in the componentized chart --> ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) <!-- Note: two small, closely-related pod-spec passthrough knobs for the componentized chart (startupProbe + hpa.behavior), grouped in one PR by request. -->

signals.title: Fix ModelResponse() PydanticUserError: forward reference not fully defined
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #36384 Calling `ModelResponse()` with no arguments crashes with: ``` pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `Message` is not fully defined; you should define `ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock`, then call `Message.model_rebuild()`. ``` ## Root Cause In `litellm/types/llms/openai.py`, the `ChatCompletionReasoningItem` TypedDict has a field: ```python summary: List["ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock"] ``` The type annotation uses a **string forward reference** (`"ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock"`), even though `ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock` is already defined earlier in the same file (line 548 vs line 553). When Pydantic builds the `Message` model (in `litellm/types/utils.py`), it recursively resolves all type annotations, including those inside TypedDicts used as field types. The string forward reference `"ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock"` cannot be resolved in the namespace of `utils.py` because `ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock` is not imported there. This causes the `PydanticUserError`. ## Fix Remove the unnecessary string quotes from the forward reference: ```python # Before summary: List["ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock"] # After summary: List[ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock] ``` Since `ChatCompletionReasoningSummaryTextBlock` is defined before `ChatCompletionReasoningItem` in the same file, the direct reference works correctly and Pydantic can resolve the type without needing it in the importing module's namespace.
