signals.title: feat(proxy): per-component response cost headers
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Callers only see a total request cost, never its component split - Attributing spend needs hand-copied pricing tables that drift per provider How it solves it: - Emits six `x-litellm-response-cost-*` component headers next to the total - Input, cache read, cache creation, output, and tool usage sum exactly to the total; reasoning is a subset of output - Reads the cost breakdown the proxy already computes per request - Omits component headers cleanly when no breakdown was computed - Existing cost, discount, and margin headers are unchanged ## User Flow Before: a platform team fronting all LLM traffic through the LiteLLM proxy wants to show each internal app where its spend goes, but callers only ever see one total, so they rebuild the split by hand from their own pricing tables 1. An app sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a prompt-cached context on a reasoning model such as gpt-5.4-nano 2. The 200 response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 7.4e-06` and the body's `usage` block carries token counts (`prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) 3. To split the total they multiply those token counts by per-model rates copied into their own pricing table, which drifts: cache-write premiums, reasoning rates, and built-in tool charges differ per provider, and tool charges never appear in `usage` at all 4. When their hand-computed components fail to sum to the header total, they cannot tell which component is wrong After: the same response states the split directly and it sums to the total 1. The app sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same prompt-cached context 2. The 200 response carries the same `x-litellm-response-cost` total and now also `x-litellm-response-cost-input`, `-output`, `-cache-read`, `-cache-creation`, `-reasoning`, and `-tool-usage` 3. Input plus cache read plus cache creation plus output plus tool usage equals the total, reasoning being a subset of output, so the team attributes spend per component with no local pricing table ## Relevant issues Closes #36875 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5617 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live-proxy legs with real OpenAI and Anthropic spend, no mocks. Before leg at commit c9917cbf99 (this PR's merge base), after leg re-proven at commit 05beb7abb5 (this PR's behavioral tip). Each leg booted a bootstrapped worktree with `.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port <port>` and hit all three unified endpoints: /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses with gpt-5.4-nano, /v1/messages with claude-haiku-4-5 carrying a ~6k-token `cache_control: ephemeral` system block sent twice to exercise cache creation then cache read. An earlier eight-scenario after leg at 9079e4c47b surfaced that the input header still contained the cache costs nested inside it (Cursor Bugbot flagged the same double-count); 05beb7abb5 fixed that by subtracting the cache components from the input header, the same split the Admin UI's cost breakdown viewer shows, and the leg below re-proves the final contract ### Before leg (c9917cbf99, port 41387): component headers absent everywhere ```bash curl -sD /tmp/h_a1.txt -o /tmp/b_a1.json -X POST http://localhost:41387/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @body_a.json grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost' /tmp/h_a1.txt ``` A1 and A2 (identical, 200 OK, prompt_tokens=1177, completion_tokens=4, answer "391"): ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00024040000000000002 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.00024040000000000002 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 ``` B (/v1/responses, 200 OK, input_tokens=12, output_tokens=5): ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 8.65e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 8.65e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 ``` C1 and C2 (/v1/messages; C1 cache_creation_input_tokens=6242, C2 cache_read_input_tokens=6242): ``` == c1 == x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0078345 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0078345 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 == c2 == x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0006562 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0006562 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 ``` Across all five before-leg responses, zero occurrences of `-input`, `-output`, `-cache-read`, `-cache-creation`, `-reasoning`, or `-tool-usage` ### After leg (05beb7abb5, port 46746): six component headers present and additive A1 (chat completions, gpt-5.4-nano, prompt_tokens=1417, completion_tokens=4, answer "391"; A2 byte-identical): ```bash curl -sD /tmp/ha2_a1.txt -o /tmp/ba2_a1.json -X POST http://localhost:46746/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @body_a.json grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost' /tmp/ha2_a1.txt ``` ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0002884 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0002884 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0002834 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 5e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 ``` B (/v1/responses, input_tokens=12, output_tokens=5): ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 8.65e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 2.4e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 6.25e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 ``` C1 (/v1/messages, cold cache, cache_creation_input_tokens=6242, input_tokens=12) then C2 (warm, cache_read_input_tokens=6242): ``` == c1 == x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0078345 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 1.1999999999999858e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 2e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-cache-creation: 0.0078025 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 == c2 == x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0006562 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 1.1999999999999966e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 2e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-cache-read: 0.0006242 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 ``` C1n/C2n (same shape, fresh nonce guaranteeing a cold cache; cache_creation then cache_read of 6267 tokens) behaved identically: creation 0.00783375, read 0.0006267, input 1.2e-05 on both Br (/v1/responses with `"reasoning": {"effort": "high"}`, input_tokens=25, output_tokens=175, reasoning_tokens=168): ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00022375 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 4.9999999999999996e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0.00021875 x-litellm-response-cost-reasoning: 0.00021 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 ``` ### Sum invariant across all eight after-leg responses Python check over the captured header files (rel_tol 1e-9, absent header = 0). Additive = input + cache-read + cache-creation + output + tool-usage; nested = input + output + tool-usage (the pre-fix contract) | Scenario | Total | Additive holds | Nested holds | reasoning<=output | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A1 | 0.0002884 | True | True | True | | A2 | 0.0002884 | True | True | True | | B | 0.00000865 | True | True | True | | C1 | 0.0078345 | True | False | True | | C2 | 0.0006562 | True | False | True | | C1n | 0.0078658 | True | False | True | | C2n | 0.0006587 | True | False | True | | Br | 0.0002238 | True | True | True | On every cache scenario the input header is exactly the 12 uncached tokens x 1e-06 = 1.2e-05, cache creation = tokens x 1.25e-06, and cache read = tokens x 1e-07, matching Haiku 4.5 pricing to the digit (rel_tol 1e-9) **Component semantics**: `_store_cost_breakdown_in_logging_obj` in cost_calculator.py records the full prompt cost (cache pricing already applied) as input_cost, so emitting it unchanged would double-count the cache once the cache headers exist. The header path therefore subtracts cache read and cache creation from input before emitting, the exact split the Admin UI's cost breakdown viewer already shows, delivering the additive contract issue #36875 asked for: input + cache-read + cache-creation + output + tool-usage = total, reasoning a subset of output. Spend-log storage is untouched QA surprises: - Stored input nests cache costs; headers now subtract them - Nested formula now fails on cache scenarios, by design - Input header carries float noise (1.19999...e-05), subtraction artifact - No specified scenario produced reasoning tokens; added Br - OpenAI auto-cache never hit on repeat prompts - .env master key is double-quoted; strip quotes - Harness reaped backgrounded proxies twice; detached Popen fixed it ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Component headers appear on non-streaming responses only (headers leave before a stream's usage exists) - Reasoning is a subset of output, so exclude it when summing components to the total - Cache and reasoning headers appear only when those costs are nonzero - The input header is the uncached input cost; spend logs keep storing the full prompt cost (cache included) as input_cost, so the header equals stored input minus the cache components ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(melious): add Melious as a provider
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `melious/*` model names do not resolve at all - Reaching Melious needs a hand-wired base URL per deployment - Its two API surfaces need two different base URLs - Spend reads zero without hand-pasted per-token prices How it solves it: - Registers `melious` across the provider map - Serves `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` natively - Ships cost-map entries for 17 flagship chat models ## User Flow Before: a developer routing to Melious wires a base URL into every deployment, and a second, different one for the Anthropic surface 1. They add a deployment with `model: openai/glm-5.1`, `api_base: https://api.melious.ai/v1`, and their Melious key 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "glm-5.1"` and get a normal completion back 3. They want Claude Code on the same account, so they add a second deployment with `model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4` and `api_base: https://api.melious.ai`, this time without the `/v1` 4. Whenever either base URL carries the wrong suffix the call returns `NotFoundError: The requested resource was not found`, which never says which surface was wrong 5. Every response header reads `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0` until they look up per-token prices and paste them into each deployment After: naming the model is the whole configuration, and one key covers both surfaces 1. signals.title: fix: preserve prompt cache for mid-conversation system on unflagged Claude models
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Mid-conversation system reminders on pre-4.8 Claude get hoisted into `system` - The hoist rewrites the cached prefix, re-billing the whole conversation How it solves it: - Convert the reminder to a user turn in place instead - Leading system runs still hoist; flagged models are untouched ## User Flow Before: a Claude Code user routed to a Vertex Claude 4.6 deployment pays full cache-write pricing every turn a reminder appears 1. They run a long session against POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with their proxy key, history carrying `cache_control` breakpoints 2. Claude Code inserts a `role: "system"` reminder mid-conversation 3. The response is 200, but `usage` shows `cache_creation_input_tokens` around 1746 with `cache_read_input_tokens` dropping to 5265: the whole prior history was re-billed at cache-write pricing (reporter's real Vertex numbers in #36559) 4. Every later reminder repeats the same full-prefix rebill After: the same session keeps its cache; only the new turn is fresh 1. They run a long session against POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with their proxy key, history carrying `cache_control` breakpoints 2. Claude Code inserts a `role: "system"` reminder mid-conversation 3. The response is 200, and `usage` shows `cache_read_input_tokens` around 6973 with `cache_creation_input_tokens` around 60: the full prior history read back from cache 4. Follow-up turns keep reading the full cached prefix ## Relevant issues Fixes #36559 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? Three things stand in for that run 1. The issue reporter measured the exact convert-in-place patch on real Vertex traffic and posted before/after usage numbers in #36559 (reminder turn: cache_read 5265 -> 6973, cache_creation 1746 -> 60) 2. Unit coverage at 658c67c152 pins the new request shape for all three partner routes plus the unmapped-model default, and keeps the flagged-model and leading-run behavior pinned unchanged 3. The two existing e2e suites (`test_messages_mid_conversation_system_e2e.py`, `test_messages_mid_conversation_system_native_providers_e2e.py`) exercise this path against live Bedrock/Vertex/Azure; a maintainer run of those two files is the real proof, and I am happy to iterate if anything goes red ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A converted reminder loses true system-role priority; tradeoff discussed and accepted in #36559 - The operator-note prefix is part of the request bytes; changing it later invalidates caches again, so it is pinned by tests ## QA runbook The e2e edits are renames and docstring updates only (hoist wording -> convert wording); signals.title: fix: add supports_mid_conversation_system to bare first-party Claude cost-map keys
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bare first-party keys (`claude-opus-4-8`, the 5 family) lack `supports_mid_conversation_system` - Regional and provider-prefixed variants of the same models carry it - A plain `custom_llm_provider="anthropic"` lookup reports the capability as unset How it solves it: - Adds the flag to the 5 bare first-party entries in both cost-map files - Adds a sweep test so future first-party entries cannot miss it ## User Flow Before: a developer checking whether their model keeps mid-conversation system messages gets a wrong answer for first-party keys 1. They call `litellm.get_model_info(model="claude-opus-4-8", custom_llm_provider="anthropic")` 2. `supports_mid_conversation_system` comes back `None`, so their code treats a model that supports the feature as unsupported 3. The same call with `model="vertex_ai/claude-opus-4-8"` returns `True`, so the same model reports different capabilities per route After: the same lookup answers consistently on every route 1. They call `litellm.get_model_info(model="claude-opus-4-8", custom_llm_provider="anthropic")` 2. `supports_mid_conversation_system` comes back `True`, matching the regional and provider-prefixed entries ## Relevant issues Surfaced by the reporter in #36559 (follow-up to #36968); this PR is the cost-map data fix only ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? The user-visible behavior is the SDK lookup itself Before, at 2bc9bb4a9d: ``` $ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.get_model_info(model='claude-opus-4-8', custom_llm_provider='anthropic').get('supports_mid_conversation_system'))" None ``` After, at this PR's head: ``` $ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.get_model_info(model='claude-opus-4-8', custom_llm_provider='anthropic').get('supports_mid_conversation_system'))" True ``` Same check returns True for claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5, claude-fable-5, and claude-mythos-5 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Data plus one sweep test only; no behavior code touched ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(a2a): keep the missing a2a-sdk error reachable
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `a2a-sdk` is optional, `litellm[proxy]` does not install it - Without it, agent calls report `NoneType takes no arguments` - The real "install a2a-sdk" message exists but never runs - The absent-SDK fallback was typed `Any`, so nothing was checked - That hid `get_agent_card` dropping the SDK's `signature_verifier` How it solves it: - Fall back to a subclassable placeholder instead of `None` - Declare the base under `TYPE_CHECKING`, fall back only at runtime - Forward `signature_verifier` to both `super()` calls - Two regression tests, each failing on today's code ## User Flow Before: an operator who installed the gateway the documented way calls their registered agent and gets an opaque Python error rather than being told which package is missing 1. They install the gateway with `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`, then register an agent named `demo-agent` under the top level `agents` key in config.yaml 2. They start the gateway and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns 200 3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent with a JSON-RPC `message/send` body 4. The call comes back HTTP 500 with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: NoneType takes no arguments"}}` 5. They check the gateway log and find only `Error invoking agent: NoneType takes no arguments`, repeated, naming no package, so they are left guessing what to install After: the same call names the missing package, so the operator knows what to do next 1. They install the gateway with `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`, then register an agent named `demo-agent` under the top level `agents` key in config.yaml 2. They start the gateway and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns 200 3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent with a JSON-RPC `message/send` body 4. The call comes back HTTP 500 with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Server error: 'a2a' package not installed. Please install 'a2a-sdk'."}}` 5. They run `pip install "a2a-sdk>=1.1.0,<2.0"`, restart the gateway, and the same POST reaches their agent ## Relevant issues Fixes #36971 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs use the same proxy, the same config, and the same request, with `a2a-sdk` uninstalled. The path fails before any call to the agent or to an LLM provider, so no provider request is involved config.yaml: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: sk-placeholder-not-used-by-this-repro agents: - agent_name: demo-agent agent_card_params: name: "Demo Agent" url: "http://localhost:10001" protocolVersion: "1.0" general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ``` python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config a2a_config.yaml --port 4000 ``` Before, at commit `423b791ee0`: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"hello"}],"messageId":"msg-1"}}}' {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: NoneType takes no arguments"}} [HTTP 500] ``` proxy log: ``` 23:54:19 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: a2a_endpoints.py:970 - Error invoking agent: NoneType takes no arguments TypeError: NoneType takes no arguments ``` After, same commit plus this change: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"hello"}],"messageId":"msg-1"}}}' {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Server error: 'a2a' package not installed. Please install 'a2a-sdk'."}} [HTTP 500] ``` proxy log for that request contains no `TypeError` With `a2a-sdk` installed, which is how CI runs, `tests/test_litellm/a2a_protocol/test_card_resolver.py` is 6 passed. Reverting only the one line character and keeping the test makes it 1 failed, 5 passed, so the new test fails on today's code rather than passing vacuously ### Typing and the override it uncovered Annotating the fallback `Any` meant the subclass was never checked. Declaring the base under `TYPE_CHECKING` restores that, following the idiom already in `litellm/types/utils.py` and `litellm/llms/bedrock.py`. On this file, `basedpyright==1.39.7`: ``` before: 25 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes after: 14 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes ``` Among the errors it could finally see: ``` card_resolver.py:118 - error: Method "get_agent_card" overrides class "A2ACardResolver" in an incompatible manner Positional parameter count mismatch; base method has 4, but override has 3 Parameter 4 mismatch: base parameter "signature_verifier" is keyword parameter ``` The SDK signature is `get_agent_card(self, relative_card_path=None, http_kwargs=None, signature_verifier=None)`, so any caller passing `signature_verifier` hit a `TypeError`. No in-repo caller passes it today, which is why it went unnoticed. There is no user-visible flow to curl for that one, so the evidence is the type checker above plus a regression test that reverts to a `TypeError` without the fix: ``` with fix: 86 passed prod file reverted: 1 failed, 6 passed FAILED test_get_agent_card_forwards_signature_verifier - TypeError ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Status stays 500 in both cases, only the message changes - Docker images install `extra_proxy`, so they were unaffected - Placeholder base is never instantiated on this path - `signature_verifier` has no in-repo caller, so no curl proof ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): exclude Pydantic defaults in /config/update so existing fields are not wiped (Fixes #36446)
signals.text: ## Summary `POST /config/update` silently wiped `router_settings.model_group_alias` to `{}` on every router-settings edit that did not explicitly include the alias map. Editing `routing_groups` or changing a `routing_strategy` through the Admin UI would clobber the existing alias map, and the `400 Invalid model name` errors that followed looked like a periodic "aliases wiped" bug. The same pattern applied to any `{}`/`[]`-defaulted field on `UpdateRouterConfig` and `ConfigGeneralSettings`. Root cause: in `update_config()`, the router-settings and general-settings update payloads are built via `dict(exclude_none=True)`, which only drops `None` values. Pydantic fields with non-`None` defaults (e.g. `UpdateRouterConfig.model_group_alias: Optional[Dict[...]] = {}`) leak their default into the serialized payload even when the caller never sent them. The shallow merge `{**existing, **updates}` then overwrites the real value with the default. Fix: add `exclude_defaults=True` to both `dict(exclude_none=True)` calls. Pydantic's `exclude_defaults` flag drops any field whose value equals the field's default — so the `{}` default for `model_group_alias` no longer leaks into the update payload, and the shallow merge correctly preserves the existing alias map. Fixes #36446. ## Changes ### `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` - Line 14532 (`general_settings` update): `dict(exclude_none=True)` → `dict(exclude_none=True, exclude_defaults=True)`. Comment block on the new kwarg documents the bug class and cross-references #36446. - Line 14607 (`router_settings` update): same one-kwarg change. Comment block explains the `model_group_alias` symptom. The two call sites are the only `dict(exclude_none=True)` calls in the proxy; the change is the minimum-scope fix. ### `tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_routes_config.py` - New `test_config_update_preserves_existing_router_settings_alias_map` regression pin. Seeds the stored config with a non-empty `model_group_alias` (`{"security": "luna"}`), sends a `/config/update` that only touches `routing_groups`, and asserts the persisted `router_settings` still has `model_group_alias == {"security": "luna"}` (not the Pydantic default `{}`). - New `test_config_update_preserves_existing_general_settings_default_dict_fields` regression pin. Seeds the stored config with a non-default `alerting_threshold`, sends a `/config/update` that only touches `alerting`, and asserts the persisted `general_settings` still has the existing `alerting_threshold` value. Both tests use the existing `_install_litellm_config` helper to install a `litellm_config` table mock, then capture the `table.upsert` call args to assert the persisted JSON. They mirror the structure of the existing `test_config_update_happy_admin` so the regression pin lives next to the existing pin. ## Verification Local (this branch, `litellm_internal_staging` @ `2bb297efa0` base): - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_routes_config.py` — 38/38 pass (36 pre-existing + 2 new). - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py` — 117/117 pass (no regressions on the related ProxyConfig / config-storage tests). - `ruff check litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` — clean. - `ruff format --check litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` — already formatted. - `scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py` — OK (every strict rule within its codebase ceiling). - `scripts/type_discipline_gate.py` — OK (every LIT rule within its codebase ceiling; no new suppressions introduced). Bug-reproduction check (cycle 14 self-audit, "fix all X" pattern from the agent memory): - Stashed the source fix, re-ran both new tests. `test_config_update_preserves_existing_router_settings_alias_map` fails with `assert persisted["model_group_alias"] == {"security": "luna"}` — `AssertionError: assert {} == {"security": "luna"}` — the exact wipe symptom the issue documents. Restored the fix, the test passes. The general_settings test is robust to the bug because `GeneralSettings` has `None` defaults (not `{}`) for the fields the test exercises; the fix is still the right pattern for symmetry with the router_settings call site, and a future `ConfigGeneralSettings` field added with a `{}` default would automatically be protected. ## Design notes - **Why `exclude_defaults=True` rather than changing the Pydantic model defaults to `None`** — the `{}` default on `UpdateRouterConfig.model_group_alias` is a deliberate API choice (it tells `update_settings` to "clear the alias map" when the caller explicitly sends `model_group_alias: {}`). Changing the default to `None` would break that contract. The issue's suggested fix is to filter at serialization, not change the model, and that's the right minimum-scope change. - **Why both the `general_settings` and `router_settings` paths get the same fix** — they have the identical shallow-merge pattern and the same bug class. The issue's "related" section calls out that "the `general_settings` handler has the identical pattern and likely needs the same treatment". Applying the same one-kwarg fix to both is the minimum-scope way to address the bug class. - **Why no change to the `litellm_settings` update path** — that path uses `dict(config_info.litellm_settings)` (a regular dict constructor) rather than `.dict(exclude_none=True)`. The bug class is the same, but the path also has success_callback special-casing that depends on the incoming dict shape. A drive-by fix there would expand the PR's surface and risk breaking the success_callback normalizer. Out of scope for this PR; a natural cycle 15+ candidate. - **Why the `SimpleNamespace(param_value=...)` mock pattern** — the `_read_section` helper inside `update_config` returns `dict(row.param_value)`, so a plain dict for `param_value` is what the helper expects. `SimpleNamespace` is the smallest mock that lets the test set just the one attribute the helper reads. - **Why two separate tests (one per update path) rather than a parametrized test** — the two paths have different shape contracts (router_settings is a single `model_group_alias` field that maps 1:1; general_settings has many fields with `None` defaults and a `_alert_to_webhook_url` side-effect handler). Two explicit tests read more clearly and pin the exact symptom in each path. ## Risks - **Very low.** The change adds a kwarg to two existing Pydantic `dict()` calls. The `exclude_defaults` flag is documented to drop any field whose value equals the Pydantic default, so fields the caller explicitly sent with the same value as the default are now dropped from the serialized payload — but the merge of an empty drop into `existing` is a no-op, so the persisted result is identical to the pre-fix behavior for that case. - The pre-existing behavior for fields the caller explicitly sent (with a value different from the default) is unchanged: those still go through `exclude_none=True` and the shallow merge applies them. ## Future improvements (not in this PR) - The same `dict(...)` pattern in the `litellm_settings` update path (line 14576) is a candidate for the same treatment. A natural cycle 15+ candidate. - Migrating the `.dict()` calls to `.model_dump(...)` is a separate drive-by refactor flagged by the Pydantic V2 deprecation warning. The deprecation applies across the file; the minimum-scope fix here uses the existing API. - A helper like `_pydantic_dict_with_excludes(model, *exclude)` would dedupe the `dict(exclude_none=True, exclude_defaults=True)` pattern across the file and make future regressions a one-line change. Out of scope for this PR. - The issue also notes that `litellm_settings` is affected by the same `{}` default leak for `plugins` (`list[PluginConfig] | None = None` — not a default-`{}` field but the sibling concern). A follow-up cycle could audit the `litellm_settings` model for fields whose defaults silently clobber the stored config.

signals.title: fix(helm): bound the migrations Job so a blocked migration cannot stall the release
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A blocked schema migration hangs the release forever - `backoffLimit` never fires: the pod never terminates - Operators must delete the Job by hand to recover - Unrelated gateway, backend and UI changes silently stop shipping How it solves it: - Add `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds` to both charts - Default 1800s, so a stuck Job fails instead of hanging - Guarded by `with`, so `null` restores the old behaviour ## User Flow Before: an operator upgrading the chart, whose migration blocks on the database, gets an upgrade that never returns 1. They run `helm upgrade litellm ./helm/litellm -f values.yaml` 2. The migration Job starts and its container blocks talking to the database 3. The command sits waiting on the pre-upgrade hook and never returns 4. `kubectl get job litellm-migrations` still reads `Running 0/1` hours later, with no conditions set 5. Nothing else in the release rolls out, so unrelated gateway, backend and UI changes never reach the cluster 6. The only way out is `kubectl delete job litellm-migrations` by hand After: the same upgrade gives up on its own, so the operator gets a failure they can act on instead of a hang 1. They run the same `helm upgrade litellm ./helm/litellm -f values.yaml` 2. The migration Job starts and blocks on the database exactly as before 3. After `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds` (1800 by default) the Job reports `Failed`, reason `DeadlineExceeded` 4. `helm upgrade` returns non-zero naming the failed hook rather than waiting forever 5. The rest of the release is no longer pinned behind a Job that cannot finish, so the next attempt can proceed once the database issue is addressed 6. An operator who wants the old unbounded behaviour sets `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds: null` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix There is no HTTP route to exercise here, so the proof is the rendered manifest plus a live Kubernetes cluster showing the two Jobs behave differently. **1. The field renders, in both charts.** Captured at `ae3e19a83f` ``` $ helm template t helm/litellm -f helm/litellm/tests/values/required.yaml | grep -A1 ttlSecondsAfterFinished ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 120 activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800 $ helm template t helm/litellm-helm | grep -B1 -A1 activeDeadlineSeconds ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 120 backoffLimit: 4 activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800 ``` **2. A blocked migration now terminates.** Live `kind` cluster, two Jobs identical except for the new field, each running a container that starts and then blocks the way a migration waiting on an unreachable database does. The 30s deadline stands in for the 1800s default so the run is observable ``` $ kubectl apply -f before.yaml -f after.yaml job.batch/mig-no-deadline-v2 created job.batch/mig-with-deadline-v2 created $ kubectl logs job/mig-no-deadline-v2 connecting to database... $ for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do sleep 15; echo "t=$((i*15))s"; kubectl get jobs --no-headers; done t=15s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 20s mig-with-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 20s t=30s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 35s mig-with-deadline-v2 FailureTarget 0/1 35s t=60s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 65s mig-with-deadline-v2 Failed 0/1 65s t=75s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 80s mig-with-deadline-v2 Failed 0/1 80s ``` Terminal state of each: ``` $ kubectl get job mig-with-deadline-v2 -o jsonpath='{range .status.conditions[*]}type={.type} reason={.reason} message={.message}{"\n"}{end}' type=FailureTarget reason=DeadlineExceeded message=Job was active longer than specified deadline type=Failed reason=DeadlineExceeded message=Job was active longer than specified deadline $ kubectl get job mig-no-deadline-v2 -o jsonpath='conditions={.status.conditions} active={.status.active}' conditions= active=1 ``` The Job without the field never reaches a terminal state, which is what leaves a release waiting on it. The Job with the field fails on its own. **3. The tests fail without the change.** Reverting only the two templates and the two values files, keeping the new tests, at base `f03df1bb42` ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm FAIL test migrations Job ServiceAccount resolution and pod hardening - bounds the Job with a deadline by default, so a blocked migration cannot stall the release forever - honours an operator-supplied deadline Tests: 2 failed, 72 passed, 74 total ``` The third new test asserts the field is absent when nulled, which passes either way, so it was mutation-tested separately: dropping the `with` guard so the field always renders makes it fail. ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/migration_job_tests.yaml' helm/litellm FAIL - omits the deadline entirely when it is nulled out, restoring the unbounded behaviour Tests: 1 failed, 15 passed, 16 total ``` Restored, both suites are green at `ae3e19a83f` ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm Tests: 74 passed, 74 total $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm-helm Tests: 97 passed, 97 total ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The container blocking was simulated, not a genuinely wedged database connection - Default changes behaviour: migrations running past 1800s now fail - Measured healthy runs finish in about 30s, so headroom is roughly 60x - The budget is shared across all `backoffLimit` retries, not per attempt - A killed migration can leave a partially applied entry needing manual resolution - `Chart.yaml` untouched, matching recent template-only changes to litellm-helm ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(passthrough): stop forwarding client Accept-Encoding upstream
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Anthropic now defaults responses to brotli - Pass-through forwarded the client's `Accept-Encoding` upstream - Proxy could not decode brotli, so bodies stayed compressed - `Content-Encoding` was stripped, leaving unreadable JSON How it solves it: - Never forward the client's `Accept-Encoding` upstream - httpx now negotiates a coding it can actually decode - neither `x-pass-accept-encoding` nor a configured custom header can re-add it ## User Flow Before: a developer using Claude Code in auto mode against the gateway gets a JSON parse failure on the non-streaming safety classifier call 1. They point Claude Code at the gateway and run a command needing auto-mode approval 2. Claude Code sends POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages?beta=true with `Accept-Encoding: br` and no `stream` 3. The response comes back HTTP 200 with `content-type: application/json`, no `content-encoding`, and a body starting with binary bytes such as `M-0^\^@^@PUUU` 4. Claude Code fails with `SyntaxError: Failed to parse JSON` and reports "<model> is temporarily unavailable, so auto mode cannot determine the safety of Bash right now" 5. Sending the same request with `Accept-Encoding: identity` returns readable JSON, confirming compression is the cause After: the same request returns readable JSON, so auto mode works 1. They point Claude Code at the gateway and run a command needing auto-mode approval 2. Claude Code sends POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages?beta=true with `Accept-Encoding: br` and no `stream` 3. The response comes back HTTP 200 with `content-type: application/json` and a plain-text body beginning `{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5-...","content":[{"type":"text","text":"pong"}]...}` 4. Claude Code parses it and auto mode decides on the command normally ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5613 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live local proxy (`python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug`) against the real Anthropic API, with brotli/brotlicffi uninstalled so httpx has only `identity, gzip, deflate` decoders, matching the reported environment Command, identical for both runs: ```bash curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages?beta=true' \ -H 'x-litellm-api-key: sk-1234' \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept-Encoding: br' \ -D headers.txt -o body.bin \ -d '{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5","max_tokens":64,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the single word: pong"}]}' head -8 headers.txt; head -c 60 body.bin | cat -v python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('body.bin'))['content'][0]['text'])" ``` Before, at commit `f03df1bb42`: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 21:20:03 GMT server: uvicorn content-type: application/json anthropic-ratelimit-input-tokens-limit: 10000000 ... M-0^\^@^@PUUUM-}M-^_M-n|V^C0s^O;M-^D^^#n^AqM-^J8^F^D(M-^HM-^[M-1M-^[)M-8M-^ZM-(M-9 UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xb0 in position 0 ``` After, at commit `02b45552b9`: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 21:22:47 GMT server: uvicorn content-type: application/json anthropic-ratelimit-input-tokens-limit: 10000000 ... {"model":"claude-haiku-4-5-20251001","id":"msg_011Ce3Lstkkgqvj6GMbaKELu","type":"m pong ``` Unit tests and lint: ``` LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/test_vertex_passthrough_load_balancing.py tests/test_litellm/passthrough -q 33 passed in 12.37s make lint All checks passed! / 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes / every LIT rule is within its codebase ceiling ``` The live run above was repeated at `02b45552b9` after the custom-header hardening, with the same readable `{"...}` body and `pong` text Streaming was re-checked: the same request with `"stream": true` and `Accept-Encoding: br` returns clean UTF-8 SSE carrying `event: message_start` and `event: content_block_delta`. Requests with `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` and with no `Accept-Encoding` header also return parseable JSON ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Proxy-to-provider hop is now uncompressed, a bandwidth tradeoff - Clients still get uncompressed bodies, as before - Verified on the Anthropic route only, though the helper is shared Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f53970c8ec1e48f09051e0f7d86436c9 Requested by: @mateo-berri

signals.title: fix(guardrails): record MCP tool guardrail evaluations and blocks in …
signals.text: > Base branch: `litellm_internal_staging` ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Guardrails Monitor reports 0 evaluations for all MCP tool traffic - It also reports 0 blocks, so MCP guardrails look inert - Admins cannot tell a firing MCP guardrail from a broken one How it solves it: - Threads the request's logger into the MCP guardrail hooks - Bridges guardrail decision records onto that logger - Flushes failure logging before the spend-log row is written - Covers every MCP tool entry point, Responses API included ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin who put a guardrail on MCP tool calls sees the Guardrails Monitor stay empty, so the guardrail looks dead even while it is refusing calls 1. They configure a guardrail on their MCP tool traffic and restart the proxy 2. They call an MCP tool through `POST http://localhost:4000/mcp` and it succeeds 3. They call it again with input the guardrail refuses, and the tool call comes back as an error naming the guardrail, so the guardrail is provably running 4. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=guardrails and the monitor shows Total Evaluations 0 and Total Blocked 0 5. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs, click into either MCP tool call, and the row carries no guardrail detail at all 6. Having no way to tell a working MCP guardrail from a misconfigured one, they cannot report on or alert off MCP guardrail activity After: the same steps, and the monitor now counts both the allowed evaluation and the refusal 1. They configure a guardrail on their MCP tool traffic and restart the proxy 2. They call an MCP tool through `POST http://localhost:4000/mcp` and it succeeds 3. They call it again with input the guardrail refuses, and the tool call comes back as an error naming the guardrail 4. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=guardrails and the monitor shows Total Evaluations 2 and Total Blocked 1 5. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs, click into either MCP tool call, and the row shows which guardrail ran and whether it allowed or blocked 6. They can now report on and alert off MCP guardrail activity the same way they already do for chat completions ## Relevant issues Reimplements #34249 (Eugene Yao) on current `litellm_internal_staging`, written from scratch against today's staging rather than rebased, since the MCP tool-call path moved underneath it It also lands the review feedback #34249 collected. This one is based on `litellm_internal_staging` instead of `main`. It reuses the `function_setup` call the Responses API MCP path already makes rather than adding a second one. It drops the metadata aliasing, so the synthetic guardrail request's metadata bucket is left as `_convert_mcp_to_llm_format` built it and nothing else reads through an alias. And it threads the Responses API entry point, which the original left on the old behavior, so `/v1/responses` MCP tool calls are counted too ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix End to end against a real proxy on `localhost:4000` backed by a real Postgres, driven by real MCP tool calls over streamable HTTP, with the counts read back from the same endpoint the Admin UI Guardrails Monitor page calls. No mocks anywhere in this section Before commit: `2bc9bb4a9d308fd8791e8af67d2e5bd92f6d5947` (this PR's parent) After commit: `c3576be27bb052e0fb49bd15863398a2b9547605` The branch tip has since been amended to `47c00f436ba713e4b34aa16d32b3df7aa887a323`. Everything between those two commits is comment and docstring wording, two rule-named `# noqa` suppressions, one return annotation, hoisting an import from function-local to module level, and one strengthened assertion in a test. Nothing that changes what the run above measured Setup is a synthetic MCP server exposing one tool, `synthetic_echo`, plus two probe guardrails registered on `mode: "pre_mcp_call"`, one that always allows and one that always blocks. Both subclass `CustomGuardrail` and carry `@log_guardrail_information`, so the real decorator path is exercised. The one configured model points at `http://127.0.0.1:9/unused` with a placeholder key, so no provider is ever contacted, and every tool argument is synthetic What the monitor actually reads: `GET /guardrails/usage/overview` in `litellm/proxy/guardrails/usage_endpoints.py`, which sums `LiteLLM_DailyGuardrailMetrics`. Those rows are aggregated by `process_spend_logs_guardrail_usage` out of `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.metadata->'guardrail_information'`. There is no dedicated guardrail column, so that one JSON key is the thing this PR makes appear | Tree | Guardrail | Tool call result | SpendLogs `status` | `metadata->'guardrail_information'` | `totalRequests` | `totalBlocked` | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Before | allow | `echo:synthetic-probe-003`, `isError:false` | `success` | **null** | **0** | **0** | | Before | block | `Error: Guardrail violation ... synthetic-block`, `isError:true` | `failure` | **null** | **0** | **0** | | After | allow | `echo:synthetic-probe-001`, `isError:false` | `success` | present, `guardrail_status: "success"` | **1** | **0** | | After | block | `Error: Guardrail violation ... synthetic-block`, `isError:true` | `failure` | present, `guardrail_status: "guardrail_intervened"` | **1** | **1** | `LiteLLM_DailyGuardrailMetrics` held zero rows on the before tree in both cases. On the after tree: ``` guardrail_id | date | requests_evaluated | passed_count | blocked_count ------------------+------------+--------------------+--------------+--------------- synthetic-allow | 2026-08-14 | 1 | 1 | 0 synthetic-block | 2026-08-14 | 1 | 0 | 1 ``` The blocked call's spend-log row on the after tree, read straight out of Postgres: ``` status | gi ---------+----------------------------------------------------- failure | [ + | { + | "duration": 0.000014, + | "end_time": 1786737260.155436, + | "start_time": 1786737260.155423, + | "guardrail_mode": "pre_call", + | "guardrail_name": "synthetic-block", + | "guardrail_status": "guardrail_intervened",+ | "guardrail_provider": null, + | "guardrail_response": "REDACTED_BY_LITELM",+ | "masked_entity_count": null + | } + | ] success | null (2 rows) ``` One thing worth stating precisely, because it bounds the claim: the before tree already wrote a `status="failure"` spend-log row for the blocked call. What changes here is that the row carries the guardrail decision record at all, and therefore that the monitor counts it. This PR does not create that failure row Scope of what the run above measures: `pre_mcp_call`, on the streamable HTTP `/mcp` route, for an authenticated key. The `during_mcp_call` hook and the Responses API entry point are covered by the unit tests rather than by this run, and blocks on anonymous calls are the known gap described under Caveats Reproducing it, with the proxy pointed at either tree by swapping `$TREE`, and the three tables truncated between runs so counts start at zero: ```bash export PATH="/path/to/venv/bin:$PATH" # the prisma CLI must be on PATH export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/litellm' export TREE=/path/to/this/branch # or the parent commit's tree docker run -d --name mcpproof-pg -p 55432:5432 \ -e POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust -e POSTGRES_DB=litellm postgres:16 prisma migrate deploy --schema="$TREE/litellm-proxy-extras/litellm_proxy_extras/schema.prisma" python stub_mcp_server.py & # FastMCP, stateless_http, exposes synthetic_echo cd "$TREE" CONFIG_FILE_PATH=config_block.yaml python -m uvicorn litellm.proxy.proxy_server:app \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4000 --loop asyncio & until curl -sf localhost:4000/health/readiness >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done MCP=(-H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'x-mcp-servers: synthetic_stub') curl -s http://localhost:4000/mcp/ "${MCP[@]}" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"probe","version":"1"}}}' curl -s http://localhost:4000/mcp/ "${MCP[@]}" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"synthetic_stub-synthetic_echo","arguments":{"text":"synthetic-probe-001"}}}' sleep 20 # spend-log flush plus daily-metrics aggregation curl -s "http://localhost:4000/guardrails/usage/overview?start_date=$(date +%F)&end_date=$(date +%F)" \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' | python -m json.tool docker exec -i mcpproof-pg psql -U postgres -d litellm -c \ 'SELECT status, metadata->>'"'"'guardrail_information'"'"' FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs";' docker exec -i mcpproof-pg psql -U postgres -d litellm -c \ 'SELECT * FROM "LiteLLM_DailyGuardrailMetrics";' ``` Expected on the before tree: `totalRequests` 0, `totalBlocked` 0, `guardrail_information` null, `LiteLLM_DailyGuardrailMetrics` empty. On this branch: 1 and 1 for the blocking config, 1 and 0 for the allowing one. The equivalent in the UI is `http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=guardrails` going from an empty monitor to a populated one Two deviations from the standard local-proxy recipe, disclosed rather than papered over. First, `proxy_cli.py` hard-codes `uvloop` off Windows and uvloop does not import on Python 3.14 (`ImportError: cannot import name 'BaseDefaultEventLoopPolicy' from 'asyncio.events'`), so the identical ASGI app was launched through `uvicorn --loop asyncio` instead of `litellm --config ...`. Same `proxy_server:app`, same config loading, same routers, only the event loop and the CLI wrapper differ, and on Python 3.12 or older the normal command should work unchanged. Second, migrations had to be applied by hand with `prisma migrate deploy` because the proxy did not run them on startup. Both proxies also logged an unrelated `AttributeError: 'Batch' object has no attribute 'litellm_dailygatewayrequests'` from `gateway_request_tracking.py`, identically on both trees, which touches gateway request counts rather than guardrails and cannot bias the comparison ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Blocks on anonymous MCP calls are still not counted - That needs a counter outside SpendLogs, which is attributable - Only guardrail decision records are bridged onto the logger - Messages and tool arguments are deliberately not copied Anonymous MCP calls, spelled out because Greptile filed it as P1 twice on #34249 and it was declined there: a guardrail block on an unauthenticated MCP call still does not reach the monitor. The failure handlers now run for those calls, so OTel and the other failure sinks see the block, but `post_call_failure_hook` stays gated on an authenticated key. That gate is deliberate and predates this PR. The spend-log writer downstream of it dereferences authenticated key and budget data, and a SpendLogs row is an attributable billing and audit record, so an anonymous row has nothing to attribute. Counting anonymous blocks needs a counter that does not live in SpendLogs, which is a separate design change rather than something to bolt onto this fix. `test_block_flushes_failure_for_anonymous_calls` pins the current behavior so the gap is visible rather than silent On what gets recorded: only guardrail decision metadata moves onto the request logger, meaning the guardrail name, the event, the outcome and the timing. The synthetic guardrail request that MCP builds also holds the tool arguments and the LLM-shaped message list, and those are deliberately left behind. Nothing the monitor renders needs them, and copying them would push end-user payload into spend logs ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(anthropic): preserve optional Responses tool properties
signals.text: Base branch: `litellm_internal_staging` This is a from-scratch reimplementation of Eugene Yao's #34784 on top of current staging, opened while he is out of office. Same bug and same fix in spirit, but the code and tests here were rewritten against today's `litellm_internal_staging` rather than rebased ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Optional Anthropic tool arguments come back filled with empty values - OpenAI-backed `/v1/messages` silently ignored the caller's `required` list - A tool-level `strict` landed inside the JSON schema, not on the function How it solves it: - Always send `strict` on Responses function tools, `false` when unset - Map Anthropic tool `strict` onto `function.strict` for chat/completions - Stop merging `strict` into the caller's `input_schema` ## User Flow Before: a developer whose Anthropic-style app calls an OpenAI model through the gateway gets every optional tool argument back as an empty string, so their handler branches on values the user never asked for 1. They point their Anthropic SDK at the gateway and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model"` set to an OpenAI-backed deployment 2. The request carries one tool, `get_weather`, whose schema has `properties` of `city`, `unit` and `include_forecast`, and `"required": ["city"]` 3. The model answers with a `tool_use` block whose `input` contains all three keys: `city` filled in, plus `unit: ""` and `include_forecast: ""` 4. Their tool handler sees `unit` and `include_forecast` as present-but-blank, so it either fetches a forecast nobody wanted or throws on an empty enum value 5. Sending the same tool with an explicit `"strict": false` changes nothing, because the gateway never forwarded that field After: the same request comes back with only the arguments the model actually chose to fill 1. They send the identical POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the identical tool 2. The model answers with a `tool_use` block whose `input` contains `city` only 3. `unit` and `include_forecast` are absent, so the handler takes its normal defaults 4. A caller who genuinely wants strict structured-output validation sends `"strict": true` on the tool and now has it forwarded, so the provider applies strict mode to their schema ## Relevant issues Reimplements #34784 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix **Honest label first: this is a payload-level probe against a local stub provider, not a call to a real provider API.** I had no OpenAI credentials available in the environment where I prepared this, so I could not produce the real-money e2e run the template asks for. What follows instead records the exact bytes the gateway put on the wire toward the provider, captured from a proxy on localhost, before and after the fix. The copy-pasteable commands for the real-provider version are in the last block of this section, and I will post that output once someone with a key runs it Only one inbound endpoint is affected, `/v1/messages`. Both of its outbound translations are covered below, the Responses API one and the chat/completions one. Callers hitting `/v1/responses` or `/v1/chat/completions` directly are untouched by this change ### Why the default matters (the premise this fix rests on) OpenAI's migration guide, under "Update function definitions and outputs": "the Responses API defaults to strict mode if the `strict` parameter is omitted, falling back to non-strict behavior only if the schema is incompatible. To explicitly maintain non-strict behavior in the Responses API, the `strict` parameter must be set to `false`" (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses) Chat Completions goes the other way. OpenAI's own OpenAPI spec puts `default: false` on `FunctionObject.strict` and lists only `name` as required (https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi/blob/main/openapi.yaml), and the function-calling guide says "Chat Completions remain non-strict by default" Strict mode is also what forces the schema rewrite: "all fields in `properties` must be marked as required" (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling). The docs do not spell out what happens next to a schema that has optional properties and no `strict`, so that part rests on reported behavior rather than on a citation: it comes back normalized instead of as an error, which is why the symptom reaches users as placeholder-filled optional arguments rather than something anyone would notice as a failure. That was reproduced independently on a different client library in https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/11869, where the Responses API with `strict` omitted returns `""` for an optional argument while Chat Completions with `strict` omitted returns `undefined` One tension worth flagging rather than papering over: the migration guide says strict falls back to non-strict when the schema is incompatible, yet a schema with optional properties gets normalized instead of falling back. #34784 and the vercel/ai report both saw the normalization. The remedy is the same either way, and it is the one the guide prescribes, which is to send `strict` as `false` explicitly when non-strict is what you want The Responses side of the codebase already agreed with this: `litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/transformation.py:1350` has always pinned `"strict": fn.get("strict", False) or False` when it builds Responses function tools. The Anthropic adapter was the one path that left the field off ### Setup `stub_provider.py`, a stand-in provider that records the request body and returns a well-formed reply: ```python import json, os, time from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer CAPTURE = os.environ.get("CAPTURE_PATH", "/tmp/captured.jsonl") def responses_reply(model): return {"id": "resp_stub_0001", "object": "response", "created_at": int(time.time()), "status": "completed", "model": model, "parallel_tool_calls": True, "tool_choice": "auto", "tools": [], "metadata": {}, "output": [{"type": "message", "id": "msg_stub_0001", "status": "completed", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "stub reply", "annotations": []}]}], "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 3, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 14}} def chat_reply(model): return {"id": "chatcmpl-stub-0001", "object": "chat.completion", "created": int(time.time()), "model": model, "choices": [{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "stub reply"}}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 11, "completion_tokens": 3, "total_tokens": 14}} class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1" def do_POST(self): body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)) or b"{}") with open(CAPTURE, "a") as fh: fh.write(json.dumps({"path": self.path, "body": body}) + "\n") reply = chat_reply if "chat/completions" in self.path else responses_reply payload = json.dumps(reply(str(body.get("model", "gpt-4o")))).encode() self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json") self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(payload) ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8901), Handler).serve_forever() ``` `stub_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: stub-openai litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o api_base: http://127.0.0.1:8901/v1 api_key: sk-stub-not-a-real-key general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Run both: ```bash CAPTURE_PATH=/tmp/captured.jsonl python stub_provider.py & python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config stub_config.yaml --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee litellm.log ``` ### 1. `/v1/messages` over the Responses API, tool with optional properties, no `strict` from the caller ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -d '{ "model": "stub-openai", "max_tokens": 256, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Boston?"}], "tools": [{ "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "description": "Optional temperature unit"}, "include_forecast": {"type": "boolean", "description": "Optional 3-day forecast"} }, "required": ["city"] } }] }' ``` Before, at `2bc9bb4a9d`, the tool the provider received on `POST /v1/responses`: ```json [ { "type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "description": "Optional temperature unit"}, "include_forecast": {"type": "boolean", "description": "Optional 3-day forecast"} }, "required": ["city"] } } ] ``` No `strict` key on the outbound tool, which is the state that leaves the provider's strict default in play. The stub records bytes and cannot show what OpenAI would then do with them After, at `4c49d03732`, same command, same tool: ```json [ { "type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "strict": false, "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "description": "Optional temperature unit"}, "include_forecast": {"type": "boolean", "description": "Optional 3-day forecast"} }, "required": ["city"] } } ] ``` `"strict": false` is now explicit, which is what the migration guide says to send for non-strict behavior, and `required` goes out as the caller wrote it ### 2. `/v1/messages` over chat/completions, tool with `strict: true` Add `use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages: true` under `litellm_settings` in `stub_config.yaml` and restart, so the same route goes out over chat/completions instead ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -d '{ "model": "stub-openai", "max_tokens": 256, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Boston?"}], "tools": [{ "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "strict": true, "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}}, "required": ["city"], "additionalProperties": false } }] }' ``` Before, at `2bc9bb4a9d`, on `POST /v1/chat/completions`: ```json [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "get_weather", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}}, "required": ["city"], "additionalProperties": false, "strict": true }, "description": "Get the current weather in a given location" } } ] ``` `strict` ended up inside `parameters`, where it is not a JSON Schema keyword and where the provider ignores it. Worse, `parameters` is the caller's own `input_schema` object, so the merge mutated it in place After, at `4c49d03732`: ```json [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "get_weather", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}}, "required": ["city"], "additionalProperties": false }, "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "strict": true } } ] ``` ### 3. Same chat/completions route, tool with no `strict`, at `4c49d03732` ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -d '{ "model": "stub-openai", "max_tokens": 256, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "search for cats"}], "tools": [{ "name": "search", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}, "cursor": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["query"] } }] }' ``` ```json [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "search", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}, "cursor": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["query"] } } } ] ``` No `strict` anywhere, which is the deliberate asymmetry described below ### The real-provider version, for whoever has a key Same probes against a real deployment, no stub. Run these in order, once on `2bc9bb4a9d` and once on `4c49d03732` 1. Write `real_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-real litellm_params: model: openai/<any current OpenAI model that supports function calling> api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` 2. Start the proxy: ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config real_config.yaml --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee litellm.log ``` 3. Send the tool with no `strict`, forcing the call so the model has to fill the arguments: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-real", "max_tokens": 256, "tool_choice": {"type": "tool", "name": "get_weather"}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Boston?"}], "tools": [{ "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "description": "Optional temperature unit"}, "include_forecast": {"type": "boolean", "description": "Optional 3-day forecast"} }, "required": ["city"], "additionalProperties": false } }] }' ``` 4. Send the same request again with `"strict": false` added next to `"description"` on the tool 5. Send it a third time with `"strict": true` instead What to expect, stated up front so it can be checked against whatever actually comes back. On `2bc9bb4a9d` all three runs should behave identically, because neither `false` nor `true` reaches the provider, with the `tool_use` block carrying all three keys: ```json {"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_...", "name": "get_weather", "input": {"city": "Boston", "unit": "", "include_forecast": ""}} ``` On `4c49d03732` the first two runs should return only what the model chose: ```json {"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_...", "name": "get_weather", "input": {"city": "Boston"}} ``` and the third, which asked for strict mode, should get every key populated with real values, since strict mode requires every property to be present: ```json {"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_...", "name": "get_weather", "input": {"city": "Boston", "unit": "celsius", "include_forecast": false}} ``` Filler values in the strict run are the model's choice and will vary between runs. What matters is whether `unit` and `include_forecast` appear at all. Then grep `litellm.log` for the outbound function tool to confirm the request side: `"strict": false` for runs 3 and 4, `"strict": true` for run 5 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Responses always sends `strict`; chat/completions omits it when unset - That asymmetry is deliberate: each API's own default differs - Proof of fix is a local wire capture, not a paid provider call - The OpenAI to Anthropic direction still drops `function.strict` On the asymmetry, so no reviewer has to go find it: the Responses adapter now emits `strict` unconditionally, while the chat/completions adapter emits it only when the caller supplied it. Sending `strict: false` explicitly to Chat Completions would be harmless but pointless, since that is already its documented default, and it would add a key to every outbound tool for providers behind the OpenAI-compatible surface that may not accept it. Responses needs the explicit value precisely because its default is the opposite ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(vertex_ai): convert messages to contents in gemini count_tokens
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `litellm.acount_tokens()` returns `total_tokens=0` with `error=False` for any `vertex_ai/gemini-*` model when called with `messages` - The Gemini branch of `VertexAITokenCounter.count_tokens` never converts `messages` to Gemini `contents`, so the request body is `{"contents": null}` - Vertex accepts that with HTTP 200 and no `totalTokens` field, and the old code read `result.get("totalTokens", 0)` as a valid zero How it solves it: - Converts `messages` to Gemini `contents` via the existing `_gemini_convert_messages_with_history` helper when `contents` is `None` - Treats a response without `totalTokens` as a failure (returns `None`) so the caller falls back to local token counting ## User Flow Before: a developer calling `acount_tokens` with `messages` on a Vertex Gemini model gets a silent zero, so their pre-flight context-window guard always passes and overflows surface later as a provider 400 1. They call `await litellm.acount_tokens(model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])` 2. The SDK returns `TokenCountResponse(total_tokens=0, tokenizer_type="", error=False)` 3. Their guard checks `total_tokens < max_tokens`, passes, and sends the real request 4. Vertex rejects the real request with a 400 because the context window is actually exceeded After: the same call returns the real token count from Vertex, or falls back to local counting 1. They call `await litellm.acount_tokens(model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])` 2. The SDK converts `messages` to Gemini `contents` format and sends `{"contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "Hello"}]}]}` to Vertex 3. Vertex returns `{"totalTokens": 3}` and the SDK returns `TokenCountResponse(total_tokens=3, tokenizer_type="gemini")` 4. Their guard correctly compares the real count against the context window ## Relevant issues Fixes #36921 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Will add curl-based proof against a live Vertex AI endpoint shortly. Unit tests verify the message-to-contents conversion and the no-totalTokens failure path: ``` python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py -k "count_tokens or token_counter" -v tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_converts_messages_to_contents_for_gemini PASSED tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_returns_none_when_api_omits_total_tokens PASSED tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_routes_gemini_models PASSED tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_routes_partner_models PASSED tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_uses_count_tokens_location PASSED 5 passed ``` ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `system` and `tools` parameters are still dropped on the Vertex Gemini count_tokens path. The issue mentions this as lower priority. Follow-up PR can address it - The local tiktoken fallback has no Gemini tokenizer, so the fallback is approximate for Gemini. Also noted in the issue as lower priority ## QA runbook
