signals.title: Revert "fix(auth): stop the team fallback from widening model access" (#36837)
signals.text: ## TLDR Reverts #36837 (`ab2333b6c4`), which locks every user out of the Admin UI. - The UI's session key is issued against a team that intentionally has no row - #36837 reads exactly that state as a hard refusal, so every dashboard request 404s ## Root cause Every Admin UI login mints its session key against the sentinel team id `litellm-dashboard` — both the password/SSO path (`litellm/proxy/auth/login_utils.py`, `"team_id": "litellm-dashboard"`) and the `EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN` JWT path (`ExperimentalUIJWTToken`). No `LiteLLM_TeamTable` row is ever created for it; it is a sentinel, and other call sites already special-case it as "not a real team" (`UI_TEAM_ID` in the MCP and agent permission handlers). So on every UI request the team lookup asks the database for `litellm-dashboard`, the database answers, and the row is not there. That is the exact state #36837 reclassified: `_get_team_object_from_user_api_key_cache` raises the new `TeamNotFoundError`, and `_token_can_vouch_for_team` refuses it outright, with no setting able to override it. The session key also carries `models=[]` and no team grant, so even the second branch would not have vouched. The result is a 404 on every Admin-UI-authenticated request. ## Proof Both legs drive the real `get_team_object` with a prisma stub whose `find_unique` returns `None` — the actual absent-row state — and feed whatever that lookup really raises into the real `_run_centralized_common_checks`, with the token shape the UI login mints. Nothing is hand-constructed or injected. ### Before, at `29fe342ead` (staging, with #36837) ``` real lookup for team='litellm-dashboard' raised: TeamNotFoundError (status 404) UI request /v1/models -> HTTP 404 Team doesn't exist in db. Team=litellm-dashboard. UI request /user/info -> HTTP 404 Team doesn't exist in db. Team=litellm-dashboard. UI request /key/list -> HTTP 404 Team doesn't exist in db. Team=litellm-dashboard. UI request /team/list -> HTTP 404 Team doesn't exist in db. Team=litellm-dashboard. UI request /model/info -> HTTP 404 Team doesn't exist in db. Team=litellm-dashboard. ``` ### After, with this revert ``` real lookup for team='litellm-dashboard' raised: HTTPException (status 404) UI request /v1/models -> SERVED UI request /user/info -> SERVED UI request /key/list -> SERVED UI request /team/list -> SERVED UI request /model/info -> SERVED ``` The lookup still fails in both legs — the difference is only whether the token-derived fallback is allowed to stand in for the sentinel team. ## Tests Every test file #36837 touched, on this revert: ``` tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_auth_checks.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_user_api_key_auth.py 361 passed tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_user_api_key_auth.py 78 passed ``` The revert is the exact inverse of `ab2333b6c4` (308 deletions, 1 insertion against its 308/1). One conflict had to be resolved by hand: a later commit added `delete_cache_key_objects` immediately below where `TeamNotFoundError` was inserted. That function is unrelated and is kept. ## What this reopens, stated plainly #36837 closed a real hole: a key whose team is deleted keeps working and reaches models the team never allowed, because `team_models=[]` on the token reads as "every model". This revert reopens that. It is the right trade right now because the dashboard is down for everyone, but it should not be left open. The re-land needs the UI sentinel exempted before the refusal is reinstated — `team_id == UI_TEAM_ID` must never reach the absent-team refusal, since it is absent by design rather than deleted. Worth checking the same question for any other synthetic team id in the auth path. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The model-access widening #36837 closed is open again until a corrected re-land - Verified against the auth path with a stubbed database, not a live proxy

signals.title: fix(guardrails): restore SSRF protection in custom code HTTP primitives
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Restores security controls that were introduced by #25004 and lost during the custom-code sandbox migration (Starlark -> RestrictedPython): the `_validate_url_for_ssrf()` blocklist and `follow_redirects=False` are absent from `main`, so the sandboxed HTTP primitives can reach loopback, RFC1918, and cloud-metadata endpoints again, and every HTTP method follows redirects. Found during a source security review of v1.96.2. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🐞 Bug fix (security regression) ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/custom_code/primitives.py` - `http_request()` now validates the URL through the canonical `litellm_core_utils.url_utils.validate_url()` before connecting: - blocks loopback, private, link-local, reserved, multicast, and cloud-metadata targets (default-deny via `ip.is_global`), which also covers `169.254.169.254` / `metadata.google.internal` / `fd00:ec2::254` - resolve-and-rewrite for plain `http` removes the DNS-rebinding/TOCTOU gap the old `_validate_url_for_ssrf` had; for `https` the TLS hostname binding keeps the connection pinned - the original hostname is restored via the `Host` header so vhost routing still works - `_execute_http_request()` passes `follow_redirects=False` on GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH so a 3xx response cannot bypass validation - operators keep two documented escape hatches (same as the rest of the codebase): `user_url_allowed_hosts` in `general_settings` for legitimate internal moderation services, and `litellm.user_url_validation = False` to disable the check entirely - reuses the existing validator instead of restoring the hand-rolled copy, so guardrail primitives and the other user-controlled fetch surfaces (RAG ingestion, OpenAPI-to-MCP spec fetch) share one SSRF policy ## Working proof Local loopback HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:8971` recording request paths, driven through the real primitives (both directly and from inside a RestrictedPython-compiled guardrail calling `http_get`): Before (v1.96.2 from PyPI): ``` check1 direct loopback: 200 {'path': '/direct-loopback'} check2 redirect followed: 200 {'path': '/landing'} | hits: ['/direct-loopback', '/hop', '/landing'] check3 sandbox end-to-end: {'action': 'block', 'reason': "reached {'path': '/sandbox-exfil?d=secret'}"} VERDICT: loopback reached = True | redirect followed = True | sandbox exfil path hit = True ``` After (this branch): ``` primitives.py:473 - Custom code http_request SSRF blocked: URL targets a blocked address (127.0.0.1). If this is a legitimate internal service, add the host to `user_url_allowed_hosts` in general_settings. check1 direct loopback: 0 None check2 redirect followed: 0 None | hits: [] check3 sandbox end-to-end: {'action': 'allow'} VERDICT: loopback reached = False | redirect followed = False | sandbox exfil path hit = False ``` The requests are refused before any connection is made, so the redirecting `/hop` endpoint is never reached and the sandboxed exfiltration payload has no network channel. ## Tests ``` $ python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/test_custom_code_security.py -q 31 passed, 1 warning in 3.89s ``` Added to the existing mapped test file (`tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/test_custom_code_security.py`): - `test_http_primitives_block_internal_targets` - loopback (IPv4 + IPv6), `localhost`, RFC1918, and `169.254.169.254` are refused with a `Blocked` error and the HTTP client is never invoked - `test_http_primitives_allow_public_url` - a public URL passes; asserts the resolve-and-rewrite connection URL, the restored `Host` header, preserved caller headers, and `follow_redirects=False` - `test_http_primitives_honor_allowlisted_internal_host` - `user_url_allowed_hosts` unblocks an internal host - `test_http_primitives_validation_can_be_disabled` - `litellm.user_url_validation = False` restores the old behavior - `test_http_primitives_do_not_follow_redirects` - a 302 is returned as-is (not followed) for POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH All tests are hermetic: DNS is monkeypatched to a global IP and the httpx client is faked; no real network calls.

signals.title: fix(ui): match the MCP servers count badge to its sibling permission badges
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - MCP Servers count badge rendered solid black, siblings rendered grey - The black pill read as an alert at a count of 0 How it solves it: - Count badges now use the neutral variant in all three sections - Red is reserved for the blocked state, the only real alert ## User Flow Before: an admin reviewing a key's object permissions sees one of three counts singled out for no reason 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click a key to open its info page 2. On the Overview tab they scroll to the Object Permissions card 3. Vector Stores and Agents show their counts in light grey pills, but MCP Servers shows its count in a solid black pill 4. The black pill reads as an alert or a selected state even when the count is 0 and nothing is configured, so they look for an MCP problem that does not exist After: all three counts read the same, and emphasis means something 1. signals.title: fix(router): stop get_router_model_info from wiping cached pricing
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/model/info` silently drops built-in pricing after traffic - Each worker loses prices for models it served - Deployment pricing defaults overwrite the shared cost cache How it solves it: - Merge deployment `model_info` into a copy, not the cached dict - Drop unset (`None`) deployment values before merging - Regression tests pin both, and fail without the fix ## User Flow Before: an admin who opens the models page after the proxy has served traffic sees pricing vanish for exactly the models people used, and repeated reads disagree with each other 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/model/info with their key and read real `input_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_token` and `cache_read_input_token_cost` values for every model 2. Someone sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets a normal 200 back 3. They send the same GET https://litellm-domain/model/info again and those three pricing fields are now missing from the model they just used 4. With more than one worker, refreshing https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models flips between prices shown and prices missing, depending on which worker answers, and restarting the pods only hides it until traffic returns After: the models page keeps reporting the same prices no matter how much traffic has gone through, or which worker answers 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/model/info with their key and read the same three pricing fields 2. Someone sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets a normal 200 back 3. They send the same GET https://litellm-domain/model/info again and the pricing fields are unchanged 4. Refreshing https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models gives one consistent answer across workers and pods ## Relevant issues Fixes #36980 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, real Anthropic calls (real $), one worker, no mocks. Config was a single `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` deployment with no pricing overrides Before, at `870a8cf764` (tip of `litellm_internal_staging`): ```bash curl -sS http://localhost:4000/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq -c '.data[] | {model_name, i: .model_info.input_cost_per_token, o: .model_info.output_cost_per_token, c: .model_info.cache_read_input_token_cost}' curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"sonnet","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with OK"}],"max_tokens":5}' | jq -c '{ok:(.choices|length>0)}' curl -sS http://localhost:4000/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq -c '.data[] | {model_name, i: .model_info.input_cost_per_token, o: .model_info.output_cost_per_token, c: .model_info.cache_read_input_token_cost}' ``` ```text {"model_name":"sonnet","i":3e-06,"o":1.5e-05,"c":3e-07} {"ok":true} {"model_name":"sonnet","i":null,"o":null,"c":null} ``` After, at `48de8106ef` (this branch), same three commands: ```text {"model_name":"sonnet","i":3e-06,"o":1.5e-05,"c":3e-07} {"ok":true} {"model_name":"sonnet","i":3e-06,"o":1.5e-05,"c":3e-07} ``` Cost tracking itself was never affected, `x-litellm-response-cost: 9e-05` on the same requests either way, since spend calculation reads a separate cache entry ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Explicit `null` in a deployment's `model_info` no longer clears a built-in price Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cabdacbe36e341778558bfaf83fd5507

signals.title: fix(ui): default user metadata to empty JSON object on create
signals.text: ## Summary Creating a new user through the LiteLLM Admin UI fails with the following error when the **Metadata** field is left empty: ```json {"detail":[{"type":"dict_type","loc":["body","metadata"],"msg":"Input should be a valid dictionary","input":""}]} ``` ### Root cause The "Create User" / "Invite User" form (`CreateUserButton.tsx`) renders the metadata `Input.TextArea` with no default value, so submitting with an untouched field sends `metadata: ""` (an empty string). `POST /user/new` expects a dict, so it rejects the empty string with the `dict_type` error above. Typing `{}` manually works, which matches the reported behavior. ### Change Default the metadata field to `"{}"` via `initialValues` in both the embedded and standalone create-user forms, so an untouched field submits a valid empty dict instead of `""`. This is the two-line diff below — no other files change. --- This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of @juanmichelini.

signals.title: feat(proxy): auto-suppress the no-Redis banner for confirmed single-worker deployments
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Single-worker proxies still get the "No Redis configured" banner - Hiding it today needs an env var plus a full restart How it solves it: - Each worker upserts a heartbeat row into the database every 60s - Readiness counts live workers and hides the banner at exactly 1 - Two or more live workers, or an unknown count, still warn - Multi-pod and multi-worker are caught by the same census - LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING override behaves exactly as before ## User Flow Before: an admin running a single-worker proxy with no Redis sees a warning banner they can only hide with an env var and a restart 1. The admin starts the proxy with one worker, a Postgres database, and no Redis configured 2. They open http://localhost:4000/ui and the dashboard's call to GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness/details comes back with `"show_no_redis_warning": true` 3. A red banner reads "No Redis configured. Redis is highly recommended" even though a single worker has nothing to share over Redis 4. The only way to hide it is to set `LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING=true` and restart the whole deployment After: the same single-worker deployment shows no banner at all, and the banner still comes back on its own the moment a second worker appears 1. The admin starts the proxy with one worker, a Postgres database, and no Redis configured 2. They open http://localhost:4000/ui and GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness/details now returns `"show_no_redis_warning": false`, so no banner renders 3. They later scale to two workers, or a second pod sharing the same database, and within a couple of minutes a refresh shows the banner again, since limits and budgets now really are split across workers 4. They scale back down to one worker and the banner disappears again, with no env var and no restart ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All legs ran against a live proxy (`litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py`) on a fresh Postgres DB with no Redis, master key `sk-qa-1234`, and this config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY ``` The check in every leg is: ```bash curl -s localhost:$PORT/health/readiness/details -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-1234" ``` Before, captured at staging tip 870a8cf764, one worker, no Redis: the banner flag is stuck on ```json {"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": true} ``` After, all legs captured at 3217b8edae. Leg A1, one worker, no Redis: the flag turns off by itself ```json {"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": false} ``` Real completion through that same proxy to prove it still serves traffic (real OpenAI call, real $): ```bash curl -s localhost:41799/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say OK"}]}' # -> "OK!" from model gpt-4o-mini ``` Leg A2, a second replica process booted on another port against the same DATABASE_URL (simulating 2 pods): both replicas flip to warning ```json replica A: {"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": true} replica B: {"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": true} ``` Leg A3, replica B stopped with SIGTERM: replica A goes quiet again immediately thanks to shutdown deregistration, and exactly 1 heartbeat row remains ```json {"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": false} ``` Leg A4, one process started with `--num_workers 2`: warns, and 2 heartbeat rows exist ```json {"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": true} ``` Leg A5, `--num_workers 2` plus `LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING=true`: the existing escape hatch still wins ```json {"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": false} ``` UI verification steps (screenshots to be attached): 1. Start the proxy with one worker, a Postgres DATABASE_URL, no Redis, then run `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard` 2. Open http://localhost:3000/ui and confirm no red Redis banner appears anywhere on the dashboard 3. Restart the proxy with `--num_workers 2`, wait a minute, refresh, and confirm the banner appears with the new "more than one worker" wording 4. Set `LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING=true`, restart, refresh, and confirm the banner is gone again ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Suppression requires a connected database; DB-less proxies keep warning - A non-graceful scale-down converges within the 3-minute liveness window - Counting is fail-safe: any census error keeps the banner on ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(scripts): queue heavy gates behind a machine-wide slot lock
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - N parallel `make check` runs across worktrees thrash one machine - Every run slows down and long commands start timing out flaky How it solves it: - New `scripts/gate_slot_lock.py`: machine-wide fcntl slot lock, 2 slots - `make check`/`bootstrap`/`lint` and the budget gates queue through it - Nested invocations reenter via an env marker, so no deadlocks - `LITELLM_GATE_SLOTS` overrides the count; `0` disables; errors fail open ## User Flow Before: a developer running several agent sessions has three worktrees run `make check` at once, and the machine becomes unusable 1. Three sessions each run `make check` in their own litellm worktree at the same time 2. Three basedpyright/prettier/pytest storms execute simultaneously, CPU and RAM peg, and every run crawls 3. Unrelated commands on the machine slow down or time out while all three grind on After: the same three runs queue two at a time and all pass 1. Three sessions each run `make check` in their own litellm worktree at the same time 2. Two runs proceed immediately; the third prints `gate_slot_lock: all 2 machine-wide slots are busy; queueing (set LITELLM_GATE_SLOTS=0 to disable)` and waits 3. As soon as one of the first two finishes, the queued run starts on its own and ends in `check: PASS` like the others 4. A developer who wants the old behavior sets `LITELLM_GATE_SLOTS=0` (or another slot count) and the lock steps aside ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Three concurrent `make check` runs in one worktree at eafddaaa12: runs 1 and 2 hold the two slots, run 3 prints the queueing notice and starts as soon as a slot frees, and all three pass ``` $ for i in 1 2 3; do bash -c "echo \"run $i launched \$(date +%T)\"; make check > /tmp/slotdemo_$i.log 2>&1; echo \"run $i exit=\$? finished \$(date +%T)\"" & done; wait run 1 launched 17:23:23 run 2 launched 17:23:23 run 3 launched 17:23:23 run 2 exit=0 finished 17:23:25 run 1 exit=0 finished 17:23:25 run 3 exit=0 finished 17:23:27 $ grep -l queueing /tmp/slotdemo_*.log && grep -h queueing /tmp/slotdemo_3.log /tmp/slotdemo_3.log gate_slot_lock: all 2 machine-wide slots are busy; queueing (set LITELLM_GATE_SLOTS=0 to disable) $ for i in 1 2 3; do echo "run $i verdict: $(grep -o 'check: PASS' /tmp/slotdemo_$i.log | head -1)"; done run 1 verdict: check: PASS run 2 verdict: check: PASS run 3 verdict: check: PASS ``` The header-documented hook install keeps working (a first draft of this change broke it; a regression test now pins it). In a fresh clone of eafddaaa12: ``` $ ln -s ../../scripts/pre_commit_lint.sh .git/hooks/pre-commit $ echo demo > demo.txt && git add demo.txt && git commit -m "chore: demo commit through the hook" check: full log: .../.git/pre_commit_lint.log [litellm_make_check_slot_lock 8d84ba99ae] chore: demo commit through the hook 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+) commit exit=0 ``` `make check` with everything staged at eafddaaa12 exits 0 with `check: PASS`, and that run itself exercises the nested chain (`make check` -> wrapper -> `check-inner` -> `bootstrap` -> `pre_commit_lint.sh` -> `make lint` -> budget gates) acquiring exactly one slot ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats (if any) - `make -jN check` sub-make may warn "jobserver unavailable"; inner targets are serial anyway - Queueing is roughly FIFO; a fresh arrival can occasionally beat a waiter to a freed slot - CI takes the instant-acquire path (one job per machine) and any lock error fails open ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(ui): direction picker and reverse-mode display for shadow evals
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - #36865 added reverse shadow evals, but only over the raw API - The dashboard form pins direction to forward with no controls - Reverse jobs would render with forward labels, inverting every win rate How it solves it: - Start form gains a direction picker and a baseline model picker - Baseline is required in reverse mode and never sent in forward - Job cards, verdict bar, and slice tables label arms per direction ## User Flow Before: an operator whose key already runs on an auto-router wants to check the router still beats a strong fixed model, and the dashboard offers no way to ask 1. They open http://localhost:3000/cost-optimization and click the Shadow evals tab 2. The "Start a shadow eval" form shows key, auto-router, sampling, duration, turn budget, and judge fields only; every eval it can start asks the adoption question 3. To run a regression check they must hand-craft a POST to http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start with `"direction": "reverse"` and `"baseline_model": "..."` 4. signals.title: feat(proxy): gate the Global Control Plane worker registry on an enterprise license
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Global Control Plane is sold as Enterprise but had no license check - Any OSS install could run one for free - Its two config keys were undeclared, so they were undiscoverable How it solves it: - Check the license when the worker registry is loaded - Fail startup loudly instead of dropping the registry silently - Declare both keys so they reach the generated config schema ## User Flow Before: an admin with no Enterprise license stands up a control plane and it just works, so the Enterprise requirement is unenforced 1. They write a config with a `worker_registry` listing two proxies, and no `LITELLM_LICENSE` in the environment 2. They start the proxy on port 4633, and it boots normally with no warning 3. They open `http://localhost:4633/.well-known/litellm-ui-config` and get `"is_control_plane": true` with both workers listed 4. They open the admin UI and get the worker selector on the login page, managing both proxies from one place, without a license After: the same admin is told at startup that this needs a license, and a licensed admin is unaffected 1. They write the same config with the same `worker_registry`, still with no `LITELLM_LICENSE` 2. They start the proxy, and it refuses to boot: `Trying to use worker_registry` followed by `You must be a LiteLLM Enterprise user to use this feature`, then `Application startup failed. Exiting.` 3. They set a valid `LITELLM_LICENSE` and start again, and the proxy boots normally 4. `http://localhost:4633/.well-known/litellm-ui-config` returns `"is_control_plane": true` with both workers, byte for byte what it returned before this change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5633 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Three legs against a live proxy on port 4633, same config file throughout, differing only in code revision and whether a license is present. Config used in all three legs: ```yaml model_list: [] general_settings: master_key: sk-5633 worker_registry: - worker_id: "worker-a" name: "Worker A" url: "http://localhost:4634" - worker_id: "worker-b" name: "Worker B" url: "http://localhost:4635" ``` ### Before, unlicensed, at `40a418440c` (base) The control plane comes up and serves the full worker registry with no license present, which is the gap this PR closes. ```bash LITELLM_LICENSE="" python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config cp_config_5633.yaml --port 4633 curl -s http://localhost:4633/.well-known/litellm-ui-config ``` ```json {"server_root_path":"","proxy_base_url":null,"auto_redirect_to_sso":false,"admin_ui_disabled":false,"sso_configured":false,"hide_default_credentials_hint":false,"is_control_plane":true,"workers":[{"worker_id":"worker-a","name":"Worker A","url":"http://localhost:4634"},{"worker_id":"worker-b","name":"Worker B","url":"http://localhost:4635"}]} ``` ### After, unlicensed, at `f622c85c9c` Same command, same config. Startup now refuses. ```bash LITELLM_LICENSE="" python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config cp_config_5633.yaml --port 4633 ``` ``` raise ValueError("Trying to use `worker_registry`" + CommonProxyErrors.not_premium_user.value) ValueError: Trying to use `worker_registry`You must be a LiteLLM Enterprise user to use this feature. If you have a license please set `LITELLM_LICENSE` in your env. Get a 7 day trial key here: https://www.litellm.ai/enterprise#trial. ERROR: Application startup failed. Exiting. ``` ### After, licensed, at `f622c85c9c` Same command with a real `LITELLM_LICENSE` set. The proxy boots and the response is identical to the before leg, so licensed deployments see no change. ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4633/.well-known/litellm-ui-config ``` ```json {"server_root_path":"","proxy_base_url":null,"auto_redirect_to_sso":false,"admin_ui_disabled":false,"sso_configured":false,"hide_default_credentials_hint":false,"is_control_plane":true,"workers":[{"worker_id":"worker-a","name":"Worker A","url":"http://localhost:4634"},{"worker_id":"worker-b","name":"Worker B","url":"http://localhost:4635"}]} ``` ### Mutation check on the new tests Each mutant applied on its own and reverted from a scratchpad copy, so the runs are independent. ``` mutant 1, gate deleted entirely -> 1 failed, 11 passed (worker_registry_requires_premium) mutant 2, `premium_user is not True` flipped to `premium_user is True` -> 2 failed, 10 passed (requires_premium and loads_for_premium) restored -> 12 passed ``` ## Review notes Greptile raised two findings on `f622c85c`, one accepted and one declined. **Accepted: a test comment violating the repo comment policy.** Removed. The test is renamed to `..._premium_invalid_worker_registry_raises`, so the name carries what the comment was explaining and nothing is lost. The mutation check was re-run after the rename, since a rename is exactly the kind of change that can silently turn an assertion vacuous, and the mutant still dies. **Declined: adding a user-controlled transition flag to soften the startup failure.** This is a licensing gate, so a flag that lets an unlicensed proxy load `worker_registry` anyway would remove the entitlement it exists to enforce. There is also no precedent for one: `litellm/proxy/` has 35 call sites using `CommonProxyErrors.not_premium_user`, and a grep for any bypass or transition mechanism across them returns nothing. Every one raises unconditionally, including the `enforced_params` gate 200 lines above this change in the same function. Adding a flag here would make this the only gate of 36 with an escape hatch. The breaking change is real and is called out under Caveats. The right mitigation is a release note naming `worker_registry`, not a bypass. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Breaking for unlicensed installs already running a worker registry - Needs a release note naming `worker_registry` - Companion litellm-docs PR renames this feature and drops its beta label - Worker selector flow still has no e2e coverage ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: test(ui): await handleSearch completion in SearchToolTester tests
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - UI Unit Tests failed on staging with a phantom "ReferenceError: window is not defined" though all 29 SearchToolTester tests passed - The failing commit was a Fireworks Python change with zero UI diff, so this was a pre-existing flake, not a bug in the commit How it solves it: - Waits for `handleSearch` to fully settle in the four tests that fired a click without observing the async result - Keeps `setIsLoading(false)` in the component's `finally` block from firing after the test file's JSDOM teardown ## User Flow Not user-facing; touches a single unit-test file for `SearchToolTester`. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Stack trace from the failing job on staging (commit 40a41844): ``` ReferenceError: window is not defined ❯ getCurrentEventPriority node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:10993:22 ❯ requestUpdateLane node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:25495:19 ❯ dispatchSetState node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:16648:14 ❯ handleSearch src/app/(dashboard)/search-tools/_components/SearchToolTester.tsx:66:7 This error originated in "src/app/(dashboard)/search-tools/_components/SearchToolTester.test.tsx" test file. This error was caught after test environment was torn down. ``` Line 66 is `setIsLoading(false)` in the `finally` block of `handleSearch`. Four tests fired the search click but did not await the async operation, so the finally's setState raced with JSDOM teardown when the file's environment closed. Before, running the isolated file passes (29/29) but under the full parallel suite the leaked setState occasionally lands after teardown and fails the whole job. After the fix, each affected test awaits the button/input being re-enabled (or the "Searching..." text disappearing) so the finally block runs before teardown. Local run after the fix: ``` $ npx vitest run src/app/\(dashboard\)/search-tools/_components/SearchToolTester.test.tsx ✓ src/app/(dashboard)/search-tools/_components/SearchToolTester.test.tsx (29 tests) 1988ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 29 passed (29) ``` ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Same class of flake has hit other files before (e.g. TeamSSOSettings.test.tsx a couple days ago); a broader test-infrastructure fix may be worthwhile as a follow-up ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(proxy): allow custom budget exceeded messages
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Budget errors expose exact spend and limits - Every client must replace the message independently How it solves it: - Adds a configurable client-facing budget error message - Preserves detailed values for logs and callbacks - Applies consistently across proxy budget enforcement paths ## User Flow Before: a developer receives internal financial limits when their assigned budget is exhausted 1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with their virtual key and chat messages 2. Below budget, they receive HTTP 200 with a `chatcmpl-...` ID and an answer 3. Once exhausted, the same request returns HTTP 429 with exact current spend and maximum budget 4. Their application must detect `error.type: budget_exceeded` and replace the message After: the same developer receives the administrator-defined message from every compatible client 1. The proxy admin sets `budget_exceeded_error_message` under `litellm_settings` 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with the same virtual key and chat messages 3. Below budget, they receive the same HTTP 200 response 4. Once exhausted, the request returns HTTP 429 with the configured message and `error.type: budget_exceeded` ## Relevant issues Fixes #36729 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? signals.title: feat(vector_stores): add Valkey as a managed vector store provider
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No vector store provider for Valkey / valkey-search - Managed vector store pipeline assumed every provider speaks HTTP How it solves it: - New valkey provider embeds the query and runs a KNN FT.SEARCH - BaseDirectVectorStoreConfig lets RESP datastores bypass the HTTP pipeline - Admin UI Add Vector Store modal gains a Valkey provider - Also registrable via vector_store_registry in the proxy config ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin whose document embeddings already live in Valkey cannot search them through the gateway 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=vector-stores and click Add Vector Store: the provider dropdown offers Bedrock, S3 Vectors, pgvector, Vertex AI, OpenAI, Azure, and Milvus, but no Valkey 2. There is no provider value they can pass to POST http://localhost:4000/vector_store/new that would make POST http://localhost:4000/v1/vector_stores/{id}/search read from their Valkey index, so their documents stay unreachable After: the same admin registers the Valkey index and searches it from the API, the UI, and the config 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=vector-stores and click Add Vector Store: the dropdown now shows Valkey with its logo, and selecting it reveals host, port, password, TLS, embedding model, text field, and vector field inputs plus a setup note explaining the FT index prerequisite 2. They enter their Valkey host and port, the FT index name as the Vector Store ID, and an embedding model, click Create, and see the store listed with provider Valkey 3. On the Test Vector Store tab they type a question and get their own documents back ranked by score 4. The same store answers POST http://localhost:4000/v1/vector_stores/{id}/search with an OpenAI-shaped results page, and an identical entry declared under vector_store_registry in the proxy config works without touching the UI or the management API ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4842 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All proofs captured at 10a95d0dd3 against a live proxy on localhost:4842, with real Vertex AI embedding calls (vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001) costing real money. The datastore is a valkey/valkey-bundle container (valkey-search module loaded) on localhost:6390, holding an FT index named litellm-qa-docs over 6 HASH docs whose embedding field was seeded with the same model API path: create the store, search it twice, delete it ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/vector_store/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"vector_store_id": "litellm-qa-docs", "custom_llm_provider": "valkey", "vector_store_name": "Valkey QA Docs", "litellm_params": {"valkey_host": "localhost", "valkey_port": 6390, "litellm_embedding_model": "vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001"}}' {"status":"success","message":"Vector store litellm-qa-docs created successfully","vector_store":{"vector_store_id":"litellm-qa-docs","custom_llm_provider":"valkey","vector_store_name":"Valkey QA Docs",...,"litellm_params":{"valkey_host":"localhost","valkey_port":6390,...,"litellm_embedding_model":"vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001",...},"team_id":null,"user_id":"default_user_id"}} $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query": "how do I pull a great espresso shot?", "max_num_results": 3}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"how do I pull a great espresso shot?","data":[{"score":0.787654995918,"content":[{"text":"To brew great espresso, use freshly roasted beans ground fine, 18 grams in, 36 grams out in about 28 seconds at 93 degrees Celsius.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:espresso","filename":"kb:espresso"},{"score":0.53844845295,"content":[{"text":"Laminated croissant dough requires folding cold butter into the detrempe over several turns to build flaky layers.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:croissant","filename":"kb:croissant"},{"score":0.451147139072,"content":[{"text":"Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun; its thin carbon dioxide atmosphere and iron oxide dust give it a reddish appearance.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:mars","filename":"kb:mars"}]} $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query": "open source fork of Redis", "max_num_results": 2}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"open source fork of Redis","data":[{"score":0.755149245262,"content":[{"text":"Valkey is an open source high-performance key-value datastore, forked from Redis and stewarded by the Linux Foundation.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:valkey","filename":"kb:valkey"},{"score":0.543505072594,"content":[{"text":"Python asyncio provides an event loop for cooperative multitasking, with coroutines scheduled via async and await syntax.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:asyncio","filename":"kb:asyncio"}]} $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/vector_store/delete -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"vector_store_id": "litellm-qa-docs"}' {"status":"success","message":"Vector store litellm-qa-docs deleted successfully"} ``` Config path: the same store declared in the proxy config instead of the management API (run at the identical tree, before the temporary config edit was reverted) ``` vector_store_registry: - vector_store_name: valkey-config-kb litellm_params: vector_store_id: litellm-qa-docs custom_llm_provider: valkey valkey_host: localhost valkey_port: "6390" litellm_embedding_model: vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001 ``` ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query": "planet with a red surface", "max_num_results": 2}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"planet with a red surface","data":[{"score":0.7229921817780001,"content":[{"text":"Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun; its thin carbon dioxide atmosphere and iron oxide dust give it a reddish appearance.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:mars","filename":"kb:mars"},{"score":0.44688546657600003,"content":[{"text":"Python asyncio provides an event loop for cooperative multitasking, with coroutines scheduled via async and await syntax.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:asyncio","filename":"kb:asyncio"}]} ``` UI path, verified end to end on the built dashboard (screenshots to be posted below): 1. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=vector-stores and go to Manage Vector Stores, then click + Add Vector Store 2. Pick Valkey in the provider dropdown (renders with the Valkey logo) and note the setup alert plus the seven provider fields appearing 3. Fill Vector Store ID with the FT index name, Valkey Host, Valkey Port, and Embedding Model, then click Create and see the success toast and the new row with provider Valkey 4. Open the Test Vector Store tab, select the store, submit a query like "how do I make croissants flaky?", and see the matching doc as Result 1 with the highest score ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Search only: file ingestion is not supported, valkey is excluded from the RAG upload dropdown - Docs page is written but must land in the separate docs repo - provider_endpoints_support.json docs link 404s until that docs page lands - Requires the valkey-search module and a pre-created FT index over HASH docs ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): normalize tuple-form JSON Schema items before the Vertex transform
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Tuple-form `items` crashes every `vertex_ai/*` request carrying that tool - Error surfaces as `APIConnectionError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` - OpenAI-compatible clients and several MCP servers emit that shape How it solves it: - Rewrite `"items": [A, B]` as `"items": {"anyOf": [A, B]}` once, before the walkers - Runs after `unpack_defs`, so `$ref`-expanded schemas are covered too - `items: []` drops out and `process_items` synthesizes `{"type": "object"}` ## User Flow Before: a developer whose tool schema declares a fixed-shape array gets a connection error from the gateway on every call, while the same tool works against other providers 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash"` and a tool whose parameters contain `"a": {"type": "array", "items": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "string"}]}` 2. The gateway answers with `litellm.APIConnectionError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`, and no request ever reaches the model 3. They retry the identical body against an OpenAI-compatible provider and get a normal completion, so the tool schema itself is fine 4. Their only way forward is a pre-call shim that rewrites the tool schema before the gateway sees it After: the same request is accepted and the tool reaches the model 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same tuple-form tool 2. The gateway forwards the tool to Vertex with that field typed as an array whose entries may be an integer or a string 3. They get a normal completion back, with a tool call if the model chooses to make one 4. The shim can come out of their stack The array position that carried a fixed order is now an unordered union, which is the closest shape Vertex can express ## Relevant issues Fixes #36848 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I do not have Vertex credentials, so there is no live provider run here. What I can show is that the failure is raised while building the request, before anything is sent, so it reproduces without a project or a key. Both runs below use the exact tool schema from the issue. Before, at `423b791e` (the parent of this branch): ``` $ python -c " from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.common_utils import _build_vertex_schema print(_build_vertex_schema({'type':'object','properties':{'a':{'type':'array','items':[{'type':'integer'},{'type':'string'}]}}}))" AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' ``` After, at `f99823bf`: ``` $ python -c " from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.common_utils import _build_vertex_schema print(_build_vertex_schema({'type':'object','properties':{'a':{'type':'array','items':[{'type':'integer'},{'type':'string'}]}}}))" {'type': 'object', 'properties': {'a': {'type': 'array', 'items': {'anyOf': [{'type': 'integer'}, {'type': 'string'}]}}}} ``` A maintainer with Vertex access can confirm the end to end path with the curl in the issue body, which is the same tool schema against a live `vertex_ai/*` deployment. Happy to add that run here if someone can share a sandbox project. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Positional constraints are lost; Vertex cannot express tuple arrays - `additionalItems` is dropped, same as every other unsupported keyword - Boolean sub-schemas (`items: [false]`) still crash, unchanged from today - `prefixItems`, the 2020-12 spelling, is untouched and still ignored - `_build_json_schema` still passes tuple `items` through unchanged ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(proxy): allow custom budget exceeded messages
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Budget errors expose exact spend and limits - Every client must replace the message independently How it solves it: - Adds a configurable client-facing budget error message - Preserves detailed values for logs and callbacks - Applies consistently across proxy budget enforcement paths ## User Flow Before: a developer receives internal financial limits when their assigned budget is exhausted 1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with their virtual key and chat messages 2. Below budget, they receive HTTP 200 with a `chatcmpl-...` ID and an answer 3. Once exhausted, the same request returns HTTP 429 with exact current spend and maximum budget 4. Their application must detect `error.type: budget_exceeded` and replace the message After: the same developer receives the administrator-defined message from every compatible client 1. The proxy admin sets `budget_exceeded_error_message` under `litellm_settings` 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with the same virtual key and chat messages 3. Below budget, they receive the same HTTP 200 response 4. Once exhausted, the request returns HTTP 429 with the configured message and `error.type: budget_exceeded` ## Relevant issues Fixes #36729 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? signal.title: feat(auto-router): scope shadow eval jobs to multiple keys
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A shadow eval job could cover exactly one key - Evaluating a router across several keys meant several jobs - Their results had to be added up by hand How it solves it: - One job now takes a list of keys - Each key carries its own turn budget - Results come back pooled and per key ## User Flow Before: an admin shadow testing an auto-router across two of their keys can only cover one key at a time, so no single result describes the router 1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start with `"api_key_ids": ["<hash A>", "<hash B>"]` and get back 422 saying `api_key_id` is required 2. They resend the request twice, one key each time, and get back two separate job ids 3. They send GET http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/<job id> for each id and get two result sets, each describing one key 4. They add the two up by hand to judge the router, and a 200 turn budget covers whichever single key that job named 5. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-optimization and find a key picker that accepts one key, so the same split shows up on screen After: the same admin covers both keys with one job and reads one result 1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start with `"api_key_ids": ["<hash A>", "<hash B>"]` and get back 201 with a single job id listing both keys, each with its own `max_turns` 2. Traffic on either key is sampled, and each key spends its own budget, so two keys at a budget of 2 judge 4 turns rather than 2, and one key going quiet never ends sampling for the other 3. They send GET http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/<job id> and get one pooled result plus a per key breakdown alongside the existing tier and model ones 4. They send GET http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval?api_key_id=<hash A> and get every job that key belongs to, not just one 5. They send POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/<job id>/stop once and sampling ends for every key under it 6. They run a forward and a reverse job over the same two keys at once, since direction is a separate slot per key, and each of the four key rows keeps its own budget 7. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-optimization and find a picker that takes several keys, with a per key table in the detail view showing each key's own budget and win rates 8. Enrolling a key that another job already covers in the same direction comes back 409 naming that key and direction, and an unknown key comes back 400 naming it, before anything is created ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes A shadow eval job now holds a list of keys instead of one. Job-wide settings (router, direction, judge model, shadow percentage, window) stay on the job, while each key carries its own sample budget and its own stop timestamp in a child row. Sampled attempts record which key they came from, which is what makes both the per key budget and the per key result slice exact rather than estimated The DB-enforced uniqueness guarantee moves with it, and keeps the direction dimension that #36865 added. The partial unique index now sits on the child table over `(api_key_id, direction) WHERE stopped_at IS NULL`, so two concurrent starts naming the same key in the same direction still cannot both win, with no read-then-write in between, while a forward and a reverse job over the same key remain independent slots. Holding direction on the child row means the child could otherwise drift from its parent, so the foreign key is composite over `(job_id, direction)` and the database rejects a key row claiming a direction its job does not have Job status stays derived rather than stored. A job reads completed once its window passes, stopped only when every key has ended, and running while any key is still sampling, so one key finishing early never hides its siblings The migration moves those three columns rather than leaving them behind. It creates the child table, backfills every existing job into a key row carrying its direction, backfills each existing attempt with its job's key before that column goes NOT NULL, then drops `api_key_id`, `max_turns` and `stopped_at` off the job. Shadow eval has never been in a release, so no deployment runs the single key code and there is no mixed version window to design around ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on localhost:4000, real billed LLM calls, no mocks and no pytest. The run below was captured at ec03a6af0a. Everything committed since answers review findings without touching the paths it exercises: migration comments, an attempt count query narrowed to exact job and key pairs, which only drops groups nothing read, and a UI only move of the per key table. The discriminator is step 7: two keys at a budget of 2 judge 4 turns, where a shared pool would have stopped at 2. Rounds 3 and 4 send real traffic on both keys and add nothing, which is the budget holding rather than the traffic running out Each round sends two kinds of request per key because forward and reverse sample opposite traffic. A forward job skips what its own router served, since duplicating it would compare the router to itself, so plain `haiku-4-5` calls feed the forward job and `auto_router1` calls feed the reverse one. Steps 6 and 9 show the two directions holding separate slots for the same pair of keys ``` commit under test: ec03a6af0a ==================== 1. schema: the per key child table, and where the race safe index now lives ==================== $ psql -c "\d \"LiteLLM_ShadowEvalJobKey\"" id|text||not null| job_id|text||not null| direction|text||not null| api_key_id|text||not null| max_turns|integer||not null| created_at|timestamp(3) without time zone||not null|CURRENT_TIMESTAMP stopped_at|timestamp(3) without time zone||| $ psql -c "\d \"LiteLLM_ShadowEvalAttempt\"" | grep api_key_id api_key_id|text||not null| ==================== 2. two virtual keys whose traffic will be shadowed ==================== key C hash: 27015286229631c0ce7f95b023c65e64d02d8236bb863a919bf8e3a1542ebee7 key D hash: c438875739cd5b6496d95d425acc64bc8260549724dcb90b0fb895d4cb9599b0 ==================== 3. an unknown key is rejected by name, and nothing is created ==================== $ curl -X POST .../shadow_eval/start -d {"api_key_ids":["<C>","sk-does-not-exist"],...} {"detail":"api_key_ids not on this proxy: sk-does-not-exist; "keys": 2} {"job_id": "cmstnqqu7000kmgodp5y1cev7", "direction": "forward", "status": "stopped", "keys": 2} ==================== done at commit ec03a6af0a ==================== ``` For the UI, with the same proxy running and `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`: 1. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-optimization and find the Shadow Eval section 2. In the key picker, search and tick two keys, confirming both appear as chips and that the picker no longer collapses to a single selection 3. Set Max turns to 2, pick a judge model, and start the job 4. Send a couple of requests on each key, then read the per key table under the tier and model breakdowns, which lists every scoped key with its status, turns against budget and win rates 5. Confirm each key shows its own turn count and its own budget, and that Stop ends both at once 6. Stop the job, expand Previous evaluations, open that job, and confirm the same per key table is there rather than only the tier and model breakdowns ### Migration An earlier revision kept the three job columns and made them nullable so that a pod on the previous image could keep serving mid rollout. That answered Greptile's flag, and it cost a NULL branch in the per key budget, an `unattributed` bucket in the API response, and three dead columns nothing reads. The window it guards cannot occur: `git tag --contains` on the shadow eval commit returns nothing, and neither the latest stable release nor the current dev pre-release ships the shadow eval migration or `shadow_eval_logger.py`, so no pod anywhere runs the single key code. The migration is destructive again and all three guards are gone with it The run below applies it to a database already holding jobs and attempts in both directions, checks the backfill and the moved constraints, then deploys the whole chain to a fresh database and diffs the result against schema.prisma ``` ==================== 1. a database already at the pre-upgrade shadow eval state, holding jobs and attempts ==================== applied the merged shadow eval migrations: 20260811172448_add_shadow_eval 20260813180408_add_shadow_eval_direction seeded 3 jobs and 3 attempts job_fwd | forward job_old | forward job_rev | reverse (3 rows) ==================== 4. every job backfilled into a key row, carrying its direction, budget and stop state ==================== id | job_id | direction | api_key_id | max_turns | active ----------------+---------+-----------+------------+-----------+-------- jobkey_job_fwd | job_fwd | forward | hash_a | 40 | t jobkey_job_old | job_old | forward | hash_b | 10 | f jobkey_job_rev | job_rev | reverse | hash_a | 25 | t (3 rows) ==================== 5. every pre-upgrade attempt attributed to its job's key, column now NOT NULL ==================== id | job_id | api_key_id ------+---------+------------ att1 | job_fwd | hash_a att2 | job_rev | hash_a att3 | job_old | hash_b (3 rows) is_nullable ------------- NO (1 row) ==================== 6. one active job per key per direction, now enforced on the child table ==================== $ INSERT a second active forward row for hash_a (already active forward) ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalJobKey_one_active_per_key_direction" DETAIL: Key (api_key_id, direction)=(hash_a, forward) already exists. $ INSERT an active forward row for hash_b (its old job was stopped) INSERT 0 1 $ INSERT a key row claiming a direction its job does not have ERROR: insert or update on table "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalJobKey" violates foreign key constraint "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalJobKey_job_id_direction_fkey" DETAIL: Key (job_id, direction)=(job_fwd, reverse) is not present in table "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalJob". ==================== 7. the whole chain on a fresh database, then diffed against schema.prisma ==================== $ prisma migrate deploy Applying migration `20260814000000_shadow_eval_multi_key` The following migrations have been applied: All migrations have been successfully applied. $ prisma migrate diff --from-url <fresh db> --to-schema-datamodel schema.prisma -- This is an empty migration. ==================== done ==================== ``` Row 4 of that run is the case worth naming: `hash_a` held an active forward job and an active reverse job before the upgrade, and comes out the other side holding two independent key rows with their own budgets, which is the shape the rest of this PR relies on ## Caveats Local direct provider credentials were dead on this rig, so the three model groups under test pointed at an OpenAI-compatible gateway upstream. The calls are real and billed, and the router really picked among them, though the provider path is one hop longer than a direct provider run. A direct provider re-run is owed before this is treated as covering provider-specific behavior `judge_spend` reads 0 above for the same reason: the substituted upstream model string is not a key in the price map, so cost lookup returns zero even though the judge calls were billed. Nothing in this change touches cost attribution Step 8 shows the job still reading `running` after both budgets are spent. Sweeping a finished key row is lazy and scoped, exactly as it was before this change, so status catches up the next time a start touches those keys. signal.title: feat(proxy): gate the Global Control Plane worker registry on an enterprise license
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Global Control Plane is sold as Enterprise but had no license check - Any OSS install could run one for free - Its two config keys were undeclared, so they were undiscoverable How it solves it: - Check the license when the worker registry is loaded - Fail startup loudly instead of dropping the registry silently - Declare both keys so they reach the generated config schema ## User Flow Before: an admin with no Enterprise license stands up a control plane and it just works, so the Enterprise requirement is unenforced 1. They write a config with a `worker_registry` listing two proxies, and no `LITELLM_LICENSE` in the environment 2. They start the proxy on port 4633, and it boots normally with no warning 3. They open `http://localhost:4633/.well-known/litellm-ui-config` and get `"is_control_plane": true` with both workers listed 4. They open the admin UI and get the worker selector on the login page, managing both proxies from one place, without a license After: the same admin is told at startup that this needs a license, and a licensed admin is unaffected 1. They write the same config with the same `worker_registry`, still with no `LITELLM_LICENSE` 2. They start the proxy, and it refuses to boot: `Trying to use worker_registry` followed by `You must be a LiteLLM Enterprise user to use this feature`, then `Application startup failed. Exiting.` 3. They set a valid `LITELLM_LICENSE` and start again, and the proxy boots normally 4. `http://localhost:4633/.well-known/litellm-ui-config` returns `"is_control_plane": true` with both workers, byte for byte what it returned before this change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5633 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Three legs against a live proxy on port 4633, same config file throughout, differing only in code revision and whether a license is present. Config used in all three legs: ```yaml model_list: [] general_settings: master_key: sk-5633 worker_registry: - worker_id: "worker-a" name: "Worker A" url: "http://localhost:4634" - worker_id: "worker-b" name: "Worker B" url: "http://localhost:4635" ``` ### Before, unlicensed, at `40a418440c` (base) The control plane comes up and serves the full worker registry with no license present, which is the gap this PR closes. ```bash LITELLM_LICENSE="" python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config cp_config_5633.yaml --port 4633 curl -s http://localhost:4633/.well-known/litellm-ui-config ``` ```json {"server_root_path":"","proxy_base_url":null,"auto_redirect_to_sso":false,"admin_ui_disabled":false,"sso_configured":false,"hide_default_credentials_hint":false,"is_control_plane":true,"workers":[{"worker_id":"worker-a","name":"Worker A","url":"http://localhost:4634"},{"worker_id":"worker-b","name":"Worker B","url":"http://localhost:4635"}]} ``` ### After, unlicensed, at `f622c85c9c` Same command, same config. Startup now refuses. ```bash LITELLM_LICENSE="" python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config cp_config_5633.yaml --port 4633 ``` ``` raise ValueError("Trying to use `worker_registry`" + CommonProxyErrors.not_premium_user.value) ValueError: Trying to use `worker_registry`You must be a LiteLLM Enterprise user to use this feature. If you have a license please set `LITELLM_LICENSE` in your env. Get a 7 day trial key here: https://www.litellm.ai/enterprise#trial. ERROR: Application startup failed. Exiting. ``` ### After, licensed, at `f622c85c9c` Same command with a real `LITELLM_LICENSE` set. The proxy boots and the response is identical to the before leg, so licensed deployments see no change. ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4633/.well-known/litellm-ui-config ``` ```json {"server_root_path":"","proxy_base_url":null,"auto_redirect_to_sso":false,"admin_ui_disabled":false,"sso_configured":false,"hide_default_credentials_hint":false,"is_control_plane":true,"workers":[{"worker_id":"worker-a","name":"Worker A","url":"http://localhost:4634"},{"worker_id":"worker-b","name":"Worker B","url":"http://localhost:4635"}]} ``` ### Mutation check on the new tests Each mutant applied on its own and reverted from a scratchpad copy, so the runs are independent. ``` mutant 1, gate deleted entirely -> 1 failed, 11 passed (worker_registry_requires_premium) mutant 2, `premium_user is not True` flipped to `premium_user is True` -> 2 failed, 10 passed (requires_premium and loads_for_premium) restored -> 12 passed ``` ## Review notes Greptile raised two findings on `f622c85c`, one accepted and one declined. **Accepted: a test comment violating the repo comment policy.** Removed. The test is renamed to `..._premium_invalid_worker_registry_raises`, so the name carries what the comment was explaining and nothing is lost. The mutation check was re-run after the rename, since a rename is exactly the kind of change that can silently turn an assertion vacuous, and the mutant still dies. **Declined: adding a user-controlled transition flag to soften the startup failure.** This is a licensing gate, so a flag that lets an unlicensed proxy load `worker_registry` anyway would remove the entitlement it exists to enforce. There is also no precedent for one: `litellm/proxy/` has 35 call sites using `CommonProxyErrors.not_premium_user`, and a grep for any bypass or transition mechanism across them returns nothing. Every one raises unconditionally, including the `enforced_params` gate 200 lines above this change in the same function. Adding a flag here would make this the only gate of 36 with an escape hatch. The breaking change is real and is called out under Caveats. The right mitigation is a release note naming `worker_registry`, not a bypass. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Breaking for unlicensed installs already running a worker registry - Needs a release note naming `worker_registry` - Companion litellm-docs PR renames this feature and drops its beta label - Worker selector flow still has no e2e coverage ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(cost): tiered pricing supports cache creation cost and is all-or-nothing
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Pricing schema rejected `cache_creation_input_token_cost` inside tiers - Cache-creation tokens were never billed at tier rates - Dashscope tiers were billed graduated, not all-or-nothing - Tiered-only models (volcengine) were billed at $0 - `tiered_pricing` under a router deployment's `litellm_params` was silently ignored - Reasoning tokens ignored the tier's reasoning rate on the generic path - With tiers now effective, a PTU deployment carrying `tiered_pricing` would bill per token on top of its reserved-capacity flat cost How it solves it: - Schema generator and committed schema accept the tier field - Tier selection now happens once, from total input tokens - Selected tier prices text, cached, cache-creation, output, reasoning - Generic cost path resolves tiered rates for any provider - Deployment mirror copies `tiered_pricing` onto model_info so custom-pricing detection fires - Generic path and cost breakdown bill reasoning tokens at the selected tier's `output_cost_per_reasoning_token` - PTU deployments refuse supplied `tiered_pricing` with the same 400 as flat rates and clear tiers already stored ## User Flow Before: someone running a Qwen deployment with prompt caching gets undercharged and inconsistently charged, and the pricing entry they need cannot even be loaded 1. They add a model entry whose `tiered_pricing` tier carries `cache_creation_input_token_cost` and the entry fails schema validation, so the rate cannot be expressed at all 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Dashscope model with a 300K-token prompt 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows spend computed by slicing the prompt across two tiers, first 256K at the cheap rate and the rest at the expensive one, which is below what the provider invoices 4. They send the same request with a cache write and the cache-creation tokens are billed at the plain input rate, so the log again understates spend 5. They point a key at a volcengine doubao-seed-2.0 deployment, which only publishes tiered rates, and every request logs at $0 spend 6. They set `tiered_pricing` under a deployment's `litellm_params` in the proxy config and every request on it still logs at the base model-map rate, ignoring their tiers entirely 7. They send a reasoning request to a Qwen model whose tier publishes a separate `output_cost_per_reasoning_token` and the log bills those tokens at the tier's plain output rate 8. An admin whose deployment carries `tiered_pricing` adds PTU config via POST https://litellm-domain/model/update, and with tiers now effective every request would keep logging per-token tier spend on top of the flat PTU cost After: the same requests log the amount the provider actually invoices 1. The same model entry with `cache_creation_input_token_cost` inside a tier loads successfully 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Dashscope model with a 300K-token prompt 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the whole request billed at the 256K-1M tier rate, matching the published all-or-nothing table 4. The same request with a cache write bills those tokens at that tier's cache-creation rate, falling back to the tier's input rate when the tier does not publish one 5. The volcengine doubao-seed-2.0 request now logs non-zero spend at the tier its input size lands in 6. The deployment with `tiered_pricing` under `litellm_params` bills every request at the configured tier rates on /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, and /v1/responses 7. The reasoning request bills reasoning tokens at the tier's `output_cost_per_reasoning_token` and the rest of the completion at the tier's output rate 8. That update clears the stored tiers so requests on the PTU deployment log $0 per-token spend, and sending `tiered_pricing` together with PTU config is refused with a 400 like any other rate ## Relevant issues Fixes #28844 Supersedes the approach in #28047 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4375 Resolves LIT-4376 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, real Anthropic spend, same config on both legs: a `qwen-tiered-sim` deployment (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`) with two-tier `tiered_pricing` under `litellm_params`, exercising the same generic cost path dashscope map entries ride ```yaml model_list: - model_name: qwen-tiered-sim litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY tiered_pricing: - range: [0, 3000] input_cost_per_token: 3.25e-7 output_cost_per_token: 1.95e-6 cache_creation_input_token_cost: 4.063e-7 cache_read_input_token_cost: 3.25e-8 - range: [3000, 128000] input_cost_per_token: 6.5e-7 output_cost_per_token: 3.9e-6 cache_creation_input_token_cost: 8.125e-7 cache_read_input_token_cost: 6.5e-8 general_settings: master_key: sk-qa-tiered-1234 ``` Cache-write request used on both legs (cache-read leg repeats it, small-prompt leg sends a 21-token user message): ```bash BIG=$(python3 -c 'print(" ".join(f"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog number {i}." for i in range(400)))') curl -sD - http://localhost:<port>/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-tiered-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"qwen-tiered-sim\",\"max_tokens\":20,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"$BIG\",\"cache_control\":{\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}}]},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Reply with the single word: ok\"}]}" ``` **Before, merge base `3b5317c40d`**: every request billed at the base model-map rates, tiers ignored entirely | Scenario | Usage | Observed header | Tier-correct value | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---| | chat cache write | text 13, creation 6502, out 4 | 0.0081605 | 0.005306925 | FAIL | | chat cache read | text 13, cached 6502, out 4 | 0.0006832 | 0.00044668 | FAIL | | /v1/messages cache read | text 13, cached 6502, out 4 | 0.0006832 | 0.00044668 | FAIL | | /v1/responses 5415 in | input 5415, out 4 | 0.005435 | 0.00353535 | FAIL | | chat small prompt | input 21, out 20 | 0.000121 | 0.000045825 | FAIL | The before numbers reconstruct exactly from claude-haiku-4-5 base rates (e.g. cache write: 13\*1e-6 + 6502\*1.25e-6 + 4\*5e-6 = 0.0081605), proving `tiered_pricing` was dead config **After, tip `5970754a85`**: every `x-litellm-response-cost` header matches the tier math computed from that response's own usage to within 1e-9 | Scenario | Tier | Observed header | Expected | Spend log | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | chat cache write (creation 5601) | 2 | 0.0045748625 | 0.0045748625 | matches (rerun: 0.00458055) | PASS | | chat cache read (cached 5601) | 2 | 0.000388115 | 0.000388115 | n/a | PASS | | /v1/messages cache read | 2 | 0.000388115 | 0.000388115 | n/a | PASS | | /v1/responses 5265 in | 2 | 0.00343785 | 0.00343785 | n/a | PASS | | chat small prompt (21 in) | 1 | 1.4625e-05 | 1.4625e-05 | 1.4625e-05 | PASS | Key proofs from the after leg - Cache-creation rate: 13\*6.5e-7 + 5601\*8.125e-7 + 4\*3.9e-6 = 0.0045748625 observed; billing creation tokens at the tier's input rate would give 0.0036647, so the dedicated `cache_creation_input_token_cost` is what's applied - All-or-nothing: the 5265-token /v1/responses request bills entirely at tier 2 (a graduated split would give 0.001718925), and the 21-token request bills entirely at tier 1 (tier 2 would give 2.925e-05) - `GET /spend/logs?request_id=<response id>` equals the header to the digit for the cache-write and small-prompt scenarios, so the persisted spend matches what the client saw **PTU interplay, tip `5970754a85`**: DB-backed proxy with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=true`, driven through the management API | Scenario | Check | Result | Verdict | |---|---|---|---| | POST /model/new, tiers + PTU | HTTP status | 400 naming tiered_pricing | PASS | | tiered deployment, no PTU yet | cost header | 1.4625e-05 (tier 1) | PASS | | PATCH /model/{id}/update adds PTU | stored blobs | tiers absent, rates 0.0 | PASS | | same completion after PTU | header, spend log | 0.0, 0.0 (fresh process) | PASS | ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Tiered rates now apply on the generic path for all providers - Volcengine doubao-seed-2.0 spend changes from $0 to real - Tier boundaries are exclusive at the start, inclusive at the end - `tiered_pricing` works in a deployment's `litellm_params` or `model_info`; passing it as a raw SDK completion kwarg is still unsupported - Legacy POST /model/update still ignores model_info patches; untouched here - register_model's additive merge keeps stale tiers until restart; untouched here ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/61c1a67073dd4a10973334cdfb1224c2 Requested by: @mateo-berri
