signal.title: [Bug]: Metadata-only model registration (e.g. mode) silently converts unknown-model cost errors into $0.00 — Router.__init__ triggers it
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. (Closest neighbors: my open PR #36561 fixes the *empty*-payload case of this and explicitly scopes this variant out; #28336 and #30198 are about pricing fields being dropped/overwritten, not about metadata-only registration converting errors into $0.) ### What happened? Registering **metadata-only** model info (for example just `{"mode": "chat"}`, no pricing) for a model that is not in the cost map makes every later cost lookup for that model return **$0.00 instead of raising "this model isn't mapped yet."** Expected: cost tracking for an unmapped model should stay loud (raise), or use real pricing — never silently bill $0. A metadata-only registration carries no pricing information, so it should not change whether the model is considered priceable. This is easy to hit without calling `register_model` yourself: a `Router` deployment whose `model_info` carries any metadata (e.g. `mode`) but whose model isn't in the cost map does this on `Router.__init__`, process-wide. ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix:** a team routing to a brand-new provider model sees their spend dashboard flatline at $0 for it, with no error anywhere. 1. The proxy admin adds a deployment to `config.yaml` with `model: deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (not yet in the public price catalog) and `model_info: {mode: chat}`, then starts the proxy. 2. A developer sends POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with that model; the request succeeds and a normal completion comes back. 3. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` — the request is logged at **$0.00 spend**. No warning, no error, on this and every subsequent request. 4. Monthly reconciliation against the provider invoice shows real charges the gateway never accounted for. **After a (hypothetical) fix:** the same setup makes the missing price visible instead of silently billing zero. 1. The proxy admin adds the same deployment with the same `model_info: {mode: chat}` and starts the proxy. 2. A developer sends the same POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions`; the completion comes back the same way. 3. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request with an explicit "pricing unknown for this model" marker (or real pricing, once the admin supplies `input_cost_per_token`/`output_cost_per_token` in `model_info`) — not a silent $0.00. 4. Reconciliation matches, because unpriced traffic was flagged the moment it happened. ### Proof the bug occurs This is a pure cost-arithmetic path — no LLM provider call is involved in computing the cost, so the proof is a complete SDK transcript (the proxy's spend logging sits directly on this function). Captured at commit `09889e1986` on `litellm_internal_staging`, Python 3.13: ``` >>> litellm.completion_cost(model="deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", prompt="hi", completion="there") raises Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 >>> litellm.register_model({"deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731": {"mode": "chat"}}) # metadata only, no pricing >>> litellm.completion_cost(model="deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", prompt="hi", completion="there") 0.0 ``` Same result through the Router path real configs hit (fresh process): ``` >>> before Router init: raises Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 >>> Router(model_list=[{"model_name": "my-deepseek", ... "litellm_params": {"model": "deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", "api_key": "sk-redacted"}, ... "model_info": {"mode": "chat"}}]) >>> after Router init: 0.0 ``` ### Additional context Verified mechanism (for whoever picks this up): the registration materializes a cost-map entry that carries no pricing keys, and the subsequent lookup treats key-existence as "mapped," synthesizing zero costs for the missing price fields. My #36561 guards the fully-empty-payload version of this; the metadata-only variant needs the fix at the cost-synthesis side instead, because metadata-only registration is legitimate for models that ARE in the built-in catalog. I'm happy to submit the PR for this once #36561 lands (I'm currently at what appears to be the per-author open-PR limit).

signal.title: fix(streaming): keep upstream usage when the usage chunk also carries choices
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Upstream `usage` is dropped when the usage chunk also has `choices` - `cached_tokens` lost, so streaming cost is billed at the full input rate How it solves it: - Normalize provider SDK usage objects to litellm's `Usage` on ingest ## Relevant issues Fixes #36168 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on `localhost:4000`, config below, streaming `/v1/chat/completions` through it. The upstream is a stand-in OpenAI-compatible server replaying the exact final SSE chunk from the issue (`choices: [{"index": 0, "delta": {}}]` plus `usage` with `cached_tokens`), because this box cannot reach an external provider that emits that shape ```yaml model_list: - model_name: kimi litellm_params: model: openai/moonshotai/kimi-k3 api_base: http://127.0.0.1:8931/v1 api_key: sk-x model_info: input_cost_per_token: 0.0000006 output_cost_per_token: 0.0000025 cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.00000015 general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash curl -s -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"kimi","stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ciao"}]}' | tail -3 ``` Before, at b66d4e6965 (upstream's 38679 prompt tokens replaced by a tokenizer estimate of 9, `prompt_tokens_details` gone) ``` data: {"id":"49c0","created":1786090761,"model":"kimi","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":1,"prompt_tokens":9,"total_tokens":10,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":32,"text_tokens":0}}} data: [DONE] ``` After, at 7853a0c607 ``` data: {"id":"49c0","created":1786090907,"model":"kimi","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":32,"prompt_tokens":38679,"total_tokens":38711,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":32,"text_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":38400}}} data: [DONE] ``` The SpendLogs row for the fixed run bills the cache read rather than the full input rate ```bash curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:4000/spend/logs' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' ``` ``` {'spend': 0.0060074, 'prompt_tokens': 38679, 'completion_tokens': 32} ``` which is `(38679 - 38400) * 6e-7 + 38400 * 1.5e-7 + 32 * 2.5e-6`, so the 38400 cached tokens are priced at the cache-read rate instead of the full input rate ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `chunk_creator` normalized the upstream usage into litellm's `Usage` when parsing the chunk, then a few lines later overwrote it with the raw `chunk.usage`, which for OpenAI-compatible providers is openai's `CompletionUsage`. That overwrite was invisible while the usage arrived on a `choices: []` chunk, since that shape returns early and never reaches it The raw object then reaches `calculate_total_usage` and `_usage_chunk_calculation_helper`, which read it with `"prompt_tokens" in usage`. Only litellm's `Usage` defines `__contains__`; on a plain pydantic model that membership test falls through to `BaseModel.__iter__` and compares the key against `(name, value)` tuples, so every field reads as absent and the usage silently counts as zero. Token counts then fall back to the local tokenizer and `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` disappears, which is the 4x over-billing in the issue The fix normalizes at both ingest points: `_normalize_usage` before the assignment in `chunk_creator`, and `_extract_usage_chunk` in the chunk builder, which declared `-> Usage | None` while happily returning whatever the chunk carried ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(streaming): preserve upstream usage with non-empty choices
signal.text: ## Problem OpenAI-compatible providers can put the final streaming `usage` object on a chunk that still contains a content-free `choices` entry. LiteLLM currently loses the provider's prompt-token counts and `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` in that shape, so downstream aggregation falls back to local tokenization and can overbill cached input. ## Root Cause The OpenAI-compatible streaming path first normalizes provider usage into LiteLLM's `Usage` model. A later generic assignment overwrites that normalized value with the raw OpenAI SDK usage object. The raw object is not handled by the streaming usage accumulator's nested detail parser, so cached-token details and provider counts are discarded. ## Solution Keep the already-normalized LiteLLM usage value when it exists, and only copy the raw chunk usage when no normalized value was produced. ## Changes - Guard the generic usage assignment in `CustomStreamWrapper.chunk_creator()` so it cannot clobber normalized usage. - Add a regression test to the existing core streaming-handler test path covering a non-empty `choices` array with provider-reported cached tokens. ## Testing - Focused regression logic — passed in the local standalone wrapper/SSE reproduction. - Local HTTP/SSE reproduction — both `choices=[]` and `choices=[{"delta":{}}]` preserve `prompt_tokens=39779` and `cached_tokens=39424`. - `py -3 -m ruff check litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py` — passed. - `py -3 -m ruff format --check litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py` — passed. - `py -3 -m py_compile litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py` — passed. - `git diff --check` — passed. - Core test file collection is not locally verifiable because this sparse Windows environment has a pre-existing Pydantic forward-reference failure while importing the existing test module; the new test includes the same model-rebuild setup used to exercise the path. - `basedpyright` — not run; the executable is not installed in this environment. - Full suite — not run; repository-wide generated/workspace dependencies are unavailable in this environment. ## Compatibility/Risk Low risk. This changes only the precedence of usage objects in the OpenAI-compatible streaming path. Providers that do not supply a normalized usage value retain the existing fallback assignment. ## Notes for Reviewer The regression is isolated to ingress parsing of provider chunks with non-empty choices. It is distinct from PR #28736, which changes LiteLLM's egress shape to emit usage-only chunks with empty choices, and from PR #32130, which prevents a later usage chunk from clobbering an earlier prompt-token detail object. The test now lives under `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils`, which is covered by the repository's Core Utilities CI job. ## Linked Issue Closes #36168

signal.title: fix(proxy): requeue spend logs when the DB write fails with a transport error
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A DB outage silently loses every queued spend log - Prisma's P1001 masquerade escaped the retry clause entirely - Failed batches were dropped, never put back on the queue How it solves it: - Classify failures with the existing transport-error helper - Requeue the batch at the head after retries exhaust - Route every enqueue and dequeue, producer appends included, through one pair that holds the queue under a byte budget so a long outage cannot OOM the pod ## User Flow Before: an admin whose primary database goes down keeps serving traffic, then finds no usage recorded for the outage window 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions repeatedly while the primary database is unreachable 2. Every request returns 200 with a normal completion, so the app is unaffected 3. The proxy logs `Error in spend logs queue monitor: Can't reach database server ... :5432 (P1001)` 4. The database comes back and they open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs filtered to the outage window 5. Nothing is there, and GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs returns no entries for those requests, so that spend is billed to nobody After: the same outage delays the records instead of losing them 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions repeatedly while the primary database is unreachable 2. Every request returns 200 with a normal completion, so the app is unaffected 3. The proxy logs the connection failure once per retry, saying how many logs are held back 4. The database comes back and they open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs filtered to the outage window 5. Every request from the outage is there with its real spend, and GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs returns all of them ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5475 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on localhost:4000 with a real Postgres and real Anthropic calls (`anthropic-haiku-4-5`, real spend). The outage is a `service postgresql stop` while traffic keeps flowing, exactly the controlled validation the customer ran. Same script for both runs, tagging the six requests with a unique `user` so the rows can be counted afterwards: ```bash PROBE="outage-probe-$(date +%s)" sudo service postgresql stop for i in $(seq 1 6); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "request $i -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" -m 60 http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"anthropic-haiku-4-5\",\"max_tokens\":8,\"user\":\"$PROBE\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"say hi $i\"}]}" done sleep 90 # flush job runs against the dead DB sudo service postgresql start sleep 90 # next flush after recovery PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h localhost -U postgres -d litellm -c \ "select count(*) from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" where end_user = '$PROBE';" ``` Before, at 3b5317c40d (this branch's merge base): ``` request 1 -> HTTP 200 request 2 -> HTTP 200 request 3 -> HTTP 200 request 4 -> HTTP 200 request 5 -> HTTP 200 request 6 -> HTTP 200 count ------- 0 (1 row) ``` After, at ebaaeaba0c (fix commit; later commits only change how the queue is bounded and a stale test import): ``` request 1 -> HTTP 200 request 2 -> HTTP 200 request 3 -> HTTP 200 request 4 -> HTTP 200 request 5 -> HTTP 200 request 6 -> HTTP 200 count ------- 6 (1 row) ``` Proxy log from the after run showing the batch surviving the outage and being retried rather than dropped: ``` 00:21:38 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: utils.py:5583 - Spend tracking - DB connection error writing spend logs, retry 1/3. logs_count=6, error=All connection attempts failed 00:21:45 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: utils.py:5583 - Spend tracking - DB connection error writing spend logs, retry 4/3. logs_count=6, error=All connection attempts failed ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Requeued rows flush out of chronological order - Queue is bounded at a fixed 64 MB, not a row count - Guardrail usage tracking still skips a failed batch Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5a90b9cf2ca84ee4ac762ffeaa0fe93f

signal.title: test(ui): await handleSearch completion in SearchToolTester tests
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - UI Unit Tests failed on staging with a phantom "ReferenceError: window is not defined" though all 29 SearchToolTester tests passed - The failing commit was a Fireworks Python change with zero UI diff, so this was a pre-existing flake, not a bug in the commit How it solves it: - Waits for `handleSearch` to fully settle in the four tests that fired a click without observing the async result - Keeps `setIsLoading(false)` in the component's `finally` block from firing after the test file's JSDOM teardown ## User Flow Not user-facing; touches a single unit-test file for `SearchToolTester`. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Stack trace from the failing job on staging (commit 40a41844): ``` ReferenceError: window is not defined ❯ getCurrentEventPriority node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:10993:22 ❯ requestUpdateLane node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:25495:19 ❯ dispatchSetState node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:16648:14 ❯ handleSearch src/app/(dashboard)/search-tools/_components/SearchToolTester.tsx:66:7 This error originated in "src/app/(dashboard)/search-tools/_components/SearchToolTester.test.tsx" test file. This error was caught after test environment was torn down. ``` Line 66 is `setIsLoading(false)` in the `finally` block of `handleSearch`. signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): convert messages to contents in gemini count_tokens
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `litellm.acount_tokens()` returns `total_tokens=0` with `error=False` for any `vertex_ai/gemini-*` model when called with `messages` - The Gemini branch of `VertexAITokenCounter.count_tokens` never converts `messages` to Gemini `contents`, so the request body is `{"contents": null}` - Vertex accepts that with HTTP 200 and no `totalTokens` field, and the old code read `result.get("totalTokens", 0)` as a valid zero How it solves it: - Converts `messages` to Gemini `contents` via the existing `_gemini_convert_messages_with_history` helper when `contents` is `None` - Treats a response without `totalTokens` as a failure (returns `None`) so the caller falls back to local token counting ## User Flow Before: a developer calling `acount_tokens` with `messages` on a Vertex Gemini model gets a silent zero, so their pre-flight context-window guard always passes and overflows surface later as a provider 400 1. They call `await litellm.acount_tokens(model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])` 2. The SDK returns `TokenCountResponse(total_tokens=0, tokenizer_type="", error=False)` 3. Their guard checks `total_tokens < max_tokens`, passes, and sends the real request 4. Vertex rejects the real request with a 400 because the context window is actually exceeded After: the same call returns the real token count from Vertex, or falls back to local counting 1. They call `await litellm.acount_tokens(model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])` 2. The SDK converts `messages` to Gemini `contents` format and sends `{"contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "Hello"}]}]}` to Vertex 3. signal.title: [Bug]: Admin UI session cookie is a non-HttpOnly JWT carrying the caller's proxy key
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? The Admin UI login sets a `token` cookie holding a JWT whose `key` claim is the caller's real proxy key, and the cookie is not marked `HttpOnly`. For a proxy admin signing in with `UI_USERNAME` / `UI_PASSWORD` or through SSO, that means a full-privilege `sk-...` key sits in `document.cookie`, readable by any script running on `/ui`, for the whole 8h cookie lifetime. Two things make it worse than a normal session cookie: The key keeps working outside the browser. Anything that can read the cookie can paste the decoded key into `curl` and mint new keys, read spend, or call models, with no session involved. Logout does not revoke it. The dashboard clears cookies client-side, so a key that was copied before logout stays valid until its own expiry. I would expect the browser to hold an opaque session identifier that the proxy resolves server-side, in an `HttpOnly` cookie, with a logout route that drops the session on the server. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run the proxy with any config that sets a master key, for example ```yaml model_list: [] general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` 2. Log in the way the Admin UI does, and look at the cookie it sets ``` $ curl -si -X POST http://localhost:4000/login -d 'username=admin&password=sk-1234' | grep -i '^set-cookie' set-cookie: token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoiZGVmYXVsdF91c2VyX2lkIiwia2V5Ijoic2steHh4eHh4...<truncated>; Path=/; SameSite=lax ``` No `HttpOnly` flag, so `document.cookie` in the devtools console on http://localhost:4000/ui/ returns the same string. 3. Decode the middle segment ``` $ echo "$TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d | python -m json.tool { "user_id": "default_user_id", "key": "sk-<the admin's real proxy key>", "user_role": "proxy_admin", "login_method": "username_password", "auth_header_name": "Authorization", "server_root_path": "", "exp": 1786805817 } ``` 4. Use that key from outside the browser ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_FROM_COOKIE" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"minted-outside-the-browser"}' { "key": "sk-...", "key_alias": "minted-outside-the-browser", "expires": null } ``` 5. Log out in the UI, then repeat step 4 with the same key; it still mints keys ### Relevant log output ```shell POST /login HTTP/1.1" 303 See Other POST /key/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 OK # using the key decoded out of the login cookie ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? UI Dashboard ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0 (reproduced on `litellm_internal_staging` at 423b791ee0) ### Possible direction I have a working change locally that swaps the JWT for an opaque `sso_<hex>` handle stored in the cache the `login_code` exchange already uses, delivered in an `HttpOnly` `SameSite=Lax` cookie, plus `/sso/session/me` for identity and `/sso/session/logout` for server-side revocation, with a credential-free `litellm_ui_session=1` marker so the dashboard can still tell a session exists. Happy to open a PR if that direction sounds right to you.

signal.title: [Bug]: Bedrock batch records all fail with `anthropic_version: Field required` when the JSONL names the proxy model alias
signal.text: ## What happened Every record in a Bedrock batch fails with `anthropic_version: Field required` when the batch JSONL names the proxy's model alias in each record's `body.model`, which is the natural thing to write when the batch is routed through a proxy deployment. `BedrockFilesConfig._map_openai_to_bedrock_params` (`litellm/llms/bedrock/files/transformation.py`) branches on the provider it infers from `body.model`. With the raw model id it takes the Anthropic branch, `AmazonAnthropicClaudeConfig.transform_request` runs, and `anthropic_version` is filled in. With an alias the provider does not resolve, the branch is skipped, and the `modelInput` written to S3 is the OpenAI body with `model` stripped and nothing added, so Bedrock rejects every record at invoke time. Nothing surfaces this until the job finishes: `POST /v1/files` returns 200, `POST /v1/batches` returns 200, Bedrock reports `Completed`, and only the manifest shows `successRecordCount: 0`. ## Relevant log output Alias in `body.model` (`{"model": "bedrock-batch", ...}`), object LiteLLM wrote to S3: ```json {"recordId": "req-1", "modelInput": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the number 1 and nothing else."}], "max_tokens": 16}} ``` Result after the job completes: ```json {"totalRecordCount":110,"processedRecordCount":110,"successRecordCount":0,"errorRecordCount":110} ``` ```json {"modelInput":{...},"error":{"errorCode":400,"errorMessage":"anthropic_version: Field required","expired":false,"retryable":false},"recordId":"req-44"} ``` Raw model id in `body.model` (`{"model": "bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", ...}`), same deployment, same route, same upload: ```json {"recordId": "a", "modelInput": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "hi"}]}], "max_tokens": 16, "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31"}} ``` ## Expected behaviour The alias should resolve to the deployment's underlying `bedrock/...` model before the per-record transformation picks a provider, so the same JSONL works whether it names the alias or the raw model id. Failing that, the upload should reject a record whose model it cannot map instead of writing a body Bedrock will refuse 110 times. ## Are you a ML Ops Team? No ## What LiteLLM version are you on? litellm_internal_staging at f6587faef5 ## Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): translate /v1/embeddings batch rows to the Gemini embedding shape
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex batch `/v1/embeddings` rows fail: "no such field: 'contents'" - The OpenAI `input` is dropped entirely on those rows - Embedding result rows come back as raw Vertex jsonl How it solves it: - Route each jsonl line by its own `url` - Embeddings lines emit an `EmbedContentRequest` row - Embedding output rows transform into OpenAI embeddings responses ## User Flow Before: a developer running an embeddings batch job through the gateway sees the batch report success while every row inside it failed and the text they asked to embed was never sent 1. They write `batch_embeddings.jsonl` where every line targets the embeddings endpoint, e.g. `{"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": "hello world from litellm batch"}}` 2. They upload it with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (`purpose=batch`, `model=gemini-embedding-001`) and get back a `file-...` id 3. They create the job with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches passing that `input_file_id` and `"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"`, and a batch id comes back 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reports `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null`, which looks like success 5. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and every row is an error, `{"custom_id": "req-1", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": "... EmbedContentRequest ... no such field: 'contents'"}}`, with not one embedding in the file After: the same job returns one OpenAI embeddings response per input line 1. They write the same `batch_embeddings.jsonl` with `"url": "/v1/embeddings"` lines 2. They upload it with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (`purpose=batch`, `model=gemini-embedding-001`) and get back a `file-...` id 3. They create the job with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches passing that `input_file_id` and `"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"`, and a batch id comes back 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reports `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null` 5. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and get one row per input line, e.g. `{"custom_id": "req-1", "response": {"status_code": 200, "body": {"object": "list", "data": [{"embedding": [...], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 7}}}, "error": null}` 6. A line whose `input` was an array of N texts comes back as one row whose `data` holds N embeddings, index-aligned with the input array ## Relevant issues Fixes #35638 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4920 Resolves LIT-5123 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? "and a second combined part about rivers"}]}}} ``` Vertex job 50095132740943872 reached `JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED` and `GET /v1/batches/<id>` went validating -> in_progress -> `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null`. Vertex accepted `#` and `/` in `key` and echoed both back verbatim, and it happened to return the rows scrambled (`req-5#1`, `req-5#2`, `req-6`, `req-4#1`, `req-5#0`, `req-1`, `req-4#0`), so the reassembly was genuinely exercised `GET /v1/files/<output_file_id>/content` returned four rows, one per input entry, custom_ids bare ```json {"id": "batch_req_...", "custom_id": "req-4", "response": {"status_code": 200, "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "object": "list", "data": [{"embedding": ["...768 floats..."], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}, {"embedding": ["...768 floats..."], "index": 1, "object": "embedding"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 18, "total_tokens": 18}}}, "error": null} ``` ``` req-5 status_code=200 error=null data=3 indexes=[0,1,2] dims=[3072,3072,3072] usage.prompt_tokens=23 req-6 status_code=200 error=null data=1 indexes=[0] dims=[3072] usage.prompt_tokens=11 req-4 status_code=200 error=null data=2 indexes=[0,1] dims=[768,768] usage.prompt_tokens=18 req-1 status_code=200 error=null data=1 indexes=[0] dims=[3072] usage.prompt_tokens=7 ``` Cosine check of each position against a live online `/v1/embeddings` call for that exact text and params confirms the order follows the input array rather than the order Vertex wrote the rows in ``` req-4 data[0] cos=1.0 vs ALPHA (0.6653 vs BETA) data[1] cos=1.0 vs BETA (0.6653 vs ALPHA) req-5 data[0] cos=1.0 vs ONE data[1] cos=1.0 vs TWO data[2] cos=1.0 vs THREE ``` </details> <details><summary>After, second run at bf723fa9c1: custom_ids that collide with the fan-out key format</summary> Same setup, one batch job over a plain scalar entry `req-a`, a lookalike scalar entry whose custom_id literally is `req-a#0/2`, an array entry whose custom_id literally is `req-b#1/1` (with `dimensions: 768`), and a plain array entry `req-c` what LiteLLM wrote to GCS ```json {"key": "req-a", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "PLAIN: koalas sleep up to twenty hours a day"}]}}} {"key": "req-a%230%2F2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "LOOKALIKE: the Rosetta Stone was found in 1799"}]}}} {"key": "req-b%231%2F1#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "GAMMA: tectonic plates drift a few centimetres a year"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"key": "req-b%231%2F1#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "DELTA: the tuba is the lowest brass instrument"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"key": "req-c#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "EPSILON: honey never spoils in a sealed jar"}]}}} {"key": "req-c#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "ZETA: Mercury has no atmosphere to speak of"}]}}} ``` Vertex job 6020509242262290432 reached `JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED` with `error: null`, the batch reached `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null`, and Vertex echoed every key back byte for byte including the escapes. It returned the rows scrambled again (`req-c#1/2`, `req-b%231%2F1#0/2`, `req-b%231%2F1#1/2`, `req-a`, `req-a%230%2F2`, `req-c#0/2`) ``` req-c status_code=200 error=null data=2 indexes=[0,1] dims=[3072,3072] usage.prompt_tokens=20 req-b#1/1 status_code=200 error=null data=2 indexes=[0,1] dims=[768,768] usage.prompt_tokens=20 req-a status_code=200 error=null data=1 indexes=[0] dims=[3072] usage.prompt_tokens=11 req-a#0/2 status_code=200 error=null data=1 indexes=[0] dims=[3072] usage.prompt_tokens=15 ``` custom_ids come back byte for byte, and the lookalike stays its own row rather than folding into `req-a`: the two carry different vectors (cosine 0.5318 between them) and their own usage, 11 and 15, matching the `promptTokenCount` Vertex reported for each. Cosine per array position against online `/v1/embeddings` for the same text and params is 1.0 (0.7192 and 0.5953 against the siblings), so ordering again came from the key rather than the file </details> <details><summary>Why the per-row config sits inside request rather than in the documented embed_content_config sibling</summary> An earlier revision of this PR emitted the shape from the docs and Vertex failed the entire job, not the row: `The column or property "embed_content_config" in the specified input data is of unsupported type. Supported types for this column are: [STRING, INTEGER, FLOAT, BOOLEAN, TIMESTAMP, DATE, DATETIME, NUMERIC].` A hand-written file copied from the docs example, submitted straight to the Vertex REST API with no LiteLLM in the loop, fails identically, so that shape simply does not work against the live API today. The same fields inside the `EmbedContentRequest` succeed, and the 768-length vectors for req-4 above show the dimensionality is honored The live runs also showed usage arriving as `response.usageMetadata.promptTokenCount` rather than the documented `response.tokenCount`, which is why the transform reads the former and keeps the latter as a fallback </details> ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Legacy `text-embedding-*` predict-shape batches stay unsupported, untouched - Per-row config rides inside `request`; live Vertex rejects documented `embed_content_config` ## Changes `VertexAIFilesConfig` only ever implemented the Gemini chat batch translation. Every jsonl line of an uploaded batch file went through `_transform_request_body`, which reads `body["messages"]`, so an `/v1/embeddings` line was rewritten as ```jsonc {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-1"}}} ``` Two independent bugs there: `EmbedContentRequest` has no `contents` field (that is the `generateContent` shape), which is the 400 the customer saw on every row, and the actual embedding `input` was never read, so even the shape-correct rows would have embedded a placeholder space. `labels` is not a field on `EmbedContentRequest` either, so the `custom_id` smuggling would have been the next 400 after fixing `contents` Lines are now routed by the `url` that OpenAI puts on each one, and embeddings lines are translated into the batch shape Vertex documents for `gemini-embedding-*` at https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/embeddings/batch-prediction-genai-embeddings ```jsonc { "key": "req-1", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "hello world"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"} } ``` `content` is singular, and the `custom_id` round-trips through the top-level `key` that Vertex echoes back, so embedding rows no longer need the label trick. The docs put the per-row config in an `embed_content_config` sibling of `request`; the live API rejects that key and fails the whole job, so it goes inside the `EmbedContentRequest` instead, which is what actually works (see the proof section). The OpenAI to `EmbedContentRequest` mapping itself is the one already used by the online `embedContent` path (`transform_openai_input_gemini_embed_content`), so `dimensions`, `task_type`, `title`, and `gs://` multimodal inputs come along for free. Chat lines are untouched and keep going through `_transform_request_body` with their labels An `EmbedContentRequest` returns exactly one vector, while an OpenAI entry with an array `input` expects one embedding per element, so array entries fan out into one Vertex row per element and the element position rides along in the key as `<custom_id>#<i>/<n>` ```jsonc {"key": "req-4#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "first"}]}}} {"key": "req-4#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "second"}]}}} ``` The custom_id half of the key is percent-encoded so that a customer one which itself ends in `#<i>/<n>` cannot be read back as the tag and merged into a different entry; ordinary ids are unreserved characters and so are unchanged on the wire Scalars and single-element arrays keep a bare key, and a nested array (OpenAI's combined-parts shape) stays one row with several `parts`, since that is genuinely one embedding. On the way back the rows are grouped by the custom_id in front of the `#` and ordered by the index behind it, so one OpenAI row comes out per original entry with `data[i]` matching `input[i]` and the prompt tokens summed; Vertex returns predictions in arbitrary order, so the key is the only thing that can carry the position. If any element of an entry failed, the whole entry's row is the error row, because a partial `data` array would silently misalign every index after the gap. A missing or duplicated fan-out row errors the entry the same way: the group size rides in the key, and a group that does not come back as exactly the indexes `0..n-1` is refused rather than silently renumbered onto the wrong input positions On the way back, `_try_transform_vertex_batch_output_to_openai` gated batch detection on `candidates` / `promptFeedback` / `processed_time`, so embedding result rows failed detection and the caller got raw Vertex jsonl. They are now detected on `response.embedding` and turned into a normal OpenAI batch row whose body is an `EmbeddingResponse`, with `usageMetadata.promptTokenCount` as the usage (the documented `tokenCount` is kept as a fallback) and the model recovered from the managed GCS path since embedding rows carry no `modelVersion` Scope is the modern Gemini embedding models. The legacy `text-embedding-*` `predict` format, which has no `request` wrapper at all, stays unsupported and is left untouched rather than half-translated; happy to do it in a follow-up if we want those models on batch ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7c5c3f3f492f4bde87289f9f46caec9e Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d389d721419d486e83067a4fb76f683f <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit f2a10f6331ef99881c5529f362c154c402c58a52. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(cost): track OpenAI/Azure web search tool cost per call
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - OpenAI/Azure web search tool cost tracked as $0 on 84 models - Multiple searches in one response were charged as one call How it solves it: - Adds flat per-call search pricing to those 84 cost map entries - $0.01/call for reasoning models, $0.025/call for gpt-4.1 entries - Dated -search-preview entries inherit their undated siblings' per-query pricing, since OpenAI resolves requests to the dated id - Multiplies per-call cost by `web_search_call` items in Responses output - Usage-count providers (gemini, anthropic, xai, vertex) keep their path ## User Flow Before: a developer routing gpt-5-nano web search traffic through the proxy sees token-only cost in LiteLLM, so month-end reconciliation against the OpenAI invoice shows a growing gap 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "gpt-5-nano"` and `"tools": [{"type": "web_search"}]` 2. The 200 response's `output` array carries two completed `web_search_call` items plus the answer text 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and that request's spend equals the token cost alone, with $0 attributed to the two web searches 4. At month end the OpenAI invoice adds $10 per 1k search calls, a charge the proxy never tracked After: the same request is billed per web search call, so proxy spend matches the OpenAI invoice 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "gpt-5-nano"` and `"tools": [{"type": "web_search"}]` 2. The 200 response's `output` array carries two completed `web_search_call` items plus the answer text 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows that request's spend at token cost plus 2 x $0.01, one charge per completed web search 4. Month-end reconciliation against the OpenAI invoice lines up ## Relevant issues Fixes #31316 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5013 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two independent bugs. First, `search_context_cost_per_query` was missing from every OpenAI/Azure entry except the two `-search-preview` chat models, so the per-call fee fell back to $0 for the other 82 models that advertise `supports_web_search` (the whole gpt-5 / 5.1-5.6 line, o3, o3-pro, o4-mini, the gpt-4.1 family, deep-research models, and their Azure mirrors). OpenAI bills a flat rate per call, so all three `search_context_size` tiers are set to the same value: $0.01 per call for reasoning models (search content tokens billed at model rates) and $0.025 for the non-reasoning gpt-4.1 entries, per https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing. Second, detection was binary: a response with three searches was charged once. The per-call cost is now multiplied by the number of `web_search_call` items in the Responses output. Providers that report a request count in usage (gemini, anthropic, xai, vertex) are priced earlier from that count and never reach this path. Chat-completions responses only expose `url_citation` annotations with no count, so they floor to a single billable search Deterministic repro through the exact entrypoint the proxy uses for spend logging (`StandardBuiltInToolCostTracking.get_cost_for_built_in_tools`), feeding a `ResponsesAPIResponse` with two completed `web_search_call` items and `custom_llm_provider="openai"` ```python from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.tool_call_cost_tracking import StandardBuiltInToolCostTracking as T from litellm.types.llms.openai import ResponsesAPIResponse from litellm.types.utils import Usage from openai.types.responses.response_function_web_search import ResponseFunctionWebSearch, ActionSearch def ws(i): return ResponseFunctionWebSearch(id=i, type="web_search_call", status="completed", action=ActionSearch(type="search", query="latest news")) usage = Usage(prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=50, total_tokens=150) for model in ["gpt-5-nano", "gpt-4o-search-preview"]: resp = ResponsesAPIResponse(id="r", created_at=0, model=model, object="response", output=[ws("ws_1"), ws("ws_2")], parallel_tool_calls=False, tool_choice="auto", tools=[]) cost = T.get_cost_for_built_in_tools(model=model, response_object=resp, usage=usage, custom_llm_provider="openai") print(f"{model:24s} tracked_cost={cost} (response has 2 web_search_call items)") ``` Before (commit 7c56317edf) ``` gpt-5-nano tracked_cost=0.0 (response has 2 web_search_call items) gpt-4o-search-preview tracked_cost=0.035 (response has 2 web_search_call items) ``` After (commit 3e4669dbc5) ``` gpt-5-nano tracked_cost=0.02 (response has 2 web_search_call items) gpt-4o-search-preview tracked_cost=0.07 (response has 2 web_search_call items) ``` gpt-5-nano goes from $0 to 2 x $0.01, and gpt-4o-search-preview goes from a single $0.035 charge to 2 x $0.035 for the two searches Live end-to-end proof, real OpenAI spend through a local proxy booted from a fresh worktree per leg: before = merge base with litellm_internal_staging (f9704497fb), after = this PR's head (7e539405ed). Each leg's config holds only the two models plus a master key, and cost is read from the end-user surface, the `x-litellm-response-cost` response header, checked against token-only arithmetic from the response usage and the cost map rates Before, /v1/responses with gpt-5-nano ``` curl -sD headers.txt -X POST http://localhost:41217/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-before-5111" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5-nano","input":"Search the web and tell me the current stable Kotlin version and the latest Node.js LTS version. Use web search for each.","tools":[{"type":"web_search"}]}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0022021999999999996 output: 4 completed web_search_call items (plus reasoning/message) usage: input_tokens=21780 (cached 0), output_tokens=2783 ``` Token-only cost = 21780 x 5e-08 + 2783 x 4e-07 = 0.0022022, an exact header match: four live web searches billed $0 Before, /v1/chat/completions with gpt-4o-search-preview ``` curl -sD headers.txt -X POST http://localhost:41217/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-before-5111" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-search-preview","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What are the top tech news headlines today? Cite your sources with links."}],"web_search_options":{"search_context_size":"medium"}}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0101675 url_citation annotations: 10 usage: prompt_tokens=15 (cached 0), completion_tokens=1013 ``` Token-only cost = 15 x 2.5e-06 + 1013 x 1e-05 = 0.0101675, again exact despite ten citations: the $0.035 fee never appeared. Live QA traced this to OpenAI echoing the dated id `gpt-4o-search-preview-2025-03-11`, whose map entry had token rates but no `search_context_cost_per_query`, which is why the head commit prices the dated entries too After, /v1/responses with gpt-5-nano ``` curl -sD headers.txt -X POST http://localhost:43817/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-after-5111" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5-nano","input":"Search the web and tell me the current stable Kotlin version and the latest Node.js LTS version. Use web search for each.","tools":[{"type":"web_search"}]}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.042766 output: 4 completed web_search_call items (plus reasoning/message) usage: input_tokens=23808 (cached 0), output_tokens=3939 ``` Token-only cost = 23808 x 5e-08 + 3939 x 4e-07 = 0.002766, and the header equals 0.002766 + 4 x 0.01 to zero error: each of the four searches billed After, /v1/chat/completions with gpt-4o-search-preview (default deployment, no base_model pin) ``` curl -sD headers.txt -X POST http://localhost:43817/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-after-5111" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-search-preview","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What are the top tech news headlines today? Cite your sources with links."}],"web_search_options":{"search_context_size":"medium"}}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0449475 url_citation annotations: 10 usage: prompt_tokens=15 (cached 0), completion_tokens=991 ``` Token-only cost = 15 x 2.5e-06 + 991 x 1e-05 = 0.0099475, and the header equals 0.0099475 + 0.035 to zero error: the search fee lands on the dated id the response actually priced under An /v1/messages probe with the same web search tool confirmed the caveat below: searches run upstream (live citations in the answer) but the Anthropic-shaped translation drops the search blocks, so the header stays exactly token-only, unchanged by this PR ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Chat-completions responses expose no call count, so they still bill one search - The Anthropic-shaped /v1/messages endpoint drops OpenAI web search blocks in translation, so searches driven through it still bill token-only: a pre-existing shape gap this PR does not touch ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 0e0c3ce0d8f5841503f246f65a71524bbc677539. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: [Bug]: web_search tool cost not tracked for GPT-5 models via Responses API (search_context_cost_per_query missing from cost map)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I searched existing issues. #16996 (closed/completed — added the web-search cost *mechanism*) and #26253 (the inverse case: Gemini `url_context` over-billed as web_search) are related but do not cover this. I did not find an open issue for GPT-5 / Responses-API `web_search` being billed at $0. ### What happened? The hosted `web_search` tool cost is **not** tracked for GPT-5 (and GPT-4o) models when used via the **Responses API** (`/responses`). `x-litellm-response-cost` (and `response_cost` in logs/callbacks) covers input/output tokens only — including the often-large web-search *result* tokens that are fed back as input — but **omits OpenAI's per-call web_search fee**. Per [OpenAI's pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), the hosted web_search tool on reasoning models (gpt-5, o-series) costs **$10.00 / 1k calls** *plus* search-content tokens at model rates. LiteLLM charges the tokens but bills the per-call fee as **$0**. **Root cause:** `model_prices_and_context_window.json` has **no `search_context_cost_per_query`** for any `gpt-5*` model (nor `gpt-4o`). Only the dedicated `*-search-preview` chat models have it, so the GA `web_search` tool on gpt-5.x via `/responses` resolves to a $0 tool fee. ### Reproduction `POST /responses` with `model: openai/gpt-5-mini`, `tools: [{"type": "web_search"}]`, and a prompt that triggers searches (e.g. *"Search the web and tell me the current stable Kotlin version."*). Observed (LiteLLM **v1.83.7**): - The response `output` contained **4** `web_search_call` items (`status: completed`). - `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.007036`, which is **exactly** the token cost: `21384 input × $0.25/1M + 845 output × $2.00/1M = 0.007036`. - The 4 web searches therefore contributed **$0** to the reported cost. OpenAI bills 4 × $0.01 = **$0.04** for them — i.e. LiteLLM captured ~15% of the true cost. - Body `usage`: `input_tokens=21384`, `output_tokens=845`, with `input_tokens_details` / `output_tokens_details` (no `prompt_tokens_details.web_search_requests`). Cost-map check (current `main`): ``` gpt-5 / gpt-5-mini / gpt-5-nano / gpt-5.1 / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.4-mini-* : search_context_cost_per_query = null gpt-4o : null gpt-4o-search-preview : {low 0.03, medium 0.035, high 0.05} → 0 of 39 gpt-5* entries have web-search pricing ``` ### Expected behavior `response_cost` / `x-litellm-response-cost` should include OpenAI's per-call `web_search` fee for gpt-5.x / gpt-4o when the model invokes the tool via the Responses API — not just the token cost. ### Likely fixes 1. Add `search_context_cost_per_query` (+ `web_search_billing_unit`) to the gpt-5.x / gpt-4o entries in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` ($10/1k ⇒ ~`0.01` per query for reasoning models). 2. Confirm the Responses-API passthrough counts web_search invocations for costing: on `/responses` the count comes from `output[].type == "web_search_call"`, and the usage block uses `input_tokens_details` — not the chat-style `usage.prompt_tokens_details.web_search_requests` the [web_search docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/web_search) reference. ### LiteLLM version `v1.83.7` (cost-map gap also confirmed against `main`).

signal.title: [Feature]: per-component response cost headers (input, output, cache read, cache write, reasoning, tool usage)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature `x-litellm-response-cost` tells the caller what a request cost in total, and the sibling headers `x-litellm-response-cost-original`, `-discount-amount`, `-margin-amount`, and `-margin-percent` already expose pricing adjustments. What is missing is the split of that total across input tokens, output tokens, cache reads, cache writes, reasoning tokens, and built-in tool usage. LiteLLM already computes exactly this split for every request and records it in spend logs, so this is surfacing work rather than new accounting Proposal: for non-streaming responses, emit one header per component next to the existing total, following the naming of the current family: `x-litellm-response-cost-input`, `x-litellm-response-cost-output`, `x-litellm-response-cost-cache-read`, `x-litellm-response-cost-cache-creation`, `x-litellm-response-cost-reasoning`, and `x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage`. Reasoning cost is a subset of output cost and should be documented as such so consumers do not double count Headers over a `cost_breakdown` field on the response body, for three reasons. The values are already available at the moment response headers are assembled, which is where the discount and margin headers come from today. Headers are purely additive, so strict OpenAI-shape response parsers keep working without any opt-in flag. And the ask is scoped to non-streaming, where headers can carry final cost. An in-band breakdown for streaming can be a follow-up on top of the existing `include_cost_in_streaming_usage` mechanism The earlier ask for an input/output split in headers (#11260) was closed stale without a fix. This supersedes it with the full component set. Requested by a customer running LiteLLM as their central gateway ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a platform team fronting all LLM traffic through the LiteLLM proxy wants to show each internal app where its spend goes, but callers only ever see one total, so they rebuild the split by hand from their own pricing tables (the same dead end as #11260) 1. An app sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a prompt-cached context on a reasoning model such as gpt-5.4-nano 2. The 200 response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 7.4e-06` and the body's `usage` block carries token counts (`prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) 3. To split the total they multiply those token counts by per-model rates copied into their own pricing table, which drifts: cache-write premiums, reasoning rates, and built-in tool charges (web search, code execution) differ per provider, and tool charges never appear in `usage` at all 4. When their hand-computed components fail to sum to the header total, they cannot tell which component is wrong After this feature (ideal user flow): the same response states the split directly and it sums to the total 1. The app sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same prompt-cached context 2. The 200 response now also carries `x-litellm-response-cost-input`, `-output`, `-cache-read`, `-cache-creation`, `-reasoning`, and `-tool-usage` 3. The components sum to `x-litellm-response-cost` (reasoning being a subset of output), so the team attributes spend per component with no local pricing table ### How far you got Config the proxy ran with, plus `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, and `DATABASE_URL` in the environment (values redacted): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.4-nano litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.4-nano api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY ``` Version or commit: 9d069f21dc Commands and their full output, hitting the real OpenAI API: ``` $ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config c19_config.yaml --port 47311 $ curl -sD headers.txt -o body.json http://localhost:47311/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-5.4-nano", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with one word: hello"}]}' $ grep -i "^x-litellm-response-cost" headers.txt x-litellm-response-cost: 7.4e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 7.4e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 $ cat body.json {"id": "chatcmpl-ECcleXkHEngsdpkRwkqLYrRXh9EvZ", "created": 1786677666, "model": "gpt-5.4-nano", "object": "chat.completion", "choices": [{"finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": {"content": "hello", "role": "assistant", "provider_specific_fields": {"refusal": null}, "annotations": []}, "provider_specific_fields": {}}], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 4, "prompt_tokens": 12, "total_tokens": 16, "completion_tokens_details": {"accepted_prediction_tokens": 0, "audio_tokens": 0, "reasoning_tokens": 0, "rejected_prediction_tokens": 0}, "prompt_tokens_details": {"audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": 0}}, "service_tier": "default"} ``` What stopped me there: step 2 of the After flow dead-ends. The response exposes the total and its pricing adjustments only. No header and no body field carries the input, output, cache, reasoning, or tool components, so the split cannot be read from the response at all ### What a fix PR should look like `_get_cost_breakdown_from_logging_obj` in `litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py` already reads the fully populated `CostBreakdown` (defined in `litellm/types/utils.py` with fields `input_cost`, `output_cost`, `cache_read_cost`, `cache_creation_cost`, `reasoning_cost`, and `tool_usage_cost`) and returns only the discount and margin fields. Widen it to hand back the component fields too, emit the six new headers next to `x-litellm-response-cost` in `get_custom_headers`, and omit them when no breakdown was computed. A regression test should assert the six headers appear on a costed non-streaming response and that input plus cache read plus cache creation plus output plus tool usage equals the total, with reasoning excluded as a subset of output. The response headers docs page (`docs/proxy/response_headers.md` in the docs repo) gains the six rows ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? signal.title: feat(proxy): per-component response cost headers
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Callers only see a total request cost, never its component split - Attributing spend needs hand-copied pricing tables that drift per provider How it solves it: - Emits six `x-litellm-response-cost-*` component headers next to the total - Input, cache read, cache creation, output, and tool usage sum exactly to the total; reasoning is a subset of output - Reads the cost breakdown the proxy already computes per request - Omits component headers cleanly when no breakdown was computed - Existing cost, discount, and margin headers are unchanged ## User Flow Before: a platform team fronting all LLM traffic through the LiteLLM proxy wants to show each internal app where its spend goes, but callers only ever see one total, so they rebuild the split by hand from their own pricing tables 1. An app sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a prompt-cached context on a reasoning model such as gpt-5.4-nano 2. The 200 response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 7.4e-06` and the body's `usage` block carries token counts (`prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) 3. To split the total they multiply those token counts by per-model rates copied into their own pricing table, which drifts: cache-write premiums, reasoning rates, and built-in tool charges differ per provider, and tool charges never appear in `usage` at all 4. When their hand-computed components fail to sum to the header total, they cannot tell which component is wrong After: the same response states the split directly and it sums to the total 1. The app sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same prompt-cached context 2. The 200 response carries the same `x-litellm-response-cost` total and now also `x-litellm-response-cost-input`, `-output`, `-cache-read`, `-cache-creation`, `-reasoning`, and `-tool-usage` 3. Input plus cache read plus cache creation plus output plus tool usage equals the total, reasoning being a subset of output, so the team attributes spend per component with no local pricing table ## Relevant issues Closes #36875 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5617 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live-proxy legs with real OpenAI and Anthropic spend, no mocks. Before leg at commit c9917cbf99 (this PR's merge base), after leg re-proven at commit 05beb7abb5 (this PR's behavioral tip). Each leg booted a bootstrapped worktree with `.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port <port>` and hit all three unified endpoints: /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses with gpt-5.4-nano, /v1/messages with claude-haiku-4-5 carrying a ~6k-token `cache_control: ephemeral` system block sent twice to exercise cache creation then cache read. An earlier eight-scenario after leg at 9079e4c47b surfaced that the input header still contained the cache costs nested inside it (Cursor Bugbot flagged the same double-count); 05beb7abb5 fixed that by subtracting the cache components from the input header, the same split the Admin UI's cost breakdown viewer shows, and the leg below re-proves the final contract ### Before leg (c9917cbf99, port 41387): component headers absent everywhere ```bash curl -sD /tmp/h_a1.txt -o /tmp/b_a1.json -X POST http://localhost:41387/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @body_a.json grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost' /tmp/h_a1.txt ``` A1 and A2 (identical, 200 OK, prompt_tokens=1177, completion_tokens=4, answer "391"): ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00024040000000000002 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.00024040000000000002 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 ``` B (/v1/responses, 200 OK, input_tokens=12, output_tokens=5): ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 8.65e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 8.65e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 ``` C1 and C2 (/v1/messages; C1 cache_creation_input_tokens=6242, C2 cache_read_input_tokens=6242): ``` == c1 == x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0078345 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0078345 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 == c2 == x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0006562 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0006562 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 ``` Across all five before-leg responses, zero occurrences of `-input`, `-output`, `-cache-read`, `-cache-creation`, `-reasoning`, or `-tool-usage` ### After leg (05beb7abb5, port 46746): six component headers present and additive A1 (chat completions, gpt-5.4-nano, prompt_tokens=1417, completion_tokens=4, answer "391"; A2 byte-identical): ```bash curl -sD /tmp/ha2_a1.txt -o /tmp/ba2_a1.json -X POST http://localhost:46746/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @body_a.json grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost' /tmp/ha2_a1.txt ``` ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0002884 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0002884 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0002834 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 5e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 ``` B (/v1/responses, input_tokens=12, output_tokens=5): ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 8.65e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 2.4e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 6.25e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 ``` C1 (/v1/messages, cold cache, cache_creation_input_tokens=6242, input_tokens=12) then C2 (warm, cache_read_input_tokens=6242): ``` == c1 == x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0078345 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 1.1999999999999858e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 2e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-cache-creation: 0.0078025 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 == c2 == x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0006562 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 1.1999999999999966e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 2e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-cache-read: 0.0006242 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 ``` C1n/C2n (same shape, fresh nonce guaranteeing a cold cache; cache_creation then cache_read of 6267 tokens) behaved identically: creation 0.00783375, read 0.0006267, input 1.2e-05 on both Br (/v1/responses with `"reasoning": {"effort": "high"}`, input_tokens=25, output_tokens=175, reasoning_tokens=168): ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00022375 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 4.9999999999999996e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0.00021875 x-litellm-response-cost-reasoning: 0.00021 x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage: 0.0 ``` ### Sum invariant across all eight after-leg responses Python check over the captured header files (rel_tol 1e-9, absent header = 0). Additive = input + cache-read + cache-creation + output + tool-usage; nested = input + output + tool-usage (the pre-fix contract) | Scenario | Total | Additive holds | Nested holds | reasoning<=output | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A1 | 0.0002884 | True | True | True | | A2 | 0.0002884 | True | True | True | | B | 0.00000865 | True | True | True | | C1 | 0.0078345 | True | False | True | | C2 | 0.0006562 | True | False | True | | C1n | 0.0078658 | True | False | True | | C2n | 0.0006587 | True | False | True | | Br | 0.0002238 | True | True | True | On every cache scenario the input header is exactly the 12 uncached tokens x 1e-06 = 1.2e-05, cache creation = tokens x 1.25e-06, and cache read = tokens x 1e-07, matching Haiku 4.5 pricing to the digit (rel_tol 1e-9) **Component semantics**: `_store_cost_breakdown_in_logging_obj` in cost_calculator.py records the full prompt cost (cache pricing already applied) as input_cost, so emitting it unchanged would double-count the cache once the cache headers exist. The header path therefore subtracts cache read and cache creation from input before emitting, the exact split the Admin UI's cost breakdown viewer already shows, delivering the additive contract issue #36875 asked for: input + cache-read + cache-creation + output + tool-usage = total, reasoning a subset of output. Spend-log storage is untouched QA surprises: - Stored input nests cache costs; headers now subtract them - Nested formula now fails on cache scenarios, by design - Input header carries float noise (1.19999...e-05), subtraction artifact - No specified scenario produced reasoning tokens; added Br - OpenAI auto-cache never hit on repeat prompts - .env master key is double-quoted; strip quotes - Harness reaped backgrounded proxies twice; detached Popen fixed it ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Component headers appear on non-streaming responses only (headers leave before a stream's usage exists) - Reasoning is a subset of output, so exclude it when summing components to the total - Cache and reasoning headers appear only when those costs are nonzero - The input header is the uncached input cost; spend logs keep storing the full prompt cost (cache included) as input_cost, so the header equals stored input minus the cache components ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(anthropic): populate inference_geo from the request so regional pricing applies
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streamed Anthropic usage loses the region it was served from - Regional traffic then gets billed at global rates How it solves it: - Streaming reassembly carries `inference_geo` through - Requested region is the fallback when the response omits it ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming Anthropic traffic out of a US region sees the gateway log no region at all, so regional pricing never applies to any streamed request 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true` 2. The response streams back fine, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at the global price with no region recorded 3. They repeat it on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages with `"stream": true`, and both log the same way 4. Dropping `"stream": true` on any of the three routes does record `us`, so their spend is only correct for non-streaming traffic After: the same streamed requests record the region, so streamed and non-streamed traffic price the same way 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true` 2. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the request served from `us` 3. The same holds on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages with `"stream": true` 4. A request that asks for no region, or that Anthropic serves globally, still records `global` and prices as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4867 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Screen recording of the before and after run, in one video, is in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1786414063855749?thread_ts=1786408619.329699&cid=C0BE49SAUE6). It captured the before at `1d3b64c66f` (current `litellm_internal_staging`) and the after at `82a64de9a2`, and reproduced the runs below Live proxy against the real Anthropic API, real spend, `claude-opus-4-8`, one request per route with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true`. Region and cost were read off the standard logging payload ```bash H=(-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01') curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions "${H[@]}" -d @chat_geo_stream.json curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d @msg_geo_stream.json curl -sS localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d @pt_geo_stream.json ``` Before, at `1d3b64c66f`, every streamed route drops the region: ``` route=acompletion geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 route=anthropic_messages geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 route=pass_through_endpoint geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 ``` After, at `82a64de9a2`, all three keep it: ``` route=acompletion geo=us cost=0.14788949999999998 route=anthropic_messages geo=us cost=0.14788949999999998 route=pass_through_endpoint geo=us cost=0.14799949999999998 ``` The cost barely moves because the uplift itself is #34850, and the point here is that without the region reaching cost calculation that PR can never fire on streamed traffic. The same three routes without `"stream": true` already recorded `us` before this change, on this branch they still do ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Merged with `litellm_internal_staging`, absorbing the #36447 speed plumbing - Cache tokens still miss the geo uplift until #34850 lands ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/13d7b3dbf5a641f0a24aa0b48893d315 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit d88193eea52b0095df6bb61d83179608497c9350. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: feat(proxy): auto-suppress the no-Redis banner for confirmed single-worker deployments
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Single-worker proxies still get the "No Redis configured" banner - Hiding it today needs an env var plus a full restart How it solves it: - Each worker upserts a heartbeat row into the database every 60s - Readiness counts live workers and hides the banner at exactly 1 - Two or more live workers, or an unknown count, still warn - Multi-pod and multi-worker are caught by the same census - LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING override behaves exactly as before ## User Flow Before: an admin running a single-worker proxy with no Redis sees a warning banner they can only hide with an env var and a restart 1. The admin starts the proxy with one worker, a Postgres database, and no Redis configured 2. They open http://localhost:4000/ui and the dashboard's call to GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness/details comes back with `"show_no_redis_warning": true` 3. A red banner reads "No Redis configured. Redis is highly recommended" even though a single worker has nothing to share over Redis 4. The only way to hide it is to set `LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING=true` and restart the whole deployment After: the same single-worker deployment shows no banner at all, and the banner still comes back on its own the moment a second worker appears 1. The admin starts the proxy with one worker, a Postgres database, and no Redis configured 2. They open http://localhost:4000/ui and GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness/details now returns `"show_no_redis_warning": false`, so no banner renders 3. They later scale to two workers, or a second pod sharing the same database, and within a couple of minutes a refresh shows the banner again, since limits and budgets now really are split across workers 4. signal.title: feat(ui): direction picker and reverse-mode display for shadow evals
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - #36865 added reverse shadow evals, but only over the raw API - The dashboard form pins direction to forward with no controls - Reverse jobs would render with forward labels, inverting every win rate How it solves it: - Start form gains a direction picker and a baseline model picker - Baseline is required in reverse mode and never sent in forward - Job cards, verdict bar, and slice tables label arms per direction ## User Flow Before: an operator whose key already runs on an auto-router wants to check the router still beats a strong fixed model, and the dashboard offers no way to ask 1. They open http://localhost:3000/cost-optimization and click the Shadow evals tab 2. The "Start a shadow eval" form shows key, auto-router, sampling, duration, turn budget, and judge fields only; every eval it can start asks the adoption question 3. To run a regression check they must hand-craft a POST to http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start with `"direction": "reverse"` and `"baseline_model": "..."` 4. When that job appears on the page it reads "Shadowing 10% via my-router" with columns "Router wins" and "Current model wins", and the numbers under them are swapped: the router's own wins sit in the "Current model wins" column After: the same operator starts and reads a reverse eval entirely from the page 1. They open http://localhost:3000/cost-optimization and click the Shadow evals tab 2. The form now leads with a Direction picker; they choose "Regression check: router's picks vs a baseline" and the copy under the title switches to describe re-running the router's traffic against a fixed baseline 3. A "Baseline model" picker appears and the Start button stays disabled until they choose one; forward mode never shows the picker 4. They pick a baseline, start the job, and the card reads "Comparing my-router to openai/gpt-4o on 10% of its traffic" 5. The headline says "Router matched or beat the baseline", the bar legend shows "Router won / Tie / Baseline won", and slice tables show "Router wins" and "Baseline wins" with each number under the arm that earned it ## Relevant issues - Frontend follow-up to #36865, which added the reverse direction to the API and pinned the dashboard to forward ## Linear ticket Part of LIT-5538 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix UI change, QA runbook to capture screenshots: 1. Open http://localhost:3000/cost-optimization and click the Shadow evals tab 3. In "Start a shadow eval", confirm the Direction field shows "Adoption check: key's traffic vs the router" and no Baseline model field is visible 4. Switch Direction to "Regression check: router's picks vs a baseline"; the description under the title changes and a Baseline model picker appears, with the Start button disabled until it is filled 5. Fill key, auto-router, baseline, and judge, click Start shadow eval, then send a few chat completions through the auto-router with that key 6. The job card should read "Comparing <router> to <baseline> on 10% of its traffic" and, once verdicts land, the headline "Router matched or beat the baseline" with "Baseline wins" columns ## Type 🆕 New Feature
