signal.title: fix(anthropic): preserve document blocks during guardrail write-back
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Guardrail write-back turns PDF `document` blocks into invalid `image` blocks - Anthropic rejects the request with a 400 for `application/pdf` How it solves it: - Route supported document data URIs through the existing file conversion path - Keep ordinary image data URIs on the existing image conversion path ## User Flow Before: a native Anthropic request containing a PDF fails after a message-mutating guardrail runs 1. The user sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages` with a base64 PDF `document` block 2. A configured pre-call guardrail modifies the structured messages 3. Anthropic receives the PDF as an `image` block with `application/pdf` and returns HTTP 400 After: the same request keeps its document type through guardrail write-back 1. The user sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages` with a base64 PDF `document` block 2. A configured pre-call guardrail modifies the structured messages 3. Anthropic receives the PDF as a `document` block with its original media type ## Relevant issues Fixes #36524 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes the focused lint, format, and unit checks - [x] My PR's scope is isolated to this document write-back bug - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The pure conversion path does not require provider credentials. At the base commit `7e80e094c4d3447007d175ed72a5e85880bc62a4`, the reported PDF data URI produced `type: image` and the regression test failed At commit `35912a2fb89e45dfdf2c045153131b005c0257b2`, the same conversion produced: ```text {'type': 'document', 'source': {'type': 'base64', 'media_type': 'application/pdf', 'data': 'AAAA'}} ``` The same run kept `data:image/png;base64,AAAA` as an Anthropic `image` block Focused checks: ```text 92 passed in 0.80s 5 passed in 2.06s ``` ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) The change covers base64 `application/pdf` and `text/plain` document data URIs. URL-backed documents are outside this write-back path ### Final Attestation - [x] The regression test fails on the base revision and passes with this fix

signal.title: fix(responses): preserve Bedrock Mantle validation errors
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock Mantle validation failures reach callers as status 500 - The upstream 400 response is treated like a connection failure How it solves it: - Routes Bedrock Mantle through the existing Bedrock status mapping - Preserves `BadRequestError`, status 400, and the upstream message ## User Flow Before: a Responses API caller receives the wrong error class for an invalid request 1. They send `POST https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/openai/v1/responses` with a Responses request 2. Mantle rejects the request with HTTP 400 and an `invalid_request_error` body 3. The caller receives `APIConnectionError` with status 500 and cannot distinguish validation from connectivity After: the same invalid request is reported as a client error 1. They send `POST https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/openai/v1/responses` with the same Responses request 2. Mantle rejects the request with HTTP 400 and an `invalid_request_error` body 3. The caller receives `BadRequestError` with status 400 and the upstream validation message ## Relevant issues Addresses the error-classification portion of #36546 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The before run was captured against commit `bea31871fc` with a mocked HTTP 400 response. Both sync and async `litellm.responses()` paths raised `APIConnectionError` with status 500 The after run was captured against commit `f6f6044e09` with the same mocked HTTP 400 response. Both paths raised `BadRequestError` with status 400 and preserved `Invalid 'input'` Targeted regression tests passed: `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py -q` -> 63 passed `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/bedrock_mantle/test_bedrock_mantle_responses_transformation.py -q` -> 116 passed No live Bedrock credentials were available in this environment, so I did not include a live provider run ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) Live Bedrock verification still needs to run with provider credentials This PR covers the 400-to-500 error masking. Input-item normalization remains a separate concern ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR AI assistance: this patch was prepared and tested with AI coding assistance. signal.title: fix(router): stop get_router_model_info from wiping cached pricing
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/model/info` silently drops built-in pricing after traffic - Each worker loses prices for models it served - Deployment pricing defaults overwrite the shared cost cache How it solves it: - Merge deployment `model_info` into a copy, not the cached dict - Drop unset (`None`) deployment values before merging - Regression tests pin both, and fail without the fix ## User Flow Before: an admin who opens the models page after the proxy has served traffic sees pricing vanish for exactly the models people used, and repeated reads disagree with each other 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/model/info with their key and read real `input_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_token` and `cache_read_input_token_cost` values for every model 2. Someone sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets a normal 200 back 3. They send the same GET https://litellm-domain/model/info again and those three pricing fields are now missing from the model they just used 4. With more than one worker, refreshing https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models flips between prices shown and prices missing, depending on which worker answers, and restarting the pods only hides it until traffic returns After: the models page keeps reporting the same prices no matter how much traffic has gone through, or which worker answers 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/model/info with their key and read the same three pricing fields 2. Someone sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets a normal 200 back 3. They send the same GET https://litellm-domain/model/info again and the pricing fields are unchanged 4. Refreshing https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models gives one consistent answer across workers and pods ## Relevant issues Fixes #36980 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, real Anthropic calls (real $), one worker, no mocks. Config was a single `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` deployment with no pricing overrides Before, at `870a8cf764` (tip of `litellm_internal_staging`): ```bash curl -sS http://localhost:4000/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq -c '.data[] | {model_name, i: .model_info.input_cost_per_token, o: .model_info.output_cost_per_token, c: .model_info.cache_read_input_token_cost}' curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"sonnet","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with OK"}],"max_tokens":5}' | jq -c '{ok:(.choices|length>0)}' curl -sS http://localhost:4000/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq -c '.data[] | {model_name, i: .model_info.input_cost_per_token, o: .model_info.output_cost_per_token, c: .model_info.cache_read_input_token_cost}' ``` ```text {"model_name":"sonnet","i":3e-06,"o":1.5e-05,"c":3e-07} {"ok":true} {"model_name":"sonnet","i":null,"o":null,"c":null} ``` After, at `48de8106ef` (this branch), same three commands: ```text {"model_name":"sonnet","i":3e-06,"o":1.5e-05,"c":3e-07} {"ok":true} {"model_name":"sonnet","i":3e-06,"o":1.5e-05,"c":3e-07} ``` Cost tracking itself was never affected, `x-litellm-response-cost: 9e-05` on the same requests either way, since spend calculation reads a separate cache entry ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Explicit `null` in a deployment's `model_info` no longer clears a built-in price Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cabdacbe36e341778558bfaf83fd5507

signal.title: feat(bedrock): forward LiteLLM identity and metadata into Bedrock requestMetadata
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock spend cannot be attributed to a LiteLLM key or team - LiteLLM identity is never forwarded into Bedrock request metadata - Invoke has no request-metadata support at all How it solves it: - Opt-in allow-list forwards identity into Bedrock request metadata - Converse body plus a signed header on both Invoke paths - Identity gets its slots first, caller keys fill the rest ## User Flow Before: a platform team paying one shared AWS bill for Bedrock cannot tell which LiteLLM team spent what, so chargeback stalls 1. A developer on the `platform-eng` team sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bedrock-converse"` using their virtual key, and attaches `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"cost_center":"cc-42"}` 2. The call returns 200 and a normal completion 3. The finance owner opens AWS Cost Explorer, groups Bedrock cost by request metadata, and finds nothing to group on: no key, no team, no cost centre reaches AWS 4. The same request on `"model": "bedrock-invoke"` and on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages behaves identically, so no Bedrock surface carries attribution 5. Reconciling the AWS bill against LiteLLM's own spend report means exporting proxy logs and joining them by timestamp After: the same requests carry the key alias, the team alias and the caller's cost centre into the AWS billing record, so Cost Explorer can group Bedrock spend by team 1. The proxy admin adds `bedrock_request_metadata_fields` to `litellm_settings` naming the fields to forward, then restarts the proxy 2. The same developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bedrock-converse"` and the same `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` header 3. The call still returns 200 and a normal completion 4. The finance owner groups Bedrock cost in AWS Cost Explorer and sees `user_api_key_alias=chargeback-demo-key`, `user_api_key_team_alias=platform-eng` and `cost_center=cc-42` on that spend 5. The same request on `"model": "bedrock-invoke"` and on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages produces the same attribution, so every Bedrock surface reconciles 6. A developer who tries to pass `user_api_key_org_alias` in their own metadata header cannot: that name is reserved, their value is dropped, and it never reaches the billing record ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5327 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs captured at `eb71df5cbe`. No AWS credentials are reachable from this environment (`grep -ic aws .env` returns 0 against a positive control of 2 for `api_key`), so a local HTTP server stood in for the Bedrock runtime endpoint and recorded every outbound request in full. What is MEASURED here is the real wire body, the real outbound headers and the real SigV4 `SignedHeaders` list produced by the proxy. What is SIMULATED is only Bedrock's acceptance of them. Setup, identical for both runs, with a Postgres on a namespaced port so the key and team aliases are real rows rather than fixtures: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/team/new \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5327-master" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_alias":"platform-eng"}' # -> {"team_id":"3a300c89-dcfb-4258-a13a-93c1905c9dc0","team_alias":"platform-eng",...} curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/key/generate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5327-master" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"key_alias":"chargeback-demo-key","team_id":"3a300c89-dcfb-4258-a13a-93c1905c9dc0","models":["bedrock-converse","bedrock-invoke"]}' # -> {"key":"sk-A-ExK5ZiL4IJh01UW7PQIg",...} ``` The three requests, driven identically against both configs. Note the caller deliberately tries to forge a proxy-namespaced key in leg 1: ```bash # 1. Converse, /v1/chat/completions (metadata variable name is `metadata` on this route) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-A-ExK5ZiL4IJh01UW7PQIg" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"cost_center":"cc-42","user_api_key_org_alias":"forged-by-caller"}' \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-converse","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"user":"end-user-7"}' # 2. Invoke, /v1/chat/completions curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-A-ExK5ZiL4IJh01UW7PQIg" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"cost_center":"cc-42"}' \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-invoke","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' # 3. Invoke, /v1/messages (metadata variable name is `litellm_metadata` on this route) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-A-ExK5ZiL4IJh01UW7PQIg" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"cost_center":"cc-42"}' \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-invoke","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` BEFORE, no `bedrock_request_metadata_fields` in `litellm_settings`. All three return `http=200` and nothing is forwarded, which is the negative control for default-off: ``` PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1%3A0/converse [Converse body] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = None SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0/invoke [Invoke, /v1/chat/completions] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = None SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0/invoke [Invoke, /v1/messages] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = None SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date ``` AFTER, with the allow-list set: ```yaml litellm_settings: bedrock_request_metadata_fields: - user_api_key_alias - user_api_key_team_alias - user_api_key_end_user_id - spend_logs_metadata ``` ``` PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1%3A0/converse [Converse body] body.requestMetadata = {"user_api_key_alias": "chargeback-demo-key", "user_api_key_team_alias": "platform-eng", "user_api_key_end_user_id": "end-user-7", "cost_center": "cc-42"} X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = None SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0/invoke [Invoke, /v1/chat/completions] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = {"user_api_key_alias":"chargeback-demo-key","user_api_key_team_alias":"platform-eng","cost_center":"cc-42"} SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date;x-amzn-bedrock-request-metadata PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0/invoke [Invoke, /v1/messages] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = {"user_api_key_alias":"chargeback-demo-key","user_api_key_team_alias":"platform-eng","cost_center":"cc-42"} SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date;x-amzn-bedrock-request-metadata ``` Three things to read off that capture. The header lands inside the SigV4 signature on both Invoke legs, which is what Bedrock requires for `X-Amzn-Bedrock-*`. Leg 3 works at all only because the resolver reads `litellm_metadata`, since `/v1/messages` is a `LITELLM_METADATA_ROUTES` route where the plain `metadata` key does not exist. And the `user_api_key_org_alias` the caller tried to forge in leg 1 is absent from the outbound body, so the reserved namespace holds on the wire and not just in unit tests. The full recorded Converse body, so the field is visible in place rather than as a summary: ```json { "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "hi"}]}], "inferenceConfig": {}, "requestMetadata": { "user_api_key_alias": "chargeback-demo-key", "user_api_key_team_alias": "platform-eng", "user_api_key_end_user_id": "end-user-7", "cost_center": "cc-42" } } ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Cost Explorer grouping is advisory on client keys, trustworthy on identity - Shared Vertex and Bedrock billing-label helper is deliberate follow-up - A concurrent PR edits the same import block - No admin UI: no generic editor for `litellm_settings` exists ## Notes for the reviewer Security bounds, since this forwards caller-influenced strings into an AWS billing record. `spend_logs_metadata` arrives from the `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` request header and is fully caller-controlled, so any virtual key holder can write chosen strings into CloudTrail and into the dimension AWS bills on, which is a different retention, access and deletion boundary than LiteLLM's own spend logs. The bounds are that the whole feature defaults off, the forwarded field set is an operator allow-list, the entire `user_api_key_` prefix is reserved against caller keys rather than only the fields the proxy happens to set, the client slot budget is capped explicitly at 16 minus the reserved count so the ordering invariant survives a refactor that reorders the merge, auto-injected values that violate Bedrock's constraints are dropped rather than sanitised or rejected, and `user_api_key_user_email` is separately opt-in because it is PII crossing into an audit store the AWS account retains on its own schedule. Cost Explorer grouping should be read as trustworthy on the reserved identity keys and advisory on every client key, since the caller cannot be relied on for uniqueness or truthfulness of anything they supply. Drop rather than raise, for auto-injected values only. `_validate_request_metadata` raises `BadRequestError`, which stays exactly as it is for a value the caller typed. Applying it to auto-injected identity would turn a working request into a 400 the moment an operator flips the setting on, for something as ordinary as a team alias with an apostrophe. Sanitising is worse than dropping, because a silently rewritten attribution key still looks authoritative in the billing report. No admin UI, deliberately. Repo convention is that a new user-facing setting should be reachable from the dashboard. This one is a global `litellm_settings` key and there is no generic editor for arbitrary `litellm_settings` keys today, so the alternative would be a purpose-built field for a single boolean-ish list. Reading this as a missed requirement would be wrong. Bedrock-local resolver rather than a shared Vertex and Bedrock lift, deliberately. Vertex does something structurally similar in `vertex_request_labels_from_litellm_params`, but it forwards only client-supplied `requester_metadata` and no proxy identity at all, which `grep -rl user_api_key --include="*.py" litellm/llms/vertex_ai/` confirms returns zero files against a control of two for `requester_metadata`. Lifting the resolver would therefore start a brand new PII-into-a-provider-billing-store path for Vertex as a side effect of a refactor, which deserves its own review rather than riding along here. The constraint models do not rhyme either: GCP labels are lowercase-only, 63 characters, up to 64 of them, while Bedrock allows 16 pairs of 256 characters over a class that permits uppercase and `@$#=/+`. The shared lift is real follow-up work, just not this PR. One coordination note: a concurrent PR edits the import block at the top of `litellm/llms/bedrock/messages/invoke_transformations/anthropic_claude3_transformation.py`. This PR only appends one import line there and reorders nothing, but whoever merges second should check the imports by hand rather than trusting a green auto-merge. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 6384bcde56260e165e6652759a7f3ab305bbd5d9. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: test(e2e): replay a real tool-search assistant turn back to Bedrock Invoke
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - tool_search coverage stopped after the first turn - No test ever replayed a `server_tool_use` block back - A beta-header gap reached a customer unseen How it solves it: - Second probe replays the real assistant turn as history - Refuses to pass unless both server-tool blocks replayed - Harness tests cover the assertion's red paths - Test-only, no production code ## User Flow Before: a developer running Claude Code against a Bedrock Invoke deployment gets one good turn and then a 400 on the next, and nothing in our suite would have caught it 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with a `tool_search_tool_regex_20251119` tool and get 200 back, carrying a `server_tool_use` block and the `tool_search_tool_result` answering it 2. They keep the conversation going, so the next POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages repeats those two blocks in `messages` with the same tools declared 3. If the gateway or the upstream mishandles those blocks, the turn fails and the session is dead from turn two onward, with a green compatibility matrix saying tool search works After: the same second turn is exercised on every matrix run, so the failure surfaces in CI instead of in a session 1. The matrix sends the same first POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and takes the real answer back 2. It sends a second POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages carrying that answer verbatim in `messages`, with the tools still declared, answering any pending tool call with the id the model actually returned 3. A non-200 on that second turn turns the tool_search x Bedrock Invoke cell red and names which turn broke 4. A first turn that never produced the two blocks also turns the cell red rather than passing on an empty history ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5326 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at `38eefb8c36`. No AWS credentials are available in this environment, so the Bedrock two-turn 200 is not run here; what follows is the request the probe puts on the wire, driven through the real Bedrock Invoke transform, plus a live confirmation of the same history against Anthropic direct The first turn is a real 200 from `api.anthropic.com` on `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` with `anthropic-beta: advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`, and its answer is fed through the shipped helper to build turn 2 ``` turn 1 -> 200 turn 1 stop_reason: end_turn turn 1 block types: ['text', 'server_tool_use', 'tool_search_tool_result', 'text'] replayed server-tool block types: ['server_tool_use', 'tool_search_tool_result'] turn 2 (replayed history) -> 200 { "model": "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "done"}], "stop_reason": "end_turn", "usage": {"input_tokens": 1257, "output_tokens": 4} } ``` Both bodies then go through the real `AmazonAnthropicClaudeMessagesConfig.transform_anthropic_messages_request` for `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, printing what Bedrock Invoke would receive. Turn 1 is what the existing probe already sends ```json { "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "If you have a tool to discover other tools, use it to find one. Otherwise reply with the word 'done'."} ], "max_tokens": 1024, "tools": [ {"type": "tool_search_tool_regex_20251119", "name": "tool_search_tool_regex"}, {"name": "add_numbers", "description": "Add two integers", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"a": {"type": "integer"}, "b": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["a", "b"]}} ], "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "anthropic_beta": ["tool-search-tool-2025-10-19"] } -- anthropic_version injected (positive control): True -- server_tool_use: False -- tool_search_tool_result: False -- tool_search_tool_regex_20251119: True ``` Turn 2 is the new one, and this is the whole point of the PR: the history really does carry `server_tool_use` and `tool_search_tool_result` with the real `srvtoolu_` id ```json { "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "If you have a tool to discover other tools, use it to find one. Otherwise reply with the word 'done'."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "I have a tool to discover other tools! Let me use it to search for available tools."}, {"type": "server_tool_use", "id": "srvtoolu_01Bq6v3jWFBhPuWokbvpg4iM", "name": "tool_search_tool_regex", "input": {"pattern": ".*"}}, {"type": "tool_search_tool_result", "tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01Bq6v3jWFBhPuWokbvpg4iM", "content": {"type": "tool_search_tool_search_result", "tool_references": [{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "tool_search_tool_regex"}, {"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "add_numbers"}]}}, {"type": "text", "text": "Great! I found the available tools: ..."} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": "Thanks. Now reply with the word 'done'."} ], "max_tokens": 64, "tools": [ {"type": "tool_search_tool_regex_20251119", "name": "tool_search_tool_regex"}, {"name": "add_numbers", "description": "Add two integers", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"a": {"type": "integer"}, "b": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["a", "b"]}} ], "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "anthropic_beta": ["tool-search-tool-2025-10-19"] } -- anthropic_version injected (positive control): True -- server_tool_use: True -- tool_search_tool_result: True -- tool_search_tool_regex_20251119: True ``` Negative control, a plain user message with no tools through the same transform, showing none of the blocks appear and that the True's above are not printed unconditionally ```json { "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello world"}], "max_tokens": 1024, "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "anthropic_beta": ["tool-search-tool-2025-10-19"] } -- anthropic_version injected (positive control): True -- server_tool_use: False -- tool_search_tool_result: False -- tool_search_tool_regex_20251119: False ``` The assertion's red paths never run in a green cell, so they get markerless harness tests. Mutating the missing-block check to `frozenset()` fails two of them, and the same run caught a real `NameError` in the rejection branch before this was pushed ``` tests/e2e/claude_code/_probe_unit_tests/test_http_probe.py ....... 7 passed in 0.01s ``` Both live tests collect, and the new cell is a known registry id (`python -m coverage_registry.collector --strict` exits 0 and does not list it as uncovered) ``` claude_code/tool_search/test_bedrock_invoke.py::test_tool_search_bedrock_invoke claude_code/tool_search/test_bedrock_invoke.py::test_tool_search_history_bedrock_invoke 2 tests collected in 0.02s ``` ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Not run against Bedrock here: no AWS credentials - Anthropic direct accepts the replayed history, 200 - No CI job runs `tests/e2e/claude_code`; the matrix is driven manually - First turn needs 1024 max_tokens; 64 truncates the pair ## QA runbook - tests/e2e/claude_code/tool_search/test_bedrock_invoke.py::test_tool_search_history_bedrock_invoke - a real `server_tool_use` plus `tool_search_tool_result` pair, replayed as history with the tools still declared, is accepted by Bedrock Invoke on all three Claude tiers - [ ] Needs AWS credentials for Bedrock and a proxy fronting the `claude-haiku-4-5-bedrock-invoke`, `claude-sonnet-4-5-bedrock-invoke` and `claude-opus-4-7-bedrock-invoke` deployments, with `LITELLM_PROXY_URL` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` exported - [ ] POST /v1/messages with `max_tokens: 1024`, a `tool_search_tool_regex_20251119` tool plus one ordinary tool, and a prompt telling the model to discover its tools; expect 200 whose `content` holds a `server_tool_use` block and the `tool_search_tool_result` answering it - [ ] POST /v1/messages again with the same tools and three messages: the original user prompt, that assistant `content` array verbatim, and a follow-up user turn; expect 200 - [ ] Repeat both steps for the other two tiers - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 38eefb8c361b96627d2c5fa1843929e85b1d7156. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(pricing): add the Vertex AI Gemini Live GA models and correct the preview
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Both GA Vertex Live models are absent, so sessions bill $0 - The existing preview entry under-prices text input by 40% How it solves it: - Add `gemini-live-2.5-flash` and `gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio` - Correct the preview to the published $0.50 input rate ## Relevant issues Fixes #31087 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Vertex AI serves two GA Live models and neither had a cost map entry, so every Live session billed $0. This is the missing-entry half of #31087. **Which models actually exist.** Probed by opening a real `BidiGenerateContent` socket and sending a `setup` per candidate, across 22 Vertex locations, with `definitely-not-a-real-model` as a negative control: ``` gemini-live-2.5-flash global only (11 regional locations refuse it) gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio 11 regions, not global gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview-native-audio-09-2025 us-central1 only definitely-not-a-real-model absent everywhere ``` No Gemini 3.x Live exists on Vertex in any location tested, which matches Google documenting 3.x Live as Developer-API only. The two endpoints are disjoint: the half-cascade model is global-only and the native-audio model is regional-only. **Before**, dev gateway at `7c6ba0a990`, a real voice session on `vertex_ai/gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio` produced audio and a correct transcript, and its spend row read `$0.00000000` because the model resolved to no entry at all. **After**, dev gateway at `ec9d9abfa2`, the same sessions on both GA models bill from `/spend/logs/v2`: ``` vertex_ai/gemini-live-2.5-flash (16 in / 30 out) $0.000318 vertex_ai/gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio (16 in / 60 out) $0.000668 ``` **The preview correction.** The existing `gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview-native-audio-09-2025` entry prices text input at `3e-07`. That is `gemini-2.5-flash`'s rate, not the Live API's. Google publishes $0.50 per 1M for Live text input, and the entry's other three columns already match the Live table ($3 input audio, $2 output text, $12 output audio), so the one odd column reads as a copy from the wrong sibling. Corrected on that entry and its `gemini/` twin. `supported_output_modalities` on the native-audio entries is now audio only, because Vertex closes the socket when `responseModalities` asks for TEXT on those models, verified directly: ``` native-audio, TEXT only -> REJECTED close=1000 native-audio, TEXT + AUDIO -> REJECTED close=1000 native-audio, AUDIO -> ACCEPTED (setupComplete) half-cascade, TEXT only -> ACCEPTED (setupComplete) ``` `supported_regions` comes from those same probes, ordered so a caller in an unsupported region falls back to `us-central1` rather than an arbitrary first entry. Note it lists `us-west4`, which Google's own region table omits but which answers `setupComplete`, so the list is empirical rather than transcribed. A live call is the proof here rather than `get_model_info` alone, since the failure mode was a billed-at-zero session rather than a lookup error. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Adds `gemini-live-2.5-flash` (half-cascade, global) and `gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio` (native audio, regional), each as a bare key and a `vertex_ai/` key, in both cost map files. Corrects the 09-2025 preview entry and its `gemini/` twin: `input_cost_per_token` `3e-07` to `5e-07`, and `supported_output_modalities` to audio only. Sets `mode` to `realtime` on the Gemini Live entries that said `chat` while listing only `/v1/realtime` in `supported_endpoints`, so health checks select the realtime probe. OpenAI's `gpt-audio` family is deliberately untouched: those genuinely also serve `/v1/chat/completions`, so `chat` is right for them. `gemini/gemini-robotics-er-2-streaming-preview` has the same `mode` mismatch and is left alone as out of scope. No new test, per the cost-map convention; the existing cost suite is the verification. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(fireworks_ai): translate NIM/vLLM extra params to Fireworks-native args
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - NIM/vLLM clients send extras Fireworks names differently or historically rejected - The legacy `/v1/completions` path 500'd on `reasoning_effort` and `response_format` How it solves it: - Translates truncate, reasoning, and guided-decoding extras to Fireworks-native params - Strips extras with no Fireworks equivalent, with a debug log - On conflicts the Fireworks-native value silently wins, matching the Fireworks gateway - Applies the same translation on the text completion path, fixing its 500 - Drops `reasoning_effort: "auto"`; omitting it already means the model default ## User Flow Before: chat requests carry the NIM/vLLM knobs, but the legacy completions endpoint dies with a 500 inside the gateway 1. Point an existing NIM/vLLM OpenAI-compatible client at the gateway and send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with a Fireworks model, `truncate_prompt_tokens: 4096`, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`, and a `guided_json` schema 2. The 200 reply honors the knobs: thinking is off and the content is valid JSON matching the schema (the Fireworks API accepts the NIM/vLLM names natively as of 2026-08-13; when this PR was opened they were ignored or rejected) 3. Send the NIM/vLLM knobs to the legacy `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/completions` with a `prompt` plus `reasoning_effort: "low"` and `best_of: 2`, and the call dies with `500 AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'reasoning_effort'` before ever reaching Fireworks After: the same client works on both endpoints 1. Point an existing NIM/vLLM OpenAI-compatible client at the gateway and send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with a Fireworks model, `truncate_prompt_tokens: 4096`, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`, and a `guided_json` schema 2. The 200 reply honors the knobs: thinking is off and the content is valid JSON matching the schema (now guaranteed by the gateway's own translation to the Fireworks-native names, not by the provider tolerating the NIM/vLLM ones) 3. The same legacy `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/completions` request returns 200 with the completion text ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5322 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix QA run 2026-08-13, real Fireworks API calls. Before leg: proxy booted from `litellm_internal_staging` tip `9d069f21dc` (no PR). After leg: proxy booted from the PR at `6b3977472b`. Both used the same config and the same curls: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: fw-glm litellm_params: model: fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p2 - model_name: fw-oss litellm_params: model: fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/gpt-oss-120b ``` Step 1, chat completions with the NIM/vLLM knobs: ``` curl -s http://localhost:<port>/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{ "model": "fw-glm", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Greet me."}], "max_tokens": 2048, "truncate_prompt_tokens": 4096, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}, "guided_json": {"type": "object", "properties": {"greeting": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["greeting"]} }' ``` Before `9d069f21dc` (200, knobs honored natively by the Fireworks API, which forwards them verbatim): ```json {"id":"chatcmpl-be20817e633346ea934002077acb224a","created":1786679063,"model":"fw-glm","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"{
"greeting": "Hello! It's a pleasure to meet you. How can I assist you today?"
}","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":25,"prompt_tokens":10,"total_tokens":35,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}}} ``` After `6b3977472b` (200, knobs honored via the gateway's translation to `prompt_truncate_len` / `reasoning_effort` / `response_format`): ```json {"id":"chatcmpl-78a484e082a64fbab186e6746e3ee9a2","created":1786679138,"model":"fw-glm","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"{
"greeting": "Welcome."
}","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":10,"prompt_tokens":10,"total_tokens":20,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}}} ``` Step 2, `reasoning_effort: "auto"` (a NIM client default): 200 on both legs. The upstream 400 "Invalid reasoning effort: auto" this PR originally worked around no longer reproduces; Fireworks accepts `auto` server-side now, and the after leg's dropping of the param is behaviorally equivalent Step 3, legacy completions endpoint: ``` curl -s http://localhost:<port>/v1/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{ "model": "fw-oss", "prompt": "Say hi in one word", "max_tokens": 60, "reasoning_effort": "low", "truncate_prompt_tokens": 4096, "best_of": 2, "top_k": 40, "min_tokens": 2 }' ``` Before `9d069f21dc` (500, dies inside the gateway before reaching Fireworks): ```json {"error":{"message":"litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'reasoning_effort'. Received Model Group=fw-oss
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` After `6b3977472b` (200): ```json {"id":"cmpl-8fec9c5d836f4a86a7f3e571dba53bde","object":"text_completion","created":1786679144,"model":"fw-oss","choices":[{"finish_reason":"length","index":0,"text":"." Output: "Hi"

Thus we may just output something like "Sure!"

...","logprobs":null}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":60,"prompt_tokens":5,"total_tokens":65}} ``` Supporting probes, same two proxies: `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` alone returns 200 with no `reasoning_content` on both legs, and a chat request carrying strip-list params (`best_of`, `stop_token_ids`, `skip_special_tokens`, `nvext`) returns 200 on both legs, so the chat-side translation changes no user-visible behavior today; it pins the documented semantics gateway-side instead of relying on the provider tolerating the NIM/vLLM names Note on `reasoning_effort: "none"`: this mirrors Fireworks' own documented normalization of `false` -> `"none"` (https://docs.fireworks.ai/api-reference/post-completions). Models that cannot disable reasoning (GPT-OSS, MiniMax M2) return the same "Invalid reasoning effort: none" 400 they would return for a direct `reasoning_effort=false`, which is consistent with first-party behavior QA observations: - Fireworks chat API now honors NIM/vLLM param names natively - `reasoning_effort: "auto"` no longer 400s upstream; drop stays harmless - Chat translation is now parity, not a fix; PR leaves behavior identical - The completions-path 500 fix is the PR's real behavioral delta QA run 2026-08-14, real Fireworks API calls, same config, for the follow-up commit `3b2ed3c018` (extra_body precedence, flagged by Bugbot). Before leg: proxy booted from `6b3977472b`. After leg: proxy booted from `3b2ed3c018`. Repro, sent to both endpoints: ``` curl -s http://localhost:<port>/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{ "model": "fw-glm", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in one word."}], "max_tokens": 300, "extra_body": {"thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 1024}, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}} }' ``` Before `6b3977472b` (400: the translated `reasoning_effort: "none"` collides with the native `thinking` the client asked for; same 400 on `/v1/completions` with a `prompt`): ```json {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: Fireworks_aiException - {"error":{"object":"error","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"invalid_request_error","message":"thinking.type='enabled' conflicts with reasoning_effort='none'"}}. Received Model Group=fw-glm
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}} ``` After `3b2ed3c018` (200 with `reasoning_content`, so the native `thinking` wins; the `/v1/completions` variant also returns 200): ```json {"id":"chatcmpl-1d10bba1868843089404a19c6a260090","created":1786743468,"model":"fw-glm","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hi.","role":"assistant","reasoning_content":"1. Identify the core request: The user wants me to say "hi" in exactly one word.
2. Formulate the response: The word is "Hi" (or "Hi!").
3. Check constraints: Must be one word.
4. Output: "Hi.""}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":65,"prompt_tokens":18,"total_tokens":83,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}}} ``` The standing scenarios were re-run at `3b2ed3c018` and stay 200: chat with the NIM/vLLM knob set returns valid guided JSON, completions with the knob set returns text, and `reasoning_effort: "auto"` stays a harmless drop QA run 2026-08-14 for the follow-up commit `b3729c50b0` (top-level `thinking` on the completions path, flagged by Bugbot). Before leg: proxy booted from the merge commit `9027ab9485`. After leg: proxy booted from `b3729c50b0`: ``` curl -s http://localhost:<port>/v1/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{ "model": "fw-glm", "prompt": "Say hi in one word:", "max_tokens": 300, "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 1024} }' ``` Before `9027ab9485` (500, dies inside the gateway before reaching Fireworks): ```json {"error":{"message":"litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'thinking'. Received Model Group=fw-glm
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` After `b3729c50b0` (200 with the completion text; the same top-level `thinking` on `/v1/chat/completions` returns 200 with `reasoning_content` on both legs, unchanged): ```json {"id":"cmpl-56505e4641234c7c8df57714237a606f","object":"text_completion","created":1786752229,"model":"fw-glm","choices":[{"finish_reason":"length","index":0,"text":"No cheating?
No cheating? If I say "hi" and you say "No cheating?", are you implying that I should cheat, or that I already have? ..."}]} ``` The five standing scenarios (NIM/vLLM knobs on both endpoints, the extra_body precedence pair on both endpoints, and `reasoning_effort: "auto"`) were re-run at `b3729c50b0` and all return 200 ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes - `litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/transformation.py`: new `map_extra_body_params` plus translation/strip helpers and a `NIM_VLLM_STRIP_PARAMS` set - `litellm/main.py`: `_complete_fireworks_ai` routes `optional_params` through the translation before the HTTP handler pops `extra_body` - `litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/completion/transformation.py`: text completion variant of the translation, reusing the chat module's shared helpers - `tests/test_litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/test_fireworks_ai_chat_transformation.py`: regression tests for each translation, each stripped param, conflict precedence, passthrough preservation, an end-to-end request-body assertion through `litellm.completion`, and a gate-contract regression test (`store` still raises `UnsupportedParamsError` / drops with `drop_params=True`) - `tests/test_litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/completion/test_fireworks_ai_text_completion_transformation.py`: new mapped test file for the completion provider Translation matrix: `truncate_prompt_tokens` -> `prompt_truncate_len`; `chat_template_kwargs` effort keys -> `reasoning_effort` (`enable_thinking`/`thinking: false` -> `"none"`, `true` -> omitted so the model default applies, `reasoning_budget` -> integer effort, `low_effort: true` -> `"low"`, matching the Fireworks API gateway's translation and published NIM compatibility docs); `guided_json` / `guided_grammar` / `guided_choice` -> `response_format` (including the `name` fields the gateway emits). Extras with no Fireworks equivalent (`stop_token_ids`, `skip_special_tokens`, `guided_regex`, `best_of`, `include_reasoning`, `nvext`, etc.) are stripped with a debug log. `min_tokens` is not stripped: the Fireworks API accepts it natively (verified live) Conflicts resolve silently in favor of the Fireworks-native value (aligned with the Fireworks API gateway): explicit `prompt_truncate_len` beats `truncate_prompt_tokens`, explicit `reasoning_effort`/`thinking` (top-level or nested in `extra_body`) beats `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`, explicit `response_format` (top-level or nested in `extra_body`) beats `guided_*`, and multiple `guided_*` resolve by priority json > grammar > choice, all with a debug log The text completion variant is adapted to the typed OpenAI SDK: everything `completions.create()` rejects (`reasoning_effort`, `response_format`, fireworks-native extras) rides inside `extra_body`, and top-level `reasoning_effort`/`response_format`/`thinking` are moved there too (they raised `TypeError` before). One endpoint-driven difference: `/v1/completions` rejects `prompt_truncate_len` (verified live), so both truncate names are stripped there instead of renamed. Unrecognized extras and fireworks-native params (`top_k`, `min_p`, ...) keep passing through verbatim, so the existing passthrough channel is unchanged. The hook is fully provider-local: `BaseConfig`, `utils.py`, and the vLLM/NIM passthrough are untouched ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(anthropic_messages): make tool_result images visible to OpenAI-compatible providers
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Images returned by tools vanish on `/v1/messages` for OpenAI-compatible models: the chat adapter buries them as text inside `role:"tool"` messages and the Responses adapter (the default openai/azure path) drops them entirely - The model answers from the filename or hallucinates a description instead of seeing the image How it solves it: - The adapter emits tool_result images as structured `image_url` parts - A shared helper moves tool images into a `role:"user"` message right after the tool messages, the shape OpenAI documents for image-producing tools - The Responses adapter forwards them as `input_image` parts ## Relevant issues Fixes #24968 (closed as stale, never fixed). That report describes the single-image flattening on the bedrock converse route; change 1 below is the direct fix for it, and the reporter's sentinel-text-block workaround becomes unnecessary ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real providers, no mocks. Plain Claude Code (claude CLI 2.1.215) with only its built-in Read tool, pointed at the proxy and asked to read a local png containing an unguessable token; the model can only report the token if it truly received the pixels ```yaml model_list: - model_name: vision-model litellm_params: model: mistral/mistral-medium-2508 # chat-completions adapter path api_key: os.environ/MISTRAL_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config config.yaml --port 4000 --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee proxy.log # from the directory containing screenshot.png: HOME=/tmp/cchome \ ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-1234 \ ANTHROPIC_MODEL=vision-model ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL=vision-model \ claude --allowedTools "Read" \ -p "Read $(pwd)/screenshot.png once. If the result isn't a viewable image, reply exactly NO_IMAGE and stop -- no retry, no OCR, no more thinking. If you can see it, reply only with the exact text in the image." ``` Note on the commit hashes below: the branch has since been rebased onto current `litellm_internal_staging` and squashed to a single commit, `bc8d2b6539`. The proof was captured at `729064d4a2`, which no longer exists in the PR. The rebase carried the fix forward unchanged apart from typing-syntax modernization that staging now requires (`Union[A, B]` written as `A | B`, `: Final` on the new module constants, and the two hook lines rewritten to bind a new local instead of rebinding the `messages` parameter now that LIT011 is enforced, plus a one-line `reportUnnecessaryComparison` suppression in `factory.py` where the widened tool-message type makes a defensive Anthropic-native image branch look dead to the type checker), so the behavior the capture shows is the behavior at the current head BEFORE (commit 1b2a7ce518): the model answers NO_IMAGE. proxy.log confirms the image reached litellm but zero image_url parts went out to Mistral; the data URI sits as text inside the `role:"tool"` message AFTER (commit 729064d4a2): the model replies with the exact token in the image ("WOMBAT-5391"). proxy.log shows the tool message carrying only the placeholder and the image going out in the next user message: ``` role': 'tool', 'tool_call_id': 'fG3gku10x', 'content': '[Tool returned an image - see the following user message]' {'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': {'url': 'data:image/png;b... ``` Responses path (model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini, the default openai route), same setup driven by the Agent SDK (claude-agent-sdk 0.2.125). BEFORE, the image is dropped and `function_call_output.output` is an empty string. AFTER: ``` ASSISTANT: The image shows the text **"ZEBRA-4712"** in large blue letters on a white background. ``` ``` function_call_output', 'call_id': 'call_NoVf5Ueh4zhHrEvCoBFYEq2R', 'output': '[Tool returned an image - see the following user message]' input_image', 'image_url': 'data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEU... ``` An MCP tool returning an image (the other real-client shape) trips and fixes the same way on both paths Both proofs re-run at 2e248c769c (post-review cleanup commit): built-in Read on the mistral path and MCP on the gpt-5.4-mini Responses path both read the exact token, with the placeholder in the tool output and the image going out in the following user message Re-run once more at 79b0ef2c66, after merging litellm_internal_staging and the type-discipline refactor: built-in Read through the mistral chat path and the gpt-5.4-mini Responses path both read the exact token from a fresh image, and the outbound bodies carry the placeholder in the tool output plus the hoisted image in the following user message on both paths ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Tools that return images on `/v1/messages` (Claude Code's built-in Read, MCP tools, computer-use screenshots) produce an Anthropic `tool_result` block with an `image` item. The chat-completions adapter (mistral, xai, qwen, openrouter, groq and every other OpenAI-compatible provider) serialized that image as a data-URI string inside the `role:"tool"` message, where the OpenAI spec only allows text, so providers read it as text. The Responses API adapter (the default for openai and azure) only extracted text parts, so the image was dropped outright. This PR fixes both paths: 1. `adapters/transformation.py`: a single-image `tool_result` becomes a structured `image_url` part instead of a bare string. This matters beyond consistency: a bare URL string is indistinguishable from a tool legitimately returning a URL as text, so no downstream code could ever fix that case. Single-item text results keep the string format 2. `common_utils.py`: new `hoist_images_from_tool_messages` replaces image content in tool messages with a text placeholder and inserts the images as a `role:"user"` message after the run of consecutive tool messages, preserving the tool_calls/tool adjacency that strict providers validate. It runs at the top of `OpenAIGPTConfig._transform_messages`, which every OpenAI-compatible provider config reaches, and in `AzureOpenAIConfig.transform_request`, which builds its request outside that pipeline 3. `responses_adapters/transformation.py`: tool_result images become `input_image` parts in the user message that already follows the `function_call_output` items; the output keeps its text plus the placeholder 4. `types/llms/openai.py`: `ChatCompletionToolMessage.content` now admits image parts, which the adapter has produced for multi-item results since computer-use support landed Native providers are unaffected: they never hit these adapters and the hoist runs only in the OpenAI-compatible layer. The Gemini and Bedrock chat-completions converters already handle structured `image_url` parts, so change 1 routes their single-image case through the supported branch; for bedrock non-Claude models that fixes the latent bug in #24968 where the data URI was forwarded as toolResult text. One pre-existing gap stays out of scope: sambanova, azure_ai and github_copilot override `_transform_messages` without reaching the base implementation Tests cover the helper in isolation (base64 and URL sources, multi-item results, parallel tool calls, bare-string and None-content pass-through, no input mutation), the full anthropic-to-openai pipeline at the transform_request level, mistral's override chain, sync and async transforms, and the responses adapter. Existing tests that pinned the bare-string shape were updated ## QA runbook Run the two proofs above: start the proxy with the mistral config and run the claude CLI command from a directory containing a png with readable text (expect the model to quote the text), then switch the model to `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and repeat (Responses path). In both runs grep proxy.log for `image_url` / `input_image` to confirm the image goes out in a user message and the tool output carries the placeholder ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: completion(stream=True) silently drops reasoning-summary streaming for OpenAI reasoning models (79s of total silence)
signal.text: ### What happened? `litellm.completion(stream=True)` routes OpenAI reasoning models through Chat Completions, which sends nothing at all while the model thinks. `litellm.responses(stream=True)` uses the Responses API and streams `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` throughout. Same model, same reasoning effort, same prompt, measured 2026-08-12 on v1.96.2: | surface | time to first byte | total | max inter-chunk gap | summary deltas | |---|---|---|---|---| | `completion(stream=True)` | **79.1s** | 79.1s | **79.1s** | 0 | | `responses(stream=True)` | **0.8s** | 76.5s | 17.2s | 1318 | The first row is 100% silence — max inter-chunk gap equals total elapsed, because nothing arrives until everything arrives. Total time is nearly identical either way, so this isn't a speed difference, it's a visibility one. **Why it matters — socket read timeouts.** Sizing a read timeout from observed inter-token gaps is the sane way to do it, and it works for every provider until you hit an OpenAI reasoning model, whose real gap is 79s where everything else is single-digit seconds. Then it times out mid-think. On the wire, a long think and a hung connection are indistinguishable. **The silent part is the actual bug, more than the routing.** Nothing in the response indicates that summary streaming was dropped — no field, no warning, no flag. The stream says nothing for 79 seconds and then completes normally. There's no way to detect the condition and compensate; you have to already know. ### User Flow Streaming a reasoning model through `completion()` in a pipeline that (a) shows progress to a user, or (b) sets a socket read timeout derived from observed inter-chunk gaps. Both are routine, and both break only for OpenAI reasoning models while working everywhere else. ### Proof the bug occurs ```python import litellm, time start = time.time() first = None for chunk in litellm.completion( model="gpt-5.5", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "<prompt requiring real reasoning>"}], reasoning_effort="high", stream=True, ): if first is None: first = time.time() - start print(f"TTFB {first:.1f}s total {time.time() - start:.1f}s") # TTFB 79.1s total 79.1s <- nothing for 79.1s, then everything # Same model, same effort, same prompt via responses(stream=True): # TTFB 0.8s total 76.5s <- 1318 response.reasoning_summary_text.delta events, # largest gap between any two chunks 17.2s ``` ### Proposal Either: 1. Route reasoning models from `completion()` to the Responses API when a summary is available, or 2. Surface the drop — any signal a caller can detect — and document the limitation prominently. (2) alone would be enough here. Today the only way to learn about it is to measure both surfaces side by side. ### Prior art (checked before filing) - #13780 asked for reasoning summaries through `/chat/completions` and was closed completed, but the resolution was `extra_body` param pass-through. That gets params *to* the Responses API; it doesn't make the default `completion(stream=True)` path stream summaries. Still 79.1s of silence on v1.96.2. - #14117 ("Route Chat Completions to OpenAI Responses API for reasoning") was the routing fix for exactly this, closed unmerged 2026-02-24. Since the routing option has been attempted and dropped once already, I'd happily take option 2. ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details @mhammett

signal.title: Title: RateLimitError doesn't distinguish non-retryable insufficient_quota from retryable 429s — retry loops spin on billing errors
signal.text: ### What happened When an OpenAI key has no remaining quota (`code: "insufficient_quota"` — a billing state), LiteLLM raises the same `litellm.RateLimitError` used for transient rate-limit 429s. Standard retry logic (SDK retries, tenacity wrappers, user backoff loops) treats `RateLimitError` as retryable — so callers retry a condition retrying cannot fix. This isn't hypothetical: I hit it building a model-comparison tool (funded account whose credit purchase hadn't completed), and prior support issues show users stuck in exactly this loop — #14547 is a user's exponential backoff spinning on an exhausted key; #12497, #12723, #5983, #6560 are the same underlying condition surfacing as confusing "rate limit" reports. ### Where the distinction is lost `litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py` @ `bf02a4a47f`: the OpenAI branch of `exception_type()` tests `ExceptionCheckers.is_error_str_rate_limit(error_str)` first (line 280) and raises `RateLimitError` (line 281). `is_error_str_rate_limit` returns True on a standalone `429` token (line 51). The OpenAI body's `code`/`type` (`insufficient_quota`) is never consulted — the string `insufficient_quota` appears nowhere in `litellm/` (non-test). `RateLimitError.__init__` (`litellm/exceptions.py:413`) then hardcodes `self.code = "429"` / `self.type = "throttling_error"` (lines 483–484) and defaults `category=VENDOR_RATE_LIMIT` — so a quota 429 and a transient 429 produce object-identical exceptions. ### Repro ```python import litellm # key from an account with $0 credit balance (prepaid billing, no auto-recharge) litellm.completion( model="gpt-5.5", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], max_tokens=5, api_key="", ) # raises: litellm.RateLimitError: RateLimitError: OpenAIException - You exceeded # your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. ... # underlying OpenAI error: {'type': 'insufficient_quota', 'code': 'insufficient_quota'} ``` Observed on litellm v1.91.1; confirmed still present at HEAD `bf02a4a47f08ad8007a24c8da2ffa8de1a1d36a2` (main, 2026-07-10) — the exception-mapping and RateLimitError code are byte-identical between the two. ### Why it matters `RateLimitError` is the class every retry policy keys on. A billing-state error inside it means (a) retry storms against providers, (b) agents/pipelines hang for their full retry budget before surfacing the real problem, (c) the actionable message ("check your plan and billing") is delayed or swallowed by retry wrappers. ### Proposal (any of these would solve it; happy to submit a PR) The exception model already distinguishes rate-limit flavors via `RateLimitErrorCategory` / `RateLimitType` (`exceptions.py`), but no existing value covers a provider billing/quota state — both quota and transient 429s land in `category="vendor_rate_limit"`. Options, most to least invasive: 1. A subtype, e.g. `InsufficientQuotaError(RateLimitError)` — backwards-compatible (existing `except RateLimitError` still catches), retry policies can exclude it. 2. Extend the existing taxonomy: set `code`/`type` from the provider body instead of hardcoding, and/or add a quota value to the category enum — callers can then branch without a new class. 3. At minimum, a docs note that `RateLimitError` includes non-retryable quota exhaustion, with the code to check. OpenAI sends `code: insufficient_quota`; other providers have analogous non-retryable billing states worth mapping in the same pass (can enumerate if useful).

signal.title: fix(guardrails): restore SSRF protection in custom code HTTP primitives
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Restores security controls that were introduced by #25004 and lost during the custom-code sandbox migration (Starlark -> RestrictedPython): the `_validate_url_for_ssrf()` blocklist and `follow_redirects=False` are absent from `main`, so the sandboxed HTTP primitives can reach loopback, RFC1918, and cloud-metadata endpoints again, and every HTTP method follows redirects. Found during a source security review of v1.96.2. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🐞 Bug fix (security regression) ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/custom_code/primitives.py` - `http_request()` now validates the URL through the canonical `litellm_core_utils.url_utils.validate_url()` before connecting: - blocks loopback, private, link-local, reserved, multicast, and cloud-metadata targets (default-deny via `ip.is_global`), which also covers `169.254.169.254` / `metadata.google.internal` / `fd00:ec2::254` - resolve-and-rewrite for plain `http` removes the DNS-rebinding/TOCTOU gap the old `_validate_url_for_ssrf` had; for `https` the TLS hostname binding keeps the connection pinned - the original hostname is restored via the `Host` header so vhost routing still works - `_execute_http_request()` passes `follow_redirects=False` on GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH so a 3xx response cannot bypass validation - operators keep two documented escape hatches (same as the rest of the codebase): `user_url_allowed_hosts` in `general_settings` for legitimate internal moderation services, and `litellm.user_url_validation = False` to disable the check entirely - reuses the existing validator instead of restoring the hand-rolled copy, so guardrail primitives and the other user-controlled fetch surfaces (RAG ingestion, OpenAPI-to-MCP spec fetch) share one SSRF policy ## Working proof Local loopback HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:8971` recording request paths, driven through the real primitives (both directly and from inside a RestrictedPython-compiled guardrail calling `http_get`): Before (v1.96.2 from PyPI): ``` check1 direct loopback: 200 {'path': '/direct-loopback'} check2 redirect followed: 200 {'path': '/landing'} | hits: ['/direct-loopback', '/hop', '/landing'] check3 sandbox end-to-end: {'action': 'block', 'reason': "reached {'path': '/sandbox-exfil?d=secret'}"} VERDICT: loopback reached = True | redirect followed = True | sandbox exfil path hit = True ``` After (this branch): ``` primitives.py:473 - Custom code http_request SSRF blocked: URL targets a blocked address (127.0.0.1). If this is a legitimate internal service, add the host to `user_url_allowed_hosts` in general_settings. check1 direct loopback: 0 None check2 redirect followed: 0 None | hits: [] check3 sandbox end-to-end: {'action': 'allow'} VERDICT: loopback reached = False | redirect followed = False | sandbox exfil path hit = False ``` The requests are refused before any connection is made, so the redirecting `/hop` endpoint is never reached and the sandboxed exfiltration payload has no network channel. ## Tests ``` $ python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/test_custom_code_security.py -q 31 passed, 1 warning in 3.89s ``` Added to the existing mapped test file (`tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/test_custom_code_security.py`): - `test_http_primitives_block_internal_targets` - loopback (IPv4 + IPv6), `localhost`, RFC1918, and `169.254.169.254` are refused with a `Blocked` error and the HTTP client is never invoked - `test_http_primitives_allow_public_url` - a public URL passes; asserts the resolve-and-rewrite connection URL, the restored `Host` header, preserved caller headers, and `follow_redirects=False` - `test_http_primitives_honor_allowlisted_internal_host` - `user_url_allowed_hosts` unblocks an internal host - `test_http_primitives_validation_can_be_disabled` - `litellm.user_url_validation = False` restores the old behavior - `test_http_primitives_do_not_follow_redirects` - a 302 is returned as-is (not followed) for POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH All tests are hermetic: DNS is monkeypatched to a global IP and the httpx client is faked; no real network calls.
