signal.title: fix(guardrails): run policy pipelines when the caller sends its own metadata (/v1/messages, Claude Code)
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Claude Code requests skipped every policy pipeline guardrail - Any caller sending its own `metadata` bypassed pipeline policies - Only `/v1/messages`, `/responses`, `batches`, `files`, `bedrock` affected How it solves it: - Read pipelines from the canonical metadata bucket, not `metadata` first - Same for the pipeline-managed skip list in the callback loop - Regression test covers a caller-supplied `metadata` on `/v1/messages` ## User Flow Before: an admin attaches a moderation policy to every request, but a developer using Claude Code sends prompts that are never screened 1. The admin attaches a policy with a `pre_call` pipeline whose step blocks disallowed content, scoped to `*` 2. From a REST client, the developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with disallowed content and gets back 400 with the guardrail's block message 3. The same user runs Claude Code against the same key, model and team, so every request carries `User-Agent: claude-cli` and a top-level `"metadata": {"user_id": "..."}` 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same disallowed content returns 200 with a normal model completion 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request with an empty `applied_guardrails`, so the audit trail says nothing ran 6. Anyone on that key could route unscreened prompts through the gateway just by sending Anthropic's own `metadata` field After: the same policy blocks the Claude Code request too, and the log records the guardrail 1. The admin attaches the same policy 2. From a REST client, POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with disallowed content returns 400 with the guardrail's block message 3. The same user runs Claude Code, so requests carry `User-Agent: claude-cli` and a top-level `"metadata": {"user_id": "..."}` 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same disallowed content now returns 400 with the same block message 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the guardrail recorded against the request 6. Sending Anthropic's `metadata` field no longer buys a caller an unscreened request ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5600 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on localhost:4000 against real Anthropic (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`), with a global policy whose `pre_call` pipeline blocks on a guardrail failure. `BLOCKME` is the disallowed content for the guardrail under test. Repro script, run identically before and after: ```bash # 1) Bruno-style: no provider metadata echo "--- no provider metadata ---" curl -s -o /tmp/r1 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-5-opus","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"BLOCKME"}]}' head -c 200 /tmp/r1; echo # 2) Claude Code style: top-level Anthropic metadata + claude-cli user agent echo "--- User-Agent: claude-cli + metadata.user_id ---" curl -s -o /tmp/r2 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST 'http://localhost:4000/v1/messages?beta=true' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.227 (external, local-agent, agent-sdk/0.3.227)' \ -d '{"model":"claude-5-opus","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"BLOCKME"}],"metadata":{"user_id":"user_abc"}}' head -c 200 /tmp/r2; echo ``` Before, at commit `6704a105ee`: the Claude Code shape is served by the model, unscreened ``` --- no provider metadata --- HTTP 400 {"error":{"message":"400: {'error': 'blocked by marker-gr', 'guardrail_name': 'marker-gr', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call'}","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400"}} --- User-Agent: claude-cli + metadata.user_id --- HTTP 200 {"model":"claude-5-opus","id":"msg_011Ce2517cEpQBus26YwLuxE","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'm Claude, an AI assistant made by Anthropic. I'm here"}],"stop_reas ``` After, at commit `f86318c4c9`: both shapes are blocked by the same policy ``` --- no provider metadata --- HTTP 400 {"error":{"message":"400: {'error': 'blocked by marker-gr', 'guardrail_name': 'marker-gr', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call'}","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400"}} --- User-Agent: claude-cli + metadata.user_id --- HTTP 400 {"error":{"message":"400: {'error': 'blocked by marker-gr', 'guardrail_name': 'marker-gr', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call'}","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400"}} ``` Video walkthrough of the same before/after runs, pre-fix `6704a105ee` on port 4000 and fixed `34b513074e` on port 4001 side by side, is posted in the [Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1786683665130109?thread_ts=1786683665.130109&cid=C0BE49SAUE6) Proxy debug logs confirm the mechanism: before the fix the Claude Code request logged `Policy engine: resolved 1 pipeline(s), managed guardrails: {'marker-gr'}` and then never reached `pipeline_executor`, and the guardrail's own hook never ran. After the fix the pipeline executes on both shapes ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Independently attached guardrails were already unaffected - Only pipeline-backed policies could be bypassed this way ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/adb590da643643b68f37fbec96628341
signal.author: devin-ai-integration[bot]

signal.title: fix(azure_ai): recognize real Search doc endpoints so teams can read/write via passthrough
signal.text: ## TLDR This is #33757 by @noahnistler, cherry-picked onto current `litellm_internal_staging` so it can land in this RC. The fork branch is six days stale, and the lint job checks out the PR head rather than the merge ref, so it dies on a composite action that only exists on newer staging. Nobody with push rights to the fork was around to update it. Authorship is preserved; on top of the reviewed head this branch merges newer staging forward, drops one redundant test comment, and classifies write endpoints before reads to close a substring collision Bugbot caught in review Problem this solves: - Teams granted an Azure AI Search index still get 403 on it - Only `POST /docs/search` was recognized, nine other routes fell through - Service-level `POST /indexes` create was never gated for non-admins - The URL scanner could authorize a different index than the one Azure receives How it solves it: - Map reads to any `GET` under `/indexes/` plus the `POST` query routes - Map writes to `POST /docs/index`, Azure's real batch document route - Enforce admin-only index create on the passthrough route itself - Take the index positionally from `/indexes/{name}`, not any segment ## User Flow Before: a data team holding read and write on one Search index cannot upload documents to it, and cannot read anything back except one search form 1. An admin registers index `team-index` and grants a team `read` and `write` on it, then mints a non-admin key for that team 2. The team sends `POST https://litellm-domain/azure_ai/indexes/team-index/docs/index?api-version=2024-07-01` with a `mergeOrUpload` batch 3. They get `403` with `User does not have permission to call vector store endpoint team-index. Ask your administrator to add the necessary permissions to your API key/Team.`, even though the administrator already did 4. `GET .../indexes/team-index`, `/docs/$count`, `/docs/{key}`, `/docs/search`, `/docs/suggest`, `/docs/autocomplete`, and `/analyze` all return the same `403`. Only `POST /docs/search` returns `200` 5. Meanwhile any non-admin key can send `POST https://litellm-domain/azure_ai/indexes?api-version=2024-07-01` and Azure returns `201`: they created a brand new index on the service 6. A second team granted `read` and `write` on an index literally named `docs` fares no better: even `POST .../indexes/docs/docs/index` into its own index returns the same `403` After: the same grant reaches the whole document surface, the create escalation is closed, and grants stay pinned to the index in the path 1. Same setup: index `team-index` registered, team granted `read` and `write`, non-admin key minted 2. The team sends the same `POST .../indexes/team-index/docs/index` batch and gets `200` with `{"value":[{"key":"1","status":true,...,"statusCode":201}]}` 3. `GET .../docs/1` returns the document, `GET .../docs/$count` returns `1` 4. Index details, stats, both search forms, suggest, autocomplete, and analyze all return `200` 5. `PUT` and `DELETE` on `.../indexes/team-index` still return `403` with `Only proxy admins can update/delete vector store indexes.` 6. `POST https://litellm-domain/azure_ai/indexes` from that team key now returns `403` with `Only proxy admins can create vector store indexes.`, while the master key still gets `201` 7. The `docs` team now uploads to `docs` and gets `200`, while the same batch aimed at `.../indexes/team-index/docs/index` returns `403`: the index authorized is taken positionally from the path, so it is exactly the one Azure receives ## Relevant issues Supersedes #33757 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5504 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two live legs against real Azure AI Search services, no mocks, every call hitting the Search data plane through a local proxy with a fresh Postgres DB per leg. The before leg runs this branch's merge base `f03df1bb42` (current `litellm_internal_staging`) with `https://litellm-qa-lit5504.search.windows.net`; the after leg runs `08966c842b` with `https://litellm-qa-lit5504b.search.windows.net`, and the whole after matrix was re-run unchanged at this PR's tip `b14c4a8d45`, which adds the collision scenario shown at the end. Setup is identical in both: the admin master key registers the index rows and vector stores, physically creates the indexes over the passthrough (`POST /azure_ai/indexes` -> `201`), then team A is granted `allowed_vector_store_indexes` with `read` and `write` on `team-index`, team B the same on an index literally named `docs`, and a non-admin virtual key is minted per team. The author's original proof on #33757 showed the same shape at the stale fork hashes Before, at `f03df1bb42`, team A's key is refused on nine of the ten non-lifecycle routes despite its grant. Only `POST /docs/search` is classified by the endpoint map, so only it works ``` upload documents POST /docs/index -> HTTP 403 get index details GET /indexes/{idx} -> HTTP 403 index stats -> HTTP 403 document count GET /docs/$count -> HTTP 403 document lookup by key GET /docs/{key} -> HTTP 403 search (GET form) -> HTTP 403 search (POST form) -> HTTP 200 suggest -> HTTP 403 autocomplete -> HTTP 403 analyze -> HTTP 403 ``` The reported upload failure, verbatim ``` $ curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:28841/azure_ai/indexes/team-index/docs/index?api-version=2024-07-01" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_A_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"value":[{"@search.action":"mergeOrUpload","id":"1","content":"the quick brown fox jumps"}]}' HTTP 403 {"detail":"User does not have permission to call vector store endpoint team-index. Ask your administrator to add the necessary permissions to your API key/Team."} ``` Team B cannot upload even to its own granted `docs` index, and the service-level create escalation is live: a non-admin key creates a brand-new index on the Search service ``` $ curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:28841/azure_ai/indexes/docs/docs/index?api-version=2024-07-01" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_B_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"value":[{"@search.action":"mergeOrUpload","id":"own1","content":"legit doc in own index"}]}' HTTP 403 {"detail":"User does not have permission to call vector store endpoint docs. Ask your administrator to add the necessary permissions to your API key/Team."} $ curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:28841/azure_ai/indexes?api-version=2024-07-01" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_A_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"name":"qa-escalation-idx","fields":[...],"suggesters":[...]}' HTTP 201 {"@odata.context":"https://litellm-qa-lit5504.search.windows.net/$metadata#indexes/$entity","name":"qa-escalation-idx",...} ``` Team B's cross-index batch at `.../indexes/team-index/docs/index` already returns `403` at this merge base, since `team-index` is itself registered and the left-to-right scan resolves it first; the divergence described under Changes concerns victims not registered with the proxy After, identical at `08966c842b` and at the tip `b14c4a8d45`, team A's key with the same grant against the same routes ``` upload documents -> HTTP 200 get index details -> HTTP 200 index stats -> HTTP 200 document count -> HTTP 200 document lookup by key -> HTTP 200 search (GET form) -> HTTP 200 search (POST form) -> HTTP 200 suggest -> HTTP 200 autocomplete -> HTTP 200 analyze -> HTTP 200 ``` The same upload, now accepted by Azure, and the document readable straight after ``` $ curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/team-index/docs/index?api-version=2024-07-01' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_A_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"value": [{"@search.action": "mergeOrUpload", "id": "1", "content": "the quick brown fox jumps"}]}' HTTP 200 {"@odata.context":"https://litellm-qa-lit5504b.search.windows.net/indexes('team-index')/$metadata#Collection(Microsoft.Azure.Search.V2024_07_01.IndexResult)","value":[{"key":"1","status":true,"errorMessage":null,"statusCode":201}]} $ curl -sS 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/team-index/docs/1?api-version=2024-07-01' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_A_KEY" HTTP 200 {"@odata.context":"...","id":"1","content":"the quick brown fox jumps"} $ curl -sS 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/team-index/docs/$count?api-version=2024-07-01' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_A_KEY" HTTP 200 1 ``` Index lifecycle stays admin-only for the team at both commits ``` $ curl -sS -X PUT 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/team-index?api-version=2024-07-01' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_A_KEY" ... HTTP 403 {"detail":"Only proxy admins can update vector store indexes. Contact your LiteLLM administrator."} $ curl -sS -X DELETE 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/team-index?api-version=2024-07-01' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_A_KEY" HTTP 403 {"detail":"Only proxy admins can delete vector store indexes. Contact your LiteLLM administrator."} ``` Service-level create is now gated: the call that returned `201` before is refused, while the master key still creates ``` $ curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes?api-version=2024-07-01' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_A_KEY" -d '{"name":"qa-admin-idx",...}' HTTP 403 {"detail":"Only proxy admins can create vector store indexes. Contact your LiteLLM administrator."} $ curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes?api-version=2024-07-01' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -d '{"name":"qa-admin-idx",...}' HTTP 201 {"name":"qa-admin-idx",...} ``` And grants stay pinned to the index in the path: team B writes its own `docs` index but cannot reach `team-index`, corroborated on Azure by the admin ``` $ curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/team-index/docs/index?api-version=2024-07-01' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_B_KEY" \ -d '{"value": [{"@search.action": "mergeOrUpload", "id": "intruder", "content": "crossed the boundary"}]}' HTTP 403 {"detail":"User does not have permission to call vector store endpoint team-index. Ask your administrator to add the necessary permissions to your API key/Team."} $ curl -sS 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/team-index/docs/intruder?api-version=2024-07-01' -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" HTTP 404 $ curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/docs/docs/index?api-version=2024-07-01' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_B_KEY" \ -d '{"value": [{"@search.action": "mergeOrUpload", "id": "b1", "content": "team b owns this doc"}]}' HTTP 200 {"@odata.context":"...","value":[{"key":"b1","status":true,"errorMessage":null,"statusCode":201}]} ``` The collision scenario from review, live at the tip `b14c4a8d45`: the admin registers and creates an index literally named `analyze`, team C gets `["read"]` on it and team D gets `["write"]`. On the read-first code team C's upload would have been let through; now it is refused while team D's succeeds, and Azure corroborates that only team D's document exists ``` $ curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/analyze/docs/index?api-version=2024-07-01' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_C_READONLY_KEY" \ -d '{"value":[{"@search.action":"mergeOrUpload","id":"c1","content":"read only smuggle"}]}' HTTP 403 {"detail":"User does not have permission to call vector store endpoint analyze. Ask your administrator to add the necessary permissions to your API key/Team."} $ curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/analyze/docs/index?api-version=2024-07-01' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_D_WRITEONLY_KEY" \ -d '{"value":[{"@search.action":"mergeOrUpload","id":"d1","content":"write grant works"}]}' HTTP 200 {"@odata.context":"https://litellm-qa-lit5504b.search.windows.net/indexes('analyze')/$metadata#Collection(...IndexResult)","value":[{"key":"d1","status":true,"errorMessage":null,"statusCode":201}]} $ curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/analyze/analyze?api-version=2024-07-01' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_C_READONLY_KEY" -d '{"text":"quick fox","analyzer":"en.lucene"}' HTTP 200 {"@odata.context":"...AnalyzeResult","tokens":[{"token":"quick",...},{"token":"fox",...}]} $ curl -sS 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/analyze/docs/c1?api-version=2024-07-01' -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" HTTP 404 $ curl -sS 'http://localhost:41873/azure_ai/indexes/analyze/docs/d1?api-version=2024-07-01' -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" HTTP 200 ``` Every index created during these runs was deleted afterward and both QA Search services were torn down. The two suites this touches pass at the tip ``` $ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync pytest \ tests/test_litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/test_llm_pass_through_endpoints.py \ tests/test_litellm/proxy/vector_store_endpoints/test_vector_store_endpoints.py -q 213 passed, 3 warnings in 17.88s ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `AzureAIVectorStoreConfig.get_vector_store_endpoints_by_type` now returns read = any `GET` under `/indexes/` (get details, stats, count, point lookup, and the GET forms of search, suggest, and autocomplete) plus the `POST` query endpoints `/docs/search`, `/docs/suggest`, `/docs/autocomplete`, and `/analyze`, with write = `POST /docs/index`. The old map declared write as `PUT /docs` and read as only `/docs/search`, so every real route above fell through the classifier and 403'd non-admins regardless of grant Every pattern stays a literal path fragment rather than a `{placeholder}` template. `_does_endpoint_match` falls back to the substring preceding a `{`, which for these routes is always `/indexes/`, so a templated read would have swallowed every documents route, `/docs/index` included. Substring matching cuts the other way too, which Bugbot caught in review: an index literally named `analyze` (or `analyzer-reports`) embeds the `/analyze` read fragment inside its own `POST /docs/index` path, and with reads classified first a read-only grant could upload documents there while a write grant was refused. Both classification sites now check write patterns before read patterns, so a path matching both demands the stronger grant. The classification is otherwise driven by HTTP semantics: `GET` never mutates a Search index, and among the `POST` routes only `/docs/index` carries `upload`, `merge`, `mergeOrUpload`, and `delete` actions Index create, update, and delete remain proxy-admin only. Those are caught earlier by the separate lifecycle check (`_is_vector_store_index_lifecycle_request` on POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH of the index itself), so widening the document read/write map does not let a team manage indexes. Because the classifier only decides read vs write, the per-index grant check still runs afterward, so a team can only reach an index it was explicitly granted The same lifecycle check had a latent bug the new create-path test surfaced: the service-level `POST /indexes` create branch matched on `normalized.endswith("/indexes")` without stripping the query string, so Azure's real `POST /indexes?api-version=...` was never classified as lifecycle and fell through to the generic permission check instead of the explicit admin-only guard. Non-admins were still denied by the catch-all, but the guard meant to own create was bypassed. It now strips the query string before the suffix check, matching how the PUT/DELETE index paths already tolerate a trailing `?` That admin-only create guard was still unreachable from the route, so it is now enforced there too. `POST /azure_ai/indexes` carries no index name, so `get_azure_ai_search_index_from_endpoint` returns `None`, no segment matches a managed index, and the request falls through to the generic Azure passthrough on the proxy's own `AZURE_API_BASE` and `AZURE_API_KEY` without ever reaching `is_allowed_to_call_vector_store_endpoint`. A non-admin could therefore create a Search index whenever `AZURE_API_BASE` points at the Search service, and the lifecycle test above hid it by exercising the gate directly rather than the route that skips it. `azure_proxy_route` now calls `assert_proxy_admin_for_vector_store_index_management` before the segment loop, scoped to `POST` on a path whose last segment is `indexes`, mirroring the `endswith("/indexes")` branch the lifecycle helper already uses so managed-index paths and ordinary Azure OpenAI traffic are untouched The passthrough route resolver (`azure_proxy_route`) is also hardened. It previously scanned URL segments left to right for one matching a registered index, authorized against that, then forwarded the original path. When the `/indexes/{victim}` segment is itself a registered index the scan happens to find it first and refuse, which the QA below confirms, but when the victim is not registered while a later segment such as `docs` matches a granted index, the caller is authorized against, and credentialed as, that granted index while Azure receives the victim path. Recognizing `POST /docs/index` as a write would have extended that divergence to document writes, so the resolver now takes the index positionally from the `/indexes/{name}` segment and authorizes and credentials against exactly that name, making the authorized index and the physical target unable to diverge Regression tests in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/vector_store_endpoints/test_vector_store_endpoints.py` exercise the real `AzureAIVectorStoreConfig` map rather than a mock, so reverting to `("PUT", "/docs")`, dropping the GET-on-index read, or dropping any of the `POST` query endpoints makes them fail. They cover a write-granted team uploading, a read-granted team reaching the full read surface (index details, stats, `$count`, point lookup, search, and both forms of suggest and autocomplete, plus analyze), a team holding only the opposite grant still being denied on each of those routes, and a team being unable to create, update, or delete an index even with a write grant. Route-level tests in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/test_llm_pass_through_endpoints.py` cover the positional index extraction, the cross-index write attempt, and the service-level create, asserting a non-admin is refused with the admin-only message and never reaches the passthrough handler while an admin still creates; removing the route guard makes that first case fail. A further set pins the collision ordering on indexes named `analyze` and `analyzer-reports`: a read-only grant cannot reach `POST /docs/index` there, a write grant can, and the read-only grant still reaches the `/analyze` route itself; on the read-first code four of those five fail ## Caveats (if any) - Close #33757 in favor of this once merged, to keep credit clear ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 08966c842b1b5a903a11a43a973ee760ce89c7f1. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(caching): cache anthropic /v1/messages responses, including streaming
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/v1/messages` requests never hit the response cache - Anthropic-only params (`system`, `top_k`) skipped the cache key - Streamed `/v1/messages` responses had no cache path How it solves it: - Add `anthropic_messages`/`aanthropic_messages` to cached call types - Feed the Anthropic Messages request shape into cache keys - Tee streams out, replay stored SSE bytes on a hit ## User Flow Before: a team routing Claude traffic through `/v1/messages` on a cache-enabled proxy never gets cache hits, so every repeated request is billed again 1. The proxy admin enables response caching (`cache: true`) and restarts the proxy 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":64,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: LIT-4796 cache probe"}]}` and gets an answer with id `msg_011Ce3Ls1e...` after ~12.6s 3. They repeat the identical request and a different id `msg_011Ce3LsMB...` comes back after ~4.3s, so the provider answered and billed both calls 4. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=caching the Cache Hits vs API Requests chart shows `/v1/messages` traffic at zero hits while the same prompts on `/v1/chat/completions` show real hits 5. The admin works around it by adding `anthropic_messages` to `cache_params.supported_call_types`; repeats now hit the cache, but a request whose only difference is `"system":"Always answer with the single word BETA"` is answered with the ALPHA response cached for a different system prompt, a wrong answer served across requests 6. Still under the workaround, sending the request with `"stream": true` twice returns two different `msg_` ids at full latency, so streams are always billed After: the same `/v1/messages` traffic is served from cache with no config override, streams replay byte for byte, and differing system prompts stay separate 1. The proxy admin enables response caching (`cache: true`) and restarts the proxy 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same body and gets an answer with id `msg_011Ce3ZKCC...` after ~2.5s 3. They repeat the identical request and the same `msg_011Ce3ZKCC...` id returns in ~0.007s, served from cache with no provider charge 4. A request differing only in `"system":"Always answer with the single word BETA"` gets its own fresh BETA answer, and repeating the ALPHA request replays the ALPHA entry 5. Sending the request with `"stream": true` twice gets the second stream back in ~0.013s, byte-identical to the first with the same `msg_` id 6. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=caching now shows `/v1/messages` cache hits and cached completion tokens climbing ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4796 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two live proxies hitting the real Anthropic API (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`), config is just `cache: true` with `cache_params.type: local`, no `supported_call_types` override: a before proxy at merge base `422d925334` (`litellm_internal_staging`) and an after proxy at `9a1e63c9f0` (this PR's tip) A side by side before/after recording of the same runs is in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1784934769340439?thread_ts=1784934769.340439&cid=C0BE49SAUE6), captured at an earlier tip of this branch Before, at `422d925334`; the same request twice returns two different `msg_` ids at full latency, so both calls were billed ``` $ for i in 1 2; do curl -s -o /tmp/ns_$i.json -w "non-streaming #$i latency=%{time_total}s " http://localhost:35726/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":64,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: LIT-4796 cache probe"}]}' python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/ns_$i.json'));print('id='+d['id'],'text='+d['content'][0]['text'])"; done non-streaming #1 latency=12.574026s id=msg_011Ce3Ls1eD4JeLETNiD75Jh text=LIT-4796 cache probe non-streaming #2 latency=4.302459s id=msg_011Ce3LsMBxMcxQzbzJVp8dX text=LIT-4796 cache probe ``` Before, at `422d925334`, with the call type forced into `cache_params.supported_call_types` as a workaround; caching turns on but two different system prompts share one entry, and the BETA request is answered with the ALPHA response at cache-hit latency ``` $ for s in ALPHA BETA; do curl -s -w ' latency=%{time_total}s
' http://localhost:35726/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -d "{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":16,"system":"Always answer with the single word $s","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}"; done system=ALPHA id=msg_011Ce3M1gKs2KuYUhheiNVHH text=ALPHA latency=6.075752s system=BETA id=msg_011Ce3M1gKs2KuYUhheiNVHH text=ALPHA latency=0.182374s ``` Before, at `422d925334`; streaming is never cached under either config, two runs of the same request return two different streams at full latency ``` stream 1: latency=5.217521s first id: msg_011Ce3LuUZGaFeSxZV33an9a stream 2: latency=2.089916s first id: msg_011Ce3LudSZGKzQM5h2XzzFk $ diff p1_stream1.sse p1_stream2.sse # STREAMS DIFFER ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; non-streaming repeats now serve from cache ``` non-streaming #1 latency=2.485229s id=msg_011Ce3ZKCCLQ9YyEvBN7UxCQ text=LIT-4796 cache probe non-streaming #2 latency=0.100351s id=msg_011Ce3ZKCCLQ9YyEvBN7UxCQ text=LIT-4796 cache probe non-streaming #3 latency=0.006568s id=msg_011Ce3ZKCCLQ9YyEvBN7UxCQ text=LIT-4796 cache probe ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; system prompts no longer collide, and repeating the first one replays its own entry ``` $ for s in ALPHA BETA ALPHA; do curl -s -w ' latency=%{time_total}s
' http://localhost:29752/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -d "{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":64,"system":"Always answer with the single word $s","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}"; done system=ALPHA id=msg_011Ce3ZKqSwN6ZLqcXKNdTW5 text=ALPHA latency=1.305376s system=BETA id=msg_011Ce3ZKwGvvzEzerYCbPdSa text=BETA latency=1.331643s system=ALPHA id=msg_011Ce3ZKqSwN6ZLqcXKNdTW5 text=ALPHA latency=0.004050s ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; an Anthropic-native param gets its own cache entry (`stop_sequences` shown live because the Anthropic API now rejects `top_k` as deprecated on claude-sonnet-5; `top_k` and `stop_sequences` key separation are both unit-tested) ``` stop_sequences #1 latency=1.145369s id=msg_011Ce3ZLeuDVXa9AaMhxEof2 text=LIT-4796 cache probe stop_sequences #2 latency=0.007018s id=msg_011Ce3ZLeuDVXa9AaMhxEof2 plain repeat: latency=0.007410s id=msg_011Ce3ZKCCLQ9YyEvBN7UxCQ (its own entry stayed intact) ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; streaming replays the stored SSE byte for byte ``` $ for i in 1 2; do curl -s -N -o /tmp/st_$i.sse -w "streaming #$i latency=%{time_total}s
" http://localhost:29752/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":32,"stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: LIT-4796 stream probe"}]}'; done streaming #1 latency=2.535861s 1325 bytes id=msg_011Ce3ZMLXSghN3PAbRW6KeQ streaming #2 latency=0.012872s 1325 bytes id=msg_011Ce3ZMLXSghN3PAbRW6KeQ $ diff /tmp/st_1.sse /tmp/st_2.sse && echo "streams byte-identical" streams byte-identical ``` After, at `9a1e63c9f0`; controls on the shared surfaces stay healthy: `/v1/chat/completions` repeats hit (same `chatcmpl-c0a1efa0...` id, 0.008s), `/v1/responses` repeats serve the cached payload (identical inner output id and `created_at`, 0.005s; the outer `resp_` envelope id is re-minted, which is pre-existing Responses behavior), and a non-streaming request after the streaming pair gets a fresh normal JSON message rather than the cached SSE bytes ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `anthropic_messages` and `aanthropic_messages` join `CachingSupportedCallTypes` and the default supported call types, which are now a single `DEFAULT_CACHING_SUPPORTED_CALL_TYPES` tuple instead of the same literal list repeated in `Cache.__init__`, `enable_cache` and `update_cache` Enabling the call type on its own would have been unsafe. The cache key is built from `ModelParamHelper._get_all_llm_api_params()`, which is the union of the chat completions, embeddings, transcription, rerank and Responses API param sets; none of those contain `system`, `top_k` or `stop_sequences`, so a `/v1/messages` request keyed on the remaining fields collides with any other request that differs only in those, as the second "before" run above shows. The Anthropic Messages request shape now contributes to that union. `system` is added to the logging exclusion set so it stays out of standard logging model parameters like `messages` and `prompt` do, and `litellm_metadata` joins `metadata` in the excluded kwargs since it is per-request bookkeeping rather than part of the request identity Streaming needed a separate path. A streamed response is handed back to the caller before `LLMCachingHandler.async_set_cache` runs; chat completion streams are teed inside `CustomStreamWrapper` and Responses API streams inside their own iterator, and Anthropic Messages had no equivalent, so `wrap_streaming_result_for_cache` wraps the outgoing iterator in `AnthropicMessagesStreamCacheWriter`. It forwards every chunk unchanged and buffers the raw bytes, then decodes, splits into SSE events, and writes them under the same cache key only once the joined stream ends in `message_stop` without an `error` event, so an abandoned or failed stream is never stored, and `aiter_bytes()` frames that split a multibyte character or an SSE line across chunk boundaries neither crash the stream nor defeat the terminal-event check. On a hit, `CachedAnthropicMessagesStreamIterator` replays those bytes and runs the usual end-of-stream logging with `cache_hit` set, and the passthrough logging handler reports zero cost for it instead of billing the replay Tests cover the miss-then-hit for both modes, the system prompt separation, `top_k` and `stop_sequences` separation, streamed and non-streamed entries not sharing a key, the two cases where a stream must not be cached, and chunk-split regressions (a multibyte character, the `message_stop` line, and an `error` event each split across frames); the cache key assertions live alongside the existing key tests in `tests/test_litellm/caching/test_caching.py` ## Caveats (if any) - `cache: true` proxies start caching `/v1/messages` by default now - Streamed and non-streamed requests cache under separate entries - Provider-specific params outside the Anthropic request shape still need `enable_caching_on_provider_specific_optional_params` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c1d7d5eab6d44b6f9a56086768f3b8e8 Requested by: @shivamrawat1

signal.title: fix(batches): mark terminal batch with no output file as processed in CheckBatchCost
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Terminal `completed` batch with no output file re-polled forever - `batch_processed` stuck `false`, so output/error files never deletable How it solves it: - Mark any terminal batch with nothing to bill as processed once - Bill `completed`/`expired` batches that did produce an output file ## User Flow Before: a batch user who never re-checks their batch can never delete its input file once every request line fails; the gateway refuses cleanup forever 1. They upload `all_failed.jsonl` (every line invalid at execution time, e.g. `temperature: 3`) via POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose="batch"` and `target_model_names`, getting back a unified `file-...` id 2. They create the batch via POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that input file id; the response shows `status: "validating"` and their pipeline moves on without polling it 3. On the provider's own dashboard the batch soon ends as `completed` with an `error_file_id` and `output_file_id: null`; nothing was served, and correctly no spend appears at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs 4. Hours later they try to clean up: DELETE https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{input_file_id} returns 400 "Cannot delete file ... referenced by 1 batch(es) in non-terminal state", telling them to wait for cost computation that never comes 5. They retry the DELETE for days; the same 400 comes back forever, no matter how long they wait 6. A different batch that expired after partially completing (the provider shows `expired` with a real `output_file_id`) also never shows any spend for its served lines at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs After: the same batch is finalized shortly after it ends, cleanup succeeds, and partially-served expired batches are billed 1. They upload `all_failed.jsonl` (every line invalid at execution time, e.g. `temperature: 3`) via POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose="batch"` and `target_model_names`, getting back a unified `file-...` id 2. They create the batch via POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that input file id; the response shows `status: "validating"` and their pipeline moves on without polling it 3. On the provider's own dashboard the batch soon ends as `completed` with an `error_file_id` and `output_file_id: null`; nothing was served, and correctly no spend appears at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs 4. Within a couple of minutes of the batch ending, DELETE https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{input_file_id} returns 200 with `"deleted": true` 5. The `expired` batch with a real `output_file_id` now shows its served lines' spend at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs ## Relevant issues Fixes #35354 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5193 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live two-leg QA against real OpenAI batches. Each leg boots a DB-backed proxy from a fresh worktree with managed files enabled and `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=15`, then drives the User Flow above with the OpenAI Python SDK pointed at the proxy. Re-checking a batch through the gateway finalizes it on both commits, so after creation neither leg ever touches the batch through the proxy again: batch state is confirmed against the provider directly, the same check an admin makes on their own OpenAI account **Before, proxy at merge base `9d069f21dc`: the batch ends `completed` with only an error file and the input file can never be deleted** (times PDT, 2026-08-14) ``` >>> client.files.create(file=open("all_failed.jsonl","rb"), purpose="batch", ... extra_body={"target_model_names": "my-gpt"}) file id: bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9vY3RldC1zdHJlYW07dW5pZmllZF9pZCw1YzM1MGU2MS0xMmI1LTQ4NTYtYWMwMS0yY2VkMjkyNTQ5ZjM7... >>> client.batches.create(input_file_id=<that file id>, endpoint="/v1/chat/completions", ... completion_window="24h") batch id: bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDpteS1ncHQtdW5pZmllZC0xO2xsbV9iYXRjaF9pZDpiYXRjaF82YTdmOGVhMmI3ZTg4MTkwYWZiYmI1MDQ2ZmZjYTIxNQ status: validating ``` The provider finishes the batch at 14:57 with nothing served (checked directly against OpenAI, not through the proxy): ``` $ curl -s https://api.openai.com/v1/batches/batch_6a7f8ea2b7e88190afbbb5046ffca215 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" {"id": "batch_6a7f8ea2b7e88190afbbb5046ffca215", "status": "completed", "output_file_id": null, "error_file_id": "file-FGjQYjjE8GfvH2pDDcsXpo", "request_counts": {"total": 1, "completed": 0, "failed": 1}, ...} ``` Every input-file DELETE through the proxy is still refused hours later, identically at 17:19:47, 17:20:47, 17:21:47, and 17:25:44, roughly 2.5 hours and ~88 polling cycles after the batch went terminal: ``` $ curl -s -w "
HTTP %{http_code}
" -X DELETE http://localhost:41287/v1/files/<unified file id> \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"error":{"message":"Cannot delete file bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9vY3RldC1zdHJlYW07... The file is referenced by 1 batch(es) in non-terminal state: bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDpteS1ncHQtdW5pZmllZC0xO2xsbV9iYXRjaF9pZDpiYXRjaF82YTdmOGVhMmI3ZTg4MTkwYWZiYmI1MDQ2ZmZjYTIxNQ: validating. To delete this file before complete cost tracking, please delete or cancel the referencing batch(es) first. Alternatively, wait for all batches to complete and for cost to be computed (batch_processed=true).","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400"}} HTTP 400 ``` **After, proxy at the PR tip `eacea13a25`: identical flow and the very first DELETE attempt succeeds** ``` (same upload + create; batch batch_6a7f8a4b3ef081909f337e714fdb3629, status validating) $ curl -s https://api.openai.com/v1/batches/batch_6a7f8a4b3ef081909f337e714fdb3629 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" {"id": "batch_6a7f8a4b3ef081909f337e714fdb3629", "status": "completed", "output_file_id": null, "error_file_id": "file-XYQYeK4k9V7Qx3ExV1dvxv", "request_counts": {"total": 1, "completed": 0, "failed": 1}, ...} $ curl -s -w "
HTTP %{http_code}" -X DELETE http://localhost:43781/v1/files/<unified file id> \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"id":"bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTph...","bytes":181,"object":"file","status":"uploaded","purpose":"batch", "filename":"modified_file.jsonl","created_at":1786743348,"expires_at":1789335348,"status_details":null} HTTP 200 ``` The batch was finalized 5 seconds after the provider marked it terminal, well inside one 15s polling cycle, and the DELETE fired ~3.5 minutes later succeeded on the first attempt with no proxy-side batch check ever made QA observations: - Expired-billing leg not live-testable (24h expiry); regression tests cover - File DELETE 200 returns file object, no deleted flag; pre-existing ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Coexists with #36714: that sweep retires aged uncostable rows, this marks terminal rows immediately - Rebase note: `expired`-with-output moved from the persists test to the billing test ## Changes `CheckBatchCost.check_batch_cost` had two arms: `completed` with an output file (bill, then mark processed) and `failed`/`expired`/`cancelled` (mark processed without billing). A `completed`/`complete` batch with `output_file_id=None` matched neither, so `batch_processed` stayed `false` and the poller re-selected the same row on every cycle for the life of the deployment; output/error file deletion is gated on `batch_processed`, so those files could never be deleted through the managed API either. The billing arm now triggers for `completed`/`complete`/`expired` when an output file is present, so an `expired` batch that really produced output is still billed (those request lines were served). It writes back the batch's real terminal status (normalizing `completed` to `complete` like the retrieve endpoint does) instead of hardcoding `complete`, so a billed `expired` batch stays `expired` in the DB, matching the stored batch JSON. The second arm now covers the full terminal set (`completed`/`complete`/`failed`/`expired`/`cancelled`) so any terminal batch with nothing to bill (failed/cancelled, or completed/expired with no output) is marked processed exactly once. Non-terminal statuses (`validating`/`in_progress`) still fall through both arms and are left for the next poll The two report-flagged behaviours are covered as tests: a still-in-progress batch is not written back, and an expired batch with an output file is billed. The `#35131`-style case where the provider fetch itself raises is unchanged and out of scope here (that row is already left for retry by the existing `except` around `aretrieve_batch`) On the rebase itself: staging's terminal arm now also mints unified managed file IDs before the write-back (`ensure_batch_response_managed_file_ids`), which this branch keeps; and since `expired`-with-output now takes the billing arm, `test_terminal_status_persists_managed_output_file_ids` parametrizes only `failed`/`cancelled`, with the expired case covered by `test_expired_with_output_file_is_billed` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit eacea13a257d934627714b554dd1fd2c2b44b261. signal.title: [Bug]: CheckBatchCost never marks a terminal batch with no output file as processed — row re-polled forever
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? A managed batch whose request lines all failed reaches a terminal provider status (`completed`) with `output_file_id=None` and only an `error_file_id`. The `CheckBatchCost` background job never transitions that row: `batch_processed` stays `false` indefinitely, so the job query re-selects the same row on every polling cycle for the lifetime of the deployment. There is no exception. The provider retrieve succeeds and returns a correct terminal status — the row is simply never handled, so nothing surfaces in the logs beyond the row being picked up again each cycle. Two consequences: - Wasted DB queries and poller work that compound as more such batches accumulate. - Output-file deletion is gated on `batch_processed`, so the batch's output and error files can never be deleted through the managed API. **Expected:** once the poller observes a terminal provider status, the row is marked terminal (`batch_processed=true`) exactly once. A batch with no output file has no billable completion output, so it should be marked terminal *without* being billed. Two behaviours a fix needs to preserve, both worth covering as test cases: - A batch still `validating` / `in_progress` must **not** be treated as terminal — otherwise it is marked processed and never polled again. - An `expired` batch that **did** produce an output file must still be billed; those request lines were really served. Only `failed` / `cancelled` / `expired`-without-output have nothing to bill. ### Possibly related #35131 reports stuck `LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable` rows in `CheckResponsesCost`. Same symptom class, but as far as we can tell a different trigger, so we are filing separately rather than commenting there: | | #35131 | This report | |---|---|---| | Poller | `CheckResponsesCost` | `CheckBatchCost` | | Rows | `file_purpose='response'` | `file_purpose='batch'` | | Stuck at | `queued` | `completed` / `expired`, `batch_processed=false` | | Behaviour | provider fetch raises, so the status logic is never reached | provider fetch succeeds and returns a terminal status; the row is not handled | Neither half of PR #35137 (fetch through `llm_router`; add `incomplete` to the terminal set) appears to affect this case — the batch retrieve already goes through the router and already returns a status that is recognised as terminal. That said, #35137's `incomplete` change is the closest analogue: a status that should be terminal but was not enumerated, leaving rows polled forever. This looks like the same shape reached by a different route. One more case, which we have **not** verified and are raising only because the same concern was flagged on #35137: a batch whose deployment has been removed or renamed since creation may be a third route to a permanently stuck row. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run a DB-backed proxy with managed files/batches enabled (`/v1/files` and `/v1/batches` returning `litellm_proxy;...` unified IDs), `CheckBatchCost` enabled, and a short poll interval — `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=5`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-gpt litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY model_info: id: my-gpt_unified-1 general_settings: database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL litellm_settings: enable_preview_features: true ``` 2. Create `all_failed.jsonl`, where every request line is rejected by the provider (`temperature: 3` is out of range): ```jsonl {"custom_id":"1","method":"POST","url":"/v1/chat/completions","body":{"model":"my-gpt","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"temperature":3}} ``` 3. Upload it and create a batch: ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url=PROXY_URL, api_key=KEY) f = client.files.create( file=open("all_failed.jsonl", "rb"), purpose="batch", extra_body={"target_model_names": "my-gpt"}, ) b = client.batches.create( input_file_id=f.id, endpoint="/v1/chat/completions", completion_window="24h", ) ``` 4. Poll until terminal, and confirm the provider-side shape: ```python b = client.batches.retrieve(b.id) print(b.status, b.output_file_id, b.error_file_id, b.request_counts) # completed None file-... {'total': 1, 'completed': 0, 'failed': 1} ``` 5. Poll the managed object row over several minutes — long enough for multiple `CheckBatchCost` cycles: ```sql SELECT unified_object_id, status, batch_processed FROM "LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable" WHERE unified_object_id = '<unified batch id>'; ``` Observe `batch_processed` stays `false` indefinitely. 6. Confirm the repetition in the poller logs — the same `unified_object_id` is picked up on every cycle. 7. Attempt to delete the batch's error file through the managed API. It is refused while `batch_processed = false`. ### Relevant log output ```shell # No exception is raised. The only symptom in the logs is the same # unified_object_id being selected by CheckBatchCost on every cycle: CheckBatchCost: processing job litellm_proxy;model_id:my-gpt_unified-1;llm_batch_id:batch_abc... CheckBatchCost: processing job litellm_proxy;model_id:my-gpt_unified-1;llm_batch_id:batch_abc... CheckBatchCost: processing job litellm_proxy;model_id:my-gpt_unified-1;llm_batch_id:batch_abc... # ... indefinitely, one per polling interval ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v.189.1 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: feat(scripts): queue heavy gates behind a machine-wide slot lock
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - N parallel `make check` runs across worktrees thrash one machine - Every run slows down and long commands start timing out flaky How it solves it: - New `scripts/gate_slot_lock.py`: machine-wide fcntl slot lock, 2 slots - `make check`/`bootstrap`/`lint` and the budget gates queue through it - Nested invocations reenter via an env marker, so no deadlocks - `LITELLM_GATE_SLOTS` overrides the count; `0` disables; errors fail open ## User Flow Before: a developer running several agent sessions has three worktrees run `make check` at once, and the machine becomes unusable 1. Three sessions each run `make check` in their own litellm worktree at the same time 2. Three basedpyright/prettier/pytest storms execute simultaneously, CPU and RAM peg, and every run crawls 3. Unrelated commands on the machine slow down or time out while all three grind on After: the same three runs queue two at a time and all pass 1. Three sessions each run `make check` in their own litellm worktree at the same time 2. Two runs proceed immediately; the third prints `gate_slot_lock: all 2 machine-wide slots are busy; queueing (set LITELLM_GATE_SLOTS=0 to disable)` and waits 3. As soon as one of the first two finishes, the queued run starts on its own and ends in `check: PASS` like the others 4. A developer who wants the old behavior sets `LITELLM_GATE_SLOTS=0` (or another slot count) and the lock steps aside ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Three concurrent `make check` runs in one worktree at eafddaaa12: runs 1 and 2 hold the two slots, run 3 prints the queueing notice and starts as soon as a slot frees, and all three pass ``` $ for i in 1 2 3; do bash -c "echo \"run $i launched \$(date +%T)\"; make check > /tmp/slotdemo_$i.log 2>&1; echo \"run $i exit=\$? finished \$(date +%T)\"" & done; wait run 1 launched 17:23:23 run 2 launched 17:23:23 run 3 launched 17:23:23 run 2 exit=0 finished 17:23:25 run 1 exit=0 finished 17:23:25 run 3 exit=0 finished 17:23:27 $ grep -l queueing /tmp/slotdemo_*.log && grep -h queueing /tmp/slotdemo_3.log /tmp/slotdemo_3.log gate_slot_lock: all 2 machine-wide slots are busy; queueing (set LITELLM_GATE_SLOTS=0 to disable) $ for i in 1 2 3; do echo "run $i verdict: $(grep -o 'check: PASS' /tmp/slotdemo_$i.log | head -1)"; done run 1 verdict: check: PASS run 2 verdict: check: PASS run 3 verdict: check: PASS ``` The header-documented hook install keeps working (a first draft of this change broke it; a regression test now pins it). In a fresh clone of eafddaaa12: ``` $ ln -s ../../scripts/pre_commit_lint.sh .git/hooks/pre-commit $ echo demo > demo.txt && git add demo.txt && git commit -m "chore: demo commit through the hook" check: full log: .../.git/pre_commit_lint.log [litellm_make_check_slot_lock 8d84ba99ae] chore: demo commit through the hook 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+) commit exit=0 ``` `make check` with everything staged at eafddaaa12 exits 0 with `check: PASS`, and that run itself exercises the nested chain (`make check` -> wrapper -> `check-inner` -> `bootstrap` -> `pre_commit_lint.sh` -> `make lint` -> budget gates) acquiring exactly one slot ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats (if any) - `make -jN check` sub-make may warn "jobserver unavailable"; inner targets are serial anyway - Queueing is roughly FIFO; a fresh arrival can occasionally beat a waiter to a freed slot - CI takes the instant-acquire path (one job per machine) and any lock error fails open ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(anthropic cost): apply regional geo uplift to cached tokens
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Anthropic regional uplift skipped cache read and write cost - Cache-heavy regional spend under-reported by roughly 10% How it solves it: - Geo multiplier now scales the full cost - `fast` multiplier stays cache-exclusive as before - Spend log cost breakdown line items carry the same multiplier, so they keep summing to the total ## User Flow Before: a developer running long-context Anthropic traffic out of a US region sees the gateway report almost exactly the non-regional price, so their spend never matches the Anthropic invoice 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `claude-opus-4-8` with `"inference_geo": "us"` and a large system prompt marked for 1h prompt caching 2. The reply comes back reporting 14784 cache-creation tokens and 9 plain input tokens 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is logged at $0.14788950, no higher than the $0.14791000 the same call without a region logs 4. The US price list is 10% above global, so they expected about $0.16270, and what they got means the uplift only reached the 9 non-cache tokens 5. They end the month reconciling by hand, adding a flat 10% on top of the gateway's Anthropic spend After: the same request is logged at the regional price, so no manual correction is needed 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and the same cached system prompt 2. The reply again reports 14784 cache-creation tokens and 9 plain input tokens 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows $0.16270100, 10% above the $0.14791000 global price 4. Traffic with no region, or on global inference, still logs $0.14791000 5. Opening that request's cost breakdown (also on GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=<response id>) shows the cache-creation line item at the uplifted rate, and the line items sum to the logged total ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4866 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy against the real Anthropic API, real spend, `claude-sonnet-5` (carries `us: 1.1` in the price map; Anthropic accepts `inference_geo` for it and echoes it back in usage). The fix rides the shared Anthropic cost path, so both legs proved all three unified endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, and /v1/responses. Every request sent a unique ~18k-token system prompt marked `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}` so nearly every prompt token is a fresh cache-creation token, the shape that made the uplift vanish, with only 9 non-cache input tokens and 0 output tokens. Cost read off the `x-litellm-response-cost` response header, the surface a caller sees Before leg at `f03df1bb42` (the merge base on `litellm_internal_staging`), after leg at `e94a97fcfc` (this PR's head). Six requests per leg: each endpoint once with `"inference_geo": "us"` in the body and once without ```bash H=(-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234') curl -sD - localhost:$PORT/v1/chat/completions "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_tokens":16,"inference_geo":"us", "messages":[{"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<18k-token unique prompt>","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}]}, {"role":"user","content":"Say OK."}]}' curl -sD - localhost:$PORT/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_tokens":16,"inference_geo":"us", "system":[{"type":"text","text":"<18k-token unique prompt>","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}], "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say OK."}]}' curl -sD - localhost:$PORT/v1/responses "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_output_tokens":16,"inference_geo":"us", "input":[{"role":"system","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"<18k-token unique prompt>","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}]}, {"role":"user","content":"Say OK."}]}' # plus the same three with inference_geo removed, each with a fresh unique prompt ``` Before, at `f03df1bb42`, asking for `us` costs the same as not asking (the 10% uplift reaches only the 9 non-cache tokens; every header value decomposes exactly as cache_tokens x $2.50/M + 9 x $2.20/M with geo vs 9 x $2.00/M without): ``` /v1/chat/completions geo=us 0.0462423 cache_create=18489 | global 0.046328 cache_create=18524 ratio 0.998 /v1/messages geo=us 0.0464923 cache_create=18589 | global 0.046488 cache_create=18588 ratio 1.000 /v1/responses geo=us 0.0464823 cache_write=18585 | global 0.046493 cache_write=18590 ratio 1.000 ``` After, at `e94a97fcfc`, the geo cost is exactly 1.10x the closed-form global price of its own token counts, cache included, and no-geo traffic is unchanged: ``` /v1/chat/completions geo=us 0.0508673 cache_create=18490 | global 0.0462305 cache_create=18485 normalized ratio 1.1000 /v1/messages geo=us 0.05113405 cache_create=18587 | global 0.0464855 cache_create=18587 raw ratio 1.1000 /v1/responses geo=us 0.05112855 cache_write=18585 | global 0.046498 cache_write=18592 normalized ratio 1.1000 ``` Every header value decomposes exactly as cache_tokens x $2.75/M + 9 x $2.20/M with geo vs cache_tokens x $2.50/M + 9 x $2.00/M without; the /v1/messages pair even landed on identical cache token counts, making the raw ratio exactly 1.1000 The review-round commit (`e94a97fcfc`) also mirrors the uplift into the per-token-type cost breakdown that spend logs carry, so line items keep summing to the total. signal.title: fix(anthropic): aggregate 5m/1h cache-write split across iterations path
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Anthropic reports cache writes per iteration when a request loops over tool calls - That nested 5m/1h split is dropped, so 1h cache writes get billed at the 5m rate How it solves it: - The per-iteration `cache_creation` breakdowns are summed into one 5m/1h split - Cache writes an iteration reports without a breakdown are billed at the default 5m rate - Top-level `cache_creation` stays the source when there are no iterations ## User Flow Before: a developer whose Anthropic traffic loops over tool calls is undercharged for 1h cache writes, so their gateway spend does not match the Anthropic console 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with a `cache_control` block of `{"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}` and tools that make the request run several iterations 2. Anthropic returns usage where each iteration carries its own `cache_creation` breakdown showing the writes were 1h 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the cache-write tokens billed at the 5m rate, roughly 40% under the 1h price After: the same request bills the 1h rate, matching what a single-iteration request with the same cache writes already cost 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages request 2. Anthropic returns the same per-iteration usage breakdown 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the cache writes at the 1h rate 4. An iteration that reports cache-write tokens without a 5m/1h breakdown still bills those writes at the 5m rate, and requests with no iterations at all are billed exactly as before The same holds on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses, which bill this traffic identically ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4868 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Screen recording of the original before and after run on the shape this PR fixes, in one video, is in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1786414063855749?thread_ts=1786408619.329699&cid=C0BE49SAUE6). It captured the before at `1d3b64c66f` and the after at the PR's first commit; the full re-run below supersedes it as written proof Latest full QA run: before at `f03df1bb42` (merge base, current `litellm_internal_staging` without the fix), after at `0ab23f5ce9` (this PR's head). Each leg booted a live proxy plus Postgres-backed spend logs from its own worktree and hit all three unified endpoints; every cost below was confirmed both in the `x-litellm-response-cost` response header and in the persisted row returned by `GET /spend/logs`. Two halves, because the two usage shapes cannot both come from the same place First, the shape this PR fixes. Nothing we could send made the real API return an `iterations` usage breakdown, so this half was driven from a stand-in Anthropic upstream emitting it: 1000 cache-write tokens, all 1h, split 500+500 across two iterations, plus 10 input and 5 output tokens ```bash H=(-H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json') curl -sS -i localhost:$PORT/v1/chat/completions "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"opus48-iter","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' curl -sS -i localhost:$PORT/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"opus48-iter","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' curl -sS -i localhost:$PORT/v1/responses "${H[@]}" -d '{"model":"opus48-iter","input":"hello"}' ``` Before, at `f03df1bb42` (proxy on port 24583), the split is lost and every route bills the 5m rate: ``` /v1/chat/completions cost=0.006425 spend_log=0.006425 /v1/messages cost=0.006425 spend_log=0.006425 /v1/responses cost=0.006425 spend_log=0.006425 ``` 0.006425 = 1000 x $6.25/M (5m write rate) + 10 x $5/M + 5 x $25/M After, at `0ab23f5ce9` (proxy on port 25733), every route bills the 1h rate, and the response usage carries the aggregated split `{ephemeral_5m_input_tokens: 0, ephemeral_1h_input_tokens: 1000}`: ``` /v1/chat/completions cost=0.010175 spend_log=0.010175 /v1/messages cost=0.010175 spend_log=0.010175 /v1/responses cost=0.010175 spend_log=0.010175 ``` 0.010175 = 1000 x $10/M (1h write rate) + 10 x $5/M + 5 x $25/M Second, the shape that was already correct, live against the real Anthropic API with real spend, `claude-opus-4-8`, a fresh unique ~8k-token system text cached with `"ttl": "1h"` on every call (same curl form, bodies in the worktree's payload files): Before, at `f03df1bb42`, all three routes bill the 1h rate to the digit: ``` /v1/chat/completions cost=0.08714 (8708 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) /v1/messages cost=0.08626 (8620 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) /v1/responses cost=0.08592 (8586 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) ``` After, at `0ab23f5ce9`, unchanged, still the 1h rate to the digit: ``` /v1/chat/completions cost=0.08037 (8031 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) /v1/messages cost=0.07972 (7966 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) /v1/responses cost=0.07959 (7953 write tokens x $10/M + 12 x $5/M) ``` So the iterations path now agrees with what the same writes already cost through the top-level shape, on every unified endpoint, in the header and the spend log alike Observations from the run, all pre-existing and untouched by this PR: - Spend-log request_id lookup wants response id, not call id - Unflushed spend rows are lost when the proxy dies - Real calls sometimes return refusals with zero output tokens ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Current `litellm_internal_staging` is merged into the branch - The `iterations` half of the proof is not real-provider traffic, see above for why - Resolving the split moved into one helper so the value is computed once instead of being reassigned across branches ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/13d7b3dbf5a641f0a24aa0b48893d315
