signal.title: fix(cost): carry modality token counts through the Responses usage bridge
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The Responses usage bridge drops modality token counts - Output audio billed as nothing: a measured 52x under-count How it solves it: - Declare and carry audio, image and video through the bridge - Replace the repeated per-field copying with a modality loop ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Realtime cost is computed from `*_tokens_details` after the usage round-trips through the Responses shape. `InputTokensDetails` declares `audio_tokens`; `OutputTokensDetails` did not, and `_transform_chat_completion_usage_to_responses_usage` copied `reasoning_tokens`, `text_tokens` and `image_tokens` but not audio. So input audio was priced and output audio, the more expensive half, was discarded. **Where it was lost.** Feeding one real Gemini Live `usageMetadata` through the chain, before the fix: ``` STEP 1 _calculate_usage -> completion_tokens: 200 completion_tokens_details: {... 'audio_tokens': 180, 'text_tokens': 20 ...} STEP 2 -> responses usage -> {"output_tokens": 200, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": null, "text_tokens": 20}} ``` 180 audio tokens are extracted correctly and then dropped one step later. **Before**, dev gateway at `53cec79d55`. A real voice session on `vertex_ai/gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio`. Vertex reported 200 output tokens of which 180 were audio, and the spend row read: ``` prompt/completion : 4 / 200 logged spend : $0.00004200 ``` `$0.0000420` is exactly `4 text in + 20 text out` at the configured rates. The 180 audio tokens cost nothing. Correct is `$0.0022020`, so the call under-billed by 52x. **After**, dev gateway at `ec9d9abfa2`, real sessions on both GA Live models, reading the spend rows back from `/spend/logs/v2`: ``` vertex_ai/gemini-live-2.5-flash (16 in / 30 out) $0.000318 -> 5 text + 25 audio out; audio is 94% of cost; pre-fix would bill $0.000018 vertex_ai/gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio (16 in / 60 out) $0.000668 -> 6 text + 54 audio out; audio is 97% of cost; pre-fix would bill $0.000020 vertex_ai/gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio (3 in / 61 out) $0.000633 -> 10 text + 51 audio out; audio is 97% of cost; pre-fix would bill $0.000021 ``` Each billed amount reconciles to exactly one text/audio split at the entry's own rates with no slack, which is what shows the audio is genuinely priced rather than merely non-zero. Audio is 94 to 97 percent of a voice call, so this is most of the cost of the modality. Input audio was measured separately and was never affected: a session fed real speech reported `input_tokens: 168` with `audio_tokens: 155` and nothing unattributed. That asymmetry between the two detail types is what located the bug. This is not Vertex-specific. OpenAI's Realtime API reports output audio tokens too, so `gpt-realtime` sessions lose them on the same path; the shared type is the right place to fix it. ## Also fixed on the input side Vertex splits prompt tokens by modality, so a Live session sending camera frames arrives with `image_tokens` set. `InputTokensDetails` declared only audio, cached and text, so image and video were folded into `text_tokens` and lost their attribution: ``` before: chat usage image_tokens 200 -> responses {audio 80, cached 0, text 20} -> back: None after: chat usage image_tokens 200 -> responses {audio 80, image 150, video 50, text 20} -> back: 150 / 50 ``` The billed amount does not move today, because the calculator falls back to `input_cost_per_token` when no per-modality rate is set (`llm_cost_calc/utils.py:589`), so those tokens were already charged at the text rate rather than lost from the bill. But they have to survive the bridge before any per-modality rate can ever apply to them, which is why it belongs with the audio fix rather than after it. Worth flagging separately, since it is not this PR's scope: on a `vertex_ai` model, `get_model_info` returns `None` for `input_cost_per_image_token` even when the cost-map entry carries it, so setting that rate has no effect today. That is a different file and it is not realtime-specific. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `OutputTokensDetails` gains `audio_tokens` and `InputTokensDetails` gains `image_tokens` and `video_tokens`, making the two symmetric. Both branches of the forward transform now carry every modality. The reverse transform already read `image_tokens`; `video_tokens` is added alongside it. The near-identical `hasattr`/`is not None` blocks became a loop over the modality names in each branch. That is not cosmetic: adding one more branch pushed `C901` over its ceiling, and the loop removes the branching entirely so a future modality costs no complexity. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(helm): bound the migrations Job so a blocked migration cannot stall the release
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A blocked schema migration hangs the release forever - `backoffLimit` never fires: the pod never terminates - Operators must delete the Job by hand to recover - Unrelated gateway, backend and UI changes silently stop shipping How it solves it: - Add `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds` to both charts - Default 1800s, so a stuck Job fails instead of hanging - Guarded by `with`, so `null` restores the old behaviour ## User Flow Before: an operator upgrading the chart, whose migration blocks on the database, gets an upgrade that never returns 1. They run `helm upgrade litellm ./helm/litellm -f values.yaml` 2. The migration Job starts and its container blocks talking to the database 3. The command sits waiting on the pre-upgrade hook and never returns 4. `kubectl get job litellm-migrations` still reads `Running 0/1` hours later, with no conditions set 5. Nothing else in the release rolls out, so unrelated gateway, backend and UI changes never reach the cluster 6. The only way out is `kubectl delete job litellm-migrations` by hand After: the same upgrade gives up on its own, so the operator gets a failure they can act on instead of a hang 1. They run the same `helm upgrade litellm ./helm/litellm -f values.yaml` 2. The migration Job starts and blocks on the database exactly as before 3. After `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds` (1800 by default) the Job reports `Failed`, reason `DeadlineExceeded` 4. `helm upgrade` returns non-zero naming the failed hook rather than waiting forever 5. The rest of the release is no longer pinned behind a Job that cannot finish, so the next attempt can proceed once the database issue is addressed 6. An operator who wants the old unbounded behaviour sets `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds: null` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix There is no HTTP route to exercise here, so the proof is the rendered manifest plus a live Kubernetes cluster showing the two Jobs behave differently. **1. The field renders, in both charts.** Captured at `ae3e19a83f` ``` $ helm template t helm/litellm -f helm/litellm/tests/values/required.yaml | grep -A1 ttlSecondsAfterFinished ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 120 activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800 $ helm template t helm/litellm-helm | grep -B1 -A1 activeDeadlineSeconds ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 120 backoffLimit: 4 activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800 ``` **2. A blocked migration now terminates.** Live `kind` cluster, two Jobs identical except for the new field, each running a container that starts and then blocks the way a migration waiting on an unreachable database does. The 30s deadline stands in for the 1800s default so the run is observable ``` $ kubectl apply -f before.yaml -f after.yaml job.batch/mig-no-deadline-v2 created job.batch/mig-with-deadline-v2 created $ kubectl logs job/mig-no-deadline-v2 connecting to database... $ for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do sleep 15; echo "t=$((i*15))s"; kubectl get jobs --no-headers; done t=15s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 20s mig-with-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 20s t=30s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 35s mig-with-deadline-v2 FailureTarget 0/1 35s t=60s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 65s mig-with-deadline-v2 Failed 0/1 65s t=75s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 80s mig-with-deadline-v2 Failed 0/1 80s ``` Terminal state of each: ``` $ kubectl get job mig-with-deadline-v2 -o jsonpath='{range .status.conditions[*]}type={.type} reason={.reason} message={.message}{"\n"}{end}' type=FailureTarget reason=DeadlineExceeded message=Job was active longer than specified deadline type=Failed reason=DeadlineExceeded message=Job was active longer than specified deadline $ kubectl get job mig-no-deadline-v2 -o jsonpath='conditions={.status.conditions} active={.status.active}' conditions= active=1 ``` The Job without the field never reaches a terminal state, which is what leaves a release waiting on it. The Job with the field fails on its own. **3. The tests fail without the change.** Reverting only the two templates and the two values files, keeping the new tests, at base `f03df1bb42` ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm FAIL test migrations Job ServiceAccount resolution and pod hardening - bounds the Job with a deadline by default, so a blocked migration cannot stall the release forever - honours an operator-supplied deadline Tests: 2 failed, 72 passed, 74 total ``` The third new test asserts the field is absent when nulled, which passes either way, so it was mutation-tested separately: dropping the `with` guard so the field always renders makes it fail. ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/migration_job_tests.yaml' helm/litellm FAIL - omits the deadline entirely when it is nulled out, restoring the unbounded behaviour Tests: 1 failed, 15 passed, 16 total ``` Restored, both suites are green at `ae3e19a83f` ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm Tests: 74 passed, 74 total $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm-helm Tests: 97 passed, 97 total ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The container blocking was simulated, not a genuinely wedged database connection - Default changes behaviour: migrations running past 1800s now fail - Measured healthy runs finish in about 30s, so headroom is roughly 60x - The budget is shared across all `backoffLimit` retries, not per attempt - A killed migration can leave a partially applied entry needing manual resolution - `Chart.yaml` untouched, matching recent template-only changes to litellm-helm ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(rerank): populate token usage in spend logs and /ui/usage
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - /ui/usage always shows 0 tokens for rerank calls, for every provider, not just hosted_vllm - hosted_vllm rerank servers returning Cohere-style `meta` usage get silently zeroed to 0 How it solves it: - Added a `meta.billed_units`/`meta.tokens` fallback to both usage-extraction functions in litellm_logging.py - Made HostedVLLMRerankConfig read usage from either `meta` (Cohere-style) or `usage` (OpenAI-style) ## Relevant issues Fixes #36185 ([Bug]: /ui/usage shows 0 tokens for rerank calls (hosted_vllm and other providers) ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Commit tested: 518d9aca9a (branch fix/rerank-usage-tracking, based on v1.95.0) 1. Rerank request: curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/rerank \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{ "model": "local/BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", "query": "Что такое vLLM?", "documents": ["vLLM это быстрый движок инференса", "Сегодня идет дождь"] }' Response: {"id":"rerank-77dab01cce4844158840b6d6778fb3d8","results":[{"index":0,"relevance_score":0.9978354573249817,"document":{"text":"vLLM это быстрый движок инференса"}},{"index":1,"relevance_score":0.000016201263861148618,"document":{"text":"Сегодня идет дождь"}}],"meta":{"billed_units":{"total_tokens":38},"tokens":{"input_tokens":38}}} 2. Spend log lookup for that request: curl "http://127.0.0.1:4000/spend/logs?request_id=rerank-77dab01cce4844158840b6d6778fb3d8" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" Relevant fields from the response (trimmed for brevity): { "request_id": "rerank-77dab01cce4844158840b6d6778fb3d8", "call_type": "arerank", "model": "hosted_vllm/BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", "total_tokens": 38, "prompt_tokens": 38, "completion_tokens": 0, "spend": 0.0 } Before this fix, total_tokens/prompt_tokens in the spend log were always 0 for rerank calls regardless of the raw response's meta.billed_units.total_tokens. After the fix, they correctly match the model's reported usage (38). ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/llms/hosted_vllm/rerank/transformation.py`: read usage from `meta` or `usage` - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py`: `get_usage_from_response_obj` and `get_usage_as_dict` now fall back to `meta.billed_units`/`meta.tokens` when there's no top-level `usage` - Added regression tests in `tests/logging_callback_tests/test_standard_logging_payload.py` and `tests/test_litellm/llms/hosted_vllm/test_hosted_vllm_rerank_transformation.py`

signal.title: [Bug]: bedrock_mantle rejects max_tokens for Gemma models (google.gemma-4-*)
signal.text: ### What happened? Bedrock Mantle's OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint rejects the `max_tokens` parameter for `google.gemma-4-*` models, and there is no per-model handling in `BedrockMantleChatConfig` to work around it — the parameter is forwarded unchanged (like any other OpenAI-compatible provider) and Bedrock returns a 400-shaped error, which surfaces as `litellm.APIConnectionError`. I also verified that the AWS docs' own sample-code parameter name for this model, `max_output_tokens` (the name used for Bedrock's native Converse/InvokeModel APIs), is **not** a valid substitute here either — it's simply not recognized on this OpenAI-compatible route at all. Omitting the parameter entirely is the only thing that succeeds. ### Relevant log output ``` litellm.APIConnectionError: Bedrock_mantleException - {"error":{"code":"unsupported_parameter","message":"Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model.","param":"max_tokens","type":"invalid_request_error"}} ``` ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0-dev (confirmed present on latest main as of 2026-08-14; also present on v1.93.0) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_ ### Reproduction ```python from litellm.llms.bedrock_mantle.chat.transformation import BedrockMantleChatConfig config = BedrockMantleChatConfig() result = config.map_openai_params( non_default_params={"max_tokens": 50}, optional_params={}, model="google.gemma-4-31b", drop_params=False, ) print(result) # Actual: {'max_tokens': 50} -- forwarded unchanged, will 400 against real Bedrock # Expected: {} -- max_tokens should not be sent for this model family ``` Confirmed against the real Bedrock endpoint (not mocked), via a `bedrock_mantle/google.gemma-4-31b` deployment: | Request body | Result | |---|---| | `max_tokens: 50` | `unsupported_parameter: max_tokens` | | `max_output_tokens: 50` (AWS's native-API param name) | `unknown_parameter: max_output_tokens` — not recognized on this route at all | | param omitted entirely | `200 OK` | Also confirmed that setting `drop_params: true` at the config/router level does **not** work around this: `drop_params` only filters parameters that `get_supported_openai_params()` already declares unsupported client-side. Since `max_tokens` is a normal, generally-supported OpenAI param and `BedrockMantleChatConfig` doesn't override `get_supported_openai_params` to exclude it for Gemma, LiteLLM has no way to know ahead of time that Bedrock will reject it server-side. ### Proposed fix `BedrockMantleChatConfig` (`litellm/llms/bedrock_mantle/chat/transformation.py`) should override `map_openai_params` to drop `max_tokens` (after the parent's existing `max_completion_tokens` → `max_tokens` rename) when the target model is a Gemma variant — following the same model-substring-exclusion pattern already used elsewhere in this file's neighborhood (e.g. `AmazonAnthropicClaudeConfig._needs_tool_workaround` in the Bedrock Invoke Anthropic transformation). Happy to open a PR with this fix plus a regression test — have already verified it end-to-end against real Bedrock in a downstream fork. Will link the PR here.

signal.title: fix(proxy): exclude Pydantic defaults in /config/update so existing fields are not wiped (Fixes #36446)
signal.text: ## Summary `POST /config/update` silently wiped `router_settings.model_group_alias` to `{}` on every router-settings edit that did not explicitly include the alias map. Editing `routing_groups` or changing a `routing_strategy` through the Admin UI would clobber the existing alias map, and the `400 Invalid model name` errors that followed looked like a periodic "aliases wiped" bug. The same pattern applied to any `{}`/`[]`-defaulted field on `UpdateRouterConfig` and `ConfigGeneralSettings`. Root cause: in `update_config()`, the router-settings and general-settings update payloads are built via `dict(exclude_none=True)`, which only drops `None` values. Pydantic fields with non-`None` defaults (e.g. `UpdateRouterConfig.model_group_alias: Optional[Dict[...]] = {}`) leak their default into the serialized payload even when the caller never sent them. The shallow merge `{**existing, **updates}` then overwrites the real value with the default. Fix: add `exclude_defaults=True` to both `dict(exclude_none=True)` calls. Pydantic's `exclude_defaults` flag drops any field whose value equals the field's default — so the `{}` default for `model_group_alias` no longer leaks into the update payload, and the shallow merge correctly preserves the existing alias map. Fixes #36446. ## Changes ### `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` - Line 14532 (`general_settings` update): `dict(exclude_none=True)` → `dict(exclude_none=True, exclude_defaults=True)`. Comment block on the new kwarg documents the bug class and cross-references #36446. - Line 14607 (`router_settings` update): same one-kwarg change. Comment block explains the `model_group_alias` symptom. The two call sites are the only `dict(exclude_none=True)` calls in the proxy; the change is the minimum-scope fix. ### `tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_routes_config.py` - New `test_config_update_preserves_existing_router_settings_alias_map` regression pin. Seeds the stored config with a non-empty `model_group_alias` (`{"security": "luna"}`), sends a `/config/update` that only touches `routing_groups`, and asserts the persisted `router_settings` still has `model_group_alias == {"security": "luna"}` (not the Pydantic default `{}`). - New `test_config_update_preserves_existing_general_settings_default_dict_fields` regression pin. Seeds the stored config with a non-default `alerting_threshold`, sends a `/config/update` that only touches `alerting`, and asserts the persisted `general_settings` still has the existing `alerting_threshold` value. Both tests use the existing `_install_litellm_config` helper to install a `litellm_config` table mock, then capture the `table.upsert` call args to assert the persisted JSON. They mirror the structure of the existing `test_config_update_happy_admin` so the regression pin lives next to the existing pin. ## Verification Local (this branch, `litellm_internal_staging` @ `2bb297efa0` base): - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_routes_config.py` — 38/38 pass (36 pre-existing + 2 new). - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py` — 117/117 pass (no regressions on the related ProxyConfig / config-storage tests). - `ruff check litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` — clean. - `ruff format --check litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` — already formatted. - `scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py` — OK (every strict rule within its codebase ceiling). - `scripts/type_discipline_gate.py` — OK (every LIT rule within its codebase ceiling; no new suppressions introduced). Bug-reproduction check (cycle 14 self-audit, "fix all X" pattern from the agent memory): - Stashed the source fix, re-ran both new tests. `test_config_update_preserves_existing_router_settings_alias_map` fails with `assert persisted["model_group_alias"] == {"security": "luna"}` — `AssertionError: assert {} == {"security": "luna"}` — the exact wipe symptom the issue documents. Restored the fix, the test passes. The general_settings test is robust to the bug because `GeneralSettings` has `None` defaults (not `{}`) for the fields the test exercises; the fix is still the right pattern for symmetry with the router_settings call site, and a future `ConfigGeneralSettings` field added with a `{}` default would automatically be protected. ## Design notes - **Why `exclude_defaults=True` rather than changing the Pydantic model defaults to `None`** — the `{}` default on `UpdateRouterConfig.model_group_alias` is a deliberate API choice (it tells `update_settings` to "clear the alias map" when the caller explicitly sends `model_group_alias: {}`). Changing the default to `None` would break that contract. The issue's suggested fix is to filter at serialization, not change the model, and that's the right minimum-scope change. - **Why both the `general_settings` and `router_settings` paths get the same fix** — they have the identical shallow-merge pattern and the same bug class. The issue's "related" section calls out that "the `general_settings` handler has the identical pattern and likely needs the same treatment". Applying the same one-kwarg fix to both is the minimum-scope way to address the bug class. - **Why no change to the `litellm_settings` update path** — that path uses `dict(config_info.litellm_settings)` (a regular dict constructor) rather than `.dict(exclude_none=True)`. The bug class is the same, but the path also has success_callback special-casing that depends on the incoming dict shape. A drive-by fix there would expand the PR's surface and risk breaking the success_callback normalizer. Out of scope for this PR; a natural cycle 15+ candidate. - **Why the `SimpleNamespace(param_value=...)` mock pattern** — the `_read_section` helper inside `update_config` returns `dict(row.param_value)`, so a plain dict for `param_value` is what the helper expects. `SimpleNamespace` is the smallest mock that lets the test set just the one attribute the helper reads. - **Why two separate tests (one per update path) rather than a parametrized test** — the two paths have different shape contracts (router_settings is a single `model_group_alias` field that maps 1:1; general_settings has many fields with `None` defaults and a `_alert_to_webhook_url` side-effect handler). Two explicit tests read more clearly and pin the exact symptom in each path. ## Risks - **Very low.** The change adds a kwarg to two existing Pydantic `dict()` calls. The `exclude_defaults` flag is documented to drop any field whose value equals the Pydantic default, so fields the caller explicitly sent with the same value as the default are now dropped from the serialized payload — but the merge of an empty drop into `existing` is a no-op, so the persisted result is identical to the pre-fix behavior for that case. - The pre-existing behavior for fields the caller explicitly sent (with a value different from the default) is unchanged: those still go through `exclude_none=True` and the shallow merge applies them. ## Future improvements (not in this PR) - The same `dict(...)` pattern in the `litellm_settings` update path (line 14576) is a candidate for the same treatment. A natural cycle 15+ candidate. - Migrating the `.dict()` calls to `.model_dump(...)` is a separate drive-by refactor flagged by the Pydantic V2 deprecation warning. The deprecation applies across the file; the minimum-scope fix here uses the existing API. - A helper like `_pydantic_dict_with_excludes(model, *exclude)` would dedupe the `dict(exclude_none=True, exclude_defaults=True)` pattern across the file and make future regressions a one-line change. Out of scope for this PR. - The issue also notes that `litellm_settings` is affected by the same `{}` default leak for `plugins` (`list[PluginConfig] | None = None` — not a default-`{}` field but the sibling concern). A follow-up cycle could audit the `litellm_settings` model for fields whose defaults silently clobber the stored config.

signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Mid-conversation system reminders on pre-4.8 Claude get hoisted into `system` - The hoist rewrites the cached prefix, re-billing the whole conversation How it solves it: - Convert the reminder to a user turn in place instead - Leading system runs still hoist; flagged models are untouched ## User Flow Before: a Claude Code user routed to a Vertex Claude 4.6 deployment pays full cache-write pricing every turn a reminder appears 1. They run a long session against POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with their proxy key, history carrying `cache_control` breakpoints 2. Claude Code inserts a `role: "system"` reminder mid-conversation 3. The response is 200, but `usage` shows `cache_creation_input_tokens` around 1746 with `cache_read_input_tokens` dropping to 5265: the whole prior history was re-billed at cache-write pricing (reporter's real Vertex numbers in #36559) 4. Every later reminder repeats the same full-prefix rebill After: the same session keeps its cache; only the new turn is fresh 1. They run a long session against POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with their proxy key, history carrying `cache_control` breakpoints 2. Claude Code inserts a `role: "system"` reminder mid-conversation 3. The response is 200, and `usage` shows `cache_read_input_tokens` around 6973 with `cache_creation_input_tokens` around 60: the full prior history read back from cache 4. Follow-up turns keep reading the full cached prefix ## Relevant issues Fixes #36559 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? Three things stand in for that run 1. signal.title: Mid-conversation system-role hoist invalidates the entire prompt-cache prefix (AnthropicMessagesConfig)
signal.text: ## Summary `AnthropicMessagesConfig._normalize_system_role_messages` (introduced in #33807) hoists mid-conversation `role: "system"` messages into the top-level `system` field for Claude models without `supports_mid_conversation_system` (pre-4.8 generation). This avoids the 400 those models throw on partner endpoints (Vertex, Azure Foundry, Bedrock Invoke) — but the hoist itself invalidates the entire cached prompt prefix on every turn a reminder appears, which is exactly the cost [mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages) are designed to avoid. ## Why the hoist breaks caching Per Anthropic's docs, prompt caching hashes the request prefix in order `tools` → `system` → `messages`, and a cache hit requires everything up to the breakpoint to match byte-for-byte. The `system` field sits early in that order, so any change to it — including appending a hoisted message — invalidates the cache for the system prompt *and every cached message after it*, not just the new content. Current code (`litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/transformation.py`, at `6a919aec6a` on `main`): ```python else: hoisted = [m for m in messages if self._is_system_role_message(m)] remaining = [m for m in messages if not self._is_system_role_message(m)] if hoisted: anthropic_messages_request["messages"] = remaining system_content: Final = [ block for source in ( anthropic_messages_request.get("system"), *(m.get("content") for m in hoisted), ) for block in self._as_system_content_blocks(source) ] ``` Every system-role message anywhere in `messages` gets pulled out and folded into `system` on every request (LiteLLM re-derives the downstream payload from the client's full history each call). The turn a *new* reminder first appears, `system`'s content changes for the first time since the last request — full cache miss on that call, reprocessing the entire prior conversation. ## Measured impact (real Vertex AI traffic, unflagged model) | | current (hoist) | proposed (convert-in-place, see below) | |---|---|---| | Reminder-turn `cache_read_input_tokens` | 5265 | 6973 (full prior history preserved) | | Reminder-turn `cache_creation_input_tokens` | 1746 | 60 | | Follow-up turn `cache_read_input_tokens` | 7011 | 7033 | Both variants return `200` — this isn't about the correctness fix from #33807, which works fine. It's specifically the caching side effect of *how* it avoids the 400. ## Proposed fix Since the model itself can't accept `role: "system"` in `messages` at all (that's the actual constraint being worked around), and the hoist target (`system`) sits earlier in the cache hash than `messages`, moving the offending message *anywhere* in `system` will always cost the full prefix. Instead: for unflagged models, mutate the message's `role` to `"user"` **in place** (same position in `messages`) rather than moving it to `system`. Nothing before that position changes, so an existing cache breakpoint still hits; only the new message needs fresh processing — the same cost as any ordinary new turn. I have this working as a local patch with the measurements above, happy to open a PR if that's useful. One tradeoff worth surfacing first: converting to `role: "user"` loses Claude's "system beats a conflicting user instruction" priority for that specific message, compared to a true system-role turn. For models that don't support the feature at all, there may not be a way to fully avoid that tradeoff — but it seemed worth confirming that's an acceptable direction before sending a PR, given it's a behavior change beyond just fixing the 400. ## Environment - litellm `main` @ `6a919aec6a2a0c54cc6a2e6f67ff7b236a3a2573` - Reproduced against real `vertex_ai/` Claude deployments (unflagged, pre-4.8 generation) with the Claude Agent SDK's `mid-conversation-system-2026-04-07` reminder shape - Related: #33807 (introduced the current model-aware hoist), #31452 (earlier draft of the same base-class idea, predates #33807, does not address caching)

signal.title: [Bug]: A2A agent calls report "NoneType takes no arguments" instead of the "install a2a-sdk" error
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. --- ### What happened? `a2a-sdk` is an optional dependency. It ships in the `extra_proxy` extra, not in `proxy`, so the documented install `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'` leaves it out. Calling a registered A2A agent in that state returns ```json {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: NoneType takes no arguments"}} ``` The gateway already has a purpose built message for exactly this case, `Server error: 'a2a' package not installed. Please install 'a2a-sdk'.`, and it never reaches the caller. Neither the response nor the proxy log names the missing package, so an operator has no way to tell what to install I expected the response to name `a2a-sdk`, which is what the gateway was built to say Official Docker images install `extra_proxy` and are not affected. This reaches people who install the gateway with pip or uv and have not separately installed `a2a-sdk` ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator who installed the gateway the documented way calls their registered agent and gets an opaque Python error rather than being told which package is missing 1. They install the gateway with `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`, then register an agent named `demo-agent` under the top level `agents` key in config.yaml 2. They start the gateway and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns 200 3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent with a JSON-RPC `message/send` body 4. The call comes back HTTP 500 with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: NoneType takes no arguments"}}` 5. They check the gateway log and find only `Error invoking agent: NoneType takes no arguments`, repeated, naming no package, so they are left guessing what to install After a (hypothetical) fix: the same call names the missing package, so the operator knows what to do next 1. They install the gateway with `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`, then register an agent named `demo-agent` under the top level `agents` key in config.yaml 2. They start the gateway and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns 200 3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent with a JSON-RPC `message/send` body 4. The call comes back HTTP 500 with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Server error: 'a2a' package not installed. Please install 'a2a-sdk'."}}` 5. They run `pip install "a2a-sdk>=1.1.0,<2.0"`, restart the gateway, and the same POST reaches their agent ### Proof the bug occurs This path fails before any call to the registered agent or to an LLM provider, so no provider request is involved and there is nothing to bill Config the proxy ran with, `a2a_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: sk-placeholder-not-used-by-this-repro agents: - agent_name: demo-agent agent_card_params: name: "Demo Agent" url: "http://localhost:10001" protocolVersion: "1.0" general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Env: `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, and `a2a-sdk` not installed (`pip uninstall a2a-sdk`) Version: commit `423b791ee0`. Also reproduced on released `v1.96.2` Start the proxy: ``` python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config a2a_config.yaml --port 4000 ``` Call the agent: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"hello"}],"messageId":"msg-1"}}}' {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: NoneType takes no arguments"}} [HTTP 500] ``` Proxy log for that request: ``` 23:54:19 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: a2a_endpoints.py:970 - Error invoking agent: NoneType takes no arguments TypeError: NoneType takes no arguments ``` For comparison, the message the gateway is meant to return here, captured on the same proxy and the same request after making the missing-package check reachable: ``` {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Server error: 'a2a' package not installed. Please install 'a2a-sdk'."}} [HTTP 500] ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2 (also reproduced at commit 423b791ee0) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(databricks): replay extended thinking as a reasoning content block
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Multi-turn extended thinking on Databricks Claude fails outright - Two internal message keys leak into the request and get rejected - Any agent replaying its own thinking breaks on the second turn How it solves it: - Convert those keys into the reasoning content block Databricks accepts - Only place the block where the API allows it ## User Flow Before: a developer building a multi-turn agent on a Databricks-served Claude model cannot get past the second turn 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Databricks Claude deployment with extended thinking enabled, and get a normal answer back 2. They append that assistant reply verbatim to their message list, exactly as the API returned it, and add a follow-up question 3. They send the second POST and get back `400 BAD_REQUEST` reading `messages.1.reasoning_content: Extra inputs are not permitted` 4. Their only workarounds are to turn extended thinking off, or to strip the reasoning out of every assistant turn by hand and lose the reasoning chain After: the same conversation continues for as many turns as they like 1. They send the same first POST and get the same answer 2. They append the assistant reply verbatim and add a follow-up question 3. The second POST returns 200 with an answer that builds on the first 4. They keep going, appending each reply verbatim, and turn three also returns 200 5. Turns where the model both reasoned and called a tool also return 200, rather than `The final block in an assistant message cannot be thinking` ## Relevant issues Fixes #36931 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a self-hosted proxy in front of Azure Databricks Foundation Model APIs, hitting `system.ai.claude-opus-5` for real. Every call costs real money Three turn conversation, appending each assistant reply back verbatim: ```py base = {"model": "claude-opus", "max_tokens": 1200, "thinking": {"type": "adaptive"}, "output_config": {"effort": "medium"}, "disable_fallbacks": True, "num_retries": 0} t1 = {**base, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 * 23? Reason briefly."}]} a1 = post(t1)["choices"][0]["message"] t2 = {**base, "messages": [t1["messages"][0], a1, {"role": "user", "content": "Now double that result."}]} a2 = post(t2)["choices"][0]["message"] t3 = {**base, "messages": t2["messages"] + [a2, {"role": "user", "content": "And subtract 82."}]} post(t3) ``` **Before**, at `v1.96.0` unmodified (tag `v1.96.0`, commit `8843766`): ``` turn 1 OK. assistant message carries: ['content', 'role', 'thinking_blocks'] turn 2 REJECTED: litellm.BadRequestError: DatabricksException - {"error_code":"BAD_REQUEST", "message":"{\"message\":\"messages.1.reasoning_content: Extra inputs are not permitted\"}"} ``` **After**, with this PR applied (commit `cd38546`): ``` turn 1 OK, answer: **391** Quick reasoning: 17 × 23 = 17 × (20 + 3) = 340 + 51 turn 2 OK, answer: **782** 391 × 2 = 782. turn 3 OK, answer: **700** 782 − 82 = 700. thinking+tool_use turn: OK ``` Each turn builds on the last, so the reasoning chain survives the round trip rather than being silently discarded ### How the accepted shape was established Rather than guess, I captured a real signed reasoning block from the live endpoint and replayed it in every candidate format: | Assistant content block shape | Result | | --- | --- | | `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": ..., "signature": ...}` (Anthropic native) | rejected, `Failed to parse ContentItem` | | `{"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"type": "reasoning_text", ...}], "encrypted_content": ...}` | rejected, `Expecting one non-null Summary` | | `{"type": "reasoning", "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": ..., "signature": ...}]}` | **accepted** | | message-level `thinking_blocks` | rejected, `Extra inputs are not permitted` | Further constraints, each verified the same way. Exactly one reasoning block per message and exactly one `summary_text` entry inside it, since two of either is rejected. The `signature` is mandatory. The text may be empty, which matters because Databricks returns an empty thinking string alongside the signature. And the block cannot sit in the final position of an assistant message, which is what a thinking-plus-tool-call turn produces once the call moves to message-level `tool_calls` and leaves nothing behind it The accepted shape is the one the existing test in `tests/test_litellm/llms/databricks/chat/test_databricks_chat_transformation.py` already asserts, and the one the provider's own response parsing produces. Worth flagging that Databricks' published docs for multi-turn reasoning describe the `content` / `reasoning_text` / `encrypted_content` shape, which the endpoint actively refuses One honesty note on how the after-run was captured. Building the full image from this branch needs the Rust extension and the admin UI bundle, which was not practical in the environment I had, so the after-run applied this PR's changes over an otherwise byte-identical `v1.96.0` copy of the affected module, verified by SHA-256 against the pristine file before replacement. The code path exercised is exactly what this PR changes. Happy to re-capture from a clean branch build if you would rather see that ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Unsigned or redacted thinking blocks are dropped, since they cannot be replayed - Multiple thinking blocks collapse to the first signed one - Reasoning is dropped when the block would land in the final position - `reasoning_effort` maps to `thinking.type=enabled`, which opus 5 rejects; unrelated, use adaptive to reproduce ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(mcp): clear and reauthorize a server's stored MCP OAuth tokens
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No way to clear an MCP server's stored OAuth token - Reauthorizing with different upstream grants meant recreating the server - Old token kept being served from caches nothing flushed How it solves it: - Admin action clears every stored token for a server - Disconnect and Reauthorize buttons on the MCP servers page - Server URL, auth type, issuer and OAuth client survive the clear ## User Flow Before: an admin who authorized an MCP server with too many upstream scopes cannot take that grant back, because nothing in the product removes the token the gateway is holding 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers, open their OAuth server and press "Authorize & Fetch Token" in the Authentication section 2. The upstream consent screen grants read, the redirect completes, and LiteLLM keeps the token 3. They want to reauthorize with a narrower grant, so they look for a way to drop it: the server's Overview tab has no such control, and its action menu offers only Test Connection and Delete 4. They try the API directly with `curl -i -X DELETE http://localhost:4000/v1/mcp/server/<id>/oauth-token` and get `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found`, `{"detail":"Not Found"}` 5. Their only remaining option is deleting the whole server and recreating it, which loses its teams, access groups, tool allowlist and cost config 6. Every other user of that server keeps whatever the gateway granted them, and nobody can revoke it short of that delete After: the same admin clears the token in place and authorizes again with the grant they want 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers, open their OAuth server and press "Authorize & Fetch Token" as before 2. The Overview tab now carries an "OAuth Connection" card with "Reauthorize" and "Disconnect / Clear token"; the same two entries sit in the server card's action menu on the list page 3. They press Disconnect / Clear token and a dialog asks what to clear, spelling out both blast radii: every stored token for this server, which revokes all users, or only their own connection, which leaves everyone else connected 4. They confirm, and a toast reports how many user tokens were cleared 5. They press "Authorize & Fetch Token" again, consent to the narrower grant, and the server is connected with the new scopes; its URL, auth type, issuer and OAuth client were never touched 6. Any other user of the server is signed out of the upstream and re-authorizes on their next tool call, and stored BYOK API keys are left alone ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5515 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs ran against a real proxy on a real Postgres, using the same script and the same routes. "Authorize & Fetch Token" persists the minted token as a per-user credential row, so the clear drives the existing server-wide purge, which also invalidates both caches that hydrate from those rows. An M2M server keeps no row and mints from an in-memory cache instead, so that cache is flushed by server id in the same call. The minted fields on the server row's own credential blob are cleared too, covering a token written straight through the API. Missing any one of the three leaves the old upstream grants live, which is the state the admin asked to get out of. The server row is written before the purge runs, so the two in-memory reconciliations happen even when the purge raises: otherwise the registry and the mint cache would go on serving material the DB no longer backs, and the admin's retry would read as a no-op. Both are idempotent. Why the declined finding about a failing credential-enumeration query is declined, since review has raised it repeatedly. Two grounds, and the second is the decisive one. First, that failure leaves the database and the caches agreeing rather than diverging: no row is deleted, every credential row is still present and valid, the cached tokens match those rows exactly, the caller gets a 500, and the retry is idempotent. Nothing is revoked because nothing happened, which is the correct failure mode for a revocation. That is precisely what distinguishes it from the deletion-failure case above, which was real and is fixed here, because there the database said revoked while the cache still said usable and a retry could not repair it since the enumeration no longer found those rows. Second, the remedy cannot be written. Per-user invalidation is keyed by user id, and the only source of those ids is the enumeration that just failed, so there is no set of users to invalidate. The cache key is `{prefix}:{user_id}:{server_id}`, user first, so there is no server-scoped prefix to target either; the only satisfying implementation would scan the entire per-user token keyspace and filter by suffix on every disconnect, which is a far worse trade than a 500 the admin retries. Why a self-scoped Reauthorize opens Tools rather than Settings, since review flagged it. Settings is admin-only, rendered behind `isProxyAdmin`, so a non-admin clearing only their own connection cannot see that tab at all and would land on a tab that is not there. The per-user authorize runs from the Tools tab, which is the same redirect-and-exchange flow the admin button uses, so Tools is where that user re-authorizes. The list page and the detail page now agree on this: self goes to Tools with editing off, all-users goes to Settings with editing on. The bug that was there, and is fixed here, was the list page sending the all-users case to Overview while the detail page sent it to Settings. On the two limits review raised for machine-to-machine servers. Such a server mints from the client_id and client_secret it was configured with, so a clear forces a fresh mint rather than revoking access; taking that access away means removing the client, which is a reconfiguration and the exact thing this ticket exists to avoid. Its mint cache is also per worker, so on a multi-worker deployment the other workers keep their own minted token until it expires. Neither is something this change can fix without turning disconnect into reconfigure, so both are stated in the dialog copy and the endpoint docs instead of being implied away, and the dialog no longer claims everyone loses access. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(datadog_llm_obs): map tool_calls to DD Message schema and cache tokens to span metrics
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Datadog Tools panel stays empty for every tool call - Cache hit ratio and cache write tokens never populate How it solves it: - Map tool calls into DD's ToolCall shape on the output message - Forward prompt-cache counts into top-level span metrics ## Relevant issues Fixes #35786 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Details Datadog's LLM Observability intake reads tool calls from `meta.output.messages[].tool_calls` using its own ToolCall shape (`name`, `arguments`, `tool_id`, `type`), and reads prompt-cache counts from top-level span `metrics`; see https://docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/setup/api/. The callback was passing the raw OpenAI-style message straight through, where the call sits under a nested `function` dict, and it was leaving cache counts nested in `metadata.usage_object`. In both cases the data reached Datadog but in a place Datadog does not read, so the Tools panel and the cache hit ratio rendered empty `_get_response_messages` now maps the assistant message into the DD shape; `arguments` that fail to parse as JSON are kept as the raw string rather than dropping the call. `create_llm_obs_payload` forwards `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_write_input_tokens` and `non_cached_input_tokens` into span metrics, and `LLMMetrics` gains those three fields The existing output tool-call test asserted the old nested-`function` shape, so it now pins the documented DD schema instead; new tests cover cache metric forwarding, an absent `usage_object`, malformed arguments, and a plain response with no tool calls Scoped out deliberately: `meta.tool_definitions` and input-side `tool_results` from the same issue. Happy to follow those up separately ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I don't have a Datadog account or paid provider credentials, so I can't post an intake screenshot from a live proxy. What I can show is the exact payload the callback now hands to `safe_dumps`, driven through `create_llm_obs_payload` with the reporter's Bedrock-style usage object (176 cache write, 16695 cache read, 16872 prompt): ``` $ python proof_of_fix.py meta.output.messages: [ { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [ { "name": "task", "arguments": { "description": "Find DD callback code" }, "tool_id": "toolu_bdrk_01F8", "type": "function" } ] } ] metrics: { "input_tokens": 16872.0, "output_tokens": 704.0, "total_tokens": 17576.0, "time_to_first_token": 0.5, "cache_read_input_tokens": 16695.0, "cache_write_input_tokens": 176.0, "non_cached_input_tokens": 177.0 } ``` Before this change the same input produced `tool_calls` still wrapped in the OpenAI `function` dict, and `metrics` carried only input/output/total tokens with the cache counts stranded in `meta.metadata.usage_object`. If a maintainer with a DD account wants the live trace before merging, I'm glad to supply the config

signal.title: feat(melious): add Melious as a provider
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `melious/*` model names do not resolve at all - Reaching Melious needs a hand-wired base URL per deployment - Its two API surfaces need two different base URLs - Spend reads zero without hand-pasted per-token prices How it solves it: - Registers `melious` across the provider map - Serves `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` natively - Ships cost-map entries for 17 flagship chat models ## User Flow Before: a developer routing to Melious wires a base URL into every deployment, and a second, different one for the Anthropic surface 1. They add a deployment with `model: openai/glm-5.1`, `api_base: https://api.melious.ai/v1`, and their Melious key 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "glm-5.1"` and get a normal completion back 3. They want Claude Code on the same account, so they add a second deployment with `model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4` and `api_base: https://api.melious.ai`, this time without the `/v1` 4. Whenever either base URL carries the wrong suffix the call returns `NotFoundError: The requested resource was not found`, which never says which surface was wrong 5. Every response header reads `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0` until they look up per-token prices and paste them into each deployment After: naming the model is the whole configuration, and one key covers both surfaces 1. They export `MELIOUS_API_KEY` and add a deployment with `model: melious/glm-5.1`, no `api_base` 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "glm-5.1"` and get the same completion back 3. For Claude Code they add `model: melious/claude-sonnet-4`, again with no `api_base` 4. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages and get an Anthropic-shaped response, streaming events included 5. Response headers carry a real `x-litellm-response-cost` with nothing pasted in by hand ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All three proofs captured at `<COMMIT_SHA>` against the live Melious API, billed to a real account. Config used: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: melious-glm litellm_params: model: melious/glm-5.1 api_key: os.environ/MELIOUS_API_KEY - model_name: melious/* litellm_params: model: melious/* api_key: os.environ/MELIOUS_API_KEY litellm_settings: drop_params: true ``` **1. `/v1/chat/completions`, non-streaming** ```bash curl http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"melious-glm","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Name one Hanseatic city. One word."}],"max_tokens":256}' ``` ``` model: melious-glm content: 'Lübeck' usage: 212 ``` Streaming on the same route, first events: ```bash curl -N http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"melious-glm","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count: 1 2 3"}],"max_tokens":128,"stream":true}' ``` ``` data: {"id":"a54bde4cb71b4a94a9c273ceee5fc2aa","created":1786719034,"model":"melious-glm","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"reasoning_content":"1","role":"assistant"}}]} data: {"id":"a54bde4cb71b4a94a9c273ceee5fc2aa","created":1786719034,"model":"melious-glm","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"reasoning_content":". **An"}}]} ``` Tool calling, and the wildcard route resolving a model with no explicit deployment: ``` tool_calls: [('get_weather', '{"city": "Hamburg"}')] model: melious/qwen3-coder-next content: 'OK! 😊' ``` Cost is computed from the shipped map, with no per-deployment prices configured: ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00026425 x-litellm-model-api-base: https://api.melious.ai/v1 ``` **2. `/v1/messages`** ```bash curl http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"melious-glm","max_tokens":512,"system":"Use tools when asked.","tools":[{"name":"get_weather","description":"Weather for a city","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"]}}],"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Weather in Hamburg? Use the tool."}]}' ``` ``` stop_reason: tool_use block types: ['thinking', 'tool_use'] tool_use: get_weather {'city': 'Hamburg'} usage: {'input_tokens': 160, 'output_tokens': 36} ``` Streaming on the same route returns the full Anthropic event set: ``` 65 event: content_block_delta 2 event: content_block_start 2 event: content_block_stop 1 event: message_delta 1 event: message_start 1 event: message_stop ``` **3. `/v1/responses`** ```bash curl http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"melious-glm","input":"Name one Hanseatic city. One word.","max_output_tokens":512}' ``` ``` object: response | status: completed | model: melious-glm reasoning / output_text : '1. Identify the core entity and constraint: The user wants the name of a Hanseatic city, and it mu message / output_text : 'Hamburg' usage: {"input_tokens": 15, "output_tokens": 171, "total_tokens": 186, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 168, "text_tokens": 3}} ``` Same route through the SDK: ```python litellm.responses(model="melious/glm-5.1", input="Name one Hanseatic city. One word.", max_output_tokens=256) ``` ``` type: ResponsesAPIResponse | model: melious/glm-5.1 | status: completed usage: input_tokens=15 output_tokens=180 total_tokens=195 reasoning_tokens=177 text_tokens=3 ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Cost map holds published EUR rates in USD fields - Same convention the existing `ovhcloud/*` entries already use - Covers 17 flagship chat models, not the full catalog - Needs a companion `litellm-docs` PR documenting the env vars ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
